6. Laptop makers, automakers, industrial equipment manufacturers and commercial facility operators.
7. Its MEMS microphones are designed into laptops by consumer electronics brands, its commercial audio systems are installed in venues and its acoustic analytics platforms are deployed in automotive testing.
8. Combines acoustic monitoring platforms developed for aerospace with industrial audio analytics and a broad portfolio of commercial audio and sensor hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Owns Electro-Voice and Arioso Systems, partners with xMEMS Labs and XMOS and supplies BMW.
Organization type: A publicly traded multinational engineering and technology company.
Business model: Component and hardware sales, commercial audio equipment sales and software platform sales.
Scale and maturity: A large multinational company established for over 90 years holding a top-ten position in the packaged MEMS microphone market.
Geography: Based in Germany and operating globally.
Beyond audio: A diversified engineering company that also produces automotive systems, industrial sensors, power tools, home appliances and electric motors.

points.name: PUI Audio
points.description: Dayton, Ohio, USA manufacturer building micro speakers and MEMS microphones for slim wearables and earphones.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of audio components that designs and sells MEMS microphones, electret condenser microphones, bone-conduction microphones and micro speakers for device makers.
1. A component manufacturer that builds audio transducers and sells them as finished hardware parts.
2. MEMS, piezoelectric and electret condenser transducer technology packaged as analog and digital microphones.
3. Sound capture with variants for high-SPL, low-noise, omnidirectional, waterproof, bone-conduction and wideband audio pickup.
4. Finished hardware components, evaluation boards and rapid prototyping services.
5. Slim wearables, earphones, condition monitoring systems and general consumer electronics.
6. Device makers, electronics distributors and electronics hobbyist kit providers.
7. Its components are designed into consumer electronics and wearables by device manufacturers.
8. Offers a piezoelectric MEMS microphone with IP68 waterproof and dustproof rating for improved fidelity and noise rejection over capacitive MEMS.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Maxim Integrated supplies its smart amplifiers for use with the company's micro speakers, and its components are distributed by Digi-Key and included in kits from SparkFun and Adafruit.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware component sales.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with a broad catalog of standard microphone parts.
Geography: Based in Dayton, Ohio, USA.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus is on audio components.

points.name: GlobalFoundries
points.description: US semiconductor foundry manufacturing low-power audio processors and MEMS microphones.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor foundry that manufactures chips and MEMS transducers for audio applications, providing wafer fabrication services to fabless chip companies and MEMS microphone developers.
1. A semiconductor foundry that provides wafer fabrication services, manufacturing chips and MEMS transducers at its fabs.
2. 22nm FD-SOI process technology with low-power and body-biasing capabilities, and piezoelectric MEMS manufacturing on 200mm wafers.
3. Fabrication of low-power audio processors and MEMS microphone transducers.
4. Fabricated wafers and manufactured chips delivered to chip design companies.
5. Low-power audio processors used in edge devices and MEMS microphones used in audio capture systems.
6. Fabless semiconductor companies and MEMS microphone developers.
7. Its fabricated wafers and manufactured MEMS elements are integrated into audio chips and microphones sold by device makers.
8. A pioneer in piezoelectric MEMS manufacturing with optimized MEMS lines specifically for audio applications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Infineon, GreenWaves, Vesper Technologies, Polyn, Witmem, Microchip, Cirrus Logic and Nordic Semiconductor.
Organization type: A publicly traded semiconductor foundry.
Business model: Wafer fabrication services and semiconductor manufacturing.
Scale and maturity: One of the largest and most advanced semiconductor foundries.
Geography: Based in Malta, New York, USA, and operates globally.
Beyond audio: A semiconductor foundry that manufactures a broad range of chips and MEMS devices across multiple industries including automotive, consumer electronics and communications.

points.name: sensiBel
points.description: Norwegian deep-tech company developing optical MEMS microphones for high-performance audio.
points.bullets:
A sensor developer that develops and manufactures optical MEMS microphones providing high-SNR, high-dynamic-range digital audio capture for professional audio, high-end consumer electronics, and automotive applications.
1. A sensor developer that designs optical MEMS microphones sold as finished components and evaluation platforms that run integrated into customers' hardware devices.
2. The core technology uses a VCSEL laser and integrated interferometer to measure the motion of a silicon MEMS diaphragm via optical readout, replacing traditional capacitive sensing.
3. The sensors deliver high signal-to-noise ratio, high dynamic range, 24-bit digital output, high acoustic overload point, and low power consumption in a miniature form factor.
4. Customers receive finished microphone components, multi-microphone arrays, and evaluation boards for development and integration.
5. The microphones are used in conferencing systems, laptops, automotive road-noise cancellation, professional audio equipment, spatial audio capture arrays, and edge AI acoustic detection devices.
6. The organization sells to professional audio equipment manufacturers, consumer electronics brands, and automotive component suppliers.
7. Its microphone components are designed into spatial audio arrays and automotive modules by equipment and system makers.
8. The optical interferometry approach replaces capacitive MEMS sensing to achieve studio-quality acoustic performance with higher signal-to-noise ratio and dynamic range in a compact form factor.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners and investors include Sennheiser, AAC Technologies, In-Q-Tel, TRUMPF Venture, Silex, Aizip, and mh acoustics.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held deep-tech startup.
Business model: The company makes money through sales of finished microphone hardware components and evaluation kits.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2016, the company has secured strategic investments led by Sennheiser and TRUMPF Venture, supported by EU funding.
Geography: The company is based in Norway and operates globally.
Beyond audio: Audio is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: Starkey
points.description: US hearing aid manufacturer integrating AI and broadcast audio into hearing devices.
points.bullets:
A hearing aid manufacturer that builds AI-powered hearing instruments and companion software for consumers and hearing health professionals.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished hearing aids containing custom neural processors running on-device in the ear, alongside companion mobile applications.
2. Custom neural processing units executing deep neural networks locally within low-power wearable hearing instruments.
3. Speech enhancement, noise reduction, spatial directionality, feedback cancellation, fall detection, balance assessment, and sleep tracking.
4. Finished hearing aid hardware, companion mobile applications, and professional fitting software.
5. Hearing aids, receiver-in-canal devices, behind-the-ear devices, and health monitoring wearables.
6. Consumers, hearing health professionals, and retail hearing aid clinics.
7. Its finished devices are distributed and fitted to patients through independent audiologists and retail hearing clinic networks.
8. Integrates custom neural processors with built-in health and wellness sensors to treat hearing aids as lifestyle and medical monitoring devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Meta, Intel, Stanford University, MED-EL, Bragi, and OrCam Technologies.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hearing aid hardware sales, direct-to-consumer retail channels, and consumer financing programs.
Scale and maturity: A billion-dollar company founded in 1967 with over 5000 employees operating in more than 100 markets.
Geography: Based in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, USA, operating globally.
Beyond audio: It also operates retail hearing aid clinics and a hearing aid financing program.

points.name: Zilltek Technology
points.description: Taiwanese MEMS microphone manufacturer designing high signal-to-noise ratio microphones and power management chips for notebooks and active noise cancellation.
points.bullets:
A Taiwan-based fabless semiconductor design house that designs and manufactures MEMS microphones, analog audio chips and power management ICs for consumer electronics manufacturers, focusing on high signal-to-noise ratios for notebook and active noise cancellation applications.
1. A chip company that designs MEMS microphone and power management ICs, sold as finished hardware components for integration into consumer electronics devices.
2. MEMS microphone designs combined with analog and digital audio integrated circuits, incorporating edge AI silicon to process voice and audio signals directly within the microphone hardware.
3. High signal-to-noise ratio audio capture, flat frequency response for active noise cancellation, and embedded edge voice recognition and noise cancellation capabilities.
4. Physical semiconductor components, including digital MEMS microphones, fully differential analog MEMS microphone chips and power management ICs.
5. High-end notebooks and consumer electronics requiring active noise cancellation.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers.
7. Its microphone and power management chips are designed into notebooks by consumer electronics brands.
8. A focus on high-performance metrics like high signal-to-noise ratios and flat frequency responses combined with early adoption of edge AI silicon integrated directly into microphone hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: PIMIC.
Organization type: Privately held semiconductor design house.
Business model: Semiconductor component sales.
Scale and maturity: An established company shipping product samples of edge AI integrated microphones.
Geography: Based in Taiwan.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus is on audio and power management semiconductors.

points.name: Sonion
points.description: Danish audio component manufacturer building miniature acoustic components for hearing aids and professional earphones.
points.bullets:
A component manufacturer that designs and produces miniature acoustic and micromechanical components for hearing aids and ear-level audio devices. It supplies balanced armature receivers, microphones, and sensors to hearing instrument makers and high-end audio brands.
1. A component manufacturer that builds acoustic transducers and sensors sold as finished hardware components to device manufacturers.
2. Balanced armature receivers, MEMS microphones, bone conduction sensors, and electrostatic tweeters engineered for miniature, in-ear acoustics.
3. High-SPL sound reproduction, voice pickup via bone conduction, low-noise audio capture, and biometric sensing.
4. Finished hardware components and modules customized in collaboration with device manufacturers.
5. Hearing aids, in-ear monitors, and ear-level wearable audio devices.
6. Hearing instrument manufacturers and high-end earphone brands.
7. Its components are designed into hearing aids and earphones by consumer electronics and medical device brands.
8. It designs ultra-small balanced armature receivers that achieve the acoustic output of components twice their size while significantly reducing vibration and feedback.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Novo Holdings A/S, InvenSense, Valencell, TDK.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Component sales and custom design collaboration.
Scale and maturity: A mature, global manufacturing company with over 3,000 employees.
Geography: Based in Denmark with manufacturing facilities in Vietnam and the Philippines, serving Europe, North America, and Asia.
Beyond audio: Its focus is exclusively on miniature acoustic and micromechanical components for ear-level devices.

points.name: Gettop Acoustic Co., Ltd.
points.description: Chinese public company manufacturing miniature electroacoustic devices like MEMS microphones and audio modules for smartphones and wearables.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of electroacoustic components that makes MEMS microphones, miniature electroacoustic devices and intelligent acoustic modules for smartphone, wearable and automotive makers.
1. A component manufacturer that builds MEMS microphones and acoustic modules sold as finished hardware embedded in customers' devices.
2. Micro-electromechanical systems and electroacoustic transducer technology for sound capture and reproduction.
3. Sound capture and reproduction through miniature microphones and acoustic modules with integrated intelligence.
4. Finished hardware components and modules sold to device manufacturers for integration into their products.
5. Smartphones, wearables and intelligent vehicle cockpits.
6. Smartphone makers, wearable device makers and automakers.
7. Its acoustic components are designed into smartphones, wearables and vehicle cockpits by consumer electronics brands and automakers.
points.profile:
Organization type: A publicly traded company listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange.
Business model: Hardware component sales through its Electroacoustic Division and a separate Distribution Division.
Scale and maturity: A company founded in 2001 with over 20 years in the industry, subsidiaries in multiple countries and acquired semiconductor and smart cockpit platform capabilities in 2022 and 2024.
Geography: Based in China with subsidiaries and offices in multiple countries and regions.
Beyond audio: The company also operates a Distribution Division alongside its core electroacoustic component business.

points.name: Wolfson Microelectronics
points.description: Scottish fabless chip company making audio codecs and DSPs for phones and tablets.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs audio codecs, digital-to-analog converters, and standalone audio DSPs, as well as manufacturing MEMS microphones, for consumer electronics and audio equipment makers.
1. A fabless chip company whose audio codecs, converters, and DSPs are sold as discrete semiconductors that run on the digital circuitry of consumer devices and hi-fi hardware.
2. Mixed-signal audio processing integrated circuits, including audio codecs, stereo digital-to-analog converters with selectable digital filters, and standalone Tensilica DSPs with fixed-point data engines.
3. Analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog audio conversion, digital audio interfacing, and standalone digital signal processing for audio.
4. Finished silicon chips sold as discrete components.
5. Phones, tablets, TVs, consumer tablets, and standalone digital-to-analog converters used in hi-fi amplifiers.
6. Consumer electronics brands, tablet makers, and high-fidelity audio equipment manufacturers.
7. Its chips are designed into consumer tablets and standalone audio hardware by electronics brands.
8. Combines mixed-signal audio codec and converter silicon with standalone Tensilica-based audio DSPs and MEMS microphone hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Microsoft, Rega, and Rotel.
Organization type: Privately held or formerly independent fabless semiconductor company.
Business model: Semiconductor component sales.
Scale and maturity: A Scottish supplier that broke through at the end of 2012 by supplying microphones to a major tablet.
Geography: Based in Edinburgh, Scotland, UK.
Beyond audio: The company is a pure-play audio semiconductor and component business.

points.name: NeoMEMS
points.description: Chinese startup making MEMS microphones and speakers.
points.bullets:
A maker of audio hardware components that designs and develops miniature MEMS microphone components for the audio device manufacturing industry.
1. A component maker that designs MEMS microphones sold as hardware components for integration into other manufacturers' products.
2. Micro-electromechanical systems technology fabricated to create miniature acoustic transducers that convert sound waves into electrical signals.
3. Acoustic capture and sound pressure conversion through MEMS microphone components.
4. Finished hardware components supplied for integration into devices.
5. Devices requiring acoustic input, where microphones are integrated by consumer electronics manufacturers.
6. Device manufacturers and consumer electronics brands requiring acoustic components.
7. Its microphone components are designed into end-user devices by consumer electronics brands.
8. It is a recent entrant in the MEMS microphone market noted for its emerging component development.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware component sales.
Scale and maturity: A new entrant operating as an early-stage company in its specific industry.
Geography: Based and operating in China.
Beyond audio: Audio hardware is the organization's entire focus, centered solely on developing MEMS microphone technology.

points.name: TDK-EPC
points.description: German electronics supplier producing MEMS microphones with digital interfaces for portable devices.
points.bullets:
A component manufacturer that produces MEMS microphones using processes derived from SAW filter production, selling miniature acoustic transducers with integrated digital interfaces to electronics makers.
1. An electronics component manufacturer that builds MEMS microphones sold as finished hardware parts for integration into customers' devices.
2. MEMS microphone technology with an integrated digital interface producing PDM output, manufactured using techniques adapted from SAW filter production.
3. Acoustic capture and conversion to digital pulse-density modulation output at low power consumption in a miniature form factor.
4. Finished surface-mount microphone components sold directly to device manufacturers.
5. Portable and compact electronic devices requiring miniature acoustic input components.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers and other device makers requiring embedded acoustic components.
7. Its microphone components are designed into portable electronic devices by product manufacturers.
8. It leverages surface acoustic wave filter manufacturing expertise to produce some of the smallest commercially available MEMS microphones.
points.profile:
Organization type: A corporate subsidiary of a large electronics and components manufacturer.
Business model: Sales of finished acoustic hardware components.
Geography: Based in Germany, operating as a new entrant in the global MEMS microphone market.
Beyond audio: It produces a broad range of electronic components beyond microphones, with audio representing one segment of its components business.

points.name: CUI Devices
points.description: Portland, Oregon electronic components manufacturer designing MEMS microphones for voice capture and noise cancellation.
points.bullets:
An electronic components manufacturer whose Audio Group produces MEMS and electret condenser microphones for voice capture and audio recording in portable consumer electronics. Its microphone catalog spans analog and digital PDM output parts in compact, low-profile packages, including waterproof and noise-cancellation-suited models, sold as components to device builders.
1. A components manufacturer that builds microphones as finished electronic components sold to equipment makers for integration into their products.
2. MEMS microphone technology fabricated in compact packages with profiles as low as 0.90 mm, offered in analog and digital PDM output variants with varying sensitivity and signal-to-noise ratio ratings.
3. Voice capture and audio recording, with specific models suited to active noise cancellation and operation in moisture and constant liquid entry conditions, including an IPX7 waterproof rating.
4. Microphones are sold as discrete electronic components in various sizes and configurations, supplied as parts for direct integration into devices.
5. Portable consumer electronics and other devices requiring microphones in moisture-exposed or challenging conditions.
6. Device makers and electronics manufacturers who integrate microphone components into their products.
7. Its microphones are designed into consumer electronics products by equipment manufacturers.
8. Its microphones combine extremely compact, low-profile packages with a broad range of sensitivities and output types, including waterproof ratings for harsh moisture environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its Audio Group operates as the audio division of its broader electronic components business.
Organization type: A components manufacturer with a dedicated audio division, part of a company spanning audio, interconnect, motion, relays, sensors, switches, and thermal management products.
Business model: Component sales of microphones and other electronic parts to equipment manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: The company maintains a broad multi-category electronic components catalog with a dedicated Audio Group that launched a waterproof MEMS microphone in September 2023.
Geography: Based in Portland, Oregon, USA.
Beyond audio: The organization produces a wide range of electronic components including interconnect, motion, relays, sensors, switches, and thermal management solutions, with audio microphones as one product category.

points.name: Nisshinbo Micro Devices Inc.
points.description: Japanese semiconductor manufacturer producing MEMS microphone elements and audio integrated circuits.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor manufacturer that produces MEMS microphone transducer elements and pre-amplifiers for audio capture, alongside analog integrated circuits and microwave products. It supplies bare wafers of MEMS transducers and pre-amplifier chips to audio module manufacturers and consumer electronics brands.
1. A semiconductor manufacturer that fabricates MEMS microphone transducer dies and analog pre-amplifier chips, sold as bare wafers for integration into packaged microphones.
2. Capacitive MEMS transducers combined with low-power analog and digital pre-amplifier integrated circuits designed for acoustic signal capture and conversion.
3. Acoustic-to-electrical signal transduction, microphone pre-amplification, pulse density modulation output, and power supply rejection.
4. Bare semiconductor wafers containing MEMS transducer dies and pre-amplifier circuits sold for packaging and module assembly.
5. Microphone modules built into consumer electronics, automotive systems, industrial equipment, and telecommunications devices.
6. Consumer electronics brands, automotive manufacturers, industrial equipment manufacturers, and telecommunications companies.
7. Its transducer dies and pre-amplifier wafers are packaged by microphone module manufacturers and designed into end-user devices by consumer electronics brands.
8. It supplies MEMS microphone transducers and pre-amplifiers as bare wafers, enabling module manufacturers to integrate the components directly into packaged microphone assemblies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Associated with New Japan Radio and holds ISO 9001 and IATF 16949 certifications.
Organization type: A privately held semiconductor and electronic components manufacturing company established in 1959.
Business model: Semiconductor wafer and integrated circuit sales.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with over 60 years of operation.
Geography: Based in Tokyo, Japan, serving global telecommunications, automotive, and consumer electronics industries.
Beyond audio: The company manufactures analog integrated circuits, power management chips, and microwave products alongside its audio components.

points.name: Projects Unlimited Inc.
points.description: US manufacturer producing audio components like MEMS microphones for consumer electronics.
points.bullets:
A component manufacturer that produces MEMS microphones and supplies them to original equipment manufacturers for integration into consumer electronics, automotive systems, and IoT devices.
1. An acoustic hardware manufacturer that builds MEMS microphones and sells them as finished physical components for integration into hardware assemblies.
2. Microelectromechanical systems comprising miniaturized mechanical acoustic sensing structures fabricated on silicon.
3. Acoustic capture for voice input, voice recognition, and noise cancellation in embedded hardware systems.
4. Finished hardware components supplied to device manufacturers.
5. Smartphones, wearables, smart home systems, automotive systems, and IoT devices.
6. Original equipment manufacturers integrating acoustic components into electronic products.
7. Its microphone components are designed into consumer electronics, automotive systems, and IoT devices by original equipment manufacturers.
8. A focus on advanced fabrication processes for miniaturized acoustic components.
points.profile:
Business model: Hardware sales of acoustic components.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer holding significant market share in the global MEMS microphone market.
Geography: Operates in the global market supplying components for international applications.
Beyond audio: Audio technology is its entire focus.

points.name: Wuxi Silicon Source Technology Co., Ltd.
points.description: Chinese audio technology company designing MEMS microphones and noise reduction algorithms for automotive, robotics, and health-tech applications.
aliases: Wuxi Silicon Source Technology Co., Ltd. (SISTC)
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs and manufactures MEMS microphones and smart microphone modules for device manufacturers, integrating in-house ASIC design with acoustic transducer fabrication.
1. A semiconductor and equipment maker that designs and manufactures MEMS microphone components, sold as finished sensors and modules that run embedded in customers' hardware.
2. CMOS/MEMS transducer technology with embedded charge pumps, analog front ends, and integrated neural processing units for always-on voice wake-up.
3. High-sensitivity audio capture with high signal-to-noise ratio, low total harmonic distortion, high acoustic overload point, low-power voice activity detection, and keyword recognition.
4. Finished hardware components, smart microphone modules, and engineering support services for acoustic cavity and sound port validation.
5. Smartphones, wearables, smart home devices, automotive in-cabin voice communication and active noise cancellation systems, industrial robotics, and condition monitoring systems.
6. Device manufacturers, automakers, and industrial equipment makers.
7. Its microphone components are designed into consumer electronics and automotive hardware by product manufacturers.
8. It operates as an integrated device manufacturer combining in-house ASIC design with 12-inch wafer fab partnerships to produce side port MEMS microphone designs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its sensors are designed into automotive platforms by BMW and Hyundai and provide audio input for Google Gemini voice models.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Component hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A company with over 15 years of operation and mass production capabilities.
Geography: Based in Wuxi, China, leveraging the regional semiconductor ecosystem.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on acoustic sensor technology and does not operate outside of audio.

points.name: RØDE
points.description: Australian manufacturer making microphones, wireless systems, and studio equipment for creators.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional and consumer audio equipment that develops and produces microphones, wireless systems, podcasting consoles, audio interfaces, and recording software for creators, musicians, broadcasters, and filmmakers.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished audio hardware and companion software products sold to end users.
2. Condenser and dynamic microphone capsules, UHF and 2.4 GHz wireless transmission systems, MEMS microphone technology, and digital audio mixing and processing integrated into standalone consoles.
3. Studio and location sound capture, directional shotgun pickup, wireless audio transmission, multi-channel podcast mixing, and mobile audio recording.
4. Finished hardware products, including microphones, wireless kits, and podcasting consoles, alongside companion mobile and desktop recording applications.
5. Home and professional recording studios, live stages, film and broadcast location sets, podcasting setups, and mobile content creation environments.
6. Consumers, creators, musicians, filmmakers, broadcasters, and podcasters.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold through retail channels directly to end users and integrated into their personal audio production workflows.
8. It develops its own MEMS microphone technology platform in partnership with semiconductor manufacturers and operates its own precision manufacturing facilities in Australia.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The Freedman Group is its parent company, Infineon manufactures its MEMS chipsets, and it acquired Mackie.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand under a privately held parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio equipment and accessories.
Scale and maturity: A company with between 201 and 500 employees, over 50 years of history, and a global export footprint across 118 countries.
Geography: Headquartered in Sydney, Australia, with offices in China, the UK, and the USA.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Freedman Group
points.description: Australian parent company managing pro audio brands like RØDE, Mackie, and Lectrosonics.
points.bullets:
A holding company and manufacturer of professional audio equipment that owns a portfolio of audio brands making microphones, wireless systems, signal processors and studio monitors for professionals and consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware and related accessories sold as physical products.
2. Analog and digital audio capture, wireless transmission and signal processing technologies, including a microphone technology platform.
3. Audio capture, wireless audio transmission, signal processing, surround sound capture and playback.
4. Finished hardware products and physical audio devices.
5. Studios, live venues, broadcast environments and consumer recording setups.
6. Consumers, recording studios, musicians, live sound engineers and broadcast professionals.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users and through retail channels.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: RØDE, Mackie, Lectrosonics, Aphex, Event Electronics and SoundField.
Organization type: Privately held parent company and holding company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A multi-brand parent company with a large catalog of professional audio products.
Geography: Headquartered in Australia with a focus on global manufacturing and export.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is on professional and consumer audio technology and equipment.

points.name: Lectrosonics
points.description: US professional audio manufacturer building wireless microphone systems for film and broadcast.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures wireless microphone systems, body pack and handheld transmitters, lavalier microphones, and in-ear monitor systems for film, broadcast, and theater applications.
1. An equipment maker that builds wireless microphone systems, transmitters, receivers, and microphones sold as finished hardware used in production environments.
2. Patented digital hybrid wireless technology and UHF radio frequency transmission combined with condenser and MEMS microphone capsules.
3. Wireless audio capture, radio frequency transmission, wide-band tuning, compandor-free audio processing, and in-ear monitoring.
4. Finished hardware products, including body packs, handheld transmitters, lavalier microphones, and slot-compatible receivers, along with firmware updates and system design consulting.
5. Film sets, broadcast studios, live theater stages, and music production environments.
6. Audio engineers, sound professionals, and retail equipment distributors.
7. Its finished wireless audio hardware and microphone systems are used directly by audio professionals in mission-critical production environments.
8. Patented digital hybrid wireless technology provides wide tuning ranges and compandor-free audio in rugged, durable hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A brand within the Freedman Group alongside RØDE, and a co-developer of the SuperSlot standard.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a privately held parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales of professional audio equipment and wireless systems, supplemented by customer consulting services.
Scale and maturity: A long-established manufacturer founded in 1971.
Geography: Headquartered in Rio Rancho, New Mexico, USA, serving professional markets globally.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on professional audio and wireless communication equipment.

points.name: RØDE's UK AI Lab
points.description: UK research and development lab building desktop applications for podcast post-production.
points.bullets:
An internal software research and development team that builds desktop applications for podcast post-production for consumers and creators.
1. A software development team that builds desktop applications sold as finished software running on personal computers.
2. Desktop audio processing software designed for podcast post-production.
3. The organization delivers its work as finished software products.
4. Its software is used in podcast post-production.
5. It serves consumers and creators.
6. Its software products are published by its parent company.
points.profile:
Organization type: It is a research and development lab and internal division.
Beyond audio: Its focus is desktop software for podcast post-production.

points.name: Audeze
points.description: Premium headphone manufacturer building high-end planar magnetic headphones and wireless gaming headsets.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and consumer headphones that designs and builds high-end planar magnetic and electrostatic headphones, in-ear monitors, wireless gaming headsets, and companion software plugins for audiophiles, gaming, and professional studio use.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished over-ear headphones and in-ear monitors, sold as physical hardware and companion software applications that run on desktop and mobile platforms.
2. Planar magnetic drivers using proprietary magnet arrays, phase management waveguides, and nano-scale diaphragm technology, alongside electrostatic drivers using carbon-nanotube polymers and acoustic airflow modulators.
3. High-fidelity sound reproduction, spatial audio rendering, personalized head-related transfer function modeling, active noise cancellation, and AI-based sidetone noise removal.
4. Finished hardware, companion desktop and mobile software applications, and spatial audio plugins.
5. Recording studios, mixing and mastering environments, esports gaming, MRI machines, and consumer listening.
6. Consumers, audiophiles, professional recording engineers, esports athletes, and specialized medical facilities.
7. Its finished headphones and headsets are sold directly to end users and through consumer electronics retailers for use in gaming and studio workflows.
8. It applies medical-grade transducer technology developed for MRI machines and proprietary acoustic airflow modulators to planar magnetic and electrostatic headphone designs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is a subsidiary of Sony Interactive Entertainment, with technology partnerships with Microchip and Embody.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales of premium headphones and headsets.
Scale and maturity: A mid-size company with 11 to 50 employees, founded in the early 2010s and acquired in 2023.
Geography: Based in California, operating globally.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play audio company entirely focused on headphone and transducer technology.

points.name: Anker Soundcore
points.description: Consumer electronics brand producing adjustable wireless earbuds with open-ear and noise-canceling modes.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics brand that designs and sells finished audio hardware, specifically earbuds, for general consumers. It builds wireless earbuds with adjustable ear hooks that switch between open-ear awareness and active noise cancellation, incorporating auto-calibrating equalization and head-tracking spatial audio.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished consumer earbuds and sells them as complete hardware products.
2. The earbuds deliver active noise cancellation, auto-calibrating equalization, head-tracking spatial audio, and support for the LDAC codec.
3. Consumers get the technology as finished hardware products.
4. The earbuds are used by general consumers in everyday listening environments.
5. The company sells directly to consumers.
6. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users through consumer retail channels.
7. Its earbuds feature a dual-form-factor design with five adjustable wearing positions that allow switching between open-ear and in-ear modes.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand of a larger consumer electronics company.
Business model: It makes money through direct hardware sales of finished consumer electronics products.
Geography: The company operates globally and showcases products at international consumer electronics trade shows.
Beyond audio: The company operates as a dedicated audio brand within a broader consumer electronics portfolio.

points.name: Edifier
points.description: Chinese audio manufacturer making consumer speakers, earbuds, and gaming headsets.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and professional audio equipment that designs, engineers, and manufactures finished speakers, headphones, earbuds, and studio monitors for consumers, gamers, and creators.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware and sells it as physical products.
2. Digital signal processing, room acoustic calibration, active noise cancellation, spatial audio, planar magnetic drivers, and balanced armature technologies embedded in finished consumer audio hardware.
3. Active noise cancellation, spatial audio, room acoustic calibration, and high-fidelity audio reproduction.
4. Finished hardware products sold to end users.
5. Earbuds, over-ear headphones, bookshelf speakers, desktop speakers, studio monitors, and gaming headsets.
6. Consumers, gamers, and home studio creators.
7. Its finished audio products are sold directly to consumers through global retail channels.
8. It maintains vertically integrated design, engineering, and manufacturing capabilities spanning a broad portfolio from entry-level multimedia speakers to premium Hi-Fi brands and professional studio monitors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The parent company of the STAX, HECATE, and AIRPULSE brands, integrating technologies and components from THX, Qualcomm, Airoha, Bestechnic, Knowles, and Linkplay.
Organization type: A privately held company and parent corporate brand.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished consumer and professional audio products.
Scale and maturity: A company founded in 1996 with over 300 employees operating in more than 80 countries.
Geography: Based in Beijing, China, with global operations across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia Pacific.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio hardware and electronics.

points.name: JLab
points.description: California audio brand making affordable wireless earbuds, headphones, and over-the-counter hearing aids.
points.bullets:
A consumer audio equipment maker that designs and sells budget-friendly headphones, true wireless earbuds, open-ear sport headsets and over-the-counter hearing aids directly to consumers.
1. A consumer electronics equipment maker that builds finished wireless audio products and hearing aids sold as packaged retail hardware.
2. Bluetooth and LE Audio wireless audio reproduction systems integrated with active noise cancellation and digital signal processing for sound customization.
3. Active noise cancellation, spatial audio, customizable equalization, wireless audio playback, low-latency audio via LE Audio, and hearing amplification.
4. Finished consumer hardware products.
5. True wireless earbuds, over-ear headphones, open-ear sports headsets, and in-the-ear hearing aids.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold through consumer retail channels.
8. It competes at the lowest price tiers by offering active noise cancellation, LE Audio support and hearing aids at a fraction of the cost of premium brands.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its products are sold by the consumer electronics retailer Best Buy and incorporate wireless chips from the semiconductor supplier Realtek.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2005 with an estimated annual revenue of $10.8 million and approximately 30 employees.
Geography: Based in Carlsbad, California, USA, operating in the consumer market.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio company focused entirely on consumer audio products and hearing aids.

points.name: Noise
points.description: Indian consumer electronics brand making wireless earbuds featuring Bose audio technology.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics brand that designs and sells true wireless earbuds, collaborating with audio technology companies to tune and enhance its products for consumers.
1. A consumer electronics brand that makes finished true wireless earbuds sold as consumer hardware.
2. Tuning and spatial audio technologies developed in collaboration with an audio brand are integrated into the earbuds.
3. The earbuds deliver spatial audio, improved audio depth, high-frequency clarity, and adaptive sound features.
4. The technology is delivered in finished true wireless earbud hardware.
5. The products are used in true wireless earbuds.
6. The company sells to consumers.
7. Its finished earbuds are sold directly to consumers through retail channels.
8. The company combines budget and fashion-forward wearables with premium audio tuning developed in collaboration with an established audio brand.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company develops products in collaboration with Bose and uses technology from Syntiant.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held consumer electronics brand.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of true wireless earbuds.
Scale and maturity: The organization is a market-dominant wearables brand in India that was active in 2025 and introduced products for CES 2026.
Geography: The company is based in India and targets both the Indian market and a global presence for its premium products.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on audio and wearable consumer electronics.

points.name: Townsend Labs
points.description: US microphone modeling pioneer creating microphones that emulate classic studio mics in software.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that developed a microphone modeling system for studios and musicians, consisting of a physical microphone that emulates classic studio microphones, now owned and sold by a parent company.
1. An equipment maker that builds a physical modeling microphone sold as finished hardware that runs in recording studios.
2. Microphone modeling technology that uses a dual-capsule physical microphone with DSP processing to emulate the frequency, polar and transient responses of classic studio microphones.
3. Emulation of classic studio microphone characteristics including frequency response, polar patterns and transient response.
4. Finished hardware microphones and companion DSP software sold as an integrated system.
5. Recording studios and project studios.
6. Studios and musicians.
7. Its microphone modeling system is sold to end users through its parent company's product lineup.
8. It originated the microphone modeling approach using a dedicated dual-capsule microphone rather than processing an arbitrary input signal.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Universal Audio.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand acquired by and operating under a parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished microphone systems.
Scale and maturity: A former standalone company acquired in 2021 whose product continues to be sold by its parent company.
Geography: Based in the USA.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Lewitt
points.description: Viennese audio manufacturer building microphones for recording, live performance, and content creation.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio equipment that designs and produces condenser, dynamic, and tube microphones, alongside headphone software, for musicians, content creators, and live performers.
1. An equipment maker that builds microphones and audio software sold as finished hardware and software products.
2. Condenser, dynamic, and tube microphone capsules with analog circuitry, alongside digital systems with encrypted transmission and spatial headphone rendering algorithms.
3. Sound capture, polar pattern selection, FET and tube circuit blending, high-frequency shaping, automatic frequency management, and spatial audio replication.
4. Finished hardware products and software products.
5. Home studios, professional recording studios, live stages, and content creation setups.
6. Musicians, recording studios, content creators, and live sound engineers.
7. Its finished microphones are sold directly to end users for use in recording and live performance environments.
8. It operates its own manufacturing facilities with anechoic chambers and studios for in-house testing and development.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborated with Elgato on the development of a USB microphone.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware and software sales.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with multiple product lines and dedicated testing facilities.
Geography: Based in Vienna, Austria, with a presence in the European market.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Sterling Audio
points.description: Studio microphone manufacturer making affordable condenser and ribbon mics for recording.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures studio microphones and accessories, building ribbon, tube condenser, and large-diaphragm condenser models along with shock mounts, and selling them to recording studios and musicians.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished microphone hardware and accessories sold as packaged physical products used in studios.
2. Analog transducer designs built around ribbon, tube, and FET condenser capsules with hand-assembled components and custom-wound transformers.
3. Sound capture across various polar patterns including cardioid, omni, figure-8, and hypercardioid, with high SPL handling and switchable highpass filters and attenuation pads.
4. The company provides its products as finished hardware that includes the microphone, shock mount, and carry case.
5. Studio recording environments, vocal and instrument capture, and home studios.
6. Recording studios, musicians, and audio engineers.
7. Its finished microphones are sold directly to recording professionals and home studio users for capture in the audio signal chain.
8. The company focuses on high-value microphones offering hand-assembled capsules and custom transformers at affordable price points.
points.profile: Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play audio equipment manufacturer.

points.name: Royer Labs
points.description: Burbank, California microphone manufacturer building ribbon microphones for recording studios and live sound.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional ribbon microphones for recording studios, broadcast facilities, live sound environments, and film and television production.
1. An equipment maker that builds professional ribbon microphones sold as finished hardware for use with analog and phantom-powered audio interfaces.
2. Ribbon microphone transducers using neodymium magnets, offset ribbon motors, and active phantom-powered or tube electronics.
3. High SPL handling, smooth high-frequency response, warm and realistic tone reproduction, and stereo or mono sound capture.
4. Finished microphone hardware.
5. Recording studios, broadcast facilities, live sound stages, and film and television production.
6. Studios and musicians, broadcast facilities, and live sound engineers.
7. Its finished microphones are used directly by engineers and producers in recording, broadcast, and live sound settings.
8. It hand-builds rugged ribbon microphones and produces phantom-powered active ribbon designs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Sounds Great Holdings.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer that has won a Technical Grammy Award.
Geography: Based in Burbank, California, USA, expanding globally.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on ribbon microphones and related audio technologies.

points.name: Mojave Audio
points.description: US microphone manufacturer building handcrafted tube condenser microphones for professional studio recording.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures large-diaphragm tube condenser microphones for recording professionals and project studio enthusiasts.
1. An equipment maker that builds studio condenser microphones and sells them as finished hardware.
2. Vacuum-tube-based analog transducer circuits using hand-selected capsules and custom audio transformers.
3. Acoustic capture with vintage-style warmth and depth, fixed-cardioid pickup patterns, and continuously variable polar patterns from omnidirectional to figure-eight.
4. Finished hardware microphones.
5. Studios and project recording environments.
6. Recording professionals, project studio enthusiasts, and home recordists.
7. Its finished microphones are purchased directly by recording engineers and studio owners.
8. It delivers vintage-style sound character and handcrafted build quality at a fraction of the cost of classic vintage microphones.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Endorsed by recording professionals such as Capitol Studios' Steve Genewick and praised by Mix Magazine.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A premium microphone manufacturer competing in the sub-thousand-dollar price segment.
Geography: A company operating in the professional audio equipment sector.

points.name: Peluso Microphone Lab
points.description: Boutique microphone manufacturer hand-crafting replicas of vintage designs and supplying aftermarket parts for audio recording.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional microphones and aftermarket components that engineers original condenser and ribbon designs to replicate the acoustic character of vintage recording microphones, selling finished hand-built hardware and replacement capsules to recording studios and audio enthusiasts.
1. An equipment maker that builds microphones and aftermarket capsules sold as finished hardware and physical components.
2. Hand-crafted true condenser, ribbon, vacuum tube, solid-state and transformer-based analog audio transducer designs.
3. Acoustic sound capture, vintage microphone sound replication, and aftermarket capsule replacement for large-diaphragm condenser microphones.
4. Finished microphone hardware, aftermarket condenser capsules, output transformers, and vintage microphone restoration services.
5. Recording studios and audio production environments.
6. Recording studios, musicians, audio enthusiasts, DIY microphone builders, and professional audio dealers.
7. Its finished microphones and components are sold through professional audio dealers to recording engineers and studio owners.
8. It engineers original components to replicate the acoustic resonance of specific vintage microphone designs without directly copying the original manufacturing, avoiding direct competition with legacy brands.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Products are sold through dealers including Thomann, RSPE Audio Solutions, Tidepool Audio, and Rock N Roll Rentals.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished microphones, aftermarket components, and vintage restoration services.
Scale and maturity: An established organization with 25 years of microphone design experience and 50 years of vintage microphone restoration experience.
Geography: Based in the United States with products distributed through a global dealer network.
Beyond audio: Audio hardware manufacturing and restoration is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: Neumann
points.description: German studio microphone manufacturer renowned for its condenser microphones and making studio monitors with room correction.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures studio microphones, studio monitors, headphones, audio interfaces, and preamps for recording, broadcast, and live sound applications.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished microphones, monitors, headphones, and audio interfaces as hardware products.
2. The core technologies include large-diaphragm condenser capsules, vacuum tube and solid-state microphone amplifier circuits, DSP-based acoustic modeling and room correction algorithms in active nearfield monitors, and binaural dummy head recording.
3. The specific audio capabilities include sound capture for vocals and instruments, nearfield and midfield sound reproduction for monitoring, acoustic room correction, binaural 3D audio recording, and headphone amplification.
4. Customers get finished hardware microphones, studio monitors, headphones, audio interfaces, and preamps, alongside companion software and calibration tools.
5. The equipment is used in recording studios, broadcast facilities, post-production houses, live sound stages, and project studios.
6. The company sells to professional recording engineers, broadcasters, musicians, recording studios, and enterprises.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users through retail channels and dealers.
8. The approach is distinguished by a nearly century-long heritage of pioneering condenser microphone design and a sustained focus on premium build quality, resulting in several industry-standard studio microphones.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a subsidiary brand of Sennheiser and collaborated with Merging Technologies on a jointly developed audio interface.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand of a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: The company makes money through sales of professional audio hardware and associated software accessories.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1928, it operates a long-established global brand with historical facilities in Berlin and Wedemark.
Geography: It is based in Berlin and Wedemark, Germany, and operates in global professional audio markets.
Beyond audio: The company is focused entirely on professional audio equipment.

points.name: CORSAIR
points.description: US public company manufacturing high-performance gaming headsets and audio gear for PC gamers and content creators.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and creator hardware that builds gaming headsets and related gear for gamers, content creators, and PC enthusiasts.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished gaming headsets sold as consumer hardware.
2. The headsets deliver balanced sound tuning and user-adjustable, cloud-synced equalizer profiles that stay consistent across devices.
3. Customers receive it as finished hardware products.
4. The devices are used in PC gaming and content creation setups.
5. The company sells to consumers.
6. Its finished hardware is sold direct to consumers through retail channels.
points.profile:
Organization type: It is a publicly traded company that owns subsidiary brands.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: It is an established, large-scale public company.
Geography: It is based in the United States and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The company develops and manufactures a broad range of high-performance computer peripherals, streaming gear, and PC components beyond audio.

points.name: Behringer
points.description: German pro audio manufacturer building budget-friendly digital mixing consoles and microphones for live sound.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures a broad catalog of hardware, including digital mixing consoles, audio interfaces, synthesizers, microphones, amplifiers, and effects pedals. The organization targets budget-conscious consumers, home studio owners, and entry-level live sound operators by providing affordable alternatives to premium gear.
1. An equipment maker that designs and builds finished audio hardware products, sold as physical units to end users.
2. Analog and digital signal processing circuits implemented in dedicated hardware, utilizing floating-point DSP for mixing consoles and analog circuitry for recreating classic synthesizer and effects topologies.
3. Audio mixing, signal routing, multitrack recording, microphone preamplification, equalization, dynamic processing, audio networking, and sound synthesis.
4. Finished hardware products, including rack-mounted and console mixers, USB audio interfaces, synthesizers, stompboxes, and microphones, along with companion software control applications and a planned free digital audio workstation.
5. Home studios, live sound venues, small production companies, conference rooms, DJ setups, and musical instrument recording.
6. Consumers, home studio owners, entry-level live sound engineers, and retail distributors.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to consumers and entry-level live sound operators through retail channels.
8. The organization distinguishes itself by mass-producing near-exact, low-cost reproductions of vintage synthesizers and classic audio gear, aggressively undercutting premium market segments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company operates under the Music Tribe parent company alongside the Midas, Klark Teknik, and Turbosound brands, uses Midas preamps in its interfaces and mixers, and integrates networking cards from Waves.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a privately held conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio equipment, synthesizers, and electronic musical instruments.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1989, the company is a high-volume manufacturer ranked as the 14th largest musical instrument maker in the world.
Geography: Founded in Germany and currently manufacturing at its own facility in China, the company distributes its products globally.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the organization produces lighting equipment and MIDI keyboard controllers.

points.name: EASTECH
points.description: Speaker driver manufacturer producing specialized transducers designed to achieve perfect time coherence and superior sound quality.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of loudspeaker transducers that produces a family of point-source speaker drivers designed by a licensor partner, for speaker brands and audio equipment makers.
1. A speaker driver manufacturer that builds loudspeaker transducers, sold as finished hardware components for integration into speaker systems.
2. Pulp cones reinforced with carbon fiber material and point-source transducer designs engineered for time coherence.
3. Sound reproduction with increased stiffness, lower distortion and time coherence.
4. Finished speaker driver components.
5. Speakers and audio systems.
6. Speaker brands and audio equipment makers.
7. Its manufactured transducers are built into speaker systems by audio brands.
8. Its point-source transducers are engineered to achieve time coherence while using pulp cones with patented carbon fiber material for stiffness and low distortion.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The transducer designs are licensed from the speaker driver design company ScanSpeak.
Organization type: Privately held manufacturer.
Business model: Component hardware sales.
Geography: Operates as a manufacturer producing transducer hardware.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on the manufacture of acoustic transducers.

points.name: USound
points.description: Austrian audio component company developing ultra-compact MEMS microspeakers for hearables and wireless earbuds.
points.bullets:
A component manufacturer that develops and makes MEMS piezoelectric microspeakers, audio amplifier ICs, and integrated audio modules for hearables and wearable devices.
1. An audio component manufacturer that produces MEMS microspeakers and audio amplifier ICs, sold as packaged hardware components for integration into consumer electronics devices.
2. Silicon-based micro-electromechanical systems using piezoelectric actuators and integrated ASIC power amplifiers to convert electrical signals into acoustic energy.
3. High-bandwidth sound reproduction up to ultrasonic frequencies, high sound pressure levels, low distortion, ultrasonic gesture sensing, spatial audio, and low power consumption.
4. Physical hardware components, packaged MEMS speakers, amplifier ICs, integrated audio modules, and reference designs for over-the-counter hearing aids.
5. True wireless earbuds, hearables, hearing aids, virtual reality devices, smart glasses, and wearable audio devices.
6. Consumer electronics brands, audio device manufacturers, original design manufacturers, and hearing aid makers.
7. Its microspeaker components are integrated by device manufacturers into consumer earbuds and hearable products.
8. Silicon-based piezoelectric MEMS drivers occupy 50% less space and consume 80% less energy than conventional voice coil microspeakers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Design and manufacturing partners include Luxshare-ICT, OBO Pro2, Soranik, Earweiss, QCY, Minami, ASE, Nordic Neuro Lab, Upstar, and Tiancheng, with distribution through Digi-Key and funding from EQventure.
Organization type: A privately held hardware technology company.
Business model: Sales of semiconductor and micro-electromechanical hardware components, audio amplifier ICs, and integrated audio modules.
Scale and maturity: A venture-backed company founded in 2014, having raised $83.8 million in Series B funding and holding over 300 patents.
Geography: Based in Austria and serving international consumer electronics and audio device markets.
Beyond audio: Its hardware components are designed solely for audio applications.

points.name: Luxshare-ICT
points.description: Chinese manufacturer assembling TWS earbuds and developing compact hybrid audio modules.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics manufacturer that builds parts, modules and systems for global brands, and assembles finished devices such as earbuds, smart speakers and wearables for device makers.
1. An electronics manufacturer that builds integrated audio modules and finished consumer devices, sold as assembled hardware and components to device brands.
2. Microelectromechanical speakers, microspeakers, amplifiers and MEMS microphones integrated into compact hybrid audio modules for true wireless earbuds.
3. Dual-driver audio output, amplification and microphone capture in miniaturized earbud modules.
4. Components, modules and finished assembled hardware built in manufacturing facilities for consumer electronics brands.
5. True wireless earbuds, headphones, smart speakers, wearables, virtual reality headsets and automotive electronics.
6. Consumer electronics brands, device makers and ODM partners that integrate modules or sell finished assembled devices.
7. Its modules and assembly services are integrated by consumer electronics brands into their earbuds and wearables.
8. It combines high-volume contract manufacturing scale with integrated module development built around strategic MEMS speaker supply partnerships.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Apple for AirPods assembly and USound for MEMS speaker supply in hybrid audio modules.
Organization type: Privately held contract manufacturer and ODM.
Business model: Manufacturing services, component and module sales, and assembled hardware production for consumer electronics brands.
Scale and maturity: One of the largest consumer electronics manufacturers and assemblers, operating multiple facilities across Asia.
Geography: Based in China with manufacturing operations in China and Vietnam.
Beyond audio: It provides integrated intelligent solutions, parts, modules and systems across enterprise infrastructure, consumer electronics and automotive markets.

points.name: Creative
points.description: Singaporean technology company producing wireless earbuds and Bluetooth audio transmitters.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment and peripherals that develops, brands and sells finished hardware products incorporating its own proprietary spatial audio and sound personalization technologies, as well as third-party components, directly to consumers.
1. A consumer electronics company that builds finished audio hardware products sold as packaged devices running embedded firmware.
2. Spatial rendering algorithms that use ear and head photography to create custom head-related transfer function profiles, integrated alongside MEMS speaker drivers, Bluetooth transmitters and digital sound card processors in standalone devices.
3. Spatial audio, personalized sound profiles, simulated room reverberation, active noise cancellation and wireless audio transmission.
4. Finished hardware products including wireless earbuds, headsets, USB dongles, sound cards and portable media players, alongside companion mobile applications.
5. Earbuds, over-ear headsets, personal computers, home entertainment systems and portable media players.
6. Consumers and gaming enthusiasts.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users through retail channels, integrating components and licensed technologies from other suppliers.
8. It operates as both a hardware manufacturer and a technology developer, building proprietary spatial audio algorithms that use ear and face scans to personalize headphone sound.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: xMEMS and Mimi.
Organization type: A publicly traded consumer electronics company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished consumer audio devices and peripherals.
Scale and maturity: A long-established company founded in 1981 with a historical user base of 400 million.
Geography: Based in Singapore with worldwide operations and sales.
Beyond audio: It historically produced portable media players competing with mainstream mobile devices and acquired synthesizer and soundcard technology companies.

points.name: MISCO
points.description: US loudspeaker manufacturer building audio components for defense, medical, aerospace, and IoT devices.
points.bullets:
A loudspeaker manufacturer that designs and produces speakers and audio systems for original equipment manufacturers, with production facilities in North America and Asia.
1. An equipment maker that manufactures loudspeakers and microspeakers sold as finished components integrated into other manufacturers' products.
2. Electromagnetic and electro-acoustic transducers designed for high-performance sound reproduction in small and rugged form factors.
3. Sound reproduction across full-range and microspeaker formats optimized for harsh and constrained environments.
4. Finished speaker components and integrated audio systems shipped to manufacturers for assembly into end products.
5. Casino gaming, mass transit, medical devices, military communication systems, aerospace including spacecraft, wearable devices, IoT products, professional audio, and musical instruments.
6. Original equipment manufacturers in defense, medical, aerospace, commercial sound, musical instrument, and consumer electronics industries.
7. Its finished speaker components are designed into end products by original equipment manufacturers across industrial and consumer markets.
8. Over 75 years of speaker manufacturing with ISO 9001:2015 certified facilities and exclusive North American distribution of electro-acoustic test instruments that support its production workflow.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NASA, Klippel, Microflown, and CESVA.
Organization type: A privately held company operating for over 75 years.
Business model: Component and audio system hardware sales to original equipment manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: A long-established manufacturer with a 70,000 square-foot facility and global production.
Geography: Based in Minnesota, USA, with production in North America and Asia.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is audio manufacturing and component supply.

points.name: SEAS
points.description: Norwegian loudspeaker manufacturer making audio drivers and tweeters.
points.bullets:
A loudspeaker driver manufacturer that designs and produces audio components for consumer electronics brands and professional audio equipment makers.
1. An audio component maker that designs and manufactures loudspeaker drivers sold as finished components to equipment manufacturers.
2. The company designs acoustic transducers using materials such as carbon composites for tweeters and other driver architectures.
3. The company delivers acoustic transduction components including tweeters, woofers and full-range drivers.
4. Customers get its products as finished loudspeaker drivers built into the customers' speaker systems.
5. Its drivers are used in wireless speaker systems, passive loudspeakers and professional studio monitors.
6. The company sells to consumer electronics brands and professional audio equipment makers.
7. Its drivers are designed into finished speaker systems by consumer audio brands and professional equipment manufacturers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Named partners include a portable audio electronics brand and a professional audio equipment maker.
Organization type: The organization is a manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through component sales of loudspeaker drivers.
Scale and maturity: The company was founded in 1948 and has operated for decades as an established driver manufacturer.
Geography: It is based in Norway.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus is audio component manufacturing.

points.name: Vifa
points.description: Danish audio manufacturer producing loudspeaker drivers and portable speakers.
points.bullets:
A loudspeaker driver manufacturer and audio IP licensor that produces driver units, licenses automotive audio algorithms and platforms, and sells finished premium wireless speakers to consumer electronics brands, automakers and consumers.
1. An audio component and IP provider that first builds loudspeaker drivers and automotive audio algorithms and platforms, selling them as licensed IP, software tools and finished consumer hardware running on DSP chips, SoCs, Android and Linux systems.
2. Patented acoustic technologies including dynamic equalization, 3D sound processing, wide-band phase alignment, customized sound tuning, force-balanced woofers and DSP signal processing implemented on DSP chips, SoCs, Android and Linux systems.
3. Multi-band equalization, customized filtering, signal chain editing, cabinet acoustic measurement, dynamic equalization, 3D sound, wide-band phase alignment, customized sound tuning and room calibration.
4. Licensed IP and algorithms, reference software platforms, measurement toolsets, loudspeaker driver units and finished portable wireless speakers.
5. Portable speakers, home theater systems, smart wearables, displays, tablet computers, projectors and automotive hi-fi systems.
6. Consumer electronics brands, automakers and consumers.
7. Its driver units and licensed algorithms are integrated into automotive audio systems by vehicle manufacturers, and its finished speakers are sold directly to consumers.
8. It combines proprietary acoustic algorithms and IP with a focus on high-fidelity sound and Danish craftsmanship, bridging technical audio engineering and premium lifestyle design.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Kvadrat.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: IP and per-unit royalties, bespoke automotive audio system design fees and direct hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1933 with 90 years of operation.
Geography: Based in Denmark and operating primarily in the loudspeaker and home and car audio segments.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is audio.

points.name: Dynaudio
points.description: Danish loudspeaker manufacturer building studio monitors, hi-fi speakers, and high-end drivers.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and finished loudspeakers that designs and manufactures high-end speaker drivers, studio monitors and hi-fi speakers for recording studios, automakers and consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds loudspeaker drivers and passive finished loudspeakers sold as physical hardware in studio, automotive and home settings.
2. Passive loudspeaker drivers built with cast aluminum baskets, custom voice coils, magnets and DDC crossover systems for controlled directivity and beam control.
3. High-output sound reproduction, controlled directivity and technical neutrality for accurate mastering and hi-fi listening.
4. Finished hardware sold as individual speaker drivers and complete passive loudspeaker systems.
5. Recording and mastering studios, high-end home hi-fi systems and automobile audio systems.
6. Studios and mastering engineers, audiophiles, consumers and automakers.
7. Its finished loudspeakers and drivers are sold directly to end users and integrated into automobile audio systems by car makers.
8. A focus on passive speaker designs using DDC crossover technology to achieve controlled directivity and technical neutrality.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its drivers have been developed in collaboration with chief engineers including Peter Larsen.
Organization type: A privately held loudspeaker manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished loudspeakers and speaker drivers.
Scale and maturity: A long-established major player in the automotive premium audio and studio monitor markets.
Geography: Based in Denmark with a global market presence.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Audio Engineering Society
points.description: New York-based professional society developing audio engineering standards and publishing technical research.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops and publishes technical standards and recommended practices for professional audio, covering digital interfaces, networked audio, loudness, loudspeaker measurement and spatial audio metadata formats. It also operates as a professional society organizing conventions and publishing research, serving audio engineers, scientists and related professionals.
1. A standards body that develops open technical standards and recommended practices published as documents and accessed via online subscription services.
2. Standardized protocols for professional digital audio interconnect, audio-over-IP interoperability, embedded audio metadata, spatial acoustic data storage formats and loudspeaker linearity measurement.
3. Interoperability for digital audio transmission, audio-over-IP networking, loudness normalization, dialogue intelligibility management and linear sound level measurement.
4. Published technical documents, open standards, peer-reviewed journals, professional certification credentials, educational web portals and industry conferences.
5. Professional broadcast equipment, networked audio systems, online streaming platforms, virtual and augmented reality systems, studio monitoring and automotive audio systems.
6. Audio engineers, scientists, professional audio industry members, broadcast organizations, equipment manufacturers and software developers.
7. Its standards are adopted and implemented by professional equipment manufacturers, broadcast organizations and software developers into their products and workflows.
8. It operates as a non-profit standards body and professional society devoted exclusively to audio technology, uniting standardization with industry conventions and peer-reviewed publishing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The European Broadcasting Union for joint standard development, with Telos Alliance, Yamaha, Samsung, Genelec and Knowles as standards contributors, convention participants or implementers.
Organization type: A 501(c)(3) non-profit corporation and professional society operating as an international standards body.
Business model: Membership dues, convention and conference revenues, publication subscriptions, standard document sales and professional certification fees.
Scale and maturity: A global organization with over 12,500 members and a history spanning more than 75 years.
Geography: Headquartered in New York, USA, operating internationally with a secretariat on US West Coast time.
Beyond audio: The organization is devoted exclusively to audio technology and its engineering standards.

points.name: Tymphany
points.description: Taiwanese audio design and manufacturing company building speaker components and integrated audio systems for consumer, professional, and automotive applications.
points.bullets:
An original design manufacturer that designs and builds loudspeakers, acoustic components, and complete audio systems, integrating transducers, amplifiers, DSP software, and mechanical solutions for consumer electronics, automotive, and professional audio brands.
1. An equipment maker and component manufacturer that designs loudspeaker transducers and finished audio systems sold as manufactured hardware to device makers.
2. Electromagnetic motors driving coaxially arranged diaphragms, ring radiator designs, AMT woofer systems, and acoustic system engineering integrated with DSP platforms.
3. Acoustic transduction, compact loudspeaker system design, acoustic system integration, and tuning tools for deploying spatial audio processing features.
