4. Finished hardware products, speaker components, licensed acoustic designs, and Windows Audio Processing Object software solutions for device manufacturers.
5. In-vehicle automotive sound systems, headrest speakers, firewall-mounted woofers, WiFi and Bluetooth speakers, soundbars, conference systems, and concept audio platforms.
6. Automakers, consumer electronics brands, professional audio brands, and device manufacturers.
7. Its transducers and acoustic systems are designed into vehicles and consumer audio products by automotive and electronics brands.
8. A 5-in-1 holistic approach integrates transducer design, amplifiers, DSP software, acoustic system design, and mechanical solutions under one manufacturing roof.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Fraunhofer IIS, DSP Concepts, Volvo, Karma, Denon, and Primax.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand operating as an original design manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales, component manufacturing, and contracted design and production services.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with over 90 years of audio design expertise and over 8,000 employees globally.
Geography: Headquartered in Nangang District, Taiwan, operating globally.
Beyond audio: Audio is the company's entire focus.

points.name: B&O
points.description: Danish consumer audio manufacturer designing high-end loudspeakers and truly wireless earbuds.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics company that manufactures high-end audio products, including truly wireless earbuds and loudspeakers, for consumers.
1. A maker of finished audio hardware that sells loudspeakers and earbuds as completed physical products.
2. Acoustic loudspeaker designs, including long-running models developed with external simulation support.
3. High-end sound reproduction for home listening and personal audio.
4. The company provides finished hardware products sold directly to end users.
5. Its products are used in home audio settings and personal listening environments.
6. The company sells to consumers seeking premium audio equipment.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly to consumers through its own retail channels and brand presence.
8. It distinguishes itself through long-lived, premium loudspeaker designs developed with specialized external acoustic simulation support.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It engaged acoustic simulation consultant Peter Larsen for speaker design support.
Organization type: It is a consumer electronics brand operating as a subsidiary.
Business model: It makes money through the sale of finished audio hardware.
Geography: The organization is based in Denmark.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on consumer audio and related electronics.

points.name: OBO Pro2
points.location: Taiwan; manufacturing operations in Dongguan, China
points.description: Taiwanese audio manufacturer designing OTC hearing aids and building audio modules using silicone rubber and MEMS technology.
points.bullets:
An audio manufacturer that provides OEM and ODM services for hearing aids, specializing in silicone rubber technology for electrodynamic drivers and integrating components into finished devices for hearing aid brands.
1. A manufacturer of finished audio hardware that designs and assembles OTC hearing aids and electrodynamic drivers for sale as complete devices to brand owners.
2. The company delivers electrodynamic driver design and full hearing aid component integration into user-friendly finished devices.
3. Customers get finished hearing aid hardware manufactured under OEM or ODM arrangements.
4. The devices are used in OTC hearing aids.
5. The company sells to hearing aid brands and audio module developers.
6. Its finished devices and manufactured components are branded and sold by consumer health and audio companies.
7. Its approach combines silicone rubber electrodynamic driver expertise with full-device OTC hearing aid integration under one manufacturing roof.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company has a strategic cooperation with a MEMS technology developer and participates in an OTC hearing aid reference design collaboration.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through OEM and ODM contract manufacturing of finished hearing aid devices and components.
Geography: The company is headquartered in Taiwan with manufacturing operations in Dongguan, China.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Singularity Audio
points.description: Audio company designing in-ear monitors using MEMS speaker technology.
points.bullets:
A maker of finished audio equipment that designs in-ear monitors incorporating micro-electromechanical speaker drivers, sold to consumers and audiophiles.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished in-ear monitors sold as physical hardware.
2. Micro-electromechanical system drivers enclosed in a titanium shell.
3. Personal audio monitoring and playback.
4. Finished hardware products.
5. In-ear monitors used for personal listening and professional monitoring.
6. Consumers and audiophiles.
7. Its finished earphones are designed around micro-electromechanical speaker drivers supplied by a component manufacturer.
8. It builds in-ear monitors using twin micro-electromechanical drivers in a titanium shell.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company is a launch partner for xMEMS.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio equipment.

points.name: iFi
points.description: UK audio equipment manufacturer building portable and desktop DACs and headphone amplifiers.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures portable and desktop digital-to-analog converters, headphone amplifiers, and streaming components for personal audio and hi-fi systems.
1. An equipment maker that designs finished audio hardware products, combining proprietary firmware on purchased silicon, which run as standalone devices.
2. Digital-to-analog conversion, headphone amplification, Bluetooth streaming, and power conditioning circuits built on Burr-Brown DAC chips and XMOS input processors programmed with bespoke firmware.
3. High-resolution digital-to-analog conversion, headphone amplification, balanced and single-ended audio output, high-resolution Bluetooth streaming, and phono signal amplification.
4. The company provides finished hardware products, including portable dongle and battery-powered DACs, desktop DACs, headphone amplifiers, and preamps.
5. Personal audio systems, desktop hi-fi setups, two-channel stereo systems, and portable headphone listening.
6. Consumers and audiophiles.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold to consumers through audio retailers.
8. The company writes its own bespoke firmware for input processing chips rather than using off-the-shelf firmware, and incorporates internal batteries into portable dongle DACs to avoid draining host device power.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is an official DAC and headphone amp technology partner for xMEMS, uses chips from Burr-Brown, XMOS, and Texas Instruments, and is a brand of Abbingdon Music Research.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of Abbingdon Music Research.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A manufacturer with a broad, established portfolio of numerous desktop and portable product lines.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom and operating in the consumer audio market.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on audio equipment.

points.name: Soranik
points.description: Vietnamese in-ear monitor manufacturer building audio products for performers using MEMS drivers.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures in-ear monitors for audio enthusiasts and performers. The organization builds finished earphones that incorporate micro-electromechanical systems drivers sourced from component suppliers. It creates products that combine different driver technologies in hybrid designs.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished in-ear monitor hardware sold to end users.
2. Hybrid micro-electromechanical systems driver configurations combining separate monolithic and tweeter elements within 3D-printed acoustic shells.
3. Personal audio monitoring with combined high-frequency and monolithic driver reproduction.
4. The company delivers finished hardware products retailing directly to consumers.
5. The products are used in in-ear monitors for audio enthusiasts and live performers.
6. The organization sells to consumers, audio enthusiasts and performers.
7. Its finished earphones are built using micro-electromechanical driver components sourced from upstream component suppliers.
8. The approach distinguishes itself by combining two different types of micro-electromechanical systems drivers from separate suppliers within a single hybrid in-ear monitor design.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company uses micro-electromechanical systems drivers from USound and xMEMS and operates as an original design manufacturer collaborating with USound.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of finished earphones.
Scale and maturity: The company was established in 2012 and operates as a manufacturer of premium in-ear monitors retailing at over one thousand US dollars.
Geography: It is based in Vietnam.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Arioso Systems
points.description: German startup building miniaturized MEMS microspeakers for audio devices.
points.bullets:
A fabless microspeaker component developer that designed miniaturized MEMS microspeakers based on a nanoscopic electrostatic drive principle for consumer electronics manufacturers.
1. A component developer that builds MEMS microspeaker structures and licenses the transducer technology to semiconductor and consumer electronics manufacturers.
2. The core technology is a nanoscopic electrostatic drive actuation principle that moves a microspeaker membrane to generate high sound pressure levels from a miniaturized active area.
3. It delivers high sound pressure level audio reproduction from a sub-square-centimeter active area.
4. It provides its technology as licensed intellectual property and microspeaker components.
5. The microspeakers are used in miniaturized audio devices such as earbuds and in-ear hearing aids.
6. It sells to consumer electronics component manufacturers and semiconductor companies.
7. Its transducer intellectual property and components are integrated into audio products by consumer electronics brands.
8. Its nanoscopic electrostatic drive principle enables generating extremely high sound pressure levels from significantly smaller active areas than conventional microspeaker designs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It was a spin-off of Fraunhofer IPMS and was acquired by Bosch Sensortec.
Organization type: It is a corporate subsidiary of a semiconductor and electronics component manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through component licensing and acquisition.
Scale and maturity: It was an early-stage startup that was acquired in 2022.
Geography: It is based in Dresden, Germany.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on audio transducer technology.

points.name: Earfab
points.description: Danish audio technology company making custom-fit eartips using 3D smartphone scanning and distributed manufacturing.
points.bullets:
A maker of custom-fit in-ear audio products and ear-scanning technology that designs passive eartips and operates a distributed manufacturing network to produce them locally for consumers and device makers.
1. A product and technology developer that builds a 3D smartphone ear-scanning platform and custom-fit passive eartips, sold as finished physical products and manufactured through a distributed network.
2. The company delivers 3D ear scanning for custom-fit ear impressions and the production of personalized passive eartips.
3. Customers receive finished custom-fit eartips manufactured locally and access to a proprietary smartphone-based 3D scanning platform.
4. The products are used in true wireless earbuds and custom in-ear monitors.
5. The company sells to consumers and audio device manufacturers.
6. Its scanning platform and manufacturing network are integrated by earbud manufacturers into personalized audio products.
7. Its approach combines a proprietary smartphone 3D scanning platform with fully automated injection molding and distributed manufacturing for local production.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company collaborates with SonicEdge to develop custom-fit true wireless earbuds integrating MEMS microspeakers.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: It makes money through the sale of finished custom-fit physical products and manufacturing services.
Scale and maturity: The company was founded in 2020 and is an early-stage enterprise.
Geography: It is based in Denmark and operates a global distributed manufacturing network.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus is on custom-fit audio products and ear-scanning technology.

points.name: SonicEdge
points.description: Israeli semiconductor company developing ultrasonic MEMS microspeakers for earbuds, headphones, and hearing aids.
points.bullets:
An IP and hardware component developer that designs silicon MEMS microspeakers using modulated ultrasound technology to deliver high-performance audio in miniature form factors for hearables.
1. A component and IP developer that builds MEMS microspeaker modules and packaged evaluation devices, sold as miniature speaker hardware and licensed intellectual property integrated into audio chipsets.
2. MEMS-based ultrasonic air pumps operate at 400 kHz and use a patented acoustic-mechanical frequency transformer to modulate ultrasound down into audible sound.
3. High-performance audio generation in miniature footprints, integrated speaker-microphone combinations, and low-frequency reproduction from micro-sized drivers.
4. Packaged MEMS hardware modules, evaluation devices containing MEMS and amplifier chips, and licensed intellectual property embedded into audio chipsets.
5. True wireless stereo earbuds, headphones, hearing aids, and custom-fit personalized audio devices.
6. Consumer electronics brands, hearable and earbud device makers, and semiconductor companies.
7. Its MEMS microspeaker modules and modulated ultrasound IP are integrated into earbuds and audio chipsets by consumer electronics brands and semiconductor partners.
8. It replaces conventional moving-coil drivers with thousands of microscopic MEMS ultrasonic air pumps that modulate ultrasound into audible sound within a sub-millimeter thickness.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with Earfab on custom-fit true wireless earbuds and has a strategic partnership with a major global semiconductor maker to embed its IP into audio chipsets.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: It generates revenue through hardware module sales, evaluation kits, and intellectual property licensing or integration agreements.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2019, it holds proprietary patents and is actively seeking investment for expansion.
Geography: Based in Israel and Denmark.
Beyond audio: Audio generation technology is its entire focus.

points.name: Earweiss
points.description: Shenzhen manufacturer building advanced earbuds and hearables that integrate MEMS speaker technology.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of earbuds and hearables that builds finished personal audio hardware for consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds earbuds and hearables sold as finished hardware products.
2. The core technology consists of personalization and advanced hearable systems integrating MEMS speaker technology.
3. The organization delivers personalization and advanced hearable capabilities in personal audio devices.
4. Customers receive finished hardware products.
5. The products are used in earbuds and hearables.
6. The company sells to consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users.
8. Its approach is distinguished by integrating MEMS speaker technology into hearable products.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization has a strategic partnership with USound to explore MEMS speaker integration.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: The company is an established manufacturer with R&D operations.
Geography: It is based in Shenzhen, China with R&D in Nanjing, China.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the company.

points.name: QCY
points.description: Chinese wireless audio manufacturer producing affordable Bluetooth earbuds and true wireless earbuds.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs, manufactures and sells wireless earbuds and headphones, integrating drivers and acoustic systems for consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished wireless earbuds and headphones sold as packaged consumer electronics.
2. Dynamic and MEMS drivers configured in dual-driver acoustic systems, combined with adaptive hybrid active noise cancellation.
3. Active noise cancellation, high-resolution audio playback and dual-driver sound reproduction with bass and treble separation.
4. Finished consumer hardware products.
5. True wireless stereo earbuds and over-ear headphones.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished earbuds are sold to consumers through retail channels, incorporating MEMS speakers designed by its component suppliers.
8. It targets the low-to-mid-tier price segment with affordable wireless audio solutions built through efficient supply chains.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with USound and uses xMEMS drivers.
Organization type: A brand and subsidiary of a privately held electronics manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established brand with over 16 years of industry experience and millions of users worldwide.
Geography: Based in China and operating globally.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on wireless audio products.

points.name: Soundpeats
points.description: Chinese audio brand manufacturing budget-friendly wireless earbuds and headphones.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that builds budget-friendly wireless earbuds and headphones for consumers, integrating components from silicon suppliers into finished products.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished wireless audio hardware sold to consumers.
2. Wireless audio playback systems combining dynamic drivers, silicon-based micro tweeters, multi-driver acoustic architectures, and adaptive hybrid active noise cancellation.
3. Wireless audio playback, active noise cancellation, multi-driver sound reproduction, adaptive equalization, hearing test-based sound personalization, and dual-device connectivity.
4. Finished hardware devices paired with a companion mobile software application.
5. Wireless earbuds and over-ear headphones.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products incorporate components designed by semiconductor vendors and are sold directly to end users.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: xMEMS Labs.
Organization type: A privately held company operating as a consumer electronics brand.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio devices.
Geography: Based in China and operating in the consumer electronics market.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio products.

points.name: Dongguan Rayking Electronics
points.description: Dongguan manufacturer building microphones and turnkey speaker modules for wireless earbuds.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of electret condenser microphones, MEMS microphones and turnkey speaker modules, building intelligent acoustic components and automotive modules for consumer electronics and automotive device makers.
1. An equipment and component maker that builds microphones and integrated speaker modules sold as finished hardware components designed into customers' devices.
2. Electret condenser microphone and MEMS microphone technology combined with integrated speaker module design that packages drivers and all external components into a single covered unit.
3. Acoustic capture through electret and MEMS microphones and audio output through turnkey speaker modules for true wireless earbuds.
4. Finished acoustic hardware components and turnkey speaker modules.
5. True wireless earbuds and automotive electronics.
6. Consumer electronics device makers and automakers.
7. Its acoustic components and speaker modules are designed into true wireless earbuds and automotive modules by consumer electronics brands.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware component sales.
Scale and maturity: Established in 2011 and operating as a component manufacturer.
Geography: Based in Dongguan, China.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on acoustic components and modules.

points.name: Noble Audio
points.description: Premium in-ear monitor brand crafting audiophile earbuds featuring hybrid MEMS and dynamic drivers.
points.bullets:
A maker of premium portable audio equipment that designs and sells in-ear monitors and true wireless earbuds for audiophiles.
1. An equipment maker whose finished wireless earbuds and wired in-ear monitors run as consumer electronics devices.
2. Hybrid driver acoustics pairing solid-state MEMS tweeters with dynamic drivers, integrated with Bluetooth codecs and companion software.
3. High-fidelity audio reproduction, active noise cancellation, transparent hearing modes, multi-point Bluetooth connectivity, and voice assistant support.
4. Finished consumer hardware products.
5. True wireless earbuds and wired in-ear monitors.
6. Consumers and audiophiles.
7. Its finished earbuds are sold directly to end users.
8. It combines solid-state silicon tweeters with dynamic drivers in true wireless earbuds targeting the audiophile market.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: xMEMS and Qualcomm.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with an award-winning product portfolio and an entry-level tier.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on audio.

points.name: Lucid Hearing
points.description: US hearing aid company selling OTC and prescription hearing aids.
points.bullets:
A vertically integrated maker of hearing aids and hearing protection that designs, manufactures and fits devices for adults with mild to moderate hearing loss. The company sells its own branded products and operates hearing aid clinics inside big-box retail stores.
1. A hearing aid manufacturer that builds finished medical devices containing proprietary digital signal processing, sold as consumer-ready hardware.
2. Adaptive Dynamic Range Optimization signal processing and up to 128-channel sound analysis algorithms running on embedded digital signal processors within the hearing aids.
3. Adaptive noise reduction, dynamic feedback cancellation, directional microphone speech enhancement, Bluetooth audio streaming and user-tuned sound equalization.
4. Finished hardware devices, companion mobile applications for device tuning, and in-person hearing evaluation services.
5. Over-the-counter and prescription hearing aids, personal sound amplifiers and hearing protection products.
6. Consumers with mild to moderate hearing loss, retail pharmacy and electronics chains, and warehouse club members.
7. Its finished devices are sold directly to consumers through its own retail clinics and partner retail chains.
8. It combines manufacturing with an exclusive retail clinic footprint inside warehouse club stores to offer free hearing tests and custom in-store fitting.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Knowles, University of Texas-Dallas, Sam's Club, Walmart, Best Buy, CVS, Walgreens, Target.com and Amazon.
Organization type: A privately held company and subsidiary brand.
Business model: Finished hearing aid hardware sales and direct-to-consumer service fees.
Scale and maturity: A mid-sized company founded in 2009 that operates over 500 hearing centers and serves hundreds of thousands of consumers nationwide.
Geography: Headquartered in Texas and operates clinics and retail distribution across the United States, China and Latin America.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on hearing health technology and consumer audio products.

points.name: Westone Laboratories Inc
points.description: US audio manufacturer making custom in-ear monitors and hearing protection for musicians.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures custom and universal in-ear monitors, earphones, and hearing protection products for professional musicians and audio enthusiasts.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment that sells finished hardware in the form of custom and universal in-ear monitors.
2. The core technology comprises balanced-armature drivers and passive crossovers housed in ergonomic custom or universal shells, supplemented by ambient port designs for environmental awareness.
3. The products deliver high-quality sound reproduction, sound isolation, on-stage ambient awareness, and hearing protection.
4. Customers receive finished hardware, including in-ear monitors, earphones, and related accessories such as cables and connectors.
5. The products are used on live performance stages, in studios, and in hearing protection settings.
6. The company sells to professional musicians, touring professionals, and discerning audio enthusiasts.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly to consumers and professionals for use in live and studio applications.
8. The approach emphasizes ergonomic custom-fit shells and ambient awareness technology to reduce ear fatigue during extended use.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Lucid Audio (Lucid Hearing) acquired the music division, and the company historically collaborated with Jerry Harvey on early in-ear monitors.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand operating under a parent hearing health and consumer audio company.
Business model: The company generates revenue through the direct sale of premium audio hardware and related accessories.
Scale and maturity: Operating since 1959, the brand has a long-standing legacy in the professional audio industry and produces custom units domestically and universal units in Asia.
Geography: The company is based and manufactures custom products in the United States, with universal models produced in Asia.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus is on audio hardware, in-ear monitors, and hearing protection.

points.name: Etymotic Research
points.description: Illinois manufacturer developing high-fidelity hearing aids, earplugs, and hearing protection products.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional and consumer audio equipment that engineers, manufactures, and sells high-fidelity in-ear earphones, hearing protection earplugs, hearing aids, and audiometric testing devices based on auditory research.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished passive and electronic in-ear audio hardware sold as physical products.
2. Balanced-armature driver earphones, tuned acoustic resonators and resistors, and directional microphone hardware.
3. High-fidelity in-ear audio reproduction, high-isolation noise attenuation, sound level limiting, ambient sound enhancement, and audiometric hearing testing.
4. Finished hardware products including insert earphones, electronic and passive earplugs, headsets, and audiometric probes.
5. Earbuds, hearing aids, personal sound amplifiers, and audiometric testing environments.
6. Consumers, audiologists, hearing care professionals, and hearing aid retail brands.
7. Its finished hardware products are distributed through hearing care retail networks and consumer audio channels.
8. Pioneered balanced-armature in-ear monitor earphones and designs products around target frequency response accuracy scores derived from auditory research.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Owned by Lucid Hearing, with distribution through Oaktree Products and Hearing Lab Technologies.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a hearing care company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished earphones, earplugs, and hearing aids.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1983 and operating as an acquired brand since 2018.
Geography: Based in Elk Grove Village, Illinois.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Knowles Hearing Health Technologies
points.description: Audio component division building transducers and MEMS microphones for hearing aids and premium audio markets.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of foundational audio transducers that designs and produces balanced armatures and MEMS microphones for hearing aid manufacturers, consumer audio brands, and professional audio equipment makers.
1. A hardware component maker that designs and manufactures physical audio transducers sold as finished components integrated into customers' devices.
2. Balanced armatures and micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) microphones operating within the transducer layer of the audio stack.
3. Physical sound capture through MEMS microphones and sound reproduction through balanced armatures.
4. Finished hardware components supplied in high volume to device manufacturers.
5. Hearing aids, over-the-counter hearing aids, consumer audio devices, and professional audio equipment.
6. Hearing aid manufacturers, consumer audio brands, and professional audio equipment makers.
7. Its transducer components are designed into hearing aids and consumer audio devices by device manufacturers.
8. It is the world's largest producer of transducers for hearing aids, with its technologies incorporated into the top seven over-the-counter hearing aid products rated by a major aging council.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The top seven over-the-counter hearing aid products rated by a major aging council all incorporate its technologies.
Organization type: A specialized division of a publicly traded corporation.
Business model: High-volume hardware sales of audio components to device manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: A well-established and mature business with roots tracing back to the 1954 invention of the balanced armature for the hearing aid industry.
Geography: Strategically positioned to capitalize on the United States market, leveraging regulatory changes like the FDA's authorization of over-the-counter hearing aids.
Beyond audio: Audio technology and hearing health solutions are the sole focus of the organization's mission.

points.name: Alango Technologies
points.description: Israeli technology company developing digital signal processing software for wireless earbuds and audio devices.
points.bullets:
A DSP software and IP licensor that develops audio and voice signal-processing algorithms and modules, licensing them to device makers and chip companies for hearables, headphones, conferencing systems and automotive audio.
1. A DSP software developer whose algorithms and modular software packages run on third-party Bluetooth SoCs and DSP cores.
2. Digital signal processing algorithms, adaptive microphone array processing, sensor fusion combining acoustic microphones with MEMS vibration sensors, and AI-based noise and dereverberation processing.
3. Acoustic echo cancellation, noise suppression, multi-microphone beamforming, speech enhancement, acoustic feedback cancellation, automatic gain and EQ control, sound personalization, and through-barrier sound acquisition.
4. Licensed algorithms, pre-integrated software modules, and surface-mounted hardware reference modules.
5. Bluetooth earbuds, headsets, hearing enhancement devices, smart speakers, conferencing systems, speakerphones, automotive audio, and aviation communication systems.
6. Device manufacturers, consumer electronics brands, chip companies, and automotive and aviation suppliers.
7. Its algorithms are integrated by chip vendors and microphone component makers into their platforms and development kits, and by device makers into finished products.
8. It combines standard microphone-array beamforming with MEMS vibration-sensor fusion to acquire clear speech through solid barriers and in high-noise environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Qualcomm, Knowles, NXP, and MIPS.
Organization type: A privately held company spun off from a parent DSP firm to focus exclusively on front-end acoustic signal processing.
Business model: Software licensing, per-unit royalties, and sales of reference hardware modules.
Scale and maturity: A 23-year-old established provider of DSP software serving the mobile, hearables, automotive, and conferencing markets.
Geography: Based in Tirat Carmel, Israel, serving global device and chip customers.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on audio, voice, and hearing enhancement DSP technologies.

points.name: Asahi Kasei Microdevices Corporation
points.description: Japanese semiconductor manufacturer building audio converters and chips for consumer and professional audio equipment.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor manufacturer that designs, makes and sells high-performance audio integrated circuits, primarily analog-to-digital converters and digital-to-analog converters, for professional and consumer audio markets.
1. A chip company that designs and manufactures audio codecs, ADCs and DACs sold as discrete semiconductor components.
2. Delta-sigma modulators, analog front ends and digital filters built on a proprietary low-noise semiconductor process.
3. High-resolution analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog audio conversion, low-power audio processing and dynamic range maximization.
4. The company provides its technology through finished semiconductor components sold to equipment manufacturers.
5. High-end audio systems, professional audio equipment and consumer high-resolution audio devices.
6. Consumer electronics brands and professional audio equipment manufacturers.
7. Its semiconductor components are designed into audio products by equipment manufacturers.
8. A proprietary two-chip digital-to-analog separation solution pairs a delta-sigma modulator with a separate DAC to maximize sound quality and minimize digital noise.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held semiconductor company.
Business model: The organization generates revenue through the design, manufacture and sale of semiconductor components.
Beyond audio: The company focuses its business entirely on audio and related semiconductor components.

points.name: Soundec
points.description: Taiwanese technology company developing AI-based audio processors and noise canceling solutions for headphones and communication devices.
points.bullets:
A chip and solutions company that develops AI-based audio processors and bundled turnkey audio solutions for consumer electronics manufacturers.
1. A chip company that designs integrated audio processors and packages them with reference algorithms and turnkey solutions sold to device makers.
2. AI audio processing algorithms and audio codecs running on an integrated processor built around a Tensilica HiFi3 DSP core.
3. Single- and multi-microphone noise cancellation, far-field beamforming, echo cancellation, howling suppression, dynamic bass enhancement, multi-band equalization, dynamic range control, and sleep-friendly sound effects.
4. Chips, turnkey hardware solutions, firmware, and evaluation kits.
5. USB microphones, noise-canceling headphones, walkie-talkies, car audio, call center headsets, esports earphones, smart TVs, vehicle cockpits, enterprise conference systems, live streaming equipment, portable speakers, soundbars, PC speakers, and pillow speakers.
6. Consumer electronics brands and device manufacturers.
7. Its processors and turnkey solutions are designed into finished consumer audio devices by electronics brands.
8. It pairs integrated audio processors based on licensed DSP cores with a broad portfolio of application-specific turnkey audio solutions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Cadence Tensilica.
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: Chip sales and turnkey hardware solution sales.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on audio processing technology and hardware.

points.name: Cadence Design Systems
points.description: California software and IP developer supplying Tensilica audio DSP cores for chipsets.
points.bullets:
A publicly traded electronic design automation company that licenses DSP IP cores and neural network engines for audio, voice, and AI processing, and sells EDA software for semiconductor design.
1. A semiconductor IP licensor and EDA software provider whose DSP IP cores are integrated into customers' chips.
2. Configurable 32-bit VLIW digital signal processors and neural processing units running low-power audio, voice, and AI algorithms.
3. Audio and voice codecs, wake-word detection, beamforming, noise reduction, object-based audio decoding, and spatial audio rendering.
4. Licensed IP cores, DSP libraries, neural network libraries, EDA software tools, and SDKs.
5. Earbuds, smartwatches, automotive infotainment systems, smart speakers, smartphones, PCs, digital TVs, and set-top boxes.
6. Semiconductor companies, chip designers, consumer electronics brands, and automakers.
7. Its IP cores are designed into SoCs by semiconductor vendors and its EDA tools are used by engineers to design and verify semiconductors.
8. It offers a high-level programming paradigm and market-leading power, performance, and area efficiency for its DSP cores.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include Dolby, Google, Analog Devices, NXP, Qualcomm, Waves, Fraunhofer, Silentium, and DSP Concepts.
Organization type: A publicly traded technology company and subsidiary brand owner.
Business model: IP licensing with per-unit royalties and EDA software licenses and subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A large, established public company that acquired Tensilica in 2013 for approximately $326 million.
Geography: Based in San Jose, California, operating globally.
Beyond audio: The company provides software, hardware, IP, and services for designing and verifying advanced semiconductors, consumer electronics, networking, and telecommunications equipment across multiple industries.

points.name: Topping
points.description: Chinese audio equipment manufacturer building desktop DACs and headphone amplifiers.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and desktop audio equipment that designs and sells digital-to-analog converters, headphone amplifiers, and combined DAC-amplifier units for audiophiles.
1. A consumer audio equipment maker that builds finished DAC and headphone amplifier hardware products for desktop use.
2. Digital-to-analog conversion chips and analog amplifier circuits running in standalone desktop audio hardware.
3. High-resolution digital-to-analog audio conversion supporting formats up to DSD256 and PCM384, balanced audio output, parametric equalization, and headphone amplification.
4. Finished physical hardware units.
5. Desktop audio setups, personal listening stations, and headphone listening systems.
6. Audiophiles and consumers.
7. Its finished audio hardware is sold directly to consumers for use in personal desktop audio systems.
8. It targets the value-oriented high-performance segment by offering balanced audio architectures and high-resolution DAC capabilities at competitive prices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It incorporates DAC chips from AKM and ESS into its hardware products.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with a catalog of multiple desktop audio products.
Geography: Based in China.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Allen & Heath
points.description: British pro audio brand building mid-tier professional digital mixing consoles for live sound.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and sells mid-tier digital mixing consoles, audio expander hardware, personal mixers, and control software for venues, touring professionals, houses of worship, and the rental market.
1. An equipment maker that designs proprietary digital mixing consoles and audio networking hardware sold as finished physical products alongside companion control software applications.
2. Field-programmable gate arrays running proprietary 96kHz audio processing engines and software interfaces integrating physical rotary controls with touchscreens.
3. Live digital audio mixing, multichannel signal routing, digital effects processing, compression, equalization, and remote system control.
4. Finished hardware consoles, physical audio expander units, and downloadable software applications for offline editing and mobile control.
5. Front-of-house live sound, stage monitoring, breakout rooms, and installed venue audio systems.
6. Venues, touring professionals, houses of worship, and audio rental companies.
7. Its finished mixing consoles and control software are deployed directly by live sound engineers and venue technicians.
8. A 96kHz FPGA-based processing engine with 0.7ms latency provides a next-generation alternative to older 48kHz DSP-based consoles in the mid-tier market.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary brand of the Audiotonix Group.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand.
Business model: Hardware sales of mixing consoles and expanders, supplemented by optional software upgrade licenses.
Scale and maturity: A mature, established organization with significant market share in the mid-tier professional digital mixing market.
Geography: Based in and operates within the professional live sound and installed audio markets.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on professional audio equipment and software.

points.name: Questyle
points.description: Chinese manufacturer making high-end portable and desktop DACs, headphone amplifiers, and digital audio players.
points.bullets:
A maker of high-end consumer and professional audio equipment that designs and sells portable and desktop DACs, headphone amplifiers, digital audio players, and Bluetooth transmitter dongles for audiophile listeners.
1. A finished audio equipment maker that builds digital-to-analog converters, headphone amplifiers, digital audio players, and wireless transmitter dongles, sold as standalone consumer hardware.
2. Digital-to-analog conversion chips paired with discrete Current Mode amplification circuitry and USB, Bluetooth, and proprietary digital audio decoding architectures.
3. High-resolution audio decoding of PCM, DSD, and MQA formats, high-fidelity signal amplification, and high-definition Bluetooth codec transmission including aptX Adaptive, LDAC, and Auracast.
4. Finished consumer hardware products, including transportable DACs, dongles, and digital audio players, accompanied by a companion mobile control application.
5. Home hi-fi listening setups, portable head-fi audio rigs, and mobile playback from smartphones and tablets.
6. Audiophile consumers, headphone enthusiasts, and portable audio hobbyists.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to consumers and integrate semiconductors, microphones, power management, and USB controllers designed by its silicon suppliers.
8. It builds portable and dongle-form-factor audio gear using discrete Current Mode amplification and dual-mono DAC architectures to achieve desktop-grade fidelity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its hardware integrates components and licenses from ESS Technology, Qualcomm, Sony, XMOS, TOREX, Infineon, Apple, and a collaboration with SEAS.
Organization type: A privately held consumer audio brand and equipment manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio equipment to consumers.
Scale and maturity: An established specialist brand with a diverse catalog of portable and desktop audio products and a dedicated enthusiast community.
Geography: Based in China, selling to global audiophile markets.
Beyond audio: A pure-play audio company focused entirely on high-fidelity playback and amplification hardware.

points.name: Musical Fidelity
points.description: UK hi-fi manufacturer making DACs, amplifiers, and turntables for high-end home audio systems.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer hi-fi equipment that manufactures standalone digital-to-analog converters and turntables for home audio systems.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished digital-to-analog converters and turntables sold as physical hardware for home use.
2. The converters use digital input processing with switchable digital filters and support Direct Stream Digital up to DSD128 via USB.
3. The products decode high-resolution digital audio signals and convert them to analog outputs for home stereo playback.
4. Customers get the products as finished hardware components for home audio systems.
5. The equipment is used in home hi-fi and stereo listening systems.
6. The company sells to consumers and home audio enthusiasts.
7. Its finished hardware is sold to consumers through retail channels and audio distributors.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales.
Geography: The company is based in the United Kingdom.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on consumer and home audio equipment.

points.name: CVJ
points.description: Consumer electronics brand making affordable wireless earbuds and portable headphone amplifiers.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that builds and sells wireless DACs, headphone amplifiers, earphones and TWS earbuds for consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds wireless DACs, headphone amplifiers and earbuds sold as finished hardware.
2. The products use dynamic speaker drivers, Bluetooth chipsets, DAC chips, operational amplifier output stages and capacitive touch sensors.
3. The devices deliver wireless audio decoding, headphone amplification, touch-based playback control and wear sensing.
4. Customers get the technology as finished hardware products.
5. The products are used in personal listening setups, portable audio chains and earbuds.
6. The company sells to consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users.
8. The organization focuses on affordable audio and smart gadgets that incorporate premium decoding and amplification components into compact wireless devices.
points.profile:
Organization type: The company is a consumer electronics brand.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Fosi Audio
points.description: Consumer audio manufacturer producing affordable DACs, preamps, and Class D amplifiers.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and desktop audio equipment that designs and sells affordable digital-to-analog converters, preamplifiers, and power amplifiers for consumers and audio enthusiasts.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished digital-to-analog converters, phono preamps, and power amplifiers sold as standalone hardware components.
2. Class D amplifier topologies, digital-to-analog conversion chips, Bluetooth receivers, and analog circuits using user-swappable operational amplifiers.
3. Digital-to-analog conversion, audio amplification, phonograph signal equalization, and wired and wireless audio input routing.
4. Finished hardware products sold directly to consumers.
5. Desktop audio systems, home stereo setups, and turntable playback chains.
6. Consumers and budget-conscious audio enthusiasts.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users for personal audio systems.
8. It targets a high price-performance ratio by combining Class D amplifier designs and swappable operational amplifiers at low retail prices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its products incorporate chips and processors from ESS Technology, XMOS, and Qualcomm.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer and consumer electronics brand.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A manufacturer of budget-oriented audio components with individual products priced below one hundred fifty dollars to under four hundred dollars for complete desktop systems.
Geography: Based and operates in the consumer audio market.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio equipment.

points.name: XMOS
points.description: UK semiconductor company supplying USB audio processors for high-resolution playback equipment.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs multicore microcontrollers and voice processors for audio, control, and edge AI tasks, providing chips, reference designs, and development tools to consumer electronics and automotive device makers.
1. A chip company that designs multicore microcontrollers and voice processing chips, sold as finished hardware components and development kits that run embedded in customers' audio equipment.
2. Multicore microcontroller architecture using software-defined interfaces for I/O, running multithreaded audio DSP pipelines and on-chip voice algorithms.
3. High-resolution USB audio streaming, acoustic echo cancellation, adaptive beamforming, noise suppression, automatic gain control, dereverberation, full-duplex operation, barge-in, and embedded wake word detection.
4. Processors, development kits, reference designs, and software libraries.
5. USB DACs, smart speakers, microphone arrays, enterprise and consumer conferencing systems, and voice assistant devices.
6. Consumer electronics brands, audio equipment manufacturers, microphone array developers, and automakers.
7. Its chips are designed into audio equipment and voice devices by consumer electronics brands.
8. Its xcore architecture uses software-defined, multithreaded processing to combine audio, control, and AI tasks on a single chip with deterministic low-latency execution.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors include Infineon and Bosch, and its chips are used by Amazon Alexa, Seeed Studio, iFi, and Mycroft, utilizing Sensory's wake word technology.
Organization type: Privately held fabless semiconductor company.
Business model: Chip sales and development kit sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2005 and headquartered in Bristol, UK, backed by corporate investors.
Geography: Based in Bristol, UK, with a global customer base.
Beyond audio: Its multicore microcontrollers also target broader control and edge AI applications beyond audio.

points.name: Bricasti Design
points.description: US high-end audio manufacturer making reference-grade digital-to-analog converters, amplifiers, and hardware reverb units for audiophile and professional applications.
points.bullets:
A maker of high-end professional and consumer audio equipment that designs and manufactures digital-to-analog converters, power amplifiers, and studio reverb units for audiophiles and recording studios.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware components sold as standalone physical units.
2. Analog and digital signal processing circuits implementing digital-to-analog conversion, power amplification, and studio reverb processing in dedicated hardware.
3. High-fidelity digital-to-analog conversion, audio power amplification, and hardware-based acoustic reverb generation.
4. Finished hardware units including standalone converters, monoblock amplifiers, and reverb processors.
5. High-end home audio systems and professional recording studios.
6. Audiophiles, recording studios, and audio professionals.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly to end users and integrated into high-end audio playback and studio signal chains.
8. Premium build quality and reference-grade sound engineering aimed at the luxury audiophile and professional studio markets.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held equipment manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio components.
Geography: Based and operating in the USA.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio hardware.

points.name: Schiit Audio
points.description: US audio manufacturer building affordable desktop hi-fi equipment, headphone amplifiers, and digital-to-analog converters.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of audio equipment that builds desktop hi-fi components, including headphone amplifiers, DACs, phono preamps and power amplifiers, sold directly to audiophile consumers at value-oriented prices.
1. A maker of finished audio hardware sold as standalone desktop components in consumer hi-fi systems.
2. Discrete and hybrid circuit topologies, current-feedback gain stages, vacuum tube and solid-state designs, and digital-to-analog conversion with USB connectivity.
3. Digital-to-analog conversion, phono signal amplification, headphone amplification, speaker amplification, surround processing, and system control via a proprietary app for EQ, balance and volume.
4. Finished hardware products sold direct-to-consumer, accompanied by a proprietary companion app for system adjustment.
5. Desktop hi-fi systems, headphone listening setups, vinyl playback chains, gaming stations and two-channel speaker systems.
6. Audiophile consumers, vinyl enthusiasts and headphone users seeking affordable, high-performance gear.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold direct to consumers for use in home audio setups.
8. A direct-to-consumer model for affordable, audiophile-grade gear, paired with proprietary circuit topologies and an app for monitoring and adjusting hardware settings.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Schiit Europe acts as the European distributor for its products.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Direct-to-consumer hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with a broad product catalog of desktop audio components.
Geography: Based in Texas, USA, with distribution extending to Europe.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on audio equipment and has no business outside of audio.

points.name: Polk Audio
points.description: US speaker manufacturer building high-quality loudspeakers and soundbars for home audio.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of consumer and automotive audio equipment that designs and builds loudspeakers, soundbars, subwoofers, headphones, and architectural speakers for consumers.
1. A maker of finished audio equipment whose loudspeakers and soundbar systems are sold as physical hardware to consumers.
2. Acoustic transducer designs using passive driver arrays and crosstalk cancellation algorithms to expand stereo imaging.
3. Spatial audio reproduction, stereo image expansion, low-frequency bass reproduction, and multi-channel surround sound simulation.
4. Finished hardware products sold directly to consumers.
5. Home theaters, living rooms, outdoor environments, cars, boats, and in-wall architectural installations.
6. Consumers seeking accessible home, car, and personal audio products.
7. Its finished audio products are sold through retail channels directly to end consumers.
8. It employs Stereo Dimensional Array technology that cancels interaural crosstalk to expand the stereo image beyond the physical boundaries of the speaker cabinets.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant platforms.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand previously under Sound United and currently being acquired by Harman International from Masimo.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio products.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1972 with 201-500 employees.
Geography: Based in Carlsbad, California, United States.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: WiiM
points.description: US manufacturer building affordable audio streamers and smart speakers for home listening.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of affordable home audio hardware that builds network music streamers, streaming amplifiers, smart speakers, soundbars and subwoofers for consumers, combining wireless multiroom streaming with integrated amplification and digital signal processing.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware and companion control software, sold as standalone consumer products that run in the home.
2. Network streaming interfaces, integrated Class D amplification, digital-to-analog conversion, and embedded digital signal processing running on the devices.
3. High-resolution audio playback up to 24-bit/192kHz, multiroom audio synchronization, parametric and graphic equalization, automatic room correction, and voice-enhanced dialog processing.
4. Finished consumer hardware devices paired with a mobile companion application used for setup, control and firmware updates.
5. Home stereo systems, legacy audio system upgrades, smart homes, multiroom wireless audio setups and home theater configurations.
6. Consumers seeking budget-friendly audiophile-grade streaming equipment for home use.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users through consumer retail channels to upgrade or build home audio systems.
8. The organization delivers feature-rich streaming capabilities, equalization and room correction at highly competitive price points through ongoing firmware updates to inexpensive hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary brand of LinkPlay Technology Inc., with products sold primarily through Amazon and integrated with platforms including Chromecast, AirPlay 2, Alexa, Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect and Roon.
Organization type: A subsidiary consumer electronics brand of a privately held parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio devices.
Scale and maturity: A newer entrant in the smart home audio space with a comprehensive range of budget-friendly network music products launched starting in late 2021.
Geography: Based in the USA with products sold primarily through US retail channels.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on home audio hardware and associated streaming control software.

points.name: Chord Electronics
points.description: British audio manufacturer building high-end DACs and headphone amplifiers.
points.bullets:
A maker of high-end consumer and professional audio electronics that builds digital-to-analog converters, headphone amplifiers, preamplifiers and power amplifiers for audiophiles and audio reviewers.
1. An equipment maker that builds digital-to-analog converters and amplifiers, sold as finished consumer hardware.
2. Digital-to-analog conversion and amplification circuits, using custom-programmed FPGA devices for digital signal processing alongside analog amplifier circuitry.
3. Digital-to-analog conversion, headphone amplification, audio streaming, preamplification and power amplification.
4. Finished hardware units.
5. High-fidelity home audio systems, desktop audio setups, portable headphone listening and audio review reference systems.
6. Consumers and audiophiles.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly to consumers for use in home and portable audio setups.
8. It uses custom-coded FPGA devices for digital-to-analog conversion instead of standard off-the-shelf DAC chips.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Geography: Based and operates in the UK.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on audio electronics.

points.name: AudioQuest
points.description: US audio equipment manufacturer building high-end audio cables and portable USB DACs.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and high-end audio equipment that manufactures portable USB DACs, headphone amplifiers, audio cables and power conditioners for audiophiles and consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds portable DACs and analog audio accessories and sells them as finished hardware products.
2. Portable digital-to-analog converter chips and analog signal conductors housed in compact USB stick form factors and cable assemblies.
3. Digital-to-analog conversion, headphone amplification, high-resolution PCM playback up to 24-bit/96kHz and MQA decoding.
4. Finished hardware products sold directly to end users.
5. Personal audio listening setups, headphone systems and home audio reproduction chains.
6. Audiophiles and consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users for personal and home audio systems.
8. It integrates DAC chips and headphone amplifiers into ultra-compact, plug-and-play USB stick form factors requiring no drivers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It uses ESS Sabre DAC chips in its portable converters.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio equipment and accessories.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with a broad product catalog spanning portable converters, cables and power conditioners.
Geography: Based and operates in the USA.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on audio and video reproduction equipment, cables and power conditioning.

points.name: Audiolab
points.description: UK audio manufacturer building affordable high-performance amplifiers and digital-to-analog converters for home stereo systems.
points.bullets:
A maker of high-fidelity audio equipment that designs and sells stereo and surround sound components, including amplifiers, CD players, digital-to-analog converters and wireless streaming devices, for home audio consumers and audiophiles.
1. An equipment maker that builds integrated amplifiers, digital-to-analog converters and network streamers sold as finished hardware for use in home audio systems.
2. The core technology comprises analog amplifier circuits utilizing complementary feedback topology for low distortion, combined with high-resolution digital-to-analog conversion and network streaming platforms.
3. The equipment delivers high-fidelity audio amplification, digital-to-analog conversion, radio tuning and wireless network streaming.
4. Consumers acquire the technology as finished hardware components.
5. The products are used in home audio systems and stereo setups.
6. The company sells directly to consumers, audiophiles and music enthusiasts.
7. Its finished hardware is distributed globally through a parent company network to retail channels.
8. The approach combines engineering focused on low-distortion analog circuitry with value-driven pricing for high-performance home audio.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is a subsidiary brand of the International Audio Group.
Organization type: The entity is a subsidiary brand of a consumer audio manufacturing group.
Business model: The company makes money through the direct sale of consumer audio hardware.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1983, the brand has decades of establishment with a global distribution network.
Geography: It is based in the United Kingdom and operates worldwide.
Beyond audio: High-fidelity audio equipment is its entire focus.

points.name: Cambridge Audio
points.description: London audio brand building hi-fi components, network streamers, and wireless speakers.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and high-fidelity audio equipment that designs and sells finished hardware components, including network streamers, integrated amplifiers, digital-to-analog converters, turntables, headphones and wireless speakers. The organization develops a proprietary streaming and control platform that powers its networked devices. It builds these products for consumers and hi-fi enthusiasts seeking pure and natural sound reproduction.
1. An equipment maker that designs finished audio hardware products and companion control applications sold as standalone consumer electronics.
2. Digital-to-analog conversion circuits, integrated streaming platforms, wireless audio streaming protocols and acoustic driver designs.
3. High-resolution audio playback, network media streaming, room optimization, equalization and active noise cancellation.
4. Finished hardware products and companion mobile software applications.
5. Home hi-fi systems, desktop audio setups, wireless speaker systems and portable headphone listening.
6. Consumers and audio enthusiasts.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end consumers through consumer electronics retailers.
8. It integrates a proprietary streaming platform and application ecosystem across a broad range of high-fidelity audio hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It uses chips from Burr-Brown and Qualcomm, and integrates streaming services like Spotify, TIDAL, Qobuz and Roon.
Organization type: A privately held consumer electronics brand.
Business model: Hardware sales and direct retail.
Scale and maturity: A well-established organization operating for over 50 years.
Geography: Based in London, United Kingdom, selling its products internationally.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on designing, manufacturing and selling audio equipment and associated software.

points.name: SPL
points.description: Audio manufacturer making high-end analog equipment, DACs, monitor controllers, and software plugins.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and sells high-end analog hardware and corresponding software plugins for recording studios and mastering engineers.
1. An equipment maker and software developer whose professional audio hardware and audio plugins run as native software in digital audio workstations.
2. Analog filter networks, digital-to-analog converters, and algorithmic emulations of analog audio processing circuits.
3. Digital-to-analog conversion, headphone amplification, stereo image shaping, equalization, compression, transient shaping, and sound replacement.
4. Finished hardware units, 500-series hardware modules, and licensed software plugins distributed through a third-party plugin alliance.
5. Recording studios, mastering facilities, and headphone monitoring setups.
6. Recording engineers, mastering engineers, and audio producers.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly to audio professionals and its plugin emulations are developed and distributed by a third-party software developer.
8. It offers a portfolio of analog hardware with directly corresponding software plugin emulations developed in cooperation with a modeling partner.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Plugin Alliance and Brainworx.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales and software plugin licenses.
Geography: The company operates within the professional audio market.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on audio processing hardware and software.

points.name: NuPrime
points.description: Audio manufacturer building high-end Class D amplifiers and DACs for audiophiles.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures high-end stereo amplifiers, mono power amplifiers, integrated amplifiers, and digital-to-analog converters for consumer audio systems.
1. An equipment maker that builds high-end audio components and sells them as finished hardware for consumer home audio setups.
2. Hybrid Class D switching amplifier circuitry using silicon MOSFETs and proprietary low-loss switching technology, combined with analog front ends and linear power supplies.
3. High-power audio amplification, digital-to-analog conversion, preamplification, headphone amplification, and harmonic generation control for adjustable sonic characteristics.
4. Finished hardware components including stereo power amplifiers, mono power amplifiers, integrated amplifiers, and DAC-preamplifier units.
5. Consumer home audio systems, high-end hi-fi setups, studio monitoring, and relaxed home listening environments.
6. Consumers and audiophile enthusiasts purchasing high-end home audio equipment.
7. Its finished audio components are sold directly to consumers for integration into their home audio systems.
8. The company combines Single-Ended Non-Negative Class A modules with Double Feedback Class D modules and uses proprietary switching technology operating at 600 to 700kHz to rival traditional Class A and tube amplifier sound.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company licenses the NuForce brand name for legacy products and its IDA-8 integrated amplifier received Product of the Year awards from The Absolute Sound and SoundStage! Network in 2015.
Organization type: A privately held audio manufacturer founded as an off-shoot of the original NuForce company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio components across two product series spanning high-end and home categories.
Scale and maturity: The company was founded in 2014 and markets its products as affordable high-end audio through cost-effective production methods.
Geography: The company operates internationally with products distributed to markets including New Zealand and reviewed by publications such as What Hi-Fi?.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the company.

points.name: HiFiMAN
points.location: New York, USA; manufacturing in China
points.description: US-Chinese audio manufacturer making planar magnetic headphones for audiophile listening.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs and manufactures audiophile-grade planar magnetic over-ear headphones for home and desktop listening.
1. A consumer audio equipment maker that builds planar magnetic headphones sold as finished physical hardware for personal use.
2. Planar magnetic driver technology using thin diaphragms and magnetic arrays to reproduce sound.
3. High-resolution audio playback with high treble energy, detailed sound, clarity, image structure, and detail retrieval.
4. Finished hardware products in the form of full-size, open-back over-ear headphones.
5. Home and desktop audiophile listening, critical audio reviews, and personal music consumption.
6. Audiophiles, headphone enthusiasts, and consumers.
7. Its finished headphones are sold directly to consumers and through specialized audio retail brands.
8. It competes aggressively on performance-per-dollar against European premium brands in the mid-to-premium tier.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Retailer Audio46 carries its planar magnetic headphones.
Organization type: A privately held consumer electronics manufacturer and challenger headphone brand.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audiophile headphones.
Scale and maturity: A challenger brand offering products priced from $350 to $5,999.
Geography: Headquartered in New York, USA, with manufacturing in China.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Qudelix
points.description: South Korean audio equipment manufacturer building portable Bluetooth amplifiers for earphones.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of portable audio equipment that builds Bluetooth DAC/AMP devices for wired headphones and IEMs, along with a companion mobile app for controlling them, for consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds portable Bluetooth DAC/AMP hardware sold as finished devices and a companion control app.
2. The devices integrate a Sabre DAC chipset and support high-resolution Bluetooth audio codecs alongside a digital signal processor for audio tuning.
3. The hardware delivers digital-to-analog conversion, headphone amplification, high-resolution wireless audio streaming and parametric equalization.
4. Customers get the products as finished consumer hardware devices and a free software application.
5. The devices are used with in-ear monitors and wired headphones for personal listening.
6. The company sells to consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users through consumer retail channels.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of its audio devices.
Geography: The company is based in South Korea.
Beyond audio: Audio is the company's entire focus.

points.name: Luxman
points.description: Japanese high-end audio manufacturer making integrated amplifiers, turntables, and SACD/CD players.
points.bullets:
A maker of high-end consumer audio equipment that designs and sells premium SACD/CD players, integrated amplifiers and turntables for audiophiles.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware sold to consumers.
2. Analog amplifier circuits, digital-to-analog conversion using discrete D/A converters, and mechanical turntable playback systems.
3. Optical disc playback, phono playback, line-level amplification and volume control.
4. Finished consumer hardware products.
5. High-end home audio systems.
6. Audiophiles and consumers.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly to consumers and integrated by owners into home audio systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: ROHM supplies its D/A converters and IAG Group is its parent company.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of IAG Group.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A globally operating brand with an established history.
Geography: Based in Japan and operating globally.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Hiby
points.description: Chinese manufacturer building high-resolution portable digital audio players for audiophiles.
points.bullets:
A maker of finished audio equipment that designs and sells high-resolution digital audio players with built-in DACs for consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished portable digital audio players running an Android OS on embedded Snapdragon chipsets.
2. Portable audio playback systems integrating application processors, mobile operating systems, and discrete digital-to-analog converter chips.
3. High-resolution audio decoding, including DSD and MQA unfolding, alongside balanced and single-ended headphone output and wireless streaming.
4. Finished hardware products sold directly to consumers.
5. Portable personal audio listening.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users in the consumer electronics market.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates chipsets and DACs from Snapdragon, ESS Technology, and Cirrus Logic.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A recognized manufacturer in a niche consumer audio market.
Geography: Based in and operates within the global consumer electronics market.

points.name: Shanling
points.description: Chinese audio manufacturer building portable music players, USB DAC/amps, and earphones.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of premium audio equipment that builds portable digital audio players, USB DAC/amplifier adapters, in-ear monitors, and desktop streamers for consumers.
1. A maker of finished audio hardware products that run standalone or connect to consumer source devices.
2. The products integrate discrete digital-to-analog converter chips, balanced armature drivers, and embedded operating systems for audio playback.
3. High-resolution audio decoding, digital-to-analog conversion, headphone amplification, and Bluetooth audio reception.
4. The hardware is sold as finished consumer devices through retail distributors.
5. Portable music listening, high-fidelity headphone listening, and desktop audio playback.
6. Consumers and retail distributors.
7. Its finished devices integrate digital-to-analog converter chips from semiconductor suppliers and are retailed to consumers by consumer electronics distributors.
8. The organization builds portable players using customized lightweight operating systems focused on local music playback alongside open Android implementations on flagship models.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its products integrate digital-to-analog converter chips from semiconductor suppliers and are retailed by consumer electronics distributors.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: The organization makes money through hardware sales.
Geography: The company is based in China and its products are showcased and retailed internationally.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play audio company.

points.name: Hidizs
points.description: Portable audio manufacturer building high-resolution music players, in-ear monitors, and headphone amplifiers.
aliases: Hidizs - HiFi Portable & Desktop Audio Gears
points.bullets:
A maker of portable audio equipment that designs and sells consumer playback hardware, including portable digital audio players, dongle and portable DACs, headphone amplifiers, in-ear monitors, headphones, CD players and streaming amplifiers for audiophiles, musicians and music enthusiasts.
1. An equipment maker whose finished audio playback hardware is sold as standalone physical products to consumers.
2. Audio playback systems built around dedicated digital-to-analog converter chips and op-amps integrated into compact portable devices with physical controls and touchscreens.
3. High-resolution audio decoding and playback supporting formats including MQA, LDAC, Aptx and DSD, alongside single-ended and balanced headphone amplification.
4. Finished hardware devices, including portable players, dongles, in-ear monitors and amplifiers.
5. Personal listening setups, portable high-resolution audio playback and mobile music listening.
6. Consumers, audiophiles, musicians, gamers and music enthusiasts.
7. Its finished consumer hardware products are sold directly to end users.
8. It packs audiophile-grade components and high-resolution audio support into compact, portable device designs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It uses digital-to-analog converter chips from ESS and launched products on Kickstarter.
Organization type: A privately held consumer audio brand.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A company founded in 2012 serving a worldwide market.
Geography: Based and operating globally.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: HIFI WALKER
points.description: Manufacturer building budget portable hi-res audio players for accessible music listening.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that builds and sells dedicated high-resolution portable audio players for consumers seeking budget audiophile devices.
1. A consumer audio equipment maker whose finished portable music player hardware runs standalone in end users' hands.
2. Portable digital audio players built around discrete digital-to-analog converters that decode high-resolution audio files.
3. Playback and decoding of high-resolution audio formats including FLAC, WAV and Native DSD up to DSD256 from removable storage.
4. Finished consumer hardware products with embedded firmware and integrated digital-to-analog converters.
5. Portable personal audio players used for mobile high-resolution music listening.
6. Consumers seeking dedicated budget audiophile music players.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to consumers for personal listening.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished portable audio players.
Geography: Based and operates as a consumer electronics manufacturer marketing portable audio players.

points.name: Moondrop
points.description: Chinese headphones and personal audio company making in-ear monitors, earbuds, and portable audio equipment using proprietary transducer designs.
points.bullets:
