Scale and maturity: A Series A1 funded company operating in the professional and consumer audio markets.
Geography: Based in Belgium and operating in global entertainment and media markets.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio technology.

points.name: Final Audio
points.description: Japanese audio manufacturer making high-end headphones, earphones, and in-ear monitors using unconventional materials.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs and sells high-end headphones, earphones and in-ear monitors, incorporating personalized sound technology based on ear scanning for consumers.
1. A consumer audio equipment maker that builds premium headphones, earphones and wireless earbuds sold as finished hardware worn by users.
2. Acoustic transducers and ear-scanning software are used to tailor frequency response to the individual listener's ear.
3. Personalized sound profiling based on ear scanning, high-fidelity audio reproduction and wireless audio reception.
4. The company delivers finished hardware and embedded software directly to end users.
5. Its products are used in personal entertainment, remote work, online learning and portable listening settings.
6. The organization sells directly to consumers.
7. Its finished audio devices are sold to consumers through retail channels in competition with other consumer electronics brands.
8. Its approach is distinguished by the use of unconventional materials and ear-scanning software to drive personalized sound.
points.profile:
Organization type: The company is a privately held manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through the direct sale of premium audio hardware.
Scale and maturity: It is an established manufacturer competing in a global market with hundreds of audio brands.
Geography: The organization is based in Japan and operates in the global market, with a strong position in the Asia-Pacific region.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on high-end personal audio equipment.

points.name: Embody
points.description: California startup creating personalized spatial audio profiles from ear images.
points.bullets:
An audio software developer that builds personalized spatial audio software and HRTF profiling applications for consumers, gamers, musicians and audio post-production.
1. An audio software developer whose spatial rendering and HRTF profiling applications run as standalone software or plugins on consumer devices and desktop workstations.
2. Spatial rendering algorithms and AI-driven personalization models that generate head-related transfer function profiles from smartphone ear images.
3. Personalized spatial audio, binaural rendering, virtual studio acoustics simulation, and 3D audio with directional sound highlighting for games.
4. Software products and plugins sold to end-users, including VST plugins, standalone applications, and mobile apps.
5. Gaming headsets, PC games, music streaming, virtual reality, and professional studio mixing and mastering workflows.
6. Consumers, gamers, recording studios, music producers, and headphone brands.
7. Its software is integrated into consumer headsets by gaming brands and its spatial audio technology is embedded into digital audio workstations by software developers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners include Audeze, Steinberg, Logitech G, Astro, Apple Music, Tidal, Amazon Music, Lurssen Mastering, and Dolby.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software sales and subscriptions, and technology licensing to headphone and audio software companies.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage startup based in San Mateo, California.
Geography: Based in San Mateo, California, operating in the global consumer electronics and audio software markets.
Beyond audio: Its focus is entirely on audio technology.

points.name: Mimi Hearing Technologies
points.description: Berlin technology company personalizing sound based on individual hearing profiles.
points.bullets:
A software and AI model developer that builds sound personalization, hearing test, and neural audio codec technologies for consumer electronics brands and AI speech model developers. It licenses algorithms and models that adapt audio output to individual hearing profiles, and it develops a low-latency neural audio codec used by cloud-based voice AI. The organization has collected a large database of digital hearing profiles to power its personalization engines.
1. A software and AI model developer whose sound personalization algorithms run on-device in consumer electronics products and whose neural audio codec runs in the cloud behind speech models.
2. Digital hearing test algorithms, hearing-profile-based audio processing, and a transformer-based neural audio codec that distills self-supervised speech representations for low-bitrate audio streaming.
3. Sound personalization, hearing assessment, dialogue and voice clarity enhancement, background noise reduction, and neural audio compression.
4. SDKs, APIs, cloud models, and licensed algorithms integrated into consumer devices, plus mobile hearing test applications.
5. Earbuds, headphones, smartphones, televisions, soundbars, automotive sound systems, smart glasses, in-flight entertainment systems, browser extensions, and cloud-based conversational voice models.
6. Consumer electronics brands, headphone and earbud makers, television manufacturers, automakers, telehealth and health-tech providers, and AI speech model developers.
7. Its algorithms and codecs are integrated by device makers into their hardware and by AI developers into their voice models.
8. It leverages a massive proprietary database of digital hearing profiles to drive its personalized sound adaptation, and its neural codec achieves low-latency, low-bitrate streaming through transformer-based architecture and self-supervised representation distillation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Nothing, Bragi, Breggz, Creative, Cleer, Montblanc, Apple Health, 3D Sound Labs, Kyutai, WavLM, EnCodec, and SoundStream.
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: Software licensing, per-unit royalties, API usage fees, and acquired intellectual property.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2014, with over one million hearing test app downloads across 180 countries and a database of over four million hearing tests.
Geography: Based in Berlin, Germany, and operating globally through consumer electronics integrations.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio, spanning hearing assessment, sound personalization, and neural audio codecs.

points.name: 3D Sound Labs
points.description: French VR audio startup developing 3D binaural software, smart headphones, and licensing SDKs to third parties.
points.bullets:
A VR audio technology company that develops 3D spatial audio software and hardware, including HRTF-based binaural engines and smart headphones. It licenses its spatial audio technology to third parties and builds finished consumer hardware for immersive listening.
1. An audio software developer whose spatial rendering engines are sold as SDKs and licensed technology, alongside finished consumer hardware devices.
2. HRTF-based Ambisonics binaural rendering engines combined with motion tracking modules for dynamic spatial audio.
3. 3D and VR audio spatial rendering, binaural sound, and motion-tracked head-related transfer function processing.
4. Software development kits, technology licensing programs, and finished smart headphones.
5. Virtual reality experiences and smart headphones.
6. Third-party hardware and software developers, and consumers.
7. Its spatial audio engines are integrated into third-party products while it also sells finished consumer hardware directly.
8. Its combination of HRTF-based Ambisonics binaural rendering with integrated motion tracking modules in both software and hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Acquired by Mimi Hearing Technologies to enhance sound personalization technology with HRTF expertise.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licensing, freemium technology licensing programs, and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A startup founded in 2014 and acquired by a hearing technology company.
Geography: Based in Paris, France.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio technology.

points.name: AudioControl
points.description: US audio equipment company building home theater processors, amplifiers, and car audio systems.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs and manufactures high-performance home theater processors, distributed audio amplifiers, car audio amplifiers, speakers, subwoofers, and signal processors for consumers, installers, and automotive integrators.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished home and car audio hardware and sells it as physical products in consumer and vehicle installations.
2. High-current Class D amplifier designs, digital signal processing with on-board DSP, bass restoration and harmonic fundamental recreation, and networked multi-zone amplification over Dante and TCP/IP.
3. Signal summing, OEM radio integration, bass restoration, parametric and graphic equalization, channel bridging, network monitoring, and multi-zone distributed audio control.
4. Finished hardware products, including amplifiers, processors, speakers, subwoofers, and line output converters.
5. Home theaters, distributed audio installations, car audio systems, and aftermarket automotive sound upgrades.
6. Consumers, custom integrators, and automotive aftermarket installers.
7. Its finished hardware is installed directly into residential and vehicle environments by integrators and consumers.
8. Products are designed with a professional recording studio heritage and feature patented bass restoration and OEM integration technologies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Dirac Research, Origin Acoustics, AVPro Global, AAMP Holdings, Oceanic Distribution, and Sales And Marketing, Inc.
Organization type: Privately held brand operating under AVPro Global for home audio and AAMP Holdings for vehicle technology.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio equipment.
Scale and maturity: A nearly 45-year-old company with research and development, manufacturing, production, and training facilities in Seattle.
Geography: Based and manufactured in Seattle, Washington, USA, with distribution extending to Australia and the United States Midwest region.
Beyond audio: The company is entirely focused on audio equipment design and manufacturing.

points.name: Marantz
points.description: Japanese audio brand manufacturing A/V receivers and amplifiers.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and high-fidelity audio equipment that designs and sells A/V receivers, preamplifiers, integrated amplifiers, and disc players for home cinema and stereo listening.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio components sold as standalone hardware in consumer home entertainment systems.
2. Digital-to-analog conversion using discrete chip sets, multi-room streaming platforms, and integrated digital signal processing for spatial audio and room correction.
3. Surround sound decoding, multi-room audio streaming, and room correction.
4. The company provides its technology through finished consumer hardware products.
5. Home theaters, dedicated stereo listening rooms, and multi-room residential audio setups.
6. Consumers and home audio enthusiasts.
7. Its finished hardware is sold through retail channels directly to end consumers and integrated into home installations.
8. The brand combines high-fidelity audio reproduction with traditional industrial design and physical controls in its component chassis.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company integrates licensed room correction and spatial audio technology from partners including Dirac, Audyssey, Auro 3D, and MPEG-H, uses digital-to-analog converters from Burr-Brown, and is being acquired by Harman International from Masimo.
Organization type: A subsidiary audio brand operating under a corporate parent.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of finished audio components.
Scale and maturity: A long-established brand with nearly 70 years of history in the audio market.
Geography: Based in Japan and operating in the global consumer electronics market.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio and home entertainment hardware.

points.name: miniDSP
points.description: Hong Kong audio technology company building digital signal processors and room correction tools for audiophiles and home theaters.
points.bullets:
An audio equipment maker that designs and sells digital signal processors, measurement microphones, and calibration software for audiophiles, engineers, and DIY enthusiasts in home theater, hi-fi, headphone, and automotive markets.
1. A maker of finished audio hardware that builds digital signal processors and USB measurement microphones sold as standalone physical devices running embedded DSP code.
2. Digital signal processing algorithms running on embedded Analog Devices SHARC processors alongside USB condenser microphone capsules.
3. Room correction, parametric equalization, active crossover design, time delay, and acoustic measurement.
4. Finished hardware products, USB measurement microphones, and accompanying control software.
5. Home theaters, hi-fi systems, headphone setups, and automotive aftermarket audio systems.
6. DIY audio enthusiasts, audiophiles, engineers, and automotive aftermarket installers.
7. Its processors and microphones are used directly by end-users and integrate licensed third-party room correction software.
8. It targets the DIY and enthusiast markets with accessible, standalone DSP hardware paired with measurement microphones.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates licensed room correction software from Dirac Research and uses DSP chips from Analog Devices.
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: Hardware sales of processors and microphones.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2009 as an established audio technology company.
Geography: Based in Kowloon Bay, Hong Kong, serving global markets.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on digital audio signal processing and acoustic measurement.

points.name: StormAudio
points.description: US-based manufacturer building high-end processors and amplifiers for premium home theaters.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional and high-end consumer audio equipment that designs and manufactures immersive audio processors, AV receivers and multi-channel amplifiers for premium home theaters and private cinemas.
1. An equipment maker that builds high-end AV processors, receivers and amplifiers sold as finished hardware in dedicated home cinema installations.
2. Digital signal processing platforms incorporating external digital-to-analog converters and licensed room correction algorithms.
3. Immersive audio decoding and processing, multi-channel signal routing and active room correction.
4. The products are delivered as finished hardware components integrated into custom home theater installations.
5. High-end home theaters, media rooms and private cinemas.
6. Custom installers, home theater integrators and high-end consumers.
7. Its finished hardware is installed in premium residential cinemas by custom integration professionals.
8. The processors are modular and designed to be future-proof and upgradeable through software add-ons and hardware expansions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Dirac, Alcons Audio, Pulse Cinemas, ASCENDO, ESS Technology and Audioholics.
Organization type: A privately held equipment manufacturer operating as a brand under Pulse Cinemas.
Business model: Hardware sales of processors, receivers and amplifiers.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with a worldwide presence through a United States subsidiary and a Hong Kong office.
Geography: Headquartered in France with operations extending globally.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on high-performance residential and cinema audio hardware.

points.name: Smaart
points.description: Audio analysis software developer creating real-time measurement tools for sound system tuning and room acoustics.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds professional real-time audio and acoustic analysis software for sound system tuning and room measurement, providing spectrum analysis and transfer-function measurement for audio engineers and system integrators.
1. A developer tools company whose acoustic measurement and analysis software runs as desktop applications and mobile iOS apps.
2. Real-time transfer-function analysis and spectrum measurement engines performing single-channel RTA, spectrograph and SPL data analysis.
3. Real-time spectrum analysis, transfer-function measurement, sound system tuning, room measurement and SPL data capture.
4. The analysis software is delivered as desktop software products and mobile applications.
5. The software is used in live sound venues, studios and sound system tuning environments.
6. The company sells to audio engineers, system integrators and sound system technicians.
7. Its measurement software is used directly by audio professionals to tune sound systems and is integrated into digital mixers by hardware manufacturers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company ports measurements to Waves TRACT via an API link and has streamlined versions of its modules integrated into PreSonus StudioLive SeriesIII mixers.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company operating under the name Rational Acoustics.
Business model: The company makes money through software licenses for its desktop and mobile applications.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play audio company entirely focused on acoustic measurement and analysis tools.

points.name: Antelope Audio
points.description: US audio equipment manufacturer building high-end interfaces and hardware processors using atomic clocking technology.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds high-end audio interfaces, analog outboard gear, and clocking technology for recording studios and engineers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished hardware sold as rackmount units and desktop devices running in professional studios.
2. Analog circuitry, FPGA-based DSP engines, and atomic clocking technologies running in dedicated hardware units.
3. AD/DA conversion, microphone preamplification, real-time DSP effects, audio clocking, and analog opto-valve compression.
4. Finished hardware products, including audio interfaces, analog compressors, and clocking generators.
5. Recording studios, post-production facilities, and professional music production environments.
6. Studios, musicians, and audio engineers.
7. Its finished hardware products are purchased directly by recording studios and engineers for use in production environments.
8. Its approach centers on FPGA-based real-time DSP processing combined with atomic audio clocking in premium interface hardware.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Geography: Based in Santa Monica, California, United States.
Beyond audio: The company is a pure-play audio equipment manufacturer.

points.name: Mackie
points.description: US pro audio manufacturer building durable mixers, loudspeakers, and PA systems for studio and stage use.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio equipment that designs and produces mixers, loudspeakers, studio monitors, microphones, and podcasting workstations for home, studio, and stage use.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished hardware products sold as physical units.
2. Analog and digital audio mixing electronics, Class-D amplification, loudspeaker drivers, DSP for feedback elimination and EQ, and wireless audio transmission.
3. Audio mixing, signal routing, sound reinforcement, studio monitoring, podcast recording, live streaming, and Bluetooth audio playback.
4. Customers get it as finished hardware products including compact and digital mixers, powered PA speakers, stage monitors, studio monitors, interfaces, microphones, and headphones.
5. Home studios, live stages, outdoor events, podcasting, live streaming, and desktop audio setups.
6. Recording artists, live performers, podcasters, streamers, creators, music stores, and live sound engineers.
7. Its finished hardware is sold through retail channels to end users.
8. It focuses on affordable, durable products positioned as workhorse gear across live sound, recording, and content creation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is owned by Røde Microphones and part of The Freedman Group.
Organization type: A professional audio brand operating as a subsidiary.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A brand founded in 1988 that ranks among the top ten manufacturers by sales volume in its market.
Geography: A brand based in the United States.
Beyond audio: It is focused entirely on professional audio equipment.

points.name: Midas
points.description: UK manufacturer building high-end mixing consoles for live sound.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio equipment that designs and builds high-end analog and digital mixing consoles, signal processors, DI boxes, and audio networking converters for live sound, installation, and broadcast applications.
1. An equipment maker that designs finished audio hardware products sold as physical units deployed in studios, live venues, and installed sound systems.
2. Analog circuit design featuring custom audio transformers and microphone preamps, digital mixing engines, and AES50 audio networking with asynchronous sample rate conversion.
3. Audio mixing, microphone preamplification, direct injection and signal splitting, analog signal processing, acoustic echo cancellation, and digital audio network bridging and extension.
4. Finished hardware products including mixing consoles, DI boxes, network bridges, and signal processors.
5. Live sound reinforcement for concert tours, broadcast studios, fixed audio installations, and public address systems.
6. Audio engineers, sound reinforcement contractors, touring productions, and broadcast facilities.
7. Its finished hardware products are operated directly by front-of-house and monitor engineers in live venues and installed into facilities by sound contractors.
8. It designs its own audio transformers and microphone preamps that are also supplied as components to affiliated brands within its parent company.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its parent company is Music Tribe, and its consoles support Waves SoundGrid networking cards, with products often bundled with Turbosound loudspeakers.
Organization type: A professional audio brand operating as a subsidiary of a global holding company.
Business model: Hardware sales of mixing consoles, signal processors, and DI boxes.
Scale and maturity: A well-established London-based manufacturer active since the 1970s and acquired by its current parent company in 2009.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom and operating globally in the professional audio market.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on professional audio hardware and signal processing.

points.name: European Broadcasting Union
points.description: European standards organization setting broadcast loudness normalization specs, notably the R128 standard targeting -23 LUFS for TV and radio audio.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops and maintains broadcasting specifications for audio loudness normalization, providing technical recommendations, implementation guidelines and test signals for broadcasters and audio product manufacturers.
1. A standards body whose audio specifications and technical guidelines are published as open standards and reference documents.
2. Loudness measurement and normalization algorithms and parameters based on Programme Loudness targeting and true peak ceiling metrics.
3. Audio loudness normalization, loudness metering and loudness range measurement.
4. Open standards, technical guidelines and test signals.
5. Television and radio broadcasting, digital streaming platforms and media player software.
6. Public service broadcasters, audio product manufacturers and software developers.
7. Its standards are implemented by broadcasters in production workflows and by audio product manufacturers in measurement tools.
8. It serves as a central collaborative authority that shifted the European broadcast industry from peak normalization to loudness normalization to eliminate audience irritation from audio level jumps.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include national public broadcasters ORF and RTVE, and MediaMonkey.
Organization type: An alliance of public service media organizations.
Business model: It does not generate revenue from audio activities through commercial product sales or licensing fees.
Scale and maturity: It operates across the European broadcast industry with adoption extending to digital streaming platforms.
Geography: It is based in Europe and hosts workshops in cities including Geneva and Madrid.
Beyond audio: It is a broadcasting union whose broader scope encompasses public service media collaboration across Europe.

points.name: Sound United
points.description: Carlsbad audio manufacturer producing home theater receivers and speakers under multiple brands.
points.bullets:
A parent company and equipment maker that owns a portfolio of consumer audio brands and sells finished home theater and personal audio products to consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished home audio hardware, including AV receivers, loudspeakers, and wireless multi-room speakers, sold as branded products.
2. Multi-room wireless audio streaming software and standard audio amplification and speaker driver technologies built into finished hardware.
3. Multi-room WiFi audio playback, home theater amplification, and spatial audio format support.
4. Finished consumer hardware products and embedded multi-room streaming software.
5. Home theaters, living rooms, and personal listening settings.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished hardware is distributed through retail channels to consumers.
8. It operates as a holding company managing multiple distinct legacy audio brands under one corporate umbrella.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is owned by Harman International, partners with Dirac for room correction, and collaborates with Fraunhofer IIS on MPEG-H Audio implementation.
Organization type: A subsidiary business unit operating under a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: The company has 1,001 to 5,000 employees and was acquired for $350 million.
Geography: The company is based in Carlsbad, California, United States, with European distribution handled by a distribution partner.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on consumer audio products.

points.name: Trinnov
points.description: French audio company building high-end processors and room correction solutions for home theaters and professional studios.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional and high-end audio equipment that designs and manufactures preamplifiers, processors, and power amplifiers featuring loudspeaker and room optimization for high-end hi-fi, home theaters, professional studios, and movie theaters.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio processors, power amplifiers, and room correction systems sold as standalone hardware.
2. DSP algorithms running on dedicated audio processing hardware that analyze acoustic measurements from a 3D measurement microphone to correct room and loudspeaker responses.
3. Room correction, loudspeaker optimization, 3D sound processing, immersive audio decoding, and multichannel amplification.
4. Finished hardware products, including processors, power amplifiers, measurement microphones, and remote controls.
5. High-end home cinemas, professional music and film studios, commercial movie theaters, and residential hi-fi systems.
6. Home cinema owners, professional studios, commercial cinema operators, and audio-video dealers and installers.
7. Its processors and amplifiers are specified by custom installers and integrated into bespoke home cinema and professional audio systems.
8. Its hardware platform is built around exclusive room optimization technology using a dedicated 3D measurement microphone to identify loudspeaker positions and analyze acoustic response.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio equipment.
Scale and maturity: An established company with over 8000 installations across 55 countries.
Geography: Based in France, where its hardware is handmade, operating globally.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on audio technology and equipment.

points.name: Dayton Audio
points.description: US audio equipment manufacturer building affordable measurement tools and loudspeaker components for DIY enthusiasts.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs and manufactures audio measurement tools and loudspeaker components for DIY audio enthusiasts and professionals.
1. An equipment maker that builds measurement microphones, loudspeaker analyzers, and loudspeaker driver components, sold as finished hardware.
2. Calibrated electret condenser microphone capsules and impedance-measurement hardware with built-in amplifiers characterize acoustic and electro-mechanical parameters.
3. Room response measurement, Thiele-Small parameter extraction, impedance measurement, phase measurement, and time-of-flight calculation.
4. Finished hardware products, including measurement microphones, USB DACs, analyzer units, and accessory kits.
5. Acoustic measurement, room correction, loudspeaker design, and DIY audio projects.
6. DIY audio enthusiasts, loudspeaker designers, and value-conscious hi-fi consumers.
7. Its measurement hardware and loudspeaker components are sold directly to consumers through an affiliated electronics distributor.
8. It targets the entry-level and value segment with affordable calibrated measurement tools and raw driver components rather than professional-grade pricing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It operates as a subsidiary brand of a consumer electronics distributor, with software compatibility provided by third-party acoustic measurement applications.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of an electronics distribution company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished measurement equipment and loudspeaker components.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with over three decades in the audio industry.
Geography: Based in Springboro, Ohio, USA, with manufacturing across North America, Europe, and Asia.
Beyond audio: The company also designs and manufactures raw loudspeaker drivers, amplifiers, exciters, and finished home audio products for consumers.

points.name: Rode
points.description: Australian audio equipment manufacturer making microphones, wireless systems, and podcasting mixers for creators.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional and creator audio equipment that designs and manufactures microphones, wireless microphone systems, podcasting mixers, loudspeakers, headphones, and audio software for content creators, professionals, and residential and commercial users.
1. An audio equipment manufacturer that builds finished hardware products and companion software, sold as physical devices and desktop and mobile applications.
2. Condenser, dynamic, lavalier, and MEMS microphone transducers, UHF wireless transmission, analog and digital podcasting mixers, and cloud-based and on-device AI-driven audio editing software.
3. Sound capture, wireless audio transmission, multi-channel audio mixing, SD card recording, timecode synchronization, 32-bit float recording, acoustic measurement, and AI-driven transcription and editing.
4. Finished hardware products including microphones, wireless systems, mixers, loudspeakers, headphones, and accessories, alongside mobile and desktop software applications.
5. Home and broadcast studios, field recording, online content production, podcasting, video production, filmmaking, residential spaces, and commercial spaces.
6. Professional and creator customers, podcasters, broadcasters, filmmakers, musicians, and residential and commercial users.
7. Its finished hardware and software products are sold directly to end users for content creation and recording.
8. It targets the content creator market with high-quality yet accessible microphone and wireless designs at price points substantially below premium manufacturer pricing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Infineon manufactures its MEMS microphone technology, it acquired Mackie, and it is part of the Freedman Group.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand within the Freedman Group.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio equipment and accessories.
Scale and maturity: Established in 1967, the company is a significant player in the global content creation and professional audio market.
Geography: Based in Australia and targeting professional and creator customers throughout the Asia-Pacific region and globally.
Beyond audio: The company's focus is entirely on audio.

points.name: Audio Foundry
points.description: Detroit collaborative platform accelerating in-vehicle audio prototyping for automakers using specialized design tools and physical test setups.
points.bullets:
A collaborative automotive audio technology platform and physical prototyping space that provides specialized equipment, design tools, and engineering services to help automakers and Tier 1 suppliers accelerate in-vehicle audio development. The organization bridges hardware and software, enabling manufacturers to test experimental speaker placements and new audio architectures before committing to production.
1. A developer tools and physical prototyping company whose platform engineers use to build, simulate and test in-vehicle audio systems in a physical demonstration environment.
2. Acoustic demonstration setups, specialized speaker configurations, and audio processing software integrated to visualize and prototype in-cabin acoustics.
3. Spatial audio, active noise cancellation, subwoofer size reduction, acoustic alignment and stabilization, and ultra-low frequency sound pressure generation.
4. Engineering services, technology licensing, platform access, and physical demonstration setups.
5. Car audio systems, automotive test and measurement, and electric and autonomous vehicle cabins.
6. Automakers, global automotive Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers, audio software developers, and hardware manufacturers.
7. Its platform and licensed IP are integrated and utilized by automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers to develop and test production audio systems.
8. It provides a physical collaborative environment and specialized demonstration setups that allow manufacturers to prototype experimental speaker placements and new audio architectures before production commitment.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: DSP Concepts, Tymphany, Dirac, Pioneer, Bluacs, and Karma.
Organization type: A collaborative platform and physical prototyping space born from a partnership between an audio software company and a speaker manufacturer.
Business model: Engineering services, technology licensing, and platform access.
Scale and maturity: A targeted intermediary in the global automotive audio market demonstrating concepts at major industry events.
Geography: Operates primarily in the global automotive market, showcasing technologies at international trade shows.
Beyond audio: The organization operates entirely within the automotive audio and test and measurement segments, bridging hardware and software for in-vehicle acoustic development.

points.name: Bluacs
points.description: Australian research company developing car cabin speaker and subwoofer technologies.
points.bullets:
An audio technology research company that develops novel speaker and acoustic designs, particularly woofer and subwoofer configurations that use full car cabin volume, for automotive audio applications.
1. An audio research and IP company that develops novel speaker and acoustic designs licensed to speaker manufacturers and automotive audio integrators.
2. Acoustic designs utilizing full cabin volume enclosures, force-cancelling woofer modules, and targeted near-field headrest speaker arrays.
3. In-cabin bass reproduction, force-cancellation vibration reduction, and localized personal bass audio delivery.
4. Licensed speaker and acoustic technologies, including subwoofer and headrest designs.
5. Automotive cabin audio systems, including firewall-mounted subwoofers and headrest speakers.
6. Speaker manufacturers and automotive audio system integrators.
7. Its acoustic designs are licensed to speaker manufacturers that supply vehicle audio systems.
8. It uses the full cabin volume for bass reproduction and creates localized personal bass fields through small-diameter headrest speakers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Tymphany, Audio Foundry, Karma Revero.
Organization type: Privately held research and development company.
Business model: Technology licensing.
Scale and maturity: A small research-focused organization.
Geography: Based in Australia.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on audio technology research.

points.name: Bose Automotive
points.description: Automotive audio supplier providing active road-noise cancellation systems for vehicles.
points.bullets:
An automotive audio supplier and division of a consumer audio brand that provides active sound management and road-noise control systems for vehicles, integrating chassis sensors, microphones, adaptive algorithms, and the vehicle sound system for automakers.
1. An automotive audio supplier that builds active noise control systems sold as integrated hardware-software solutions running in vehicles.
2. Adaptive algorithms process input from chassis sensors and cabin microphones to drive active noise cancellation through the vehicle sound system.
3. The organization delivers active road-noise control that detects road- and chassis-related input and reduces road noise at occupied positions in the cabin.
4. The systems are delivered as integrated hardware-software solutions combining accelerometers, microphones, and adaptive algorithms.
5. The technology is used in cars and other vehicles.
6. The organization sells to automakers.
7. Its active sound management systems are designed into vehicles by automakers.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a division of a consumer audio brand.
Beyond audio: The parent brand is a consumer and professional audio equipment maker, with this division focused on automotive audio.

points.name: Panasonic Automotive Systems
points.description: Japanese automotive supplier developing in-car audio, noise cancellation, and infotainment systems for vehicles.
points.bullets:
An automotive supplier that develops premium audio systems, active noise control systems, and infotainment processor platforms for automakers.
1. An automotive supplier that builds finished premium audio systems, active noise control systems, and infotainment platforms that are integrated into vehicles.
2. Premium audio tuning and spatial surround algorithms, active noise control using vibration sensing and broadband processing, and infotainment processing for multi-zone audio and video distribution.
3. Spatial audio rendering, active road and engine noise cancellation, multi-zone audio distribution, and 4K video processing.
4. Finished hardware systems, embedded software, and processor platforms supplied for vehicle integration.
5. Passenger vehicles and series-hybrid vehicles.
6. Automakers.
7. Its audio systems and technologies are designed into vehicle models by automakers.
8. It combines proprietary spatial audio algorithms with integrated active noise control systems tuned for series-hybrid vehicle architectures.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Amazon, Texas Instruments, Klipsch, Nissan, Elliot Scheiner, and the Wireless Power Consortium.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded consumer electronics company, set to be rebranded as an independent entity.
Business model: Tier 1 automotive system sales and supplier contracts with automakers.
Scale and maturity: A long-established automotive supplier with partnerships spanning over 20 years.
Geography: Based in Japan and supplies automakers globally.
Beyond audio: It develops automotive multimedia, infotainment, and wireless charging technologies alongside audio.

points.name: Silentium
points.description: Israeli company developing active noise cancellation technology for automotive cabins.
points.bullets:
An audio software company that develops active noise cancellation and active sound management software, licensing it to automotive manufacturers and other industries to reduce unwanted noise and shape cabin acoustics.
1. An audio software developer whose active noise cancellation algorithms run on DSP cores and audio processors embedded in customers' automotive and industrial platforms.
2. Active noise control and road noise cancellation algorithms that generate anti-noise signals to attenuate unwanted sound in real time.
3. Active road noise cancellation, in-cabin noise reduction up to 1 kHz, personalized quiet zones, and active sound management for mechanical and industrial equipment.
4. Software and algorithms licensed for integration into audio voice processors, DSP platforms, and finished hardware cabinets.
5. Vehicle cabins, server and networking equipment racks, home appliances, and HVAC systems.
6. Automotive OEMs, semiconductor and audio processor companies, and industrial equipment manufacturers.
7. Its software is ported and integrated by DSP and chip vendors onto their platforms, which are then designed into vehicles by automakers.
8. It creates localized personalized quiet zones around individual occupants using active road noise cancellation rather than whole-cabin broadband suppression alone.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its software is integrated with Cadence Tensilica HiFi DSPs and AKM audio voice processors, and it is developing integrations with SonicEdge ultrasonic speaker arrays.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licensing and per-unit royalties.
Scale and maturity: An established company with multiple commercialized active noise control product lines.
Geography: Based in Israel, serving global automotive and industrial markets.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on active noise cancellation and sound management technology.

points.name: JL Audio
points.description: US audio manufacturer building subwoofers, speakers, and amplifiers for car and marine audio systems.
points.bullets:
A maker of finished audio equipment that designs, manufactures and sells car and marine speakers, subwoofers, amplifiers and signal processors for consumers and installers.
1. A consumer and car audio equipment maker that builds speakers, subwoofers and amplifiers sold as finished physical hardware for vehicles and boats.
2. The core technology consists of loudspeaker driver design using Dynamic Motor Analysis, voice-coil and elevated-frame cooling thermal management, and integrated digital signal processing built into amplifiers.
3. The equipment delivers high-fidelity bass reproduction, multi-channel sound amplification, signal conversion and digital signal processing for vehicle and marine sound systems.
4. Customers get the products as finished hardware, including vehicle-specific subwoofer enclosures, loaded subwoofer boxes, standalone speakers, amplifier chassis and wiring kits.
5. The products are used in cars, trucks, boats and marine vessels for aftermarket audio system upgrades and installations.
6. The company sells to consumers, vehicle owners, aftermarket car audio retailers and professional installers.
7. Its finished hardware products are retailed by car audio and consumer electronics dealers to end users for vehicle installation.
8. The company's approach is distinguished by vehicle-specific subwoofer enclosures engineered for fit and sound in specific vehicles alongside a focus on low-distortion, high-output bass.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization operates as a subsidiary brand of Garmin, with its products retailed by consumer electronics dealers.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand of a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: The company makes money through the sale of finished audio hardware products.
Scale and maturity: The company has 201 to 500 employees and a long history as an established loudspeaker manufacturer.
Geography: The organization is based in the United States and operates domestically.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio hardware.

points.name: Kenwood Corporation
points.description: Japanese manufacturer building car audio systems and communications equipment.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of car audio systems, wireless communication systems, and high-end audio equipment for consumer, professional, and industrial markets.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware products sold to consumers and professionals.
2. The company's products incorporate digital-to-analog conversion circuitry and wireless radio transmission technology.
3. The organization delivers in-car audio playback, high-resolution digital-to-analog audio conversion, and wireless audio communication.
4. Customers get the company's offerings as finished hardware products.
5. The products are used in cars, professional audio settings, and communication environments.
6. The company sells to consumers and professionals.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly into the consumer retail and professional equipment markets.
8. The organization provides a uniquely integrated portfolio combining automotive audio electronics with professional wireless communication systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company is a subsidiary brand of JVCKenwood.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand of a publicly traded electronics company.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: The company is an established, long-standing electronics brand that merged with another major electronics manufacturer in 2008.
Geography: The company is based in Japan and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The organization also provides wireless communication systems for various industries.

points.name: Continental
points.description: German automotive technology company developing speaker-free sound systems and voice assistants for vehicles.
points.bullets:
An automotive technology supplier that develops and manufactures speaker-free automotive sound systems and in-vehicle voice assistants for automakers.
1. An automotive technology company that builds exciter-based audio systems and in-vehicle voice assistants, sold as finished components integrated into vehicles.
2. The sound system uses actuators to excite vehicle surfaces such as the A-pillar, door trim and roof lining to create sound, and the voice assistant uses a hybrid AI solution for data processing.
3. The systems deliver surface-excited audio reproduction and conversational voice command processing for vehicle functions like navigation and climate control.
4. The products are sold as finished hardware systems and software integrated into vehicle platforms.
5. The products are used in cars and vehicle interiors.
6. The company sells to automakers and automotive manufacturers.
7. Its systems and assistants are designed into vehicles by automotive brands.
8. Its approach replaces traditional loudspeakers by exciting the vehicle's interior surfaces to produce sound.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partnered with Infineon Technologies on server-based automotive architectures and collaborated with Sennheiser for 3D AMBEO software.
Organization type: The organization is an automotive technology company and supplier.
Business model: The company makes money through the supply of automotive components and systems to vehicle manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: It is a top manufacturer in the global automotive audio market.
Geography: The company is based in Germany.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, it develops broader automotive technologies including server-based automotive architectures, high-performance processors and zone control units.

points.name: RTW
points.description: German pro audio company building visual meters and monitoring devices to measure audio loudness for production.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds hardware meters and software plug-ins for measuring audio loudness and levels, used by audio professionals to ensure content meets international delivery standards.
1. An equipment maker and software developer that builds hardware loudness meters and software plug-ins that run on dedicated hardware units and Windows and Mac OS workstations.
2. Digital signal processing and visual display systems that analyze and depict audio levels, loudness, and vectorscope data according to international broadcast standards.
3. Loudness measurement, audio level metering, vectorscope display, real-time analysis, mono-to-7.1 channel measurement, and compliance with EBU R128 and ITU-R BS.1770 standards.
4. Finished hardware devices and software plug-ins.
5. Broadcast control rooms, television and radio studios, post-production facilities, and professional mastering environments.
6. Audio professionals, broadcasters, and post-production studios.
7. Its hardware units and software plug-ins are used by audio professionals to measure and monitor audio signals during production, mastering, and broadcast delivery.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales and software licenses.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1965, established as a long-standing specialist in audio metering.
Geography: Based in Germany, operating worldwide.

points.name: D&R
points.description: Danish manufacturer building audio mixing consoles for radio broadcast studios.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures analog audio mixing consoles for radio broadcast, providing small-format mixers for small and medium studios.
1. An equipment maker that builds analog radio broadcast mixing consoles sold as finished rack-mounted hardware.
2. The mixers use analog signal processing and low-noise circuitry with built-in telephone hybrid, USB, and Bluetooth connectivity.
3. The consoles deliver multi-channel audio mixing, microphone input routing, telephone line integration, and USB send and return for broadcast production.
4. Customers get the products as finished hardware units.
5. The mixing consoles are used in radio broadcast studios and production booths.
6. The organization sells to broadcast studios, radio stations, and production DJs.
7. Its finished hardware is installed directly into radio broadcast facilities.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held manufacturing company.
Business model: The organization makes money through hardware sales of mixing consoles.
Geography: The organization is based in Denmark.

points.name: ITU-R
points.description: Geneva-based standards organization publishing the BS.1770 loudness measurement algorithm used across broadcast audio production.
points.bullets:
A standards organization that develops recommendations and standards for radiocommunication, including audio broadcasting. It defines algorithms for measuring audio program loudness and true-peak audio level, and specifies file formats for the international exchange of audio programme materials with metadata.
1. A standards body that publishes recommendation documents specifying algorithms and file formats.
2. The core technology is a standardized algorithm that measures audio program loudness in LUFS and true-peak audio level.
3. It delivers standardized loudness measurement, true-peak detection, and metadata exchange for audio programs.
4. Customers get it through published recommendation documents and standards.
5. The standards are used in television broadcasting, audio production, and international audio program exchange.
6. Broadcasters, audio equipment manufacturers, and production facilities adopt the standards.
7. Its standards are implemented by audio equipment and software vendors into their loudness meters and broadcast systems.
8. It provides internationally agreed, formally standardized algorithms and formats rather than commercial products.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a sector of the International Telecommunication Union.
Organization type: A standards body and specialized agency of the United Nations.
Business model: It operates through international treaty agreements and publishes standards.
Scale and maturity: A long-established global organization with a broad scope of radiocommunication oversight.
Geography: It is based in Geneva, Switzerland, and operates internationally.
Beyond audio: It develops standards and recommendations for all radiocommunication, including television broadcasting and spectrum management, beyond audio.

points.name: EBU
points.description: Geneva-based standards organization issuing loudness recommendations for European broadcast and online audio delivery.
points.bullets:
A standards organization that develops and publishes technical recommendations and specifications for audio loudness normalization, metering and IP-based audio contribution, primarily for the European broadcasting industry.
1. A standards body that publishes technical recommendations, specifications and measurement methodologies adopted by broadcasters and implemented in their equipment and workflows.
2. Loudness normalization algorithms and measurement methodologies based on LUFS and true-peak limiting, alongside interoperability standards for audio contribution over IP networks.
3. Loudness normalization targeting specific LUFS levels and true-peak ceilings, standardized loudness metering, and interoperability for audio contribution over IP equipment.
4. Published technical recommendations, specifications and methodologies available to broadcasters and equipment manufacturers.
5. Television and radio broadcast, online audio delivery and audio contribution over IP networks.
6. Broadcasters, media organizations and equipment manufacturers.
7. Its specifications are implemented by equipment manufacturers and enforced by broadcasters in their production and delivery workflows.
8. Its loudness recommendations have been adopted as law in multiple countries, establishing a mandatory regulatory framework for audio normalization.
points.profile:
Organization type: A standards organization and professional association of broadcasters.
Geography: Based in Geneva, Switzerland, focusing on the European broadcasting sector.
Beyond audio: It is a broadcasting union that addresses broader media production, distribution, technology and legal affairs beyond audio.

points.name: SoundBridge
points.description: Software company developing a digital audio workstation for music production, scoring, and remote sound collaboration.
points.bullets:
A software company that develops a digital audio workstation (DAW) providing high-fidelity audio processing, zero-latency remote tracking, and loudness-aware workflows for music producers and engineers.
1. A software developer whose digital audio workstation runs as a software product installed on users' computers.
2. A digital audio workstation engine featuring sample-accurate latency compensation, high-fidelity audio processing up to 192kHz, and zero-latency remote tracking technology.
3. Multitrack audio and MIDI recording, editing, and mixing, integrated video scoring, advanced tempo editing, and real-time collaborative loudness-corrected mix review with talkback.
4. The software is delivered as free and premium digital audio workstation software products downloaded by users.
5. The software is used in music production, sound design, audio scoring, and remote mixing collaboration workflows.
6. The software is sold to music producers, audio engineers, and sound designers.
7. Its software is installed directly by end-users as their primary digital audio workstation environment.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a software company.
Business model: It makes money through software sales, offering a free base version and charging for a premium version that unlocks unlimited tracks, advanced MIDI editing, and video scoring features.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is on its digital audio workstation and audio production software.

points.name: Orban
points.description: US audio processing manufacturer building broadcast processors and loudness meters for radio and streaming.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that develops and manufactures audio processing hardware and software for radio, television and streaming broadcasters.
1. An equipment maker that designs and builds professional audio processors and loudness meters sold as finished rack-mount hardware.
2. Digital signal processing hardware running multiband compression, peak limiting, stereo enhancement, automatic gain control, multiplex power control and loudness measurement algorithms.
3. Multiband audio compression, peak limiting, stereo enhancement, automatic gain control, multiplex power control, loudness measurement and control, and stereo encoding.
4. Finished rack-mount hardware products, software processors and optional IP signal transmission features.
5. AM, FM, digital radio, HD Radio, DAB+, digital television, Internet streaming and broadcast studios.
6. Radio broadcasters, television broadcasters, telecommunications operators and streaming providers.
7. Its finished hardware is installed in broadcast transmission chains and studios by broadcasters.
8. Multiband limiting and processing algorithms designed for broadcast transmission quality, modulation density and coverage, backed by a five-year warranty.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Owned by DaySequerra, with products distributed by Sonifex and compatible with iBiquity HD Radio systems.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of DaySequerra.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: Established over 50 years ago with engineering teams in the United States and Germany.
Geography: Based in Pennsauken, New Jersey; San Francisco, California; and Ludwigsburg, Germany, operating globally through a network of local distributors.
Beyond audio: Broadcast audio processing is its entire focus.

points.name: Telos Alliance
points.description: US broadcast audio technology company making IP-audio, telephony, and audio processing equipment for radio and television studios.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that develops and manufactures broadcast audio processing, mixing, IP intercom, and Audio-over-IP networking solutions for radio, television, and streaming facilities.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished hardware products, software-based processors, and network interfaces, sold as rack-mount units, physical panels, and virtualized software running on standard servers.
2. Audio-over-IP networking protocols, FFT-based clipping algorithms, multiband audio processing, and VoIP codecs operating across Ethernet networks and cloud platforms.
3. Audio-over-IP transport, network routing, loudness control, stereo-to-surround upmixing and downmixing, FFT clipping, broadcast mixing, IP intercom, audio watermarking, and VoIP integration.
4. Finished hardware products, software-based processors, virtualized cloud platforms, Windows audio drivers, and published networking protocols.
5. Television broadcast facilities, radio studios, streaming environments, live production remote broadcasts, and on-demand content facilities.
6. Broadcasters, television networks, radio stations, streaming providers, and live production professionals.
7. Its equipment is installed directly into broadcast facilities by network operators and integration engineers.
8. It developed and maintains the Livewire+ AoIP protocol alongside its founding role in establishing the AES67 standard.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Syndicate of Sounds, Telestream, Jünger Audio, the Media Networking Alliance, and the X.192 group.
Organization type: A privately held company operating as a parent organization to multiple audio technology brands.
Business model: Hardware sales, software licenses, service-level agreements, and professional consulting services.
Scale and maturity: An established organization with 51-200 employees that has operated for more than three decades.
Geography: Based in Cleveland, Ohio, USA, with global distribution and support operations.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses exclusively on audio technology for broadcast, production, and streaming applications.

points.name: Total Sonics
points.description: Boston-based business unit developing DSP audio enhancement software to optimize sound in home consumer electronics.
points.bullets:
A developer of audio enhancement software that provides a suite of DSP algorithms for optimizing electroacoustic response, extending bass, and rendering spatial audio for consumer electronics manufacturers.
1. An audio software developer whose DSP algorithms and calibration tools run on consumer audio devices and users' phones.
2. Dynamic equalization, psychoacoustic bass extension, compression, and universal height rendering algorithms.
3. Bass extension, loudness control, sound field expansion, dialog clarity enhancement, and automated acoustic calibration.
4. Licensed software suites and algorithms.
5. Consumer home audio devices and televisions.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers.
7. Its software is integrated into audio devices by consumer electronics brands.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A business unit of THAT Corporation and an implementer of technology from Psy(x) Research.
Organization type: A business unit of a publicly traded semiconductor and IP company.
Business model: Software licenses.
Geography: Based in Boston, USA.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio enhancement technology.

points.name: THAT Corporation
points.description: US semiconductor company designing high-performance audio integrated circuits for professional audio equipment.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that designs and manufactures high-performance audio integrated circuits and licenses audio processing technology for professional audio applications. It develops analog and mixed-signal ICs such as phase-locked loop clock cleaners and programmable microphone preamplifiers, alongside licensing audio enhancement algorithms. The organization serves professional audio equipment manufacturers and broadcast audio providers.
1. A semiconductor company that designs high-performance audio integrated circuits, sold as packaged chips that run in professional audio equipment.
2. The core technology comprises analog integrated circuits, including phase-locked loops for audio clock cleanup and low-noise, digitally controlled microphone preamplifiers.
3. The specific audio capabilities it delivers are audio clock jitter reduction and low-noise microphone signal amplification.
4. Customers get its technology as packaged semiconductor chips and through licensed audio processing algorithms.
5. The products it makes are used in professional audio equipment, broadcast television audio, and studio recording gear.
6. The organization sells to professional audio equipment manufacturers and broadcast audio providers.
7. Its integrated circuits are designed into professional audio hardware by equipment manufacturers.
8. Its approach is distinguished by a focus on high-performance analog signal processing integrated circuits specifically engineered for low noise and low jitter in professional audio signal chains.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A notable partner is a distributor appointed to sell its integrated circuits in Japan, and it operates a business unit formerly part of a noise reduction technology company.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held semiconductor company.
Business model: It makes money through semiconductor chip sales and technology licensing.
Scale and maturity: The company was spun off in 1989 and operates as an established provider in the professional audio semiconductor market.
Geography: It is based in the USA and operates internationally, including distribution channels in Japan.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio integrated circuits and related licensing.

points.name: dbx
points.description: US audio brand manufacturing signal processing equipment for live sound and studio applications.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds analog and digital signal processing hardware and personal monitor controllers for studios, live sound, and installed audio applications.
1. An equipment maker that builds professional audio signal processors, dynamics processors, equalizers, microphone preamps, and loudspeaker management systems, sold as finished hardware in studio and live sound racks.
2. Analog circuitry and digital signal processing running in standalone hardware units and 500-series module formats.
3. Dynamic range compression and limiting, expansion and gating, equalization, de-essing, subharmonic synthesis, loudspeaker management, and personal monitor mixing.
4. Finished hardware units, rack-mounted processors, modular 500-series hardware, and companion control software and mobile apps.
5. Recording studios, live sound reinforcement, installed audio systems, and personal in-ear monitor setups.
6. Studios and musicians, live sound engineers, installers, and audio professionals.
7. Its finished hardware is deployed directly in professional audio chains and integrated into networked audio systems within its parent company's broader ecosystem.
8. It delivers analog and digital signal processing hardware with proprietary dynamics algorithms and deep parameter control in both standalone and modular formats.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: HARMAN International Industries, AKG, and BSS.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of HARMAN Professional Solutions.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio equipment and processors.
Scale and maturity: A long-established brand operating as a division within a large publicly traded parent company.
Geography: Based in the USA and operates globally through the professional audio market.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio company focused entirely on professional audio signal processing and monitoring.

points.name: Audiokinetic
points.description: Canadian software company developing interactive audio tools for video games.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds and licenses audio middleware for interactive media and gaming, providing a runtime mixing engine, state logic, spatial audio, and plug-ins to game developers.
1. A developer tools company whose interactive audio middleware runs as licensed software integrated into game engines on developers' workstations and target game platforms.
2. A runtime audio mixing engine that manages interactive audio states, switches, and real-time spatial acoustic modeling including diffraction and reflection simulation.
3. Adaptive audio, 3D spatial audio, interactive music sequencing, real-time room modeling, footstep sound randomization, and native haptic support.
4. Licensed software middleware, plug-ins, sample projects, and integration SDKs for game engines.
5. Video games, interactive media, and other real-time interactive applications.
6. Game development studios, independent game developers, and audio professionals.
7. Its middleware is licensed by game developers and integrated into their game projects alongside other engine components.
8. Advanced state management for complex audio behaviors and an advanced interactive music engine distinguish its middleware from competing audio tools.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates with game engines and audio workstations including Unity, Nuendo, and Resonance Audio, and collaborated with Sony AI and CRAS.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses, including free licenses for independent developers and commercial licenses for larger studios.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2006 and widely established as a standard audio middleware in AAA game development.
Geography: Based in Montreal, Quebec, Canada.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on interactive audio middleware and tools.

points.name: Cockos
points.description: Software company developing digital audio workstations for recording and mixing audio tracks.
points.bullets:
A software developer that builds a digital audio workstation for recording, editing, processing, and mixing audio and MIDI tracks for audio engineers, producers, and musicians.
1. A software developer whose digital audio workstation runs as a desktop application on customer computers.
2. A multitrack audio and MIDI processing engine with real-time pitch shifting, time-stretching, and support for third-party plugins and virtual instruments.
3. Multitrack audio recording, non-destructive editing, real-time pitch shifting, time-stretching, and audio mixing.
4. The digital audio workstation is delivered as downloadable software products.
5. Studios, music production environments, and sound design workflows.
6. Independent artists, small to medium-sized music production studios, large studios, audio engineers, music producers, sound designers, and composers.
7. Its software is used directly by end-users to record, edit, and mix audio projects.
8. A highly customizable, cross-platform digital audio workstation offered at a lower price point than industry-standard alternatives.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses sold through a one-time payment structure with tiered personal and commercial pricing.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on digital audio workstation software.

points.name: Pro Sound Effects
points.description: Sound library company providing vast rights-cleared audio assets and desktop software for searching and managing sound effects in audio production.
points.bullets:
A professional audio software and content provider that supplies rights-cleared sound effects libraries and asset management software for audio post-production and music production. It builds a desktop application for indexing, organizing, and searching local audio files, paired with a large catalog of tagged, high-quality audio recordings. It serves sound designers, sound artists, and producers who need to source and manage audio assets for creative workflows.
1. A software and content company whose asset management application and sound effects libraries run as desktop software on macOS.
2. A desktop audio asset manager featuring keyword and predictive search algorithms that index and organize local files up to 192kHz/32-bit across multiple formats, including drag-and-drop integration with major digital audio workstations.
3. Audio file indexing, keyword and predictive search, and drag-and-drop asset retrieval for sound design workflows.
4. Finished software products and digital sound effects libraries delivered as desktop applications and digital downloads.
5. Audio post-production studios, music production environments, and sound design workflows.
6. Sound designers, sound artists, and music producers.
7. Its sound libraries and software are used directly by audio professionals to source and manage assets within their digital audio workstations.
8. It differentiates itself from other library managers by combining a perpetual software license model with a bundled, rights-cleared sound library and external database connectivity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates with major editing software including Pro Tools, Logic, and Premiere, and connects to external databases like Freesound.org.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses and sound library sales, including perpetual licenses and pay-for-what-you-need content access.
Geography: Operates within the professional audio post-production and music production markets.

points.name: iZotope
points.description: US software company developing AI-assisted audio plug-ins for mixing, mastering, and noise reduction.
points.bullets:
An AI model and software developer that builds audio repair, mixing, mastering, and stem separation software, sold as plug-ins and standalone applications for audio engineers, editors, and sound designers.
1. An AI model and software developer whose audio processing models and plug-ins run on-device on users' macOS and Windows desktop and laptop computers, utilizing local CPU and GPU resources.
2. Digital signal processing combined with machine learning and neural networks operating within standalone spectral editors and host-embedded plug-in architectures.
3. Noise reduction, dialogue isolation, stem separation, dereverberation, breath control, de-bleeding, vocal processing, mixing assistance, and automated mastering.
4. Software products delivered as downloadable standalone applications and standard audio plug-ins for digital audio workstations.
5. Recording, post-production, broadcast, film, podcast, and music production studios.
6. Audio engineers, editors, sound designers, musicians, and post-production professionals.
7. Its plug-ins are integrated into digital audio workstations by end-users to execute audio processing tasks within their production workflows.
8. It integrates deep spectral editing with custom-trained machine learning models for targeted audio repair and automated, source-aware mixing and mastering decisions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Boris FX, Native Instruments, inMusic, Francisco Partners, Blue Microphones, and JUCE.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand operating under a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: Software licenses, perpetual product sales, subscription services, and certification programs.
Scale and maturity: A mature organization founded in 2001 with roughly 200 employees.
Geography: Based in Boston, Massachusetts, USA, selling its products globally.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on audio processing, repair, and production software.

points.name: Sound Particles
points.description: Portuguese software company creating CGI-like spatial audio tools for post-production sound design.
points.bullets:
A developer of professional audio software that builds spatial audio generation and sound design tools for post-production, film, television, games, and music production. The company creates native 3D audio software and spatial synthesizers that let users generate and manipulate thousands of simultaneous sounds in a virtual space using object-based audio and personalized binaural monitoring.
1. A software developer whose spatial audio tools run as desktop applications on users' computers.
2. CGI-like audio software using particle-based sound generation in 3D virtual spaces, integrating Higher Order Ambisonics, object-based audio rendering, and a spatial audio synthesis engine with MIDI-controlled spatial panning.
3. Spatial audio generation, particle-based sound design, binaural monitoring, Higher Order Ambisonics encoding, Dolby Atmos support, ADM object exporting, and spatial sound synthesis.
4. The software is delivered as perpetual software licenses for professional and enterprise tiers.
5. Post-production workflows for cinema, television, games, VR, and music production.
6. Studios, sound designers, mixing engineers, musicians, and producers.
7. Its software is used by audio post-production professionals in major film and television studios to create spatial soundscapes and object-based mixes.
8. It combines particle-based spatial audio generation with native spatial sound synthesis, allowing per-note spatial panning directly inside a synthesizer rather than relying on external 3D panners.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its software has been used in productions including Dune, Oppenheimer, Star Wars 9, Game of Thrones, Stranger Things, and Frozen 2, and it has raised seed funding from Indico Capital Partners and 200M.
Organization type: A privately held software company.
Business model: The company makes money through perpetual software license sales across professional and enterprise tiers.
Scale and maturity: A seed-stage company that has raised $4.2 million in funding.
Geography: The company is based in Portugal and operates in the professional audio post-production market.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is on spatial audio software for professional sound design and music production.

points.name: Stability AI
points.description: UK AI company developing generative audio models and licensing them via API and open-weight releases.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds open-weight generative audio models and a cloud API for creating music, sound effects, and production elements, trained on licensed and Creative Commons recordings for enterprise and individual creators.
1. An AI model developer whose audio generation models are sold as open-weight models running on-device on consumer hardware and mobile chips, and as cloud models accessed behind an API.
2. Continuous-latent diffusion models, variational autoencoders, and text encoders that generate audio from text prompts.
3. Text-to-audio generation, music generation, sound effects generation, audio style transfer, latent space watermark embedding, and custom model fine-tuning.
4. Open-weight models distributed on model hubs, cloud APIs, and a software plugin for digital audio workstations.
5. Music production workflows, post-production, mobile devices, and enterprise media generation.
6. Music professionals, developers, enterprises, and consumer hardware users.
7. Its models are integrated by enterprises and developers into their own products, and its plugins are used directly by music professionals in production workflows.
8. It provides open-weight generative audio models trained on licensed and Creative Commons datasets, with a focus on preventing copyright infringement using content recognition technology during training.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Amazon Web Services, Hugging Face, Google, Arm, AudioSparx, Freesound, Audible Magic, Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group, and Sony.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Enterprise licenses for commercial use, API usage fees, and subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: The company underwent restructuring in 2024 and has raised over $76 million in funding.
Geography: Based in London, United Kingdom.
Beyond audio: It is a multimodal generative AI company that also develops image, video, and 3D generation models.

points.name: JUCE
points.description: Software framework building cross-platform audio applications and plugins.
points.bullets:
