A developer tools company that provides an open-source C++ software framework used by developers to build audio plugins and applications for desktop and mobile operating systems.
1. A developer tools company whose platform engineers use to build cross-platform audio plugins and applications compiled into standard plugin formats that run in digital audio workstations.
2. A C++ application framework with classes for audio DSP, MIDI processing, and GUI development, featuring sample-accurate parameter automation, a clear separation between GUI and audio threads, and project management tools.
3. It enables the development of custom audio DSP, software synthesizers, MIDI processors like arpeggiators, noise gates, and multi-channel surround monitors.
4. It is provided as a software framework distributed under open-source and commercial licenses, including project configuration tools and educational courses.
5. It is used to build virtual studio instruments and effects that run in digital audio workstations on desktop and mobile devices.
6. It is used by audio software developers, amateur programmers, and music technology companies building plugins and audio applications.
7. Its framework is used by audio software companies to build commercial plugins and applications for end-users.
8. It allows a single codebase to be compiled across all major desktop and mobile operating systems and plugin formats, dominating audio plugin development over competing open-source frameworks.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is used by audio software companies including Arturia, Avid, iZotope, Valhalla DSP, UAD, and Antares, and co-hosts the Audio Developer Conference with PACE Anti-Piracy, Inc.
Organization type: It is a partially open-source software project and framework with commercial licensing options.
Business model: It makes money through commercial software licenses for the framework, with free educational and open-source GPL licensing options available.
Scale and maturity: It is an industry-standard framework with a free audio plugin development course offering 50 video lessons for beginners.
Geography: It operates globally as a software framework and digital product.
Beyond audio: It is entirely focused on audio software development frameworks and education.

points.name: Celemony
points.description: Software company developing pitch correction tools and audio editing plug-ins.
points.bullets:
A software company that develops pitch and time correction software for audio production, sold as standalone editors and DAW plug-ins. It also co-developed an audio plug-in API extension that allows tighter integration between its software and host digital audio workstations. Its tools are used by musicians, producers, and engineers for precise vocal and dialogue editing.
1. A software company whose pitch and time correction algorithms run as DAW plug-ins or standalone desktop applications.
2. Spectral tone-object editing algorithms that analyze audio and map pitch and timing changes to individual audio objects, combined with an audio plug-in API extension for DAW integration.
3. Monophonic and polyphonic pitch shifting, time stretching, sibilant adjustment, pitch analysis, and note-level audio object manipulation with minimal artifacts.
4. The software is delivered as licensed plug-ins and standalone editors, with lite versions bundled into third-party DAWs and audio interfaces.
5. The software is used in recording studios, post-production facilities, and home studios for vocal and dialogue editing.
6. The company sells to musicians, audio producers, and engineers, and licenses its technology to DAW developers.
7. Its software plug-ins are integrated into digital audio workstations by audio software vendors and bundled with audio interfaces by hardware manufacturers.
8. Its approach distinguishes itself through tone-object spectral editing that enables direct manipulation of individual notes within mixed audio while preserving audio fidelity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company developed its plug-in API extension with a major DAW developer, and its software is bundled or integrated by multiple digital audio workstation and hardware brands.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held software company.
Business model: The company makes money through software license sales of its plug-ins and standalone editors, and through licensing agreements for DAW integration.
Scale and maturity: The company is an established software vendor with multiple tiers of its core product widely bundled across the audio production industry.
Geography: The company is based in Germany and operates globally within the audio production market.
Beyond audio: The organization's focus is entirely on audio software and plug-in API development.

points.name: Brainworx
points.description: German software company developing audio plugins that emulate analog hardware.
points.bullets:
An audio software company that develops high-end software emulations of analog hardware in the form of plugins for professional users. The organization builds analog modeling processors used in professional recording, post-production, and live sound workflows.
1. An audio software developer whose analog modeling algorithms run as plugins in digital audio workstation software.
2. Software algorithms that digitally emulate the behavior and circuitry of analog audio hardware.
3. Analog hardware emulation, guitar amp emulation, and audio processing for mixing and mastering.
4. Audio plugins delivered as software products.
5. Recording, post-production, live sound, mixing, and mastering studios.
6. Creatives, audio engineers, and musicians worldwide.
7. Its plugins are integrated by professional users into digital audio workstation workflows.
8. It develops emulations of specific third-party analog hardware devices in direct cooperation with the original hardware manufacturers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: RCKFRC, SPL, Universal Audio, Plugin Alliance, and Native Instruments.
Organization type: A brand operating under a corporate audio group umbrella.
Business model: Sales of software plugins.
Scale and maturity: A professional audio brand founded over 20 years ago that has undergone multiple corporate acquisitions and re-acquisitions.
Geography: Based in Germany and serving creatives worldwide.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio software.

points.name: Google Cloud
points.description: US cloud provider powering text-to-speech and speech-to-text APIs.
points.bullets:
A cloud computing provider and AI model developer offering enterprise-grade speech recognition, text-to-speech, and generative audio services through cloud APIs, as well as on-device speech models for connected and offline environments.
1. A cloud computing and AI model developer whose speech and audio models run in the cloud behind APIs and on-device in customers' connected products.
2. Deep learning neural networks, large generative language models for audio synthesis, neural audio codecs, and transformer-based semantic and acoustic tokenization frameworks.
3. Speech-to-text recognition, text-to-speech synthesis, multi-speaker diarization, voice cloning, instant custom voice creation, high-definition voice generation, and audio content generation for speech and music.
4. Cloud APIs, managed machine learning platforms, on-device speech models, and conversational AI development tools.
5. Contact centers, in-vehicle infotainment systems, voice agents, audiobook narration, video voice-overs, and enterprise conversational platforms.
6. Enterprises, automakers, contact center operators, software developers, and cloud application developers.
7. Its cloud APIs and AI models are integrated by enterprises into their customer experience platforms and conversational applications.
8. It leverages proprietary foundational audio research from its in-house AI division to power a vertically integrated stack of cloud and on-device speech services.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Toyota, Mercedes-Benz, The Home Depot, Zoom, ElevenLabs, Resemble AI, and Symphony.
Organization type: A subsidiary cloud computing division of a publicly traded technology conglomerate.
Business model: Cloud computing usage fees, API billing based on processing time or character count, and enterprise platform subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A large-scale global infrastructure provider processing over one billion minutes of speech per month.
Geography: Based in the United States and operating globally.
Beyond audio: The organization provides a comprehensive suite of cloud computing services, machine learning platforms, and generative AI tools spanning text, video, image, and data analytics, with audio being one component of its broader enterprise ecosystem.

points.name: Deepgram
points.description: US speech AI company developing voice recognition and text-to-speech models.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and audio intelligence models, offering them through cloud and on-premises APIs to enterprises and developers building real-time voice applications.
1. An AI model developer whose speech and audio intelligence models run primarily in the cloud behind APIs, with options for on-premises and on-device deployment.
2. Deep learning models purpose-built for speech recognition and synthesis, optimized for low-latency streaming and capable of running on neural processing units at the edge.
3. The company delivers speech recognition, speaker diarization, text-to-speech, semantic end-of-turn detection, and spoken language understanding including summarization, sentiment analysis, intent recognition, and topic detection.
4. Customers access the models through cloud APIs, WebSocket endpoints, software development kits, and single-tenant private infrastructure.
5. The models are used in contact centers, voice agent pipelines, restaurant ordering systems, telephony transcription, and space-to-ground communications.
6. The organization sells to enterprises, developers, contact-center operators, healthcare applications, and restaurant chains.
7. Its models are integrated into enterprise voice platforms and cascading voice-agent pipelines as modular speech components.
8. The company focuses on low-latency, high-accuracy speech models trained from scratch specifically for real-time voice agents rather than general-purpose large language models.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company has partnerships with Qualcomm, Cloudflare, IBM, Together AI, and various voice-agent framework platforms, with backing from investors including Nvidia, Tiger Global, and Y Combinator.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: It makes money through per-minute API usage billing for streaming and batch transcription, per-character billing for text-to-speech, and subscriptions for dedicated infrastructure.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, the company has raised over $200 million at a $1.3 billion valuation and processes billions of minutes of audio annually for over 200,000 developers.
Geography: The company is based in San Francisco, California, and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on voice artificial intelligence.

points.name: Soniox

points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and voice cloning models, along with a speech-centric language model, providing a complete infrastructure platform for real-time voice applications accessible via cloud APIs for developers and enterprises.
1. An AI model developer whose speech and language models run in the cloud behind APIs and integrate with real-time voice-agent frameworks.
2. Large generative speech models and large language models running in the cloud, featuring proprietary codecs and inference infrastructure.
3. Multilingual speech-to-text transcription with structured output, real-time and async speech recognition, expressive text-to-speech, voice cloning from short reference recordings, and audio understanding.
4. Cloud APIs, regional sovereign cloud deployments, and a consumer mobile application.
5. Real-time voice agents, live voice interactions, and general speech-to-text workflows.
6. Developers, enterprises, and media publications.
7. Its models are accessed by developers directly through APIs and integrated into real-time voice-agent frameworks.
8. It owns the entire infrastructure stack encompassing the model, codec, and inference, offering high-accuracy multilingual speech models at a low cost per hour.

Key partners and customers: Integrates with Pipecat and LiveKit, participates in VapiCon 2026, and is used by audioXpress.

points.name: Speechmatics

An AI model developer whose speech-to-text models run in the cloud, on-premises and on-device for media, broadcast, healthcare, contact center and enterprise organizations.

3. The models deliver real-time and batch speech-to-text transcription, speaker diarization, translation and custom dictionaries across 55+ languages.
4. Customers get the technology through a cloud API, on-premises software, an on-device C/C++ library and SaaS.
5. The technology is used in media production pipelines, live broadcast captioning, subtitle generation, content indexing, contact centers and healthcare applications.
6. The company sells to technology providers, media broadcasters, healthcare companies, contact centers and enterprises.
7. Its models are integrated by technology providers into their software platforms and enterprise workflows.
8. Specialized language packs and domain-specific tuning provide high accuracy on regional accents and industry-specific technical terminology.

points.name: Kaldi

2. A traditional multi-stage pipeline implemented in C++ that uses feature extraction, acoustic modeling, language modeling, and decoding to process speech.
3. Streaming speech-to-text transcription using specialized models trained for specific tasks.
4. An open-source C++ toolkit with modular building blocks.
5. Research environments and custom automatic speech recognition systems.
6. Speech researchers and machine learning engineers.
7. Its toolkit is used by engineers and researchers to construct their own speech recognition systems.
8. It provides total control over every component of the recognition pipeline rather than a fully capable pre-trained model.
points.profile:
Organization type: An open-source project.
Business model: Free open-source software released under a permissive license.
Beyond audio: The project's entire focus is speech recognition.

points.name: xAI

An AI model developer whose speech-to-speech, speech-to-text and text-to-speech models run in the cloud behind APIs. It builds large generative voice models and transcription models, alongside a no-code platform for building voice agents, for developers and enterprises.

5. In-car voice assistants, customer service call centers and developer-built voice applications.
6. Automakers, enterprises operating call centers, and software developers building voice applications.
7. Its models are accessed by developers through cloud APIs and integrated into enterprise call centers and vehicle infotainment systems.

points.name: Bland AI

An AI model and platform developer that provides a developer-centric voice platform automating inbound and outbound phone calls using human-sounding conversational agents for enterprises.

8. The platform distinguishes itself with massive concurrency capacity supporting thousands of simultaneous calls and deep programmability for complex, branched conversation logic.

Key partners and customers: Integrates with telephony and contact center platforms including Twilio, Genesys, and NICE, alongside SIP providers.

Scale and maturity: Operates with multiple service tiers and enterprise-level infrastructure, positioning itself against direct competitors in the conversational AI space.
Geography: Operates within the cloud telephony and AI software markets.

A cloud-based AI model and software developer that provides a no-code platform for enterprises to build, deploy, and manage conversational voice agents for automated phone calls.

An AI model developer that builds a cloud-based software platform for deploying natural-sounding AI voice agents for automated telephony, enabling businesses to manage real-time conversational interactions.

points.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS)

A cloud platform provider that offers cloud-based speech synthesis and conversational AI services, providing text-to-speech engines and voice chatbot development tools for developers and enterprises.

5. Telephony interactive voice response systems, cloud-based contact centers, e-learning platforms, accessibility tools, IoT devices, and healthcare applications.
6. Developers and enterprises, including those in highly regulated sectors like healthcare and government.

8. It offers a tiered portfolio of text-to-speech synthesis engines ranging from concatenative to billion-parameter transformer models, billed per million characters with generous free tiers.

4. Software platforms integrated into automotive systems and deployed for enterprise contact centers.
5. Cars and enterprise call centers in the banking, financial services, and insurance sector.
6. Automakers and enterprises, specifically domestic and international automotive original equipment manufacturers and financial institutions.
7. Its voice platforms are deployed directly into vehicles by automakers and into contact center operations by financial enterprises.
8. The software is tuned to overcome high-noise acoustic environments and recognize regional dialects and vernacular languages, enabling on-device processing that eliminates recurring cloud infrastructure costs and ensures data sovereignty.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Tata Motors, Qualcomm Technologies, Canara HSBC Life Insurance, Angel One, and Kissht.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Software deployments and enterprise licensing.
Scale and maturity: A scaling company with a recent funding round and projections for a fivefold revenue increase to ₹200 crore.
Geography: Based in India and expanding internationally to include UK, US, Spanish, and Portuguese language markets.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on voice AI and audio processing technology.

points.name: Picovoice
points.description: Canadian software company building on-device voice AI platforms for speech recognition and noise suppression.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and platform company that provides a web-based console and SDKs for building custom voice features, offering on-device speech-to-text, noise suppression, speaker recognition, and wake word detection for developers.
1. An AI model and software developer whose voice engines run on-device across embedded, mobile, web, desktop, and server platforms, delivered as SDKs.
2. Neural networks and digital signal processing algorithms running entirely on-device for real-time, low-latency audio analysis.
3. Wake word detection, speech-to-intent, speech-to-text transcription, noise suppression, speaker recognition, voice activity detection, and speaker diarization.
4. Software development kits and a web-based console for training custom models.
5. Voice-enabled hardware and software products using microphone arrays, such as those built with multi-mic array hardware.
6. Developers and enterprises building custom voice products.
7. Its SDKs are integrated by developers directly into their hardware and software products.
8. It processes audio entirely on-device with no cloud dependency, using memory-efficient algorithms that prioritize low-latency and privacy compliance.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Seeed Studio
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2018.
Geography: Based in Vancouver, Canada.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is voice artificial intelligence technology.

points.name: Cleer
points.description: Americas audio brand building smart headphones and camera-equipped earbuds.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs and markets true wireless open-ear earbuds, over-ear headphones, and smart speakers, incorporating spatial audio, active noise cancellation, and high-resolution wireless audio technologies for consumers.
1. A consumer electronics manufacturer that builds finished audio hardware and companion mobile software, sold as retail wearables running on embedded audio platforms.
2. Acoustic transducers and dynamic drivers integrated with wireless Bluetooth chipsets, spatial rendering algorithms, active noise reduction, and multimodal sensory processing.
3. High-resolution audio playback, spatial audio with head tracking, active noise cancellation, voice call noise reduction, sound personalization, and contextual awareness using integrated cameras.
4. Finished hardware products and companion mobile applications.
5. Consumer earbuds, over-ear headphones, and smart speakers.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products incorporate licensed algorithms and semiconductor platforms from chip vendors, and are sold directly to consumers.
8. Focuses on open-ear wearable designs integrating high-resolution audio, spatial sound certification, and emerging multimodal visual and audio context processing into consumer earbuds.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Operates as a concept collaborator and software ecosystem partner with Qualcomm, integrates sound personalization from Mimi, and holds spatial audio certification from THX and Dolby.
Organization type: A consumer audio brand operating under parent company Shenzhen Grandsun Electronic.
Business model: Hardware sales of consumer audio devices.
Scale and maturity: A specialty audio brand managing a range of consumer headphones and earbuds across global markets.
Geography: Based in the Americas and operates in global consumer electronics markets.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio products and wearable listening experiences.

points.name: Doppler Labs
points.description: US startup developing wireless earbuds that let users customize ambient sound in real time.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that developed wireless earbuds for consumers, enabling real-time customization of ambient sound using onboard microphones, a codec, and a companion smartphone app.
1. An equipment maker that builds wireless hearable hardware, sold as finished consumer earbuds, running its audio processing onboard the devices.
2. A microphone and codec processing audio with a latency of 30-millionths of a second, paired with a smartphone application for user control.
3. Real-time ambient sound customization, five-band equalization, and audio effects including reverb, flange, delay, and fuzz.
4. Finished consumer hardware earbuds controlled through a companion software application.
5. Consumer wireless earbuds.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished hardware was sold directly to consumers.
8. Its earbuds allowed users to actively modify and effects-process ambient environmental sound in real-time rather than solely playing back audio or passively isolating noise.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Live Nation Entertainment and Universal Music Group invested in its Series B funding round.
Organization type: A privately held startup that ultimately shuttered.
Business model: Hardware sales of consumer earbuds.
Scale and maturity: A funded startup that launched a flagship product in 2016 and subsequently ceased operations.
Geography: Based and operated in the United States.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus was on audio technology and hearable devices.

points.name: Elehear
points.description: US hearing aid manufacturer developing AI-powered over-the-counter hearing aids with real-time translation and tinnitus relief.
points.bullets:
A maker of over-the-counter hearing aids that develops proprietary audio algorithms and embedded chips and sells finished medical-grade wearable devices direct to consumers.
1. An equipment maker that designs its own hearing aid chips and algorithms and sells them as finished wearable devices running on-device.
2. Deep learning and computational auditory scene analysis algorithms running on a proprietary embedded chip for ultra-low latency sound processing.
3. Noise reduction, speech extraction, feedback cancellation, directional microphones, amplification, real-time translation and tinnitus masking.
4. Finished hearing aid hardware sold with a companion mobile app for customization.
5. Over-the-counter hearing aids and consumer wearable devices.
6. Consumers seeking affordable hearing care.
7. Its proprietary algorithms and chips are integrated into its own finished hearing aids sold direct to consumers.
8. It combines proprietary AI chips and algorithms with an over-the-counter direct-to-consumer model to deliver medical-grade hearing care at budget prices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The National Council on Aging and various global tech leaders and research institutes.
Organization type: A privately held integrated brand encompassing R&D, manufacturing and global sales.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished hearing aids.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017 with its algorithms installed in over 200 million consumer devices worldwide.
Geography: Based in Las Vegas, Nevada, USA with global sales operations.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Oticon
points.description: Danish hearing aid manufacturer integrating deep neural networks into hearing aids to improve sound processing.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs, builds and sells finished hearing aids and accessories incorporating embedded deep neural networks and custom DSP chipsets for hearing care professionals and consumers.
1. A hearing aid manufacturer whose custom DSP chipsets and embedded neural network models run on-device in finished hearing aids and companion wireless accessories it sells as finished hardware.
2. Custom digital signal processing chipsets running embedded deep neural networks trained on millions of real-world sound scenes, combined with head-motion sensors and adaptive beamforming algorithms.
3. Noise suppression, speech enhancement, feedback cancellation, wind noise reduction, binaural spatial sound processing, listening intent inference and Bluetooth audio streaming.
4. Finished hardware devices including behind-the-ear and in-the-ear hearing aids, along with companion mobile apps, wireless adapters and remote controls.
5. Hearing aids, assistive listening devices and clinical audiology fittings for adults and children.
6. Hearing care professionals, audiology clinics, national health services and consumers.
7. Its finished hearing aids and custom chipsets are sold through and fitted by hearing care professionals and audiology clinics for end users.
8. It integrates purpose-built DSP chipsets with on-board deep neural networks trained on 12 million real-life sound scenes to process sound without compressing the auditory scene.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of Demant A/S with products distributed by hearing care networks and connectivity support for Apple devices and Android ASHA.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded hearing healthcare company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished hearing aids and accessories, often transacted through volume purchase contracts with public health services or audiology clinics.
Scale and maturity: The world's second-largest hearing aid manufacturer, founded in 1904, operating with over 20,000 employees globally under its parent company.
Geography: Headquartered in Denmark with a United States subsidiary and a global distribution and sales network.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on hearing aids, audiological research and hearing healthcare technology.

points.name: Signia
points.description: German hearing aid manufacturer developing AI-powered platforms that adapt to dynamic sound environments.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of advanced hearing aids that develops and sells AI-powered prescription hearing devices and companion software for individuals with hearing loss.
1. An equipment maker that designs finished hearing aids and proprietary audio processing chips, sold as medical hardware to hearing care providers and clinics.
2. Deep neural networks and split-processing audio algorithms run on custom proprietary microchips inside the hearing aids to process real-time acoustic environments.
3. Speech detection, own-voice processing, ambient scene adaptation, dynamic noise control, directional beamforming, and tinnitus management.
4. Finished hearing aid hardware, accessory devices, and mobile applications delivered through hearing care professionals and retail clinic networks.
5. Prescription hearing aids, wearable hearables, and remote audiology care platforms used in everyday listening environments and group conversations.
6. Hearing care professionals, audiology clinics, retail hearing aid distributors, and individual consumers with hearing loss.
7. Its finished devices and proprietary chips are distributed through audiology clinics and retail hearing care networks to end users.
8. Simultaneously operates four task-specific deep neural networks on a custom chip to locate and enhance multiple moving conversation partners in real-time group settings.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Operates as a brand under the parent company WS Audiology and has co-developed hearing aids with the hear.com retail platform.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of the publicly traded hearing healthcare company WS Audiology.
Business model: Hardware sales of medical devices, accessories, and associated software billed through hearing care professionals and retail networks.
Scale and maturity: A global hearing aid brand originating from technology first developed in 1913, operating as a standalone brand since 2015.
Geography: Based in Germany with global distribution and operations.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on hearing healthcare, audiology technology, and assistive listening devices.

points.name: EssilorLuxottica
points.description: French eyewear conglomerate building smart glasses and over-the-counter hearing aid eyewear.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of eyewear and wearable technology that builds smart glasses and over-the-counter hearing aid glasses with integrated audio enhancement capabilities for consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished smart glasses and hearing aid glasses sold as consumer hardware worn on the head.
2. Beamforming and open-ear audio technologies integrated into eyewear frames, controlled by companion software including a software-as-a-medical-device application.
3. Conversation clarity in noisy environments, directional hearing enhancement, noise reduction and open-ear audio playback.
4. Finished hardware products sold through optical retailers, accompanied by mobile applications for calibration and control.
5. Smart glasses, over-the-counter hearing aids and AI-integrated wearable eyewear.
6. Consumers with mild-to-moderate hearing loss and consumers of wearable technology.
7. Its frames and finished audio glasses are sold directly to consumers through retail optical chains, and it manufactures eyewear for a technology partner's smart glasses.
8. Integrates hearing aid and audio technology into conventional prescription eyewear frames to combine vision correction, hearing enhancement and style.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Meta Platforms, Transitions Optical Limited, National Acoustic Laboratories, Western University, Qualcomm and acquired startups Nuance Hearing and Pulse Audition.
Organization type: Publicly traded multinational eyewear manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished glasses and frames through owned retail chains.
Scale and maturity: A large multinational corporation generating over 26 billion euros in annual revenue with over 200,000 employees and thousands of retail stores.
Geography: Based in Paris, France with global retail, manufacturing and distribution operations.
Beyond audio: The organization designs, manufactures and distributes vision care products, prescription lenses, sunglasses and retail optical services worldwide.

points.name: Ray-Ban
points.description: Italian eyewear brand partnering with Meta to produce smart glasses featuring open-ear audio and microphone arrays.
points.bullets:
A consumer eyewear brand that co-develops smart glasses with a technology partner, providing the frames and distribution for wearable audio devices with integrated AI features for consumers.
1. An eyewear brand that co-develops finished smart glasses hardware with a technology partner and sells it to consumers through retail channels.
2. The smart glasses deliver open-ear audio and conversation focus features using a five-microphone array.
3. Customers get the audio technology embedded in finished hardware smart glasses.
4. The technology is used in smart glasses and wearable AI eyewear.
5. The company sells to consumers.
6. Its eyewear designs and brand are combined with a technology partner's AI and hardware platforms to form co-branded finished products.
7. It applies established eyewear fashion design and global retail distribution to smart glasses rather than developing the underlying audio or AI technology.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with Meta to produce and distribute the smart glasses.
Organization type: It is a subsidiary brand of a publicly traded eyewear conglomerate.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of finished smart glasses and eyewear.
Scale and maturity: The co-developed smart glasses line surpassed 1 million units in global sales in 2025.
Geography: The company is based in Milan, Italy, and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The organization is a global eyewear and sunglasses brand.

points.name: Nuance Audio
points.description: Israeli startup developing smart glasses that combine vision correction with hearing assistance using directional microphones and open-ear speakers.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer wearable audio hardware that designs and sells smart glasses with built-in hearing assistance, integrating directional microphones and open-ear speakers for people with mild to moderate hearing loss.
1. An equipment maker whose finished hardware is sold as FDA-cleared over-the-counter hearing aids integrated into eyewear, worn on the head by consumers.
2. Acoustic amplification systems using microphone arrays and directional beamforming processed alongside open-ear speaker drivers.
3. Sound amplification, speech clarity in noisy environments and directional listening.
4. Finished hardware glasses with embedded electronics, physical volume controls and integrated battery systems.
5. Over-the-counter hearing aids, social settings and everyday wearable assistive listening devices.
6. Consumers with mild to moderate hearing loss seeking over-the-counter hearing solutions.
7. Its finished glasses are sold directly to consumers as integrated over-the-counter medical-grade wearables.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its parent company is EssilorLuxottica, an eyewear conglomerate that partners with Meta on separate smart glasses products.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded eyewear conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished smart glasses.
Scale and maturity: A recently established brand selling its second-generation product at prices starting around $699 to $829.
Geography: Based in Israel as an acquired startup, operating under a global parent company and targeting the United States over-the-counter hearing aid market.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on combining eyewear with audio hearing assistance technology.

points.name: Cearvol
points.description: US consumer audio brand making AI-powered OTC hearing aids and smart hearing wearables.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs and sells AI-powered, over-the-counter hearing wearables and smart hearing glasses for individuals with mild to moderate hearing loss.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished wearable hearing devices and smart glasses sold as consumer hardware products.
2. The devices run on an on-device AI platform for real-time environmental analysis.
3. The devices deliver hearing assistance, sound mode adaptation for different environments, audio streaming, and voice prompts.
4. Customers get the technology as finished hardware wearables with companion charging cases.
5. The products are used as over-the-counter hearing aids and smart hearing glasses in home, restaurant, and outdoor settings.
6. The company sells directly to consumers experiencing mild to moderate hearing loss.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users as a branded consumer electronics manufacturer.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of finished wearable devices.
Geography: The company is based in Las Vegas, Nevada, USA.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio and hearing assistance wearables.

points.name: Ceretone
points.description: Las Vegas consumer health company making affordable over-the-counter hearing aids with screen-adjustable charging cases.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer hearing aids that designs, manufactures and sells over-the-counter, invisible-in-canal hearing devices for consumers with mild to moderate hearing loss.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished over-the-counter hearing aids sold as complete hardware devices worn in the ear.
2. Digital hearing aid devices built around audio processing chips, running preset listening modes and tinnitus masking algorithms.
3. Hearing amplification, tinnitus masking and preset listening modes for environments such as restaurants and outdoor settings.
4. Finished hearing aid hardware sold directly to consumers, accompanied by a charging case with an integrated display screen.
5. Over-the-counter hearing aids worn in the ear canal.
6. Consumers with mild to moderate hearing loss.
7. Its finished hearing aids are sold directly to end users as standalone consumer health devices.
8. It eliminates the need for a smartphone app by embedding a display screen into the charging case for preset selection.

Key partners and customers: It uses chips from Intricon in its hearing aids.
Organization type: A privately held consumer health technology company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished hearing aids.
Scale and maturity: An FDA-cleared device manufacturer operating in the direct-to-consumer hearing aid market.
Geography: Based in Las Vegas, Nevada, USA.
Beyond audio: The company is a pure-play consumer hearing aid manufacturer.

points.name: Kardome
points.description: Israeli startup building voice recognition technology for smart devices and vehicles.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose on-device voice AI models run in customers' embedded platforms to provide spatial voice enhancement and recognition for consumer electronics, automotive, and enterprise hardware.
1. An AI model developer whose speech and spatial audio models run on-device in edge hardware platforms.
2. Spatial hearing and acoustical modeling algorithms, neural network-based noise suppression, and wake word detection models running on embedded systems.
3. Sound source localization, speaker separation, noise suppression, speaker identification, wake word detection, and contextual speech enhancement for automatic speech recognition.
4. Software development kits, embedded software libraries, and edge AI models that run on customers' devices.
5. Vehicle infotainment systems, smart home devices, smart speakers, and voice-enabled consumer electronics.
6. Consumer electronics brands, automakers, and smart home device manufacturers.
7. Its edge AI software is integrated by device manufacturers into their embedded hardware platforms.

points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with NVIDIA, LG Electronics, KT, Qualcomm, and ARM, and its technology runs on HIFI4 DSP cores.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses, embedded software licensing fees, and per-unit royalties.

points.name: GN Hearing

A hearing aid manufacturer that designs and produces finished prescription and over-the-counter hearing aids, associated wireless streaming accessories, and fitting software for hearing care professionals and consumers.

points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of GN Group being acquired by Amplifon, with bimodal hearing collaborations with Cochlear and Bluetooth SIG membership for Auracast deployment.
Organization type: A corporate subsidiary division of a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales of hearing aids and accessories, alongside associated clinical fitting software.
Scale and maturity: Part of a parent group founded in 1869 with 7,000 employees, positioned as one of the top five global hearing aid manufacturers.
Geography: Based in Ballerup, Denmark with a presence in North America, Europe, and India.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on hearing healthcare and hearing aid technology.

points.name: pyannote.audio
points.description: Open-source Python library providing pre-trained models for identifying and segmenting speakers in audio recordings.

An open-source software developer that provides a Python library and pre-trained models for speaker diarization, built on PyTorch for speech processing researchers and application developers.

2. Neural networks built on PyTorch that execute a full diarization pipeline, including speaker segmentation and embedding extraction.
3. Speaker diarization and speaker segmentation.
4. Open-source software libraries and pre-trained models distributed via code repositories.
5. Speech processing research pipelines, automated transcription systems, and spoken audio processing workflows.

Key partners and customers: Its pipeline is frequently integrated with the Whisper ASR model in third-party tools such as WhisperX.
Organization type: Open-source software project.
Business model: Open-source software distribution.
Scale and maturity: The most widely adopted open-source speaker diarization toolkit.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio processing software.

points.name: Shunya Labs
points.description: Indian startup building voice AI platforms for real-time speech processing and translation.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose speech and audio models run on-premise at the edge and in the cloud for enterprises, providing speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and real-time translation systems focused on Indic languages.
1. An AI model developer whose speech models run on standard CPUs and GPUs in on-premise edge servers and the cloud behind APIs.
2. Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Networks and a clinical knowledge graph running on standard CPUs and GPUs.
3. Speech recognition, text-to-speech, real-time translation, and emotional intelligence for 55 Indian languages.
4. Cloud APIs and on-premise edge software models.
5. Call centers, hospitals, banks, government agencies, and defense environments.
6. Enterprises, government agencies, and defense organizations.
7. Its speech models are deployed as foundational voice infrastructure directly into enterprise environments.
8. Specialization in Indic languages with optimized algorithms for standard CPUs that reduce cloud computing costs and low word error rates.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: United We Care and Hugging Face.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: API usage and enterprise voice infrastructure software.
Scale and maturity: Spun out in 2025 with production deployments planned across multiple global markets.
Geography: Based in India with a focus on the Indian market and planned global operations.
Beyond audio: The organization develops AI voice infrastructure for mental health and wellness applications.

points.name: Seeed Studio
points.description: Chinese hardware manufacturer making open-source microcontroller boards and microphone arrays for audio prototyping.
points.bullets:
A hardware manufacturer that produces microphone arrays, edge computing gateways, and microcontroller boards for voice capture, IoT, and embedded machine learning applications. It manufactures the ReSpeaker line of USB and Raspberry Pi HAT microphone arrays with onboard DSP processing, as well as reComputer edge gateways for local AI inference.
1. A hardware manufacturer that builds finished microphone array products, Raspberry Pi HATs, edge computing gateways, and microcontroller boards, sold as physical hardware through its Bazaar store.
2. microphone arrays using XMOS DSP chips for hardware-level acoustic processing, combined with edge computing gateways powered by NVIDIA Orin or Rockchip NPUs for on-device speech recognition and LLM inference.
3. far-field voice capture with beamforming, direction of arrival detection, acoustic echo cancellation, noise suppression, dereverberation, and multi-channel concurrent speech recognition on edge gateways.
4. finished hardware products including USB microphone arrays, Raspberry Pi HATs, wearable recording devices, edge computing gateways, and microcontroller boards, along with open-source Linux drivers and software libraries.
5. smart speakers, interactive kiosks, robots, desktop transcription, near-field recording, ceiling and wall-mounted microphones, voice assistant integration, and edge AI voice processing.
6. makers, developers, enterprises building voice-enabled products, and hobbyists integrating voice interfaces into Raspberry Pi and IoT projects.
7. its microphone array hardware is integrated into voice-enabled products by developers and makers, and its edge gateways are used to run on-device speech recognition models for local AI processing.
8. combines open-source hardware manufacturing with integrated XMOS DSP-based acoustic processing and edge computing gateways designed for on-device AI inference.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: XMOS supplies DSP processors, STMicroelectronics supplies microphones, NVIDIA supplies Orin NX modules, and Picovoice provides voice software integrated with its hardware.
Organization type: a privately held hardware company based in Shenzhen, China.
Business model: hardware sales through its online Bazaar store, with customization and manufacturing services for IoT and maker applications.
Scale and maturity: an established company with a broad product catalog spanning microcontrollers, microphone arrays, and edge computing gateways.
Geography: headquartered in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China, serving global maker and developer markets.
Beyond audio: an open-source hardware company serving the broader IoT and embedded electronics ecosystem, with audio products as one segment of its offerings.

points.name: Whisper
points.description: US AI company developing subscription-based hearing aids with real-time sound separation.

An AI model developer that builds a large speech recognition model and an AI-powered hearing aid system, providing automatic sound separation and environmental adjustment for hearing-impaired users and transcription for software platforms.
1. An AI model developer whose cloud-based speech recognition models run behind developer APIs and whose hearing aid sound separation models run on-device in finished hardware.
2. Large language model-based neural networks for speech recognition and real-time artificial intelligence sound separation engines.
3. Speech recognition, speech-to-text transcription, real-time sound separation, and automatic acoustic environmental adjustment.
4. Open-source AI models, cloud APIs, and finished hearing aid hardware sold under a subscription model.
5. Hearing aids, noisy environments, restaurants, television listening, transcription software architectures, and audio embedding extraction systems.
6. Software developers, hearing aid wearers, and hearing aid system subscribers.
7. Its speech recognition models are integrated by software developers into their platforms, and its hearing aid hardware is sold directly to consumers.
8. It offers a subscription-based hearing aid service with free continuous software updates rather than selling a static hardware device.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: OpenAI, Simplismart, Qwen2-Audio, Switchboard, LTU-AS, Voicegain, and AF-Whisper.
Organization type: Privately held startup and AI model developer.
Business model: Hardware subscriptions and open-source AI model licensing.
Scale and maturity: Has raised USD 53 million in Series B funding.
Geography: Based in the USA.

points.name: Nexa AI
points.description: AI company developing multimodal audio-language models and edge inference engines for on-device sound recognition.

An AI model developer that builds an audio-language multimodal model and an edge inference engine for on-device deployment. It combines speech recognition with large language model capabilities in a single model, and provides a software development kit for running that model locally, for developers building edge AI applications.

2. A multimodal neural network architecture combining an audio transcription model with a text-based large language model via a custom projector module.

4. AI models and an inference SDK delivered as downloadable software to developers.
5. Edge AI applications running speech recognition and language reasoning on local hardware.
6. Developers building on-device AI applications.
7. It unifies audio speech recognition and large language model reasoning into a single multimodal model optimized for edge inference.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held startup.

points.name: AONDevices
points.description: California fabless chip company making ultra-low-power AI processors for voice and sound recognition in battery-powered devices.

A fabless semiconductor company that designs and markets ultra-low-power edge AI processors and associated software for on-device voice, sound, and motion recognition in battery-powered devices.
1. A fabless chip company that designs ultra-low-power application-specific edge AI processors sold as chips and evaluation kits, accompanied by a software platform for model training and deployment.
2. Proprietary neural network technology running on dedicated on-device cores for multi-modal sensing and single-microphone speech enhancement.
3. Wake word detection, voice command recognition, acoustic event detection, motion pattern detection, and single-microphone speech denoising.
4. Processors sold as integrated circuits, hardware IP, evaluation kits, and a software platform for model optimization and deployment.
5. Hearing aids, wireless earbuds, smartphones, wearables, and always-on remote controls.
6. Device makers and sensor module manufacturers requiring battery-efficient multi-modal sensing.
7. Its processors and IP are designed into battery-powered consumer devices by electronics brands.

Business model: The company makes money through chip sales and hardware IP licensing.

Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is on ultra-low-power edge AI processing for audio and sensor fusion.

points.name: Liquid AI
points.description: Foundation-model startup building efficient, low-memory on-device AI models for agentic behavior and data extraction.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose foundation models run on-device in customers' hardware. It builds compact, open-weight multimodal models that process text, vision, and audio natively on edge processors for automakers and enterprises, avoiding cloud latency.

3. High-fidelity digital reverberation, multi-effects processing, acoustic enhancement and monitor reverb.
4. Finished hardware units and software plug-ins.
5. Studios, live tracking, venues and home theater systems.
6. Studios and musicians, live sound engineers and consumers.
7. Its finished hardware and software are purchased directly by end users for studio and live use.
8. A pioneer in digital reverb technology whose vintage hardware remains highly valued on the secondhand market.

Key partners and customers: A brand owned by HARMAN under its High Performance A/V division, a sister brand to DigiTech, with products compatible with Dirac Live software.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales and software licenses.
Scale and maturity: A long-established brand active since the late 1970s.
Geography: Based in the USA.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is audio signal processing.

points.name: BSS
points.description: UK professional audio manufacturer building signal processors for live and installed sound.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio signal processing equipment that designs and builds open-architecture digital signal processors, conferencing processors, I/O expanders, and configuration software for fixed installations and live sound.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment that builds digital signal processors, networked audio bridges, and control software sold as finished hardware and companion software for installed and live sound applications.
2. Open-architecture digital signal processing hardware running configurable audio routing, processing, and control algorithms over Dante, AVB, and CobraNet audio networking protocols.
3. Dynamic equalization, compression, limiting, acoustic echo cancellation, loudspeaker management, crossovers, digital delay lines, teleconferencing signal processing, and multi-zone audio distribution and control.
4. Finished hardware products including DSPs, I/O expanders, network bridges, and wall controllers, alongside software suites for system configuration, control, and management.
5. Large venues, stadiums, arenas, convention centers, hospitality settings, corporate installations, universities, and live concert tours.
6. System integrators, audio professionals, live sound engineers, and installation contractors in the commercial audio market.
7. Its finished hardware and software products are integrated by system integrators into large-scale professional audio installations alongside amplifiers, loudspeakers, and control systems.
8. Pioneering open-architecture distributed DSP systems that allow highly configurable, networked audio routing and processing across complex multi-zone fixed installations.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A brand within HARMAN Professional Solutions, with products frequently integrated alongside sister brands JBL, Crown, dbx, and AMX, and incorporating Audinate Dante and NETGEAR AVB networking.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand operating within a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales of professional audio processors, expanders, and controllers, supplemented by companion configuration and control software.
Scale and maturity: A long-established brand founded in 1979 with a decades-long history and a global presence in the professional audio market.
Geography: Based in London, UK, with installations and operations globally.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play professional audio company focused entirely on signal processing, networking, and control solutions.

points.name: Sonifex
points.description: British audio equipment manufacturer building mixing consoles and broadcast audio interfaces for studios and professional installations.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures broadcast audio equipment, mixing consoles, interfaces, and audio networking products for broadcast, pro AV, and installed sound applications.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished hardware products and stand-alone device control software, sold as rack-mounted units, desktop consoles, and installed equipment.
2. Analog and digital audio mixing, routing, and signal processing hardware, integrated with audio over IP networking using Dante, AES67, and RAVENNA protocols, alongside SDI video audio embedding and de-embedding.
3. Audio mixing, IP audio streaming, audio delay synchronization, Dolby encoding and decoding, SDI audio embedding and de-embedding, format conversion, signal distribution, and reference monitoring.
4. Finished hardware products, including rack-mounted units, analog mixers, commentator units, IP streamers, and illuminated studio signs, along with stand-alone device control software.
5. Radio and TV broadcast studios, sports grounds and stadia, live venues, meeting rooms, conference rooms, and fixed installations.
6. Broadcasters, professional AV integrators, installed sound contractors, and distribution partners.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold to broadcasters and installed in professional audio and video facilities.
8. It provides a broad portfolio of specialized broadcast infrastructure equipment, including bespoke custom channel strip configurations for analog mixers and dedicated radio capture devices for direct Dante network flow.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Broadcast Radio and Orban.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales and distribution of third-party audio processors.
Scale and maturity: An established company with over 55 years of operation.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom, designing and manufacturing products for worldwide distribution.
Beyond audio: Its sole focus is professional audio and broadcast equipment manufacturing.

points.name: AEQ
points.description: Broadcast equipment manufacturer building intercom systems, mixing consoles, and audio routing solutions for the broadcast industry.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that develops, manufactures and sells hardware and software systems for broadcast audio and video applications, including mixing consoles, intercom systems, audiocodecs, phone systems and routers for broadcasters.
1. A broadcast equipment manufacturer that builds finished hardware and companion software sold as studio and facility production systems running in radio and television broadcast environments.
2. Digital signal processing, Dante and AES67 IP audio networking, SIP telephony and matrixless IP intercom architecture implemented in dedicated mixing engines, consoles, terminal devices and codecs.
3. Multichannel audio mixing and routing, IP-based intercom communication, bidirectional audio contribution and distribution, and broadcast telephony with talk-show call management.
4. Finished hardware products and accompanying software, including mixing consoles, intercom terminals, portable and stationary audiocodecs, and IP phone systems.
5. Radio studios, television studios, outside broadcast vehicles, sports broadcast facilities and live event broadcasting.
6. Broadcast networks, television and radio stations, outside broadcast providers and system integrators.
7. Its finished equipment is installed as the core production infrastructure in radio and television studios by system integrators and broadcasters.
8. A forty-year focus on providing the full chain of broadcast studio equipment spanning mixing, intercom, codec and telephony functions for radio and television under a single brand.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Studiotech Belgium, Dante and AES67 network ecosystems, and the RTNC broadcaster.
Organization type: A privately held company operating under its own brand.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished equipment and systems, with associated broadcast engineering and installation services.
Scale and maturity: A well-established company with commercial offices in six countries, a network of over 135 local partners, products deployed in over 15000 radio studios and 4500 television sets, and exports to more than 100 countries worldwide.
Geography: Based in Madrid with additional commercial offices across Spain, the United States, Portugal, Mexico and India, and operating globally.
Beyond audio: The company also develops and manufactures video equipment, including video monitors, and provides automation and production systems for broadcast television.

points.name: Lawo
points.description: German broadcast audio company building mixing consoles and IP-based media infrastructure.
points.bullets:
A professional equipment maker that develops and manufactures digital audio mixing consoles and IP-based media infrastructure for broadcast and live media production. It builds physical mixing surfaces, DSP cores, stage I/O devices and software management platforms, combining workflow control, signal processing and human interfaces into integrated production systems for broadcasters and live venues.
1. A professional equipment maker that builds digital audio mixing consoles, audio DSP cores and network I/O devices, sold as finished hardware alongside virtualized mixing and management software that runs on standard servers and in broadcast control rooms.
2. The core technology is IP-native audio networking based on audio-over-IP standards and software-defined DSP processing running on dedicated rack units and virtualized server instances.
3. It delivers high-channel-count audio mixing, routing, signal processing, automated mic gain leveling and mixing, multi-format I/O conversion and centralized orchestration of IP media infrastructure.
4. Customers get the technology as finished hardware consoles, stage I/O devices, rack-mounted DSP engines and licensed software platforms.
5. The products are used in television broadcast studios, on-air radio facilities, remote broadcast vans, performing arts venues, houses of worship and corporate AV environments.
6. The company sells to broadcast networks, radio stations, system integrators and professional AV facilities.
7. Its consoles and IP infrastructure are deployed by broadcasters and integrated by system integrators into live production facilities and remote broadcast workflows.
8. It unifies physical control surfaces, DSP cores, I/O nodes and cloud-ready management software under a single IP-native, microservices-based platform built on open audio-over-IP standards.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company has investments in ALC NetworX and partners with POPE Professional Acoustics, Waves and SLG Broadcast, with RTL News and Kronehit as named customers.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales and perpetual software licenses combined with flexible software subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: The company is an established global manufacturer with a long history, headquartered in Rastatt, Germany.
Geography: The company is based in Rastatt, Germany, and operates globally across broadcast and professional AV markets.
Beyond audio: The organization also develops video processing, monitoring and control technology for IP-based media production environments.

points.name: Calrec
points.description: UK broadcast audio manufacturer building mixing consoles for live production.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures broadcast audio mixing consoles, IP-based audio processing engines, modular I/O platforms, and cloud-based mixing software for television, radio, and other professional media applications.
1. An equipment maker whose hardware and virtualized DSP software run in broadcast control rooms, production studios, and cloud environments.
2. Audio mixing consoles, digital signal processing engines, modular routing platforms, and audio networking protocols utilizing IP-native ST2110, AES67, Dante, MADI, and Waves SoundGrid connectivity.
3. Audio mixing, signal routing, immersive audio panning, virtualized DSP processing, and remote production control for broadcast workflows.
4. Finished hardware consoles, 1RU audio processing engines, modular I/O hardware, and cloud-based software hosted in public cloud infrastructure.
5. Television broadcast control rooms, radio studios, sports stadiums, podcast studios, corporate events, houses of worship, and remote production workflows.
6. Large broadcasters, local television and radio stations, and professional media production companies.
7. Its broadcast consoles and processing engines are installed in broadcast facilities and remote production units by media organizations.
8. It provides highly configurable IP-native hardware and virtualized cloud mixing systems integrated with industry-standard ST2110 and NMOS protocols for flexible broadcast workflows.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company is a subsidiary brand of Audiotonix, uses AWS to host its cloud DSP software, and integrates with Waves SoundGrid networking.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand within a larger professional audio manufacturing group.
Business model: Hardware sales of mixing consoles and processing engines, alongside software licenses and subscriptions for virtualized DSP and cloud mixing platforms.
Scale and maturity: A long-established manufacturer with six decades of history serving major global broadcasters.
Geography: Based in the UK and serving global professional broadcast markets.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on professional broadcast audio mixing, processing, and routing technology.

points.name: Wheatstone
points.description: US broadcast equipment manufacturer building mixing consoles and audio networking systems for radio and television studios.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds mixing consoles, audio processors, virtual mixers, audio editors, streaming appliances, and Audio over IP networking elements for radio and television broadcast facilities.
1. A professional audio equipment maker that builds broadcast consoles, audio networking hardware, and virtual mixing software sold as finished hardware and software products running in studio environments.
2. Audio over IP networking protocols, digital mixing and signal processing engines, and software-based virtual mixing architectures.

5. Radio and television broadcast studios, live news broadcasts, commercial facilities, and remote broadcasting setups.
6. Broadcast facilities, radio and television stations, and commercial broadcast networks.
7. Its finished studio equipment and networking infrastructure are deployed directly by broadcasters in their facilities.
8. It engineers, manufactures, and supports its complete studio product range under one roof alongside its own layer-3 audio networking protocol.

Key partners and customers: Broadcast Depot serves as a distributor in the United States and Latin America.
Organization type: A privately held company operating multiple brands.
Business model: Hardware sales and software product sales.

Geography: Based in New Bern, North Carolina, United States, serving broadcast facilities globally.

points.name: Audient
points.description: UK audio manufacturer making mixing consoles and audio interfaces for home studios.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and sells audio interfaces, mixing consoles, microphone preamps, and monitor controllers for home and professional studios.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio interfaces and related recording hardware, sold as standalone physical products that connect to host computers and mobile devices.
2. Analog and digital audio conversion circuitry, JFET instrument inputs, USB-C and USB connectivity, and built-in DSP for speaker processing and automatic gain staging.
3. Analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog audio conversion, microphone preamplification, multi-channel routing, spatial speaker configuration and downmixing, and automatic gain control.
4. Customers get the technology through finished physical hardware products purchased as standalone units.
5. Home studios, project studios, professional recording studios, and immersive spatial audio monitoring setups.
6. Home studio users, beginners in audio recording, and professional recording engineers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to recording engineers and home studio users for use in their own recording setups.
8. The company adapts its high-end professional console preamplifier technology into affordable, user-friendly interfaces with automated features like Smartgain.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company sells its EVO range under the EVO by Audient brand and designs products compatible with modern iOS devices.
Organization type: A privately held company that operates as a standalone audio hardware brand.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of its finished audio products.
Scale and maturity: The company is an established manufacturer with a recognized, broad product range spanning entry-level to professional interfaces.
Geography: The company is based in the United Kingdom and operates in the global audio equipment market.
Beyond audio: The company is a pure-play audio hardware manufacturer whose entire focus is on recording and monitoring equipment.

points.name: Shenzhen Maono Technology Co., Ltd.
points.description: Chinese audio hardware brand building microphones, interfaces, and headphones for podcasters, streamers, and content creators.

A maker of consumer and prosumer audio equipment that manufactures microphones, audio interfaces, mixers, and monitoring headphones for content creators such as podcasters, streamers, and gamers.

2. Digital and analog audio capture, processing, and routing circuits built into standalone devices.

6. The company sells directly to consumers and content creators, including podcasters, gamers, vloggers, and musicians.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users for content creation setups.

Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.

points.name: Apogee

A maker of professional audio equipment that develops audio interfaces, AD/DA converters, microphones and audio plugins for high-end studios and recording professionals.

points.name: KRK
points.description: US audio manufacturer building studio monitors for music production.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures active near-field studio monitors and accompanying control software for music producers, engineers, and recording studios.

Organization type: A subsidiary brand of an audio equipment company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished studio monitors and accessories.

points.name: Adam Audio

Organization type: A subsidiary brand operating under a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished active studio monitors and loudspeakers.

points.name: Kali Audio

points.name: Eventide

A manufacturer of professional audio equipment that builds hardware effects processors and software plugins for recording studios, live sound and musicians. It develops and sells digital audio effects units, rackmount multi-effects processors, stompbox pedals and native plugin versions of its algorithms. The organization targets audio engineers, producers, broadcasters and guitarists with pitch shifting, reverb, delay, modulation and dynamics processing.

4. Finished hardware units and native software plugins.

Organization type: A privately held company.

Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded company.
Business model: Software licenses and monthly subscriptions.

An audio software company that develops reverberation plugins for professional audio production. It builds software emulations of hardware reverberators and algorithmic reverbs for mixing engineers and post-production professionals.

2. Digital signal processing algorithms that model the acoustic and electronic behavior of classic hardware reverb units and analog equalizers.
3. Reverb effects processing and mastering equalization.

5. Recording studios, mastering studios, and music production environments.
6. Audio professionals, mixing engineers, mastering engineers, and music producers.

2. Digital signal processing for hardware reverb and dynamic compression, velocity-sensitive pad sensors for electronic percussion, and USB and five-pin MIDI protocols for keyboard controllers.

A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures high-end analog and tube studio processors, including compressors, equalizers, channel strips and summing mixers, for recording, mixing and mastering engineers.
