2. Classic European tube and solid-state analog circuit designs, alongside DSP-based reverb engines paired with analog input and output transformers.
3. Dynamics control, equalization, summing, saturation, reverb processing and master bus compression for adding analog depth and cohesion to audio signals.
4. Finished hardware units, motorized hardware controllable via software plugins, and studio connectivity cables.
5. Professional recording studios, high-end project rooms, tracking, mixing and mastering setups.
6. Recording engineers, producers and studio owners seeking authentic analog character.
7. Its finished hardware processors are integrated into the signal chains of professional and project studios by engineers and producers.
8. A boutique, less-is-more approach focused on essential controls, broad sweet spots and combining tube warmth with solid-state clarity in single units.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Geography: Based and operates in Berlin, Germany, serving studios worldwide.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Black Lion Audio
points.description: Chicago manufacturer building premium audio interfaces, mic preamps, and master word clocks.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures original outboard gear, converters, interfaces, and clocking, and performs modification services on existing audio interfaces for recording studios and live sound engineers.
1. A manufacturer of finished pro-audio hardware and upgrade modification services, sold as physical rackmount units, 500-series modules, and audio interfaces running as standalone equipment in studios and live sound rigs.
2. Analog circuit design for microphone preamplifiers, FET compression, analog summing, and clocking, along with upgraded analog front ends and clocking modifications for third-party converters.
3. Microphone preamplification, analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog conversion, master word clock generation, analog summing, FET compression, and audio interface signal routing.
4. Finished hardware products, including rack units, half-rack interfaces, 500-series chassis, and digital cables, along with hardware modification services for existing interfaces.
5. Recording studios, project studios, and live sound environments.
6. Recording engineers, studio operators, producers, and live sound professionals.
7. Its finished hardware and interface modifications are integrated directly into the recording and live sound signal chains of audio professionals.
8. The company began by modifying third-party audio interfaces to improve their analog and clocking performance before expanding into manufacturing its own line of original pro-audio gear.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales and hardware modification service fees.
Geography: Based in Chicago, USA.
Beyond audio: Audio equipment manufacturing and modification is its entire focus.

points.name: Chandler Limited
points.description: US boutique audio equipment manufacturer building hand-made analog signal processors and recreations of classic studio consoles.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures high-end analog signal processors, mixers, preamplifiers, microphones and outboard gear for musicians and audio professionals, building authorized recreations of classic studio console modules.
1. An equipment maker that builds hand-made analog hardware sold as finished rackmount units, 500 Series modules, standalone microphones and modular mixing consoles.
2. Analog audio circuits utilizing vacuum tubes, transformers and germanium transistors based on historic recording console designs.
3. Microphone preamplification, equalization, compression, limiting, direct injection, buss routing and studio monitoring control.
4. Finished hardware products and licensed circuit designs for software emulation.
5. Professional recording studios and live audio environments.
6. Musicians, audio professionals, recording studios and mastering engineers.
7. Its finished hardware is purchased by engineers for use in professional studios, and its analog circuit designs are licensed to software developers for plugin emulation.
8. It is the singular manufacturer authorized to develop official equipment recreations based on historic console technology.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: EMI and Abbey Road Studios.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales and circuit licensing.
Geography: Based in Shell Rock, Iowa, operating globally.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Softube
points.description: Swedish software company developing audio plugins and mixing suites for music production.
points.bullets:
A software company that develops audio plugins and hardware controllers for music production and mixing, specializing in emulating analog outboard gear, synthesizers, and studio equipment for musicians and audio engineers.
1. A software company whose audio plugins and mixing suites run as native formats inside digital audio workstations, alongside a dedicated hardware controller for its plug-in ecosystem.
2. The core technology consists of digital signal processing algorithms that model the characteristics of analog hardware, tape saturation, and modular synthesizer components.
3. The specific audio capabilities it delivers include equalization, dynamics compression, tape saturation, stereo widening, peak clipping, bus processing, and modular synthesis.
4. Customers get it through perpetual software licenses, subscription-based plugin suites, and finished hardware controllers.
5. It is used in recording studios, mixing sessions, and mastering rooms.
6. It sells to musicians, mixing engineers, mastering engineers, and audio producers.
7. Its software plugins are used by audio engineers within digital audio workstations to process and mix recorded audio tracks.
8. What distinguishes its approach is the development of authorized emulations of specific high-end analog hardware units in collaboration with the original hardware manufacturers and renowned engineers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Named partners include Weiss Engineering, Chandler Limited, Tube-Tech, Empirical Labs, Abbey Road Studios, and Jonathan Wyner.
Organization type: It is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through software licenses, plugin subscriptions, and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: It is an established company that generated SEK 85.6 million in revenue in 2024.
Geography: It is based in Linkoping, Sweden.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: UnderTone Audio
points.description: US pro audio brand building high-end analog outboard gear and rack-mount compressors for recording studios.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures high-end analog outboard recording gear, including recreations of classic compressors, equalizers, and preamps, for professional studios and engineers.
1. An equipment maker whose finished rack-mount analog hardware is sold to professional studios and engineers.
2. Analog audio circuits and signal processing components.
3. Audio compression, equalization, microphone preamplification, wet/dry mixing, and sidechain filtering.
4. Finished hardware products and physical accessories.
5. Professional recording studios.
6. Professional studios, engineers, recording artists, and pro audio dealers.
7. Its finished hardware is sold to professional studios and engineers through direct sales and retail partnerships.
8. A meticulous, slow-to-market design philosophy delivers classic analog sounds with modern, surgical flexibility.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Vintage King and Royer Labs.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of Royer Labs.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A boutique manufacturer with a focused range of products.
Geography: Based and operates within the professional audio market.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is professional audio equipment.

points.name: Image-Line
points.description: Belgian software company developing digital audio workstations for electronic music production.
points.bullets:
A music software company that develops a digital audio workstation and bundled plugins for music production and composition, targeting beat makers and electronic music producers. The organization builds desktop and mobile DAW software, virtual instruments, and audio effects, distributing them directly to consumers and through retailers. It also operates a companion cloud service that provides sound packs, third-party plugins, and music distribution.
1. A software developer whose digital audio workstation, virtual instruments, and effects run as desktop and mobile software products.
2. Pattern-based sequencing algorithms, digital synthesizers, and audio processing algorithms for mixing and mastering.
3. Audio recording and playback, MIDI sequencing, subtractive and additive synthesis, time and pitch manipulation, stereo widening, multiband compression, reverb generation, AI stem separation, AI mastering, and AI-assisted chord progression generation.
4. Software products and companion cloud services.
5. Recording studios, beat production, electronic music production, and audio editing.
6. Consumers, electronic music producers, and beat makers.
7. Its software products are used directly by musicians and producers to create and master music.
8. A pattern-based non-linear workflow and a lifetime free updates policy for its digital audio workstation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Distribution and plugin partners include DistroKid, Native Instruments, UVI, Baby Audio, Minimal Audio, MeldaProduction, W. A. Production, and UnitedPlugins.
Organization type: Privately held software company.
Business model: Software licenses and companion cloud service subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A major global vendor of digital audio workstation software established in 1998.
Geography: Based in Brussels, Belgium, and operating globally.
Beyond audio: The organization's focus is entirely on music production software and audio technology.

points.name: Reason Studios
points.description: Swedish software company developing a rack-based digital audio workstation and plugin effects.
points.bullets:
A software company that develops a rack-based digital audio workstation and a companion plugin rack for music production. It builds virtual instruments, effects and a modular environment for composers and producers, sold as standalone software and as a plugin that runs inside other DAWs.
1. A software developer whose digital audio workstation and plugin rack run as desktop software and plugins on users' computers.
2. A modular software environment emulating hardware rack routing, including virtual instruments and effects with CV routing for complex signal chains.
3. Music composition, sound design, virtual synthesis, sampling, loop playback and audio effects processing.
4. Software products and plugins downloaded by users, offered as perpetual licenses and as a subscription service.
5. Studios and home music production setups.
6. Musicians, producers and composers.
7. Its DAW and plugins are used directly by end users for music production.
8. Its core interface emulates physical hardware rack routing within software, allowing modular signal chaining and use of its devices inside other digital audio workstations.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A Snapdragon-native version is in development and the company operates as its own brand under LANDR after acquisition.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand operating under a publicly known parent company.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions.
Geography: Based in Stockholm, Sweden.
Beyond audio: Audio and music production software is its entire focus.

points.name: Tracktion
points.description: Software company developing digital audio workstations and plugins for music production.
points.bullets:
A software company that develops digital audio workstation software and audio plugins, offering a free cross-platform DAW with professional features and a paid Pro version, for musicians and producers.
1. A software company whose digital audio workstation and plugins run as desktop software on Windows, macOS, Linux, and Raspberry Pi.
2. Audio recording, arranging, mixing, and mastering software incorporating MIDI sequencing, clip-based sequencing, wavetable synthesis, and AI-powered mix analysis.
3. Multitrack audio and MIDI recording, clip launching, wavetable synthesis, audio mixing and mastering, and AI mix analysis.
4. Finished software products, including a free unrestricted DAW, a paid DAW, and standalone plugins.
5. Home and project studios, music production, live performance, and audio post-production.
6. Musicians, producers, and audio engineers.
7. Its software products are used directly by consumers and audio professionals to create and produce music.
8. It offers a fully featured, no-cost digital audio workstation with no track limits, watermarks, or export restrictions across all desktop operating systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Mode Audio provides sound content for inclusion in its products.
Organization type: A privately held software company.
Business model: Software sales and in-app purchases, including paid DAW licenses, optional paid add-ons, and plugins.
Geography: It develops software available globally for Windows, macOS, Linux, and Raspberry Pi.
Beyond audio: Audio software development is its entire focus.

points.name: Hit'n'Mix
points.description: UK software company developing AI tools for separating and editing audio stems.
points.bullets:
An AI software developer that builds an AI-powered digital audio workstation for stem separation, audio cleanup and note-level editing, sold to remixers, DJs, producers and musicians.
1. An AI software developer whose audio editing and separation software runs as a desktop application on users' computers.
2. Deep learning algorithms for audio source separation combined with a proprietary audio format that represents musical notes for non-destructive editing.
3. AI-driven separation of mixed audio into six or more stems, forensic isolation of individual sounds, stem cleanup, unpitched audio editing and note-level manipulation.
4. Software products sold as one-time purchase licenses with paid upgrades.
5. Studios, music production workflows, DJ sets and remixing.
6. Remixers, DJs, producers, creators and musicians.
7. Its software is used directly by end users as a standalone workstation or integrated alongside other digital audio workstations.
8. It separates audio into editable individual notes using a proprietary format rather than separating only into fixed instrument stems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its software is being developed to run on Apple's Vision Pro headset.
Organization type: A privately held software company.
Business model: Software licenses and paid upgrades.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom.
Beyond audio: It developed optical music recognition software for scoring and notation.

points.name: DJ.Studio
points.description: Software company developing a DAW specifically for DJs, with AI-powered stem separation, and integrations with major DJ platforms.
points.bullets:
A software developer that builds a digital audio workstation specifically for DJs, offering timeline-based mixing, stem separation, and library integration tools for hobbyist and professional performers.
1. A software developer whose DJ workstation application runs as a desktop product on users' computers.
2. A digital audio workstation engine combined with AI-powered source separation algorithms for stem extraction.
3. Timeline-based mix sequencing, library synchronization with DJ software formats, video mixing visualization, and AI stem separation.
4. Software products sold directly to users, including tiered bundles with standalone stem separation capabilities.
5. DJ studios, live sets, mashup production, and mix preparation.
6. DJs, including over 200,000 users ranging from hobbyists to professionals.
7. It targets the DJ workflow specifically, bridging timeline-based audio editing with DJ performance library formats.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates with the Rekordbox, Serato, and Traktor DJ software platforms.
Organization type: Privately held software company.
Business model: Software licenses and tiered subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: Used by over 200,000 DJs.
Geography: Operates digitally with a global user base.
Beyond audio: Its focus is entirely on DJ performance and mix creation software.

points.name: MeldaProduction
points.description: Music software company making audio effect and instrument plug-ins.
points.bullets:
A music software company that develops audio effect and instrument plug-ins for digital audio workstations, providing a range of free and paid processing utilities for music producers and audio engineers.
1. A software developer whose audio effect and instrument plug-ins run as standard format plug-ins inside customers' digital audio workstation software on desktop and laptop computers.
2. Digital signal processing algorithms implemented as native audio plug-ins.
3. Reverb, compression, distortion, flanging, phasing, filtering, ring modulation, stereo image widening, instrument tuning, pitch correction and programmed panning.
4. Software plug-ins and utility bundles downloaded and installed directly by users.
5. Digital audio workstations used in music production studios and home recording setups.
6. Music producers, audio engineers and musicians.
7. Its plug-ins are hosted directly by end-users within digital audio workstation software.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company participates as a third-party plug-in provider within another developer's cloud plugin platform and reward voucher redemption program.
Organization type: A privately held software company.
Business model: Software sales and free plug-in bundles.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on music production software.

points.name: Spitfire Audio
points.description: London virtual instrument developer creating realistic orchestral sample libraries and software instruments for digital audio workstations.
points.bullets:
A developer of virtual instruments and sample libraries that produces recorded orchestral and acoustic instrument collections for musicians and composers.
1. A virtual instrument and sample library developer whose software instruments run as plugins inside third-party hosts and sample players on computers.
2. Multi-gigabyte sampled audio recordings of real instruments and ensembles mapped to playable software instruments.
3. Realistic orchestral and acoustic instrument emulation, multi-articulation sampling and true legato playback.
4. Software libraries and virtual instruments sold as downloadable plugins and sample sets.
5. Digital audio workstations, film scoring, music production and composition studios.
6. Composers, musicians and music producers.
7. Its sample libraries are distributed through plugin marketplaces and host applications to end-user composers.
8. High-fidelity orchestral and ensemble recordings captured in professional recording studios.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Recorded at AIR Studios Lyndhurst Hall, distributed through Muse Hub, acquired by Splice.
Organization type: Privately held subsidiary.
Business model: Software licenses and sample library sales.
Scale and maturity: A developer with a catalog of over 60 sample libraries.
Geography: Based in London, UK.
Beyond audio: A sound design and music software company whose entire focus is audio sample library production.

points.name: Manley Laboratories
points.description: Audio equipment manufacturer building high-end vacuum tube microphones, preamps, and equalizers for professional recording studios.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional analog audio equipment that designs and builds vacuum tube hardware for recording studios and high-end audio systems, now a subsidiary brand within a holding company.
1. A professional audio equipment manufacturer that designs and sells finished analog hardware built with vacuum tubes.
2. Vacuum tube analog circuitry, including tube preamplifiers, compressors, equalizers, phono stages and microphones, with products designed and built in-house.
3. Analog signal amplification, equalization, dynamic range compression, phonograph equalization and acoustic capture using tube circuits.
4. Finished hardware products, including channel strips, standalone processors and microphones.
5. Recording studios and high-end home audio systems.
6. Studios and musicians and high-end audio consumers.
7. Its finished hardware is sold to recording engineers and high-end audio consumers for use in their studio and home audio systems.
8. It designs and builds all products in-house around vacuum tube circuitry known for sonic character and reliability.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of Rockforce Tech Holding Inc. and part of the RCKFRC audio group alongside Plugin Alliance and Brainworx, with a collaboration with Apogee expected to lead to hybrid products and exclusive collaboration on UAD plugins.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in the late 1980s, separated from VTL in 1993, acquired in an all-cash transaction in July 2025.
Geography: Based at a facility in California.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play professional audio equipment manufacturer whose entire focus is analog and vacuum tube audio hardware.

points.name: RCKFRC
points.description: Audio group owning and managing pro audio brands like Brainworx, Plugin Alliance, Apogee, and Manley Labs.
points.bullets:
An umbrella company that owns professional audio brands making hardware, converters, interfaces and software plugins for recording studios, mixing and mastering engineers, and musicians.
1. An equipment maker and software developer that builds professional audio hardware and analog modeling plugins sold as finished products and software licenses.
2. Analog circuit design, digital audio conversion and analog modeling algorithms.
3. Analog audio processing, analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog audio conversion, and software-based audio mixing and mastering.
4. Finished hardware and software plugins.
5. Recording studios, mixing and mastering workflows, and music production.
6. Studios, musicians, and audio engineers.
7. Its products are sold directly to end users and through distribution to recording professionals.
8. It consolidates multiple established professional audio brands spanning both hardware and software under a single umbrella.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Founded and owned by Dirk Ulrich, the company owns Apogee, Manley Labs, Plugin Alliance, and Brainworx.
Organization type: A privately held family-owned umbrella company.
Business model: Hardware sales and software licenses.
Scale and maturity: A newly founded organization that acquired multiple audio brands in 2025 and 2026.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: inMusic
points.description: US parent company owning DJ, music instrument, and pro audio brands.
points.bullets:
A holding company that owns and operates a broad portfolio of audio, musical instrument, and DJ technology brands. It makes and markets finished hardware, software, and virtual instruments for musicians, producers, DJs, and consumers.
1. An equipment maker and holding company that builds finished hardware and software products under multiple subsidiary brands, sold to consumers and professionals.
2. The portfolio spans analog synthesizers, electronic drum and cymbal pads, standalone music production platforms, MIDI controllers, DJ hardware, and virtual instrument software.
3. It delivers audio generation, music production, DJ performance control, sound reinforcement, and electronic musical instrument capabilities.
4. The organization provides finished hardware products, software products, and virtual instruments through its global distribution network.
5. Its products are used in studios, live performances, DJ sets, and consumer music-making settings.
6. It sells to consumers, DJs, musicians, producers, and live sound professionals.
7. As a parent company, it markets finished products directly to end users and provides its subsidiary brands with global distribution and supply chain infrastructure.
8. It operates as a conglomerate with a highly diversified brand portfolio spanning entry-level consumer audio, professional DJ equipment, analog synthesizers, and software instruments, unified by centralized supply chain and distribution management.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It owns subsidiary brands including Akai Professional, Moog Music, Alesis, Numark, Denon DJ, Rane, M-Audio, and Native Instruments.
Organization type: A privately held holding company and conglomerate.
Business model: It generates revenue through sales of finished hardware and software products across its portfolio of brands.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1992, it operates a large portfolio of established audio brands.
Geography: It is based in Cumberland, Rhode Island, USA, and operates global distribution and supply chain networks.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on music technology, consumer electronics, and pro audio.

points.name: Elysia
points.description: German pro audio manufacturer building high-end analog dynamics processors for mastering applications.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and sells high-end analog dynamics processors for mastering, mixing and live sound engineering.
1. An equipment maker whose analog hardware processors are sold as finished 19-inch rack units, 500 Series modules and portable hardware units.
2. Discrete Class-A analog circuitry incorporating M/S processing matrices, parallel compression paths, switchable transformers and multiband signal splitting.
3. Transparent dynamics processing including stereo bus compression, multiband compression, mid/side encoding and parallel compression.
4. Finished hardware sold as 19-inch rack units, 500 Series modules and compact hardware units, with its hardware designs also ported to digital audio software plug-ins.
5. Mastering studios, recording studios and live sound engineering setups.
6. Audio professionals including mastering engineers, mixing engineers and live sound engineers.
7. Its finished hardware processors are purchased directly by mastering and mixing engineers for use in professional studio signal chains.
8. The combination of transparent Class-A analog circuitry with advanced M/S and multiband processing in multiple hardware form factors.

Key partners and customers: Mastering engineers Stephen Marcussen, Eric Valentine and Brian Lucey, and digital plug-in platform Plugin Alliance.
Organization type: Privately held audio equipment manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of premium analog outboard processors.
Scale and maturity: Established high-end boutique equipment manufacturer with products retailing above $2,000.
Geography: Based in Germany.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is on professional audio equipment and software.

points.name: Acon Digital
points.description: Norwegian software company developing audio editing applications and restoration plugins.
points.bullets:
An audio software company that develops digital audio workstation software and audio processing plugins for recording, editing, mastering and restoration, integrating AI and machine learning into its products for studios and musicians.
1. An audio software developer whose standalone applications and plugin formats run natively on desktop operating systems inside digital audio workstations.
2. Spectral editing algorithms, machine learning models and digital signal processing chains operating on desktop computer processors.
3. Noise reduction, de-reverberation, dialogue extraction, click and hum removal, audio gap filling, immersive audio support up to 9.1.6 channels, and drum stem separation.
4. Perpetual-license software applications and audio processing plugins in formats including AAX.
5. Recording studios, post-production workflows, music mastering sessions, and digital audio workstation environments.
6. Studios and musicians, audio engineers, and post-production professionals.
7. Its software products are purchased and operated directly by end-users inside their chosen digital audio workstations.
8. It offers surgical, problem-first audio cleanup tools with batch processing and direct digital audio workstation session integration through a dedicated transfer plugin.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Avid, through Pro Tools integration, and the founders created the separate HANCE audio processing organization.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Perpetual software licenses.
Scale and maturity: An established software vendor offering mature eighth-generation product versions.
Geography: Based in Oslo, Norway.

points.name: Cranborne Audio
points.description: UK pro audio manufacturer building preamps, mixing consoles, and studio networking interfaces.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures hardware preamps, equalizers, audio interfaces, and studio routing systems for recording studios and audio professionals.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished hardware products for studio recording and audio routing.
2. Analog preamp topologies, analog saturation circuits, harmonic equalization, and Ethernet-based audio routing for studio environments.
3. Microphone preamplification, analog harmonic saturation, audio equalization, analog-to-digital conversion, and studio audio routing.
4. Finished hardware units, including 500 series modular components, 1U rackmount devices, desktop units, and passive breakout boxes.
5. Recording studios, project studios, and digital audio workstation production environments.
6. Audio professionals, recording engineers, and project studio owners.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to recording professionals and integrated into studio signal chains.
8. The combination of transparent preamp topologies with switchable analog saturation circuits and Ethernet-based studio cabling systems in 500 series compatible formats.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Compatible with the 500 series modular format established by another equipment manufacturer.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom.
Beyond audio: Audio is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: Sound Radix
points.description: Global software company building intelligent audio plugins that help sound engineers and producers achieve better sound faster.
points.bullets:
A software developer that builds intelligent audio plugins for sound engineers, producers, and post-production professionals. The company designs signal-processing algorithms that solve complex audio alignment and editing problems in post-production. Its tools are built to improve speed and accuracy in professional audio workflows.
1. A software developer whose audio processing algorithms are sold as plugins that run inside digital audio workstations used by audio professionals.
2. Signal-processing algorithms that analyze and time-align multiple microphone recordings within a digital audio workstation.
3. Microphone time-alignment and phase alignment for post-production audio.
4. Software plugins compatible with digital audio workstation formats including ARA-integrated versions.
5. Post-production studios and audio editing environments for film, television, and music production.
6. Sound engineers, producers, and sonic creators.
7. Its plugins are purchased by audio professionals and integrated into their digital audio workstation workflows for post-production tasks.
8. The organization builds tools grounded in real-world use and audio science, recognized with a Primetime Engineering Emmy and an Academy Scientific and Engineering Award.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held, bootstrapped company with no outside investors.
Business model: Software licenses for its audio plugins.
Scale and maturity: A small, globally distributed team founded in 2010.
Geography: A global team working remotely from studios and offices around the world.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is on building intelligent audio software tools for professional sound creators.

points.name: Kii Audio GmbH
points.description: German manufacturer building active loudspeakers with controlled directivity to reduce room interference.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs and manufactures active loudspeaker systems featuring advanced DSP, controlled directivity, and fully integrated active architecture for studio and high-end residential listening.
1. An equipment maker that builds active loudspeakers and companion control hardware sold as finished physical products running self-contained DSP.
2. Integrated digital signal processing and multi-driver configurations, including side-firing woofers, used to control directivity and actively manage bass response.
3. Room correction, directivity control, and acoustic boundary cancellation to reduce the influence of the listening room.
4. Finished hardware loudspeakers, companion control units, and mobile configuration software.
5. Studios, high-end residential listening rooms, and Dolby Atmos demonstration setups.
6. Audiophiles, recording studios, and music producers.
7. Its finished loudspeakers are sold directly to end users and demonstrated in high-end audio retail environments.
8. The combination of fully integrated active architecture and controlled directivity using multiple bass drivers to achieve room-removal capabilities.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held manufacturing company.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Audiotonix
points.description: UK pro audio group acquiring and managing brands that build mixing consoles, audio interfaces, and live sound equipment.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and holding company for a portfolio of premium pro audio brands, designing and manufacturing mixing consoles, ancillary products and cloud-based audio processing for live events and broadcast.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures professional audio mixing consoles and ancillary hardware, and develops cloud-based audio processing software that runs in virtualized Linux environments on x86 CPUs.
2. The core technology comprises professional audio mixing consoles, analog and digital audio signal processing, and patented optimal core processing software for deterministic, low-latency audio mixing on x86 CPUs.
3. The specific audio capabilities it delivers are real-time audio mixing, broadcast sound reinforcement, and deterministic low-latency audio processing.
4. Customers get it as finished hardware mixing consoles, ancillary equipment, and cloud-based audio broadcast production solutions.
5. The products are used in live events, broadcast studios, and live sound reinforcement venues.
6. The organization sells to professional audio engineers, broadcasters, live event production companies, and recording studios.
7. Its finished hardware and cloud software products are sold directly to professional end users and integrated into live event and broadcast production workflows.
8. What distinguishes its approach is its portfolio strategy of acquiring, maintaining, and supporting multiple premium, standalone audio brands under a single corporate umbrella.

Key partners and customers: Intel is a technology partner, Astorg is the parent company, and the organization is a Promoter Member of the Avnu Alliance advancing the Milan ecosystem.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held multinational holding company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of professional audio equipment and software licenses for cloud-based audio production solutions.
Scale and maturity: It is a global market leader in professional audio mixing consoles, established in 2014, operating a large portfolio of acquired brands.
Geography: The organization is based in the United Kingdom and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on professional audio technology and the acquisition of premium audio brands.

points.name: Slate Digital
points.location: Los Angeles, California, USA and Grenoble, France
points.description: US-French software company making digital audio plugins that model analog hardware.
points.bullets:
A software and hardware company that develops analog-modeled DSP plugins, virtual microphone systems, and AI mastering services for music recording, mixing, and mastering. It provides digital emulations of vintage audio hardware and microphones alongside physical microphones and control surfaces. The organization serves recording artists, producers, and audio engineers with subscription-based plugin offerings and specialized hardware.
1. A music production software and equipment company whose DSP plugins run as native software in digital audio workstations and whose AI mastering service runs in the cloud, with a secondary business in finished physical microphones and hardware interfaces.
2. Analog-modeled DSP algorithms that digitally reproduce vintage compressors, equalizers, exciters, and microphones, alongside cloud-based AI mastering algorithms.
3. Dynamics processing, equalization, harmonic excitation, microphone and preamp modeling, and automated AI audio mastering.
4. Software plugins delivered via subscription or perpetual licenses, cloud-based mastering services accessed via the web, and finished hardware microphones and audio interfaces.
5. Professional and project recording studios, mixing and mastering workflows, and music production environments.
6. Recording artists, mixing and mastering engineers, music producers, and recording studios.
7. Its software plugins are integrated by end-users into their digital audio workstations, and its physical microphones and hardware are used directly in recording chains.
8. It pairs physically transparent microphones and neutral preamps with DSP software that models rare and highly prized vintage microphones and hardware, providing access to a wide range of analog sounds from a single hardware chain.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: PACE provides licensing and anti-piracy solutions, it operates as a subsidiary brand of Audiotonix, and Steven Slate is an associated co-founder.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand within a publicly traded parent company's portfolio.
Business model: Software subscriptions and perpetual licenses, hardware sales, cloud-based service fees, and educational subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2008 and acquired by Audiotonix in October 2022, established with an expanding product line of plugins and hardware.
Geography: Based in Los Angeles, California, USA and Grenoble, France.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the organization offers an educational subscription service teaching users how to operate its production tools.

points.name: Sonnox
points.description: British audio software company developing premium mixing and mastering plugins derived from Oxford DSP algorithms.
points.bullets:
A professional audio software company that develops premium DSP plugins for mixing, mastering, post-production, and broadcast applications for audio engineers.
1. A software developer that builds digital signal processing algorithms and sells them as audio plugins running inside digital audio workstations on macOS and Windows computers.
2. Highly accurate DSP algorithms utilizing 48-bit double precision calculation, feed-forward architectures, and look-ahead techniques.
3. Parametric equalization, dynamics processing, transient modulation, reverberation, limiting, and audio restoration including noise, click, and buzz removal.
4. Software plugins distributed in standard formats for digital audio workstations and protected by iLok digital rights management.
5. Mixing, mastering, post-production, and broadcast workflows.
6. Top-tier mixing, mastering, and post-production engineers.
7. Its plugins are integrated by engineers into digital audio workstation workflows during music and post-production sessions.
8. It leverages legacy algorithms derived from a professional digital mixing console and a reputation for transparency and artistic flexibility.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Pro audio retailers and a parent audio hardware manufacturer.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of an audio hardware manufacturer.
Business model: Direct sale of proprietary plugins and bundled software collections at a premium price point.
Scale and maturity: Established company acquired in late 2022.
Geography: Operates globally within the professional audio market.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: KLANG:technologies
points.description: German audio brand making immersive in-ear monitoring systems for live sound.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that develops and sells immersive in-ear monitor mixing processors for live sound engineers and audio professionals.
1. A professional audio equipment maker that builds hardware immersive in-ear monitor mixing processors sold as finished rack-mount units running in live sound signal chains.
2. 3D audio processing algorithms running on FPGA-based hardware processing up to 64 input channels with sub-millisecond latency.
3. Spatial in-ear monitor mixing, MADI and Dante audio networking, immersive 3D audio rendering, and low-latency channel routing.
4. Finished hardware processors.
5. Live sound stages, concert venues and professional touring rigs.
6. Live sound engineers and audio production professionals.
7. Its processors are integrated into live sound mixing workflows by front-of-house and monitor engineers.
8. Ultra-compact form factors delivering 64-channel immersive in-ear monitor mixing with 0.25ms latency.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Owned by Audiotonix and integrated as a brand within DiGiCo.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly held audio group.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established brand operating within a large professional audio group.
Geography: Based in Germany and operating within the global professional audio market.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Innosonix
points.description: German audio company manufacturing multichannel DSP-driven amplifiers for immersive and architectural sound installations.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures high-channel-count Class D amplifiers using GaN technology and FPGA-based DSP, providing tools for engineers working in immersive audio, themed entertainment, and architectural installations.
1. An equipment maker that builds multichannel digital audio amplifiers sold as finished hardware running in professional installation environments.
2. Gallium nitride power transistors, FPGA-based digital signal processing, and Power-over-Ethernet capabilities integrated into high-density rack-mount Class D amplifier designs.
3. Up to 32 configurable input and output channels of amplified audio processing in a single rack unit.
4. Finished hardware products comprising multichannel amplifier units designed for professional rack installations.
5. Immersive audio systems, themed entertainment venues, and architectural installations.
6. Professional audio engineers and systems integrators designing large-scale installed audio systems.
7. Its finished hardware is distributed through exclusive regional partners to engineers who specify it into venue installations.
8. High channel density in a compact single-rack-unit form factor achieved through GaN power technology and FPGA-based DSP.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: EPC supplies GaN-based power transistors, and AC Americas holds an exclusive distribution partnership for the United States.
Organization type: A privately held engineering startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished multichannel amplifier products.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2009 and based in Ahorn, Bavaria, operating as a specialized engineering company.
Geography: Based in Germany with distribution extending to the United States.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is professional audio hardware design and manufacturing.

points.name: POPE Professional Acoustics Ltd
points.description: Indian pro audio company making loudspeakers, line arrays, amplifiers and digital signal processors for professional installations.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures loudspeakers, subwoofers, line arrays, amplifiers and digital signal processors for the professional AV market.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished professional audio hardware and electronics sold as physical products for installation and live sound.
2. The company delivers sound reinforcement, low-frequency reproduction, line array directivity, amplification and digital signal processing.
3. Customers get the company's products as finished hardware.
4. The products are used in live venues, installed sound systems and professional AV environments.
5. The company sells to professional AV integrators, sound contractors and live sound engineers.
6. Its finished audio equipment is specified and installed by professional integrators in venues and commercial spaces.
7. The company combines loudspeaker manufacturing with built-in digital signal processing in a single professional audio product portfolio.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company is a partner in the RAVENNA audio-over-IP community alongside professional audio networking companies.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of finished professional audio equipment.
Scale and maturity: The company is an established professional audio brand operating in India.
Geography: The company is based in India and operates in the Indian professional AV market.
Beyond audio: The company's focus is entirely on professional audio equipment.

points.name: DPA Microphones
points.description: Danish microphone manufacturer building high-end condenser microphones for studio recording, live sound, and broadcast.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures high-end condenser microphones and proprietary transducer capsules for studio recording, live sound, broadcast, and test-and-measurement applications.
1. A professional audio equipment maker that builds condenser microphones and proprietary transducer capsules sold as finished hardware for physical capture.
2. The core technology consists of condenser microphone capsules and hardware mounting mechanisms engineered for acoustic capture and off-axis sound rejection.
3. The organization delivers high-fidelity sound reproduction, high speech intelligibility, off-axis rejection, and acoustic feedback rejection.
4. Customers get finished microphone hardware products.
5. The microphones are used in studios, live sound venues, broadcast environments, and test-and-measurement settings.
6. The organization sells to audio professionals, broadcasters, and measurement engineers.
7. Its finished microphone hardware is used directly by audio professionals and engineers in production and measurement environments.
8. The approach is distinguished by precision engineering of proprietary condenser capsules prioritizing natural, undistorted sound and durability over mass-market pricing.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a specialized professional audio manufacturer.
Business model: The company makes money through premium hardware sales.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Wisycom
points.description: Italian manufacturer building wireless audio and RF solutions for broadcast, live events, and location sound.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional wireless audio equipment that designs and produces wireless microphone systems, in-ear monitoring and IFB receivers, antenna matrices, and RF over fiber products for broadcast and production applications.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished wireless audio hardware sold as professional products.
2. RF transmission, reception, and distribution systems operating across wide UHF and broadband frequency ranges with coaxial and fiber-optic transport.
3. Wireless microphone transmission, in-ear monitoring, IFB reception, RF signal distribution over coaxial and fiber, antenna combining, multiband bodypack transmission, and spectrum analysis.
4. Finished hardware products, including bodypack and handheld transmitters, receivers, antenna matrices, RF over fiber transport units, and companion control software applications.
5. Broadcast studios and outside broadcast vehicles, film production, theater, live music, corporate production, and location sound.
6. Broadcast networks, live event production companies, audio rental houses, and location sound professionals.
7. Its finished wireless equipment is deployed directly in professional broadcast and live event productions by sound engineers and audio teams.
8. RF over fiber transport and multiband bodypack transmitter design with rugged, splash-resistant hardware operating across ultra-wideband frequency ranges up to 1,260 MHz.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Planned for acquisition by Audiotonix; a collaborator on the SuperSlot standard; products used by Jetwave Wireless for PBS broadcasts; compatible with DPA MicroLock connectors.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer with a newly opened Americas subsidiary, operating for over 30 years and slated for acquisition.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished professional wireless audio and RF distribution equipment.
Scale and maturity: A company with over 30 years of experience, a global distribution footprint, and a newly established Americas subsidiary.
Geography: Based in Italy with global distribution and a dedicated Americas subsidiary.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is wireless audio and RF solutions for professional production.

points.name: Austrian Audio
points.description: Vienna-based audio manufacturer making high-quality microphones and headphones with modern engineering.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures wired microphones and headphones for recording, mixing, and live sound applications, drawing on a legacy of acoustic engineering.
1. An equipment maker that designs wired condenser microphones and dynamic driver headphones sold as finished physical hardware.
2. Electret condenser capsules with variable polar pattern control and dynamic driver headphones with ring magnet systems and coated diaphragms.
3. High-fidelity audio capture with selectable polar patterns and critical listening for mixing, mastering, and broadcast applications.
4. Finished physical hardware sold directly to users.
5. Recording studios, live sound stages, podcasting setups, and critical listening environments.
6. Recording engineers, musicians, podcasters, and audio professionals.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly to audio professionals and distributed through pro audio retailers.
8. The company leverages the acoustic engineering heritage and capsule designs of a legacy Vienna microphone brand while applying modern manufacturing techniques.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A majority-owned brand of DPA Microphones, slated for acquisition by Audiotonix.
Organization type: A privately held equipment manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of microphones and headphones.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017 by a core team of legacy acoustic engineers with centuries of cumulative experience.
Geography: Based and operating in Vienna, Austria.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play audio company focused entirely on microphone and headphone manufacturing.

points.name: DiGiGrid
points.description: UK pro audio brand building audio networking interfaces and DSP servers.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds audio networking interfaces and DSP servers for professional audio environments.
1. An equipment maker whose finished hardware interfaces and servers run in professional studios and live sound rigs.
2. Audio networking interfaces and DSP servers leveraging a third-party networking platform for ultra-low latency processing and distribution.
3. Ultra-low latency audio networking, digital format conversion, multichannel I/O routing, and plugin processing.
4. Finished hardware products, including rackmount and desktop interfaces and standalone DSP servers.
5. Live shows, studio sessions, control rooms, and broadcast environments.
6. Studios and musicians, live sound engineers, and broadcast facilities.
7. Its finished hardware is deployed by audio engineers in professional sound reinforcement and studio workflows.
8. It integrates a proprietary audio networking platform into dedicated hardware interfaces and DSP servers to handle demanding plugin loads.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Operates under a parent company and leverages a third-party audio networking platform.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a professional audio company.
Business model: Hardware sales of interfaces and DSP servers.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom and operating in the professional audio market.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Fourier Audio
points.description: UK audio technology company building networked hardware servers that run studio software plugins for live sound and theatre productions.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds dedicated hardware servers for running studio-grade software plugins in demanding live production environments. The company bridges the gap between studio audio software and live sound reinforcement for professional audio engineers.
1. An equipment maker whose hardware hosts VST3-native software plugins in dedicated touring-grade server chassis designed for live environments.
2. A Dante-connected server platform that runs VST3-native software plugins and recalls plugin states via MIDI connection.
3. The hardware delivers studio-grade audio plugin processing, cue snapshot recall over MIDI, and Dante audio network connectivity for live productions.
4. The company provides finished hardware units housed in touring-grade chassis with redundant power supplies.
5. The equipment is used in Broadway and West End theatre productions, international music tours, flypack rigs, and smaller live productions.
6. The company sells to professional audio engineers and live sound production crews.
7. Its hardware servers are deployed directly into live sound reinforcement rigs by professional audio engineers.
8. The hardware is specifically designed to bring studio-grade VST3 plugins into the demanding live production environment rather than the studio.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company is a brand within the Audiotonix portfolio and offers a DiGiCo integration mode for its hardware.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand acquired by Audiotonix in 2023.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of its audio plugin server units.
Scale and maturity: The company is a UK-based startup acquired in 2023.
Geography: The company is based in the United Kingdom and operates internationally across global live production markets.
Beyond audio: Audio technology is the entire focus of the company.

points.name: Harrison Audio
points.description: US audio equipment manufacturer building large-format analog mixing consoles, digital audio workstations, and audio processing plugins.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and software that designs and manufactures large-format analog mixing consoles, digital audio workstations, and audio processing plugins for recording studios, post-production facilities, and home recording enthusiasts.
1. An equipment and software maker that builds large-format analog mixing consoles and modular analog hardware alongside digital audio workstation software and audio plugins that run on studio computers.
2. The hardware relies on analog circuitry, transformer-coupled microphone preamps, and four-band parametric equalizer designs, while the software uses digital emulation of analog console workflows and signal processing.
3. The company delivers audio mixing, summing, monitoring, equalization, compression, and noise management.
4. Customers get finished hardware, modular 500 series hardware units, and software products.
5. The products are used in recording studios, post-production facilities, and home recording setups.
6. The organization sells to high-end recording studios, post-production facilities, and home recording enthusiasts.
7. Its finished hardware and software products are used directly by audio engineers and musicians in studio environments.
8. The approach is distinguished by a legacy analog filtering and equalizer design that achieves a specific sonic signature characterized by clean bass, clear vocals, and transparent highs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The brand operates as a part of Solid State Logic and leverages that parent company's global distribution network.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand of a publicly traded professional audio equipment company.
Business model: The company makes money through the direct sale of premium hardware and software products.
Scale and maturity: The company leverages a nearly 50-year legacy in the professional audio market.
Geography: The company reaches global customers through its parent company's distribution network.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play audio company, with its entire focus on professional audio equipment and software.

points.name: JH Audio
points.description: US in-ear monitor manufacturer making custom earphones for professional audio.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio equipment that builds custom in-ear monitors and universal-fit earphones for live performers and audio professionals.
1. An equipment maker that designs and builds finished in-ear monitors and earphones sold as physical hardware worn on stage or in the studio.
2. Multi-driver balanced armature arrays combined with acoustic waveguide technology to achieve phase coherence across frequency drivers.
3. High-fidelity sound reproduction, phase-correct audio delivery, and adjustable bass response tuning.
4. Finished hardware products sold as custom-molded or universal-fit in-ear monitors.
5. Live stage performances, mastering studios, and professional monitoring environments.
6. Live performers, touring musicians, and audio professionals.
7. Its finished hardware products are worn directly by performers and audio engineers in live and studio settings.
8. It maintains pricing power through proprietary acoustic waveguide designs and personalized custom-molded fitting.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partnered with L-Acoustics on in-ear monitor development and operates under the Sound Devices and Audiotonix parent group.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand within a larger pro audio corporate portfolio.
Business model: Hardware sales of premium custom and universal in-ear monitors priced between $1,200 and $3,500 per pair.
Scale and maturity: An established brand with premium market positioning and high unit prices, operating as part of a large pro audio group.
Geography: Based in the United States, serving the global professional audio market.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio company whose entire focus is in-ear monitoring hardware.

points.name: Sonible
points.description: Austrian software company developing AI-powered audio plugins that simplify mixing tasks for sound engineers.
points.bullets:
A software company that develops AI-based audio processing plug-ins and smart hardware for professional audio engineers.
1. An AI software developer whose audio processing plug-ins run as native software on engineers' digital audio workstations.
2. Artificial intelligence engines and neural networks perform adaptive learning and automatic parameter adjustments for equalization, compression, reverb, limiting and noise gating.
3. Intelligent equalization, frequency balancing, cross-channel processing, compression, reverb, limiting and noise gating.
4. Software plug-ins for digital audio workstations and finished hardware processors.
5. Professional recording studios and live sound engineering environments.
6. Live sound engineers, musicians and professional audio engineers.
7. Its plug-ins are loaded directly into the digital audio workstations of audio engineers and its hardware is integrated into live sound rigs.
8. It applies adaptive artificial intelligence algorithms to automate complex mixing tasks while providing detailed parameter control for professionals.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a brand within the Audiotonix portfolio and has co-launched plug-ins with Solid State Logic, with hardware recommended by KLANG:technologies.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a larger professional audio group.
Business model: Software licenses and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established brand with a mature product portfolio integrated into a major professional audio group.
Geography: It is based in Austria and operates globally.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on AI-based audio processing software and hardware for the professional audio market.

points.name: Sound Devices
points.description: Wisconsin audio equipment manufacturer building portable recorders, field mixers, and wireless systems for sound professionals.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures portable audio recorders, field production mixers, wireless microphone systems, and in-ear monitors for sound professionals in production and live sound.
1. An equipment maker that builds portable mixers, digital recorders, RF wireless transmitters and receivers, and in-ear monitors sold as finished hardware.
2. FPGA-based audio processing, RF wireless transmission, and microphone preamp circuitry.
3. Multi-track audio recording, audio mixing, wireless microphone transmission and reception, Ambisonics decoding, and remote gain control.
4. Finished hardware devices, accompanying mobile control software, and an open wireless receiver integration standard.
5. Film sets, television production, live events, houses of worship, broadcasting, touring, and acoustical test and measurement.
6. Sound professionals, production sound mixers, musicians, live sound engineers, and audio rental houses.
7. Its finished hardware products are used directly by sound professionals on location and integrated into live sound rigs by audio engineers.
8. It develops open hardware specifications for wireless receiver integration to provide unified power, audio, and control within its mixer-recorders.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its parent company is Audiotonix, and its SuperSlot standard partners include Lectrosonics, Wisycom, Sennheiser, and Audio Ltd.
Organization type: A brand within the Audiotonix group portfolio.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A company with over 25 years of operation and a global hardware presence.
Geography: Based in Reedsburg, Wisconsin, with additional offices in Madison, Wisconsin and Watford, UK, serving markets worldwide.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Biamp
points.description: US manufacturer building audio and video conferencing systems for commercial spaces.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio and video equipment that designs and manufactures digital signal processors, ceiling microphones, loudspeakers, sound masking systems, and control interfaces for commercial and enterprise installations.
1. An equipment maker whose finished hardware and companion configuration software run as installed AV systems in conference rooms and large public venues.
2. Digital signal processing platforms, microphone array beamtracking, and AV-over-IP networking.
3. Acoustic echo cancellation, microphone beamforming with 360-degree coverage, automixing, signal routing, and distributed sound masking.
4. Finished hardware devices, including audio processors, ceiling microphones, conferencing hubs, loudspeakers, and control panels, alongside design and configuration software.
5. Conference rooms, boardrooms, performing arts venues, stadiums, courtrooms, hospitals, transportation hubs, classrooms, and corporate open floor plans.
6. Enterprises, facility managers, and authorized commercial AV resellers and integrators.
7. Its finished hardware and software systems are installed by commercial integrators into corporate and public venue environments.
8. It provides comprehensive end-to-end networked AV ecosystems spanning audio processing, beamtracking microphones, sound masking, and video distribution.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It co-founded the Milan protocol under the Avnu Alliance, integrates with Sennheiser TeamConnect Ceiling 2 microphones, and holds Microsoft Teams Room and Zoom Rooms certifications.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales, software platform provisioning, and design assistance services.
Scale and maturity: A company with between 501 and 1,000 employees, founded in 1976.
Geography: Headquartered in Beaverton, Oregon, USA, with a global footprint spanning professional AV installations in over 100 countries.
Beyond audio: It develops audiovisual hardware and software, including AV-over-IP video distribution, touch interfaces, control systems, and room booking systems.

points.name: ClearOne
points.description: Utah-based professional audio company manufacturing conferencing solutions and beamforming microphone arrays.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio and video conferencing equipment that develops beamforming microphone arrays, DSP mixers, cameras and collaboration devices for enterprise meeting rooms.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished conferencing hardware and configuration software, sold as integrated room systems that run in conference rooms.
2. Beamforming microphone array algorithms, acoustic echo cancellation and noise cancellation running on dedicated digital signal processors.
3. Beamforming with adaptive steering, deep sidelobe rejection, echo cancellation, noise cancellation, auto-mixing, Voice Lift and camera tracking.
4. Finished hardware products including ceiling microphone arrays, DSP mixers, speakerphones, PTZ cameras and soundbars, plus configuration and management software.
5. Conference rooms, huddle rooms, mid-sized meeting rooms and enterprise collaboration spaces.
6. Enterprises, integrators and organizations outfitting meeting and collaboration spaces.
7. Its finished hardware and software are installed in meeting rooms by AV integrators and enterprises.
8. Integration of beamforming microphone arrays into ceiling tiles with frequency-invariant wideband coverage and deep sidelobe rejection below -40 dB.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its solutions support Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, GoToMeeting and Webex, and select patents and assets were acquired by Biamp.
Organization type: A publicly traded company that was acquired by Biamp.
Business model: Hardware sales, with supporting software and management platforms.
Scale and maturity: A publicly traded company on NASDAQ that introduced the first professional conferencing beamforming microphone array in 2012.
Geography: Based in Salt Lake City, Utah, USA, operating globally.
Beyond audio: The company also makes video conferencing cameras, collaboration devices and AV network management software alongside its audio products.

points.name: Rohde & Schwarz
points.description: German test and measurement company building audio analyzers and wireless testing equipment for hearing aids and communications systems.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of electronic test and measurement equipment that builds audio analyzers and radio communication testers for validating devices against international standards. The organization provides hardware analyzers and software packages used to test hearing aids, wireless audio, and Bluetooth connectivity for device makers and test labs.
1. An equipment maker that builds self-contained audio analyzers and radio communication testers sold as finished hardware instruments with companion software packages that run in laboratory and test environments.
2. Digital signal processing and RF generation and analysis architectures implemented in benchtop test instruments that perform standardized acoustic and wireless measurements.
3. Hearing aid measurements per ANSI and IEC standards, wireless and hands-free audio measurements, Bluetooth LE testing, and cellular and non-cellular radio communication testing.
4. Finished hardware instruments and companion software packages.
5. Hearing aid test labs, wireless device testing, broadcast and media, and radio communication test environments.
6. Device manufacturers, test laboratories, telecommunications companies, and broadcast and media organizations.
7. Its test instruments are used by device manufacturers and test labs to validate audio and wireless products against standards.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates technology from HEAD acoustics and the Interacoustics test box, and collaborates on Bluetooth LE testing with industry partners.
Organization type: A privately held global technology group.
Business model: Hardware instrument sales and companion software licenses.
Scale and maturity: A large, established organization with around 15,000 employees and net revenue of EUR 3.16 billion in the 2024/2025 fiscal year.
Geography: Based in Munich, Germany, and operates globally.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the organization provides test and measurement, secure communications, networks and cybersecurity, and broadcast and media systems.

points.name: Hall Technologies
points.description: Manufacturer building presentation switchers and scalers for audio-visual systems.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of audio-visual equipment that builds presentation switchers and scalers for pro AV integration, processing and routing multiple 4K video and audio sources for presentation environments.
1. An equipment maker that builds presentation switchers and scalers sold as finished hardware.
2. Digital signal processing and routing hardware that switches, scales and composites multiple 4K sources with picture-in-picture and picture-outside-picture.
3. Multi-source audio and video switching, scaling, compositing and presentation recording.
4. Finished hardware products.
5. Presentation spaces, meeting rooms and audio-visual installations.
6. Pro AV integrators, enterprises and facilities.
7. Its finished hardware is installed by integrators into enterprise presentation and meeting spaces.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Acquired the Atlona portfolio from Panduit.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Geography: Based in the United States.
Beyond audio: The company manufactures broader audio-visual and video distribution equipment beyond audio processing.

points.name: Sonance
points.description: California manufacturer building hidden architectural speakers for seamless home audio integration.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional and architectural audio equipment that designs and sells hidden, in-wall, in-ceiling, and surface-mount loudspeakers for custom integration and commercial sound reinforcement.
1. An equipment maker that designs finished loudspeakers sold as physical hardware for installation in built environments.
2. Passive loudspeaker designs incorporating high-excursion woofers, chambered tweeters, full-fidelity transformers, and weatherized enclosures.
3. High-fidelity sound reproduction and distributed audio line matching with selectable 70V, 100V, and 8-ohm operation.
4. Finished hardware loudspeakers and related architectural audio products.
5. Living spaces, commercial venues, and sound reinforcement installations requiring discreet architectural integration.
6. Custom integration professionals and commercial audio installers.
7. Its finished loudspeakers are installed by custom integrators into residential and commercial built environments.
8. It focuses on hidden architectural audio solutions engineered to integrate visually and physically into rooms and structures.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a brand under Dana Innovations and has acquired Blaze Audio, James Loudspeaker, and IPORT while collaborating with Pascal A/S.
Organization type: A privately held equipment manufacturer operating as a subsidiary brand.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished loudspeakers.
Scale and maturity: A company founded more than four decades ago with 201-500 reported employees.
Geography: Based in San Clemente, California, United States, operating globally in the professional audio sector.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play audio company.

points.name: Blaze Audio
points.description: Danish audio technology company building multi-zone power amplifiers and sound systems for commercial installations.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that develops, manufactures, and sells multi-zone DSP power amplifiers, networked wall controllers, and configuration software for commercial fixed-installation sound systems. The organization designs high-performance Class-D amplification and sound reinforcement loudspeakers, distributed through integrators and system designers for the commercial audio market.
1. An audio equipment maker that designs and manufactures networked DSP amplifiers, control hardware, and management software, sold as finished hardware and software products for commercial installations.
2. Class-D amplification combined with digital signal processing, Dante audio networking, and a proprietary software platform for routing and system control.
3. Multi-zone sound reinforcement, software-controlled DSP routing, remote volume and source control via networked wall controllers, and Dante-enabled audio distribution.
4. Finished hardware amplifiers, wall controllers, and a web-based DSP control platform.
5. Commercial fixed-installation multi-zone audio systems, sound reinforcement projects, and professional commercial venues.
6. System designers, integrators, and installers in the commercial audio market.
7. Its finished amplification hardware and software are sold directly to integration professionals to deploy in commercial fixed-installation audio systems.
8. Integration of Danish engineering heritage with OEM amplifier manufacturing infrastructure from its parent company to deliver configurable, easy-to-use multi-zone audio solutions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Parent company Pascal A/S and acquirer Sonance.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a parent manufacturing company, operating under an acquirer's corporate umbrella.
Business model: Hardware sales of amplifiers and controllers, along with associated commercial audio products.
Geography: Based in Copenhagen, Denmark, with operations spanning EMEA, APAC, the Middle East, and a Singapore office.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is professional audio amplification and control hardware for the commercial installation market.

points.name: K-array
points.description: Italian pro audio manufacturer building ultra-compact high-performance loudspeakers.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio equipment that designs and builds loudspeakers, amplifiers, and integrated audio-lighting systems for consultants, integrators, and sound engineers.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished loudspeakers, subwoofers, amplifiers, and digital matrix systems sold as physical hardware.
2. Professional loudspeaker transducers, line array elements, tri-axial driver configurations, passive radiators, and beam-steering technologies housed in compact aluminum enclosures.
3. High-output sound reinforcement, precise beam-steering, discrete architectural audio distribution, marine-grade weatherproofing, and integrated signal routing.
4. Finished hardware products sold through integrators, distributors, and dealers.
5. Concert tours, cathedrals, stadia, theatres, restaurants, hotels, corporate spaces, luxury residential installations, and marine environments.
6. Professional audio consultants, systems integrators, sound engineers, architects, and distributors.
7. Its finished hardware products are installed in venues and buildings by systems integrators and consultants.
8. Combines ultra-compact, high-power loudspeaker designs with aluminum enclosures and marine-grade construction for discreet architectural and live sound integration.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is being acquired by Powersoft Group and runs a United States subsidiary for domestic distribution.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer operating as a group of three brands.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished professional audio equipment.
Scale and maturity: A company founded in 1990 with a factory employing over 80 people, selling products in over 50 countries.
Geography: Headquartered in Florence, Italy with a United States subsidiary and warehouses outside Boston.
Beyond audio: The organization also designs architectural lighting products that integrate with its audio systems.

points.name: Cakewalk
points.description: US pro audio brand developing digital audio workstations for music production.
points.bullets:
A pro audio brand that develops digital audio workstation software for musicians, producers, and composers worldwide. It provides a software platform used to record, edit, mix, and produce music on personal computers.
1. A software company that builds digital audio workstation software sold as a desktop application running on personal computers.
2. Software-based multitrack audio recording, editing, and mixing algorithms running on desktop operating systems.
3. Audio recording, MIDI sequencing, editing, mixing, and effects processing for music production.
4. Software products distributed via digital download.
5. Recording studios, project studios, and home music production setups.
6. Musicians, producers, audio engineers, and composers.
7. Its software products are installed directly by end-users on their personal computers.
8. The brand operates as a major vendor in the digital audio workstation market with a long history of serving global music creators.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Acquired by BandLab after being divested by Gibson.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a larger music technology company.
Business model: Software sales or subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A major vendor in the pro audio market with global distribution.
Geography: Based in the US and operates globally.
