points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Panasonic Automotive Systems Company of America
points.description: US automotive supplier developing premium audio systems for electric vehicles.
points.bullets:
A tier-one automotive supplier and division of an electronics conglomerate that develops and manufactures integrated automotive infotainment, connectivity, and premium audio systems for vehicle manufacturers.
1. An equipment maker and systems integrator that builds finished automotive infotainment, cockpit domain controllers, and premium audio hardware integrated directly into vehicles.
2. Scalable modular audio architectures, cockpit domain controllers, and Android-based in-vehicle infotainment platforms running integrated voice assistant services.
3. Premium in-cabin audio reproduction, spatial 3D audio rendering, infotainment display management, digital cluster control, and embedded voice assistant integration.
4. Finished hardware components, software platforms, and integrated audio systems supplied directly to vehicle assembly lines.
5. Electric vehicles, luxury SUVs, automotive cabins, digital cockpits, and autonomous driving environments.
6. Automakers and electric vehicle manufacturers.
7. Its integrated systems and audio hardware are designed by automakers into their production vehicles.
8. It combines premium branded audio system design with broader cockpit domain controller and infotainment platform integration for electric vehicles.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Fisker, Range Rover, Google, Amazon Alexa, and Kanzi UI.
Organization type: A subsidiary division of a publicly traded electronics conglomerate.
Business model: Tier-one automotive system sales and component supply contracts.
Scale and maturity: A global tier-one automotive supplier operating as a major regional division of a large electronics corporation.
Geography: Based in Peachtree City, Georgia, USA, operating as the North American affiliate of a global automotive systems entity.
Beyond audio: The organization develops broader automotive technologies including in-vehicle infotainment platforms, cockpit domain controllers, electric powertrain systems, cabin air purification, and autonomous driving concepts.

points.name: Infinity
points.description: US car audio manufacturer building aftermarket speakers, amplifiers, and multimedia players for automotive sound systems.
points.bullets:
A maker of aftermarket automotive audio equipment that designs and sells replacement speakers, amplifiers and multimedia players for consumers upgrading factory-installed car audio systems.
1. A maker of finished audio hardware that designs and sells loudspeakers, amplifiers and car multimedia players to consumers.
2. The core technologies include loudspeaker driver designs with extended-bass cones, 3-ohm voice coils for true 4-ohm performance, UniPivot directional tweeters, and multichannel amplifier topologies with variable electronic crossovers.
3. The company delivers extended bass response, directional audio aiming, multichannel audio amplification, and smartphone-paired media streaming in a vehicle.
4. The products are delivered as finished hardware, including full-range speakers, component loudspeakers, amplifiers, and head units.
5. The equipment is used in cars and vehicles for aftermarket audio system upgrades and interior or exterior media playback.
6. The organization sells directly to consumers through retail channels.
7. Its finished audio hardware is purchased by consumers to replace factory-installed audio systems in their vehicles.
8. The approach is distinguished by high-value, easy-to-install replacement audio solutions integrated into a broader global corporate audio ecosystem.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization operates as an audio brand under Harman International, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Samsung Electronics.
Organization type: The company is a subsidiary brand of a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: The organization makes money through the direct retail sale of finished aftermarket automotive audio hardware across a range of price points.
Scale and maturity: The brand offers a wide range of products spanning from entry-level components priced under one hundred dollars to high-performance systems, backed by a global corporate parent.
Geography: The company operates globally as part of a large international electronics corporation.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is on automotive audio equipment and aftermarket car multimedia products.

points.name: Neurochrome
points.description: Audio equipment company making DIY audio kits, amplifiers, and high-performance audio measurement devices.
points.bullets:
An audio equipment company that produces audio kits, amplifiers, power supplies, and chassis, and is developing a high-performance audio analyzer for measurement applications.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware and electronic kits sold to customers.
2. Analog and digital circuit design for audio amplification and an ASIO-compatible measurement instrument.
3. Audio signal amplification, power supply regulation, and high-performance audio measurement.
4. Finished hardware products, electronic kits, and chassis.
5. Electronics workbenches and audio testing setups.
6. Audio enthusiasts and engineers.
7. Its finished hardware and kits are used directly by hobbyists and professionals in audio projects.
8. It targets high-performance audio analyzer performance at a substantially reduced cost compared to advanced measurement devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The NAx1 audio analyzer design is a collaboration with Jens Hansen.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Geography: Founded by Tom Christiansen.
Beyond audio: It produces power supplies and chassis for electronics projects.

points.name: Axiometrix Solutions
points.description: Parent company overseeing test and measurement brands that build audio analysis equipment and microphones.
points.bullets:
A parent organization of multiple test and measurement brands that provides audio and vibration analysis equipment and solutions for engineers.
1. A test solutions provider that owns brands making finished measurement hardware and software used in engineering labs and production lines.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Owned by Battery Ventures and operating brands including Audio Precision and GRAS Sound & Vibration.
Organization type: A privately held parent company of multiple measurement brands.
Business model: Hardware and software sales through its subsidiary brands.
Beyond audio: A broader test and measurement entity whose portfolio includes acoustic, vibration and general instrumentation brands.

points.name: QuantAsylum
points.description: US test equipment manufacturer building affordable precision audio analyzers for manufacturing facilities and hobbyists.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that builds precision audio analyzers and companion software for measuring audio signals, sold to manufacturing test facilities, audio professionals and hobbyists.
1. A test equipment maker that builds audio analyzers and companion control software, sold as finished hardware instruments.
2. The analyzers use 32-bit ADCs and DACs, balanced inputs and outputs, and digitally controlled attenuators controlled by measurement software.
3. The instruments measure total harmonic distortion, power and other audio signal parameters.
4. Customers receive finished hardware audio analyzers alongside associated software.
5. The analyzers are used in manufacturing test facilities, electronics workbenches and personal hobbyist setups.
6. The organization sells to audio professionals, manufacturing test facilities and hobbyists.
7. Its finished test instruments are distributed by regional electronics distributors to end users.
8. The organization positions its instruments as affordable, high-performance precision measurement devices that serve as lower-cost alternatives to high-end audio analyzers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Elektor and Saelig Company act as regional distributors for the hardware.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of its audio analyzers.
Geography: It is based in the USA and operates through distributors in Europe and other regions.
Beyond audio: Audio test and measurement is the organization's sole focus.

points.name: Listen
points.description: US audio technology company making hardware and software for testing audio devices in production environments.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and equipment company that provides professional audio test and measurement systems, consisting of software-based audio analyzers, multichannel audio interfaces, and calibrated precision microphones, used by manufacturers to test and characterize audio devices in production and laboratory environments.
1. A developer tools company and equipment maker whose audio measurement software runs on standard computers paired with the organization's own USB audio interfaces and measurement microphones.
2. Software-based virtual instruments including signal generators, oscilloscopes, and spectrum analyzers, combined with customizable test sequences, running on host computers connected to high-resolution multichannel hardware interfaces and calibrated acoustic transducers.
3. Audio and electroacoustic measurement, analysis, and characterization, including hearing aid testing to ANSI and IEC standards, across loudspeakers, headphones, microphones, smart devices, and communication systems.
4. Software products sold alongside finished measurement hardware, including audio interfaces and calibrated microphone kits, with prewritten and customizable test scripts.
5. Production lines and laboratory test environments for loudspeakers, headphones, microphones, smart devices, communication systems, hearing aids, and automotive audio.
6. Audio device manufacturers, electroacoustic engineers, and production test facilities.
7. Its measurement systems are deployed by device manufacturers in their production lines and R&D labs, and its software integrates with test chambers and microphones supplied by other test equipment vendors.
8. Its software-based audio analyzer architecture replaces dedicated standalone test equipment with virtual instruments running on a host computer, offering customizable test sequences and modular hardware configurations.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Interacoustics, Brüel & Kjær, and G.R.A.S. supply compatible test chambers, couplers, microphones, and fixtures; the organization is an investor in Legato.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses and hardware sales of test interfaces and measurement microphones.
Scale and maturity: An established company with over 30 years of experience operating globally.
Geography: Based in Boston, Massachusetts, USA, operating globally.
Beyond audio: Audio test and measurement is its entire focus.

points.name: DAAS
points.description: German acoustic measurement company producing PC-based systems for measuring loudspeaker frequency and impulse responses.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds PC-controlled acoustic measurement systems used to measure loudspeaker responses and other acoustic parameters for engineers and designers.
1. A developer tools company whose acoustic measurement software and hardware systems run on PCs for engineers testing audio equipment.
2. PC-based acoustic measurement systems that process impulse responses to derive frequency responses, cumulative spectral decay, and quasi-anechoic measurements.
3. Impulse response measurement, frequency response measurement, cumulative spectral decay analysis, quasi-anechoic response calculation, and low-frequency response combination from near-field woofer and port measurements.
4. Software and hardware measurement systems.
5. Loudspeaker testing and acoustic measurement in engineering and design environments.
6. Audio engineers, loudspeaker designers, and acoustics professionals.
7. Its measurement systems are used by engineers and designers to test and evaluate loudspeakers and audio equipment.
8. Provides quasi-anechoic response calculations and routines to combine near-field woofer and port measurements for low-frequency response determination.
points.profile: Beyond audio: Acoustic measurement and test instrumentation is its entire focus.

points.name: DRA Labs
points.description: Audio laboratory building speaker measurement systems for acoustic testing.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds acoustic measurement systems for loudspeaker testing, providing instrumentation that generates frequency response and dispersion data for audio reviewers and engineers.
1. A developer tools company whose acoustic measurement instruments run as hardware-software products used by engineers and reviewers to test loudspeakers.
2. Fast Fourier Transform-based measurement using maximum-length sequence stimulus signals to produce response data files with a linear frequency scale.
3. Farfield frequency response measurement, dispersion measurement, and loudspeaker acoustic analysis.
4. Finished measurement hardware and software products.
5. Loudspeaker testing and acoustic measurement in review and laboratory settings.
6. Audio reviewers, acoustic laboratories, and loudspeaker engineers.
7. Its measurement instruments are used by audio reviewers and engineers to characterize loudspeakers.
8. It provides a dedicated loudspeaker measurement system based on FFT analysis producing response data with a linear frequency scale.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held laboratory.
Business model: Hardware and software instrument sales.
Beyond audio: Its focus is entirely on acoustic measurement instrumentation.

points.name: B&K
points.description: Danish audio measurement manufacturer making precision microphones and analysis systems for loudspeaker testing and acoustic measurements.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of measurement microphones and audio measurement systems for recording and loudspeaker measurement applications. It builds calibrated reference microphones and measurement hardware used to generate and record audio signals in anechoic chambers. Its products are used by engineers and acousticians for loudspeaker measurements and recording work.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment that builds measurement microphones and hardware measurement systems sold as finished hardware.
2. The core technology comprises omnidirectional microphone capsules with flat frequency responses and hardware systems for generating and recording audio signals at high sampling rates.
3. It delivers calibrated, flat-frequency-response audio capture and signal generation for loudspeaker measurement and recording.
4. Customers get its products as finished hardware.
5. Its products are used in anechoic chambers, recording studios and loudspeaker measurement setups.
6. It sells to engineers, acousticians and measurement professionals.
7. Its finished measurement hardware is purchased directly by acoustic measurement professionals and engineers.
8. It provides highly calibrated microphones with tight flat-response tolerances for measurement-grade applications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: ATI has purchased it from the bank that administered its bankruptcy, and George Reamsnyder has opened a fee-based service facility for its products.
Organization type: It was a privately held company that has gone bankrupt and been purchased from the bank.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of microphones and measurement systems.
Scale and maturity: It was a longstanding US audio company with US manufacturing that has ceased operations.
Geography: It is based in the US and manufactures in the US.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Earthworks
points.description: Manufacturer of precision microphones used for audio measurement and recording.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures calibrated microphones and microphone preamplifiers for audio measurement and recording applications.
1. An equipment maker that builds calibrated measurement microphones and preamplifiers sold as finished hardware.
2. High-accuracy audio capture and measurement using calibrated microphone capsules and low-noise preamplifier circuitry.
3. Finished microphone and preamplifier hardware products.
4. Measurement setups, piano recording, studio recording and acoustic testing environments.
5. Recording studios, musicians, audio engineers and acoustic measurement professionals.
6. Its finished hardware products are used directly by engineers and musicians in measurement and studio recording workflows.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales.

points.name: Mitey Mike
points.description: Manufacturer producing calibrated microphones for audio measurements.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of calibrated microphones used in audio measurements, providing specialized hardware for the test and measurement layer of the audio technology stack.
1. An equipment maker that builds calibrated measurement microphones and sells them as finished hardware.
2. Precision microphone capsules engineered and individually calibrated for accurate, repeatable audio measurement.
3. Audio capture with known sensitivity and frequency response for measurement and analysis.
4. Finished physical hardware products.
5. Test and measurement settings, acoustic test benches, and measurement environments.
6. Professionals and customers operating in the test and measurement sector.
7. Its finished hardware is used by engineers and acousticians as instrumentation for audio measurement and validation.
points.profile:
Business model: Direct sales of specialized hardware products.
Beyond audio: Audio technology is the entire focus of the organization's manufacturing operations.

points.name: Studio Six Digital
points.description: Mobile app developer creating iOS acoustic measurement software.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and software that develops a calibrated acoustic measurement microphone and an iOS acoustic measurement suite for audio professionals and installers.
1. An equipment maker and software developer that builds calibrated measurement microphones and an iOS acoustic measurement application that runs on Apple mobile devices.
2. The measurement suite uses real-time analysis, sound level measurement, log swept sine and room response algorithms running on mobile devices, paired with calibrated measurement microphones.
3. The organization delivers real-time spectrum analysis, sound pressure level measurement, log swept sine analysis and room response measurement.
4. Customers get the offering as finished hardware microphones and as a software application installed on iOS devices.
5. The products are used in acoustic measurement, room analysis and audio system calibration.
6. The company sells to audio professionals, acousticians and system installers.
7. Its hardware microphones and software applications are used directly by end users for acoustic measurement and system calibration.
8. The organization pairs calibrated measurement microphones with an integrated iOS application that supports importing external calibration files.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization integrates with calibration files provided by a consumer audio parts brand.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of calibrated microphones and software sales of the iOS measurement application.
Geography: The company operates in the United States.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on acoustic measurement tools and audio analysis.

points.name: Holoplot
points.description: Berlin pro audio manufacturer building 3D spatial sound systems for immersive experiences.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures matrix array sound systems for immersive sound reinforcement, and develops accompanying control and simulation software for audio system designers and integrators.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished loudspeaker arrays and audio modules, alongside proprietary control and simulation software that runs on standard computing hardware.
2. Wave Field Synthesis and 3D audio beamforming algorithms processing individual drivers in two-dimensional matrix arrays to create controlled sound fields and authentic spatial localization.
3. 3D sound field manipulation, multiple simultaneous sound field generation from single arrays, complete horizontal and vertical beam control, and authentic sound localization at high sound pressure levels.
4. Finished hardware loudspeaker modules and arrays, alongside proprietary software for system design, acoustic simulation, and operational control.
5. Large-scale immersive entertainment venues, permanent installations, and live events requiring spatial sound reinforcement.
6. Immersive experience operators, entertainment venue owners, event producers, and professional audio system integrators.
7. Its finished hardware and software are deployed directly into permanent installations and live event productions by venue operators and integrators.
8. It scales wave field synthesis technology to high sound pressure level applications through large matrix arrays of individually processed drivers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Acquired by Sphere Entertainment, with measurement technology from Klippel, acoustic simulation software compatibility with AFMG EASE, and deployments for Nintendo and Illuminarium.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded entertainment company.
Business model: Hardware sales of loudspeaker arrays and modules, alongside associated software.
Scale and maturity: An established company with proven commercial deployments in large-scale global entertainment venues.
Geography: Based in Berlin, Germany, deploying systems in global entertainment markets.
Beyond audio: Audio is the sole focus of the organization.

points.name: Von Schweikert Audio
points.description: Loudspeaker manufacturer building high-fidelity speakers with powered woofers for audiophiles.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds full-range loudspeakers featuring powered woofers, a midrange unit, and a tweeter for audiophile consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished loudspeakers sold as physical hardware in listening rooms.
2. The core technology is a full-range loudspeaker design combining discrete driver units with powered woofers and passive radiating elements.
3. The equipment delivers full-range sound reproduction across low, mid, and high frequency bands.
4. Customers receive finished physical loudspeaker hardware.
5. The loudspeakers are used in high-fidelity listening rooms and consumer audio setups.
6. The company sells to consumers and audiophiles.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly into consumer audio systems.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of finished loudspeakers.
Scale and maturity: The company is an established audio manufacturer.
Geography: The company operates within the consumer audio market.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is audio hardware manufacturing.

points.name: Open Acoustic Devices

An equipment maker that builds miniature acoustic monitoring hardware for researchers and conservationists.

2. A battery-powered recording device built around a MEMS microphone.
3. Autonomous acoustic recording of wildlife activity.
4. Finished hardware devices.
5. Field deployments for wildlife monitoring and ecological research.
6. Researchers, conservationists, and academic institutions.
points.profile:
Organization type: An organization or research initiative.

points.name: HEAD acoustics
points.description: German acoustic engineering company developing measurement systems and analysis software for evaluating vehicle sound quality and voice communications.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and equipment company that provides hardware, software and simulation systems for measuring, analyzing and optimizing acoustics, vibration, speech and audio quality for device manufacturers and developers.
1. A developer tools and equipment maker whose test and measurement instruments and analysis software run in engineering laboratories and simulation environments.
2. Acoustic measurement and simulation systems using binaural artificial heads, data acquisition hardware and perceptual modeling algorithms.
3. Sound and vibration analysis, audio and speech quality assessment, acoustic environment and background noise simulation, and voice recognition performance testing.
4. Hardware data acquisition platforms, artificial heads, acoustic cameras, analysis software, simulation software and consulting services.
5. Automotive development, telephony, smart home devices, broadcast AV, staging and audio product development laboratories.
6. Device manufacturers, automotive suppliers and developers.
7. Its measurement and simulation tools are used by manufacturers and developers to test, benchmark and tune their audio products during development.
8. It provides holistic acoustic test environments that combine binaural recording hardware with software for objective, perception-based quality scoring.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Yobe, Rohde & Schwarz.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales, software licenses and consulting services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1986, holding a 3 percent share of the acoustic measurement market revenue in 2025.
Geography: Headquartered in Germany with subsidiaries in China, France, Italy, India, Japan, South Korea, the UK and the USA.
Beyond audio: It focuses on acoustics, vibration and speech-related measurement and analysis.

points.name: NHT (Now Hear This)
points.description: US speaker manufacturer building acoustic suspension speakers and subwoofers for home theater systems.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs and manufactures passive and powered loudspeakers and subwoofers for home audio enthusiasts building stereo and home theater systems.
1. A consumer audio equipment maker whose finished loudspeaker and subwoofer hardware runs in home listening rooms.
2. Traditional acoustic suspension loudspeaker designs using matched dome tweeters, cone woofers and up-firing drivers.
3. Two-way and three-way sound reproduction, low-frequency bass extension and Dolby Atmos spatial audio elevation effects.
4. Finished passive and powered speaker hardware, including floor-standing, satellite, center-channel and add-on modules.
5. Home stereo systems and multi-channel Dolby Atmos home theater setups.
6. Consumers and home audio enthusiasts.
7. Its finished speakers are sold through consumer retail channels to end users.
8. It delivers high-performance acoustics using compact footprints and broad dispersion for home system builders.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales through retail channels.
Geography: A company operating in the home audio market and distributing through online retail channels.

points.name: HBK
points.description: Danish measurement technology company producing high-precision microphones, sound level meters, and audio analyzers for acoustic and vibration testing.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio and vibration measurement equipment that supplies precision microphones, sound level meters, analyzers, acoustic calibrators, head and torso simulators, and data acquisition software for acoustic compliance testing, research, and product development.
1. An equipment maker and software developer that builds finished acoustic measurement hardware and analysis software sold as laboratory instruments and application licenses running on dedicated hardware and PCs.
2. The core technology comprises precision acoustic transducers, analog front ends, head and torso simulators with realistic ear simulators, and modular data acquisition and analysis software.
3. The organization delivers high-precision sound pressure level measurement, frequency analysis, acoustic calibration, building acoustics measurement, hearing aid measurement, transducer measurement, and sound imaging.
4. Customers receive the offerings as finished hardware instruments, measurement microphones, test chambers, acoustic calibrators, and licensed software applications.
5. The products are used in acoustic laboratories, product development facilities, compliance testing facilities, building acoustics assessments, and consumer audio testing labs.
6. The organization sells to enterprises, research institutions, consumer electronics brands, acoustic test laboratories, and developers of audio measurement systems.
7. Its measurement instruments are used by device manufacturers and test labs to validate and develop audio products.
8. Its approach is distinguished by a long-established focus on high-precision Class 1 measurement standards and a comprehensive ecosystem of modular hardware and software built for acoustic analysis.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its products are used by consumer audio reviewers and supplied as components for use with test software platforms developed by third-party audio measurement software companies.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand of a larger engineering group.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of instruments and microphones and software licenses or subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: Established in 1942, it is a large, long-established provider with a multi-decade presence in the acoustic measurement market.
Geography: It is based in Denmark and operates globally.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, it provides sensors, data acquisition systems, and equipment for vibration measurement, structural dynamics, and propulsion efficiency testing.

points.name: DAS
points.description: Professional audio manufacturer building precision condenser microphones for acoustic measurement and studio recording.
points.bullets:
A professional audio equipment manufacturer that designs and manufactures precision condenser measurement microphones and related solutions for acoustic analysis, studio recording, broadcast, and sound reinforcement.
1. A professional audio equipment maker that designs and sells finished microphone hardware for laboratory-grade precision and professional audio applications.
2. The core technology is precision microphone design, including calibrated, omnidirectional electret condenser capsules engineered for a flat frequency response and uncolored sound capture.
3. It delivers high-clarity, low-noise sound capture with exceptional reliability and precise acoustic measurement capabilities for critical analysis.
4. Customers get finished hardware, premium measurement microphones, alongside calibration services and serialized calibration files.
5. The products are used in acoustic analysis, studio recording, broadcast, theater, and sound reinforcement environments.
6. Customers are audio professionals, including those performing on-location acoustic analysis, speaker driver output measurement, and whole-room response testing.
7. Its finished measurement microphones and calibration data are used directly by audio professionals and integrated into acoustic test and measurement workflows.
8. The approach is distinguished by the production of calibrated, flat-frequency-response microphones that offer pure, uncolored sound with unparalleled specifications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its products are paired with third-party audio-analysis software applications, and the organization has roots tracing back to its predecessor, a pioneer in precisely accurate measurement microphones.
Organization type: It is a pure-play professional audio equipment manufacturer with a history tracing back to the 1950s.
Business model: It makes money through direct sales of premium microphone hardware, alongside calibration services, serialized calibration files, and related tools.
Scale and maturity: Leveraging decades of microphone design experience, the organization operates a purpose-built factory to serve a global professional market.
Geography: The company is based in Denmark, where it operates a purpose-built factory, and sells its products globally.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio company whose entire focus is the design and manufacturing of high-end professional audio solutions for measurement and recording applications.

points.name: Tecnare
points.description: Spanish manufacturer building loudspeakers and power amplifiers for professional sound reinforcement.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures loudspeaker cabinets and power amplifiers for professional sound reinforcement, providing finished hardware and setup software for live, touring, and installed sound environments.
1. An equipment maker that builds analog and Class D power amplifiers, loudspeakers, and configuration software sold as finished hardware and software products running in professional sound systems.
2. Analog and Class D amplifier electronics and loudspeaker cabinet acoustics, supported by acoustic simulation data formatted as GLL files for system design platforms.
3. Multi-channel sound amplification across a wide range of power outputs, and sound reinforcement for venues and live events using loudspeaker enclosures and subwoofers.
4. Finished hardware products, including power amplifiers and loudspeakers, plus system configuration software and acoustic simulation data files.
5. Live touring sound systems, installed sound in venues, sports competition audio, restaurants, and nightclubs.
6. Audio professionals, system integrators, installation contractors, and regional audio equipment distributors.
7. Its finished hardware is specified and installed by integration companies and distributors into professional sound reinforcement venues.
8. It supplies both the power amplification and the loudspeaker enclosures as finished hardware, accompanied by proprietary configuration software and acoustic simulation data for system design.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its acoustic data integrates with AFMG EASE software platforms, and its equipment is distributed and installed by regional integrators.
Organization type: A privately held company and established audio brand.
Business model: Hardware sales of amplifiers and loudspeakers.
Scale and maturity: A brand founded in 1984 serving professionals in over 40 countries.
Geography: Based in Spain, operating through a global network of distributors.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is professional audio equipment manufacturing.

points.name: AFMG
points.description: Berlin software company developing acoustic simulation tools for room and loudspeaker modeling.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds acoustic simulation and measurement software for sound system designers, acousticians and loudspeaker manufacturers.
1. A developer tools company whose simulation and measurement software runs as desktop applications on Windows PCs.
2. Geometric acoustic modeling, electroacoustic simulation and acoustic measurement algorithms.
3. Room acoustic modeling, loudspeaker behavior prediction, speech intelligibility prediction, coverage mapping and FIR filter generation.
4. Software products distributed through software licenses and activation keys, with a free simulation viewer and a database of loudspeaker data files.
5. Sound system design for venues, room acoustic simulations, line array configuration and acoustic measurement.
6. Acousticians, sound system designers, audio engineers, consultants, loudspeaker manufacturers and system integrators.
7. Its simulation software is used by consultants and system designers to model sound systems prior to installation in venues.
8. The company's software is a brand-agnostic industry standard for acoustic simulation, supported by a proprietary loudspeaker data format and a database of over 30,000 loudspeaker files.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company cooperates with SDA Software Design Ahnert GmbH and collaborates with L-Acoustics for software workflow integration.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: Founded in the early 1990s and established as an industry standard software provider.
Geography: Based in Berlin, Germany, with a North American team.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on acoustic simulation, modeling and measurement software.

points.name: COMSOL
points.description: Swedish software company developing multiphysics simulation tools for modeling acoustic performance in audio R&D.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds multiphysics simulation software with an acoustics add-on module, used by engineers and researchers to model acoustic performance and sound fields.
1. A developer tools company whose simulation platform and acoustics module run as installed software on engineering workstations and local servers.
2. Finite element and multiphysics modeling solvers that couple acoustic formulations with structural dynamics and fluid dynamics from infrasound to ultrasound.
3. Acoustic simulation of sound fields, internal air velocity, and driver diaphragm behavior.
4. The organization provides its tools as licensed software products and add-on modules, with a server product for deploying simulation apps to users.
5. The tools are used in headphone research and development, concert hall acoustics, and loudspeaker design.
6. The company sells to simulation specialists, engineers, and research organizations.
7. Its simulation software is used by product engineers to design and evaluate acoustic devices and spaces.
8. The platform couples acoustic modeling with multiple physics domains in a single environment, enabling multiscale and coupled-physics analysis.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held software company.
Business model: It makes money through software licenses and add-on module sales.
Scale and maturity: The US subsidiary was established in 1998, operating as part of a larger Swedish corporate group.
Geography: The parent company is based in Stockholm, Sweden, with a US subsidiary in Burlington, Massachusetts.
Beyond audio: The organization develops general-purpose multiphysics simulation software for fluid dynamics, structural mechanics, and other fields beyond acoustics.

points.name: Fulcrum Acoustic
points.description: US professional audio manufacturer building loudspeakers and software for immersive venue sound.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio equipment and developer of audio software that designs and builds loudspeakers, amplifiers, and digital signal processing technology, alongside acoustic simulation and immersive audio software for installed venues.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished loudspeakers, amplifiers, and audio processors, and develops its own companion design and simulation software.
2. Coaxial loudspeaker designs, passive cardioid sound dispersion technology, temporal equalization algorithms, and object-based immersive audio processing.
3. Sound dispersion control, directivity management, room acoustic correction, active acoustics, and object-based mixing.
4. The company sells finished hardware devices and software platforms for system design and simulation.
5. Performance spaces, sports venues, houses of worship, and public environments.
6. Audio professionals, system integrators, and venue operators.
7. Its loudspeakers and processors are installed in public venues by audio professionals.
8. The company integrates digital signal processing as a core design ingredient in its coaxial loudspeakers, using temporal equalization to improve real-world sound in difficult rooms.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company operates as an independent brand under its parent company, Bose Professional.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand operating under a parent company.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales and software provision.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2008, the company was established and later acquired.
Geography: Based in Whitinsville, Massachusetts, USA, with products deployed in venues worldwide.
Beyond audio: The company's focus is entirely on professional audio.

points.name: Treble Technologies
points.description: Icelandic startup developing cloud-based acoustic simulation software for product design and AI training.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides a cloud-based acoustic simulation platform used by engineers to virtually prototype audio hardware and generate synthetic audio datasets for training and testing AI models.
1. A developer tools company whose acoustic simulation software and software development kit run in the cloud.
2. A cloud-native hybrid solver combining finite element and geometrical acoustics to simulate wave-based sound propagation, capturing diffraction, phase effects, and interference.
3. It delivers room impulse response generation, binaural spatial audio rendering, acoustic digital twins, and synthetic acoustic scene creation.
4. Customers access the simulation tools through a cloud-based web application and a Python software development kit.
5. The technology is used for virtual prototyping of wearables and smart glasses, architectural room acoustics, and generating training data for speech enhancement and noise suppression models.
6. The company sells to device manufacturers, audio hardware brands, acoustic engineering firms, and AI model developers.
7. Its simulation software and synthetic datasets are used directly by product engineers and AI researchers to design and validate audio hardware and voice models.
8. Its hybrid wave-based solver computes complex acoustic phenomena up to 100 times faster than conventional methods while maintaining physically accurate results across the full frequency spectrum.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners and customers include Amazon, Logitech, Jabra, L-Acoustics, Arup, Saint-Gobain, Spatial, and investors such as Paladin Capital Group.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup and a university spin-off.
Business model: It generates revenue through cloud software licenses and software development kit subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: The company was founded in 2020, employs around 35 people, and has raised $18 million in Series A and A2 funding rounds.
Geography: The company is based in Iceland and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on acoustic simulation and synthetic audio data generation.

points.name: Audionamix
points.description: US audio software company isolating individual sounds like vocals from mixed recordings using AI.
points.bullets:
An audio software company that develops AI-driven source separation algorithms and intellectual property for professional audio engineers, providing tools to isolate or extract specific audio elements from mixed recordings for film, television and music production.
1. An AI model and software developer whose source separation software runs as standalone software products on professional workstations.
2. Artificial intelligence processes and advanced algorithms that differentiate and separate sound sources within mixed audio recordings.
3. Audio source separation and the isolation or extraction of specific audio elements from mixed recordings.
4. Software products and licensed intellectual property containing proprietary source separation algorithms.
5. Film, television and music production.
6. Business-to-business clients and professional audio engineers who require isolated audio tracks.
7. Its software and proprietary algorithms are used by professional audio engineers to manipulate, remix or restore audio in professional production workflows.
8. It was an early entrant into the market and established a position in the niche field of audio source separation.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company operating in the professional audio equipment and software sector.
Business model: It monetizes its technology through specialized software solutions and licensing its proprietary algorithms.
Beyond audio: It operates exclusively in the professional audio software sector, with its entire focus on audio source separation technology.

points.name: GPU Audio
points.description: Audio technology company offloading complex audio processing from the CPU to the GPU.
points.bullets:
An audio technology company that develops GPU-accelerated audio processing software and plugins, providing an SDK for developers to build effects that offload DSP tasks from the CPU to the GPU for audio professionals.
1. A software and developer tools company whose audio plugins and SDK run on consumer GPUs inside desktop digital audio workstations.
2. GPU-accelerated digital signal processing algorithms, including neural network amp modeling and finite impulse response convolution, that execute on graphics processing units.
3. Low-latency multi-channel audio processing, convolution reverb, neural amp modeling and FIR convolution effects.
4. Software plugins for end users and a software development kit for developers.
5. Professional audio production environments, digital audio workstations, studio workflows and live sound processing.
6. Audio professionals, developers, musicians and audio software retailers.
7. Its developer SDK is used by plugin developers to build GPU-accelerated audio effects, and its finished plugins are sold to audio professionals through retailers.
8. It offloads complex audio DSP workloads from the CPU to the GPU to achieve nearly zero latency for pro-level effects.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its SDK supports graphics cards from NVIDIA and AMD, its plugins are distributed through Sweetwater, and Shure is testing integration of its DSP technology.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software license sales and a silver conference sponsorship.

points.name: ISO
points.description: Geneva-based standards organization publishing global audio compression standards like AAC.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops and publishes international audio coding standards, specifying compression formats and related conformance specifications for use by the audio industry.
1. A standards organization that develops audio coding specifications that are sold as published international standards implemented by others.
2. Audio compression formats defined by international standards specifications.
3. Standardized audio compression, gapless encoding and low-complexity enhancement coding.
4. Published international standard specifications and final draft international standards.
5. Audio streaming and storage.
6. Device makers, codec implementers, software developers and broadcasters.
7. Its specifications are implemented and built into products by codec developers and device manufacturers.
8. It produces formal international standards through a consensus process among national standards organizations rather than building commercial products.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The International Electrotechnical Commission is a close collaborator under a joint agreement.
Organization type: An international standards body composed of representatives from various national standards organizations.
Business model: Publication of international standards.
Scale and maturity: A long-established international organization operating globally.
Geography: Based in Geneva, Switzerland, operating internationally.
Beyond audio: It develops international standards across fields beyond audio including quality management, information technology and multimedia coding.

points.name: IEC
points.description: Geneva-based standards organization publishing technical specifications for electroacoustic and audiometric test and measurement equipment.
points.bullets:
A standards body that publishes technical standards defining performance specifications, test methods and calibration requirements for electroacoustic and audiometric test and measurement equipment, serving equipment manufacturers, health professionals and metrology bodies.
1. A standards body that develops technical standards distributed as published documents.
2. Formal technical specifications that define mandatory instrument functions, test conditions, stimulus signal parameters and harmonic distortion requirements.
3. Standardized measurement and calibration of otoacoustic emissions, audiometric instrument conformance testing and acoustic stimulus level control.
4. Published technical standards documents.
5. Audiometric test and measurement equipment and electroacoustic measurement instruments.
6. Equipment manufacturers, occupational health professionals and national metrology bodies.
7. Its standards are used by equipment manufacturers to build compliant measurement instruments and by metrology bodies to perform periodic calibration.
8. It defines mandatory functions, permitted deviation limits and conformance test methods rather than building physical instruments or software.
points.profile:
Organization type: A standards body.
Business model: Publication of technical standards.
Geography: It operates internationally.

points.name: Radial Engineering
points.description: Canadian pro audio manufacturer building signal distribution tools for live sound and studios.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures analog and digital signal management, distribution, and direct box tools for studio, live sound, broadcast, and installation environments.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished professional audio hardware products sold as standalone units.
2. Analog signal routing and isolation circuits incorporating premium components such as Jensen transformers and discrete Class-A circuitry, alongside AES digital audio transmission over standard Cat 5 cable.
3. Audio signal routing, distribution, level matching, isolation, and re-amping for microphones and instruments.
4. The company delivers finished hardware products in heavy-duty steel enclosures.
5. Studios, live sound stages, broadcast trucks, touring rigs, and permanent audio installations.
6. Audio engineers, musicians, technicians, and broadcast professionals.
7. Its finished hardware products are purchased directly by audio professionals for integration into their signal chains.
8. Its approach prioritizes sonic transparency, rugged road-ready construction, and the integration of premium components to ensure audio tools disappear from the signal path.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company incorporates components from Jensen Transformers.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: The organization makes money through hardware sales of professional audio equipment.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with a broad catalog of professional audio tools.
Geography: The company is based in Canada and operates in professional audio markets.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: ISO/IEC
points.description: Geneva-based standards organization jointly developing audio coding standards for digital media.
points.bullets:
A standards organization that develops and publishes specifications for audio and video coding, including compression, spatial audio, and immersive rendering, for use by device makers, software developers, and broadcasters.
1. A standards body that develops technical specifications and standards sold as published documents that run on any compliant hardware or software implementation.
2. Compression algorithms, spatial audio coding formats, and geometry-based acoustic environment rendering models.
3. Audio compression, immersive spatial audio coding, 6DoF interactive audio rendering, and scene description.
4. Published technical specifications and standards licensed to industry implementers.
5. Digital television, XR environments, streaming media, and multimedia systems.
6. Device manufacturers, software developers, broadcasters, and codec implementers.
7. Its standards are implemented by hardware and software vendors into their own products and platforms.
8. It establishes the normative specifications and baseline profiles that define interoperability for audio and visual coding across industries.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: ISO, IEC, and MPEG.
Organization type: International standards organization.
Business model: Standards publication and licensing.
Scale and maturity: Established international body operating since 1988.
Geography: Based in Geneva, Switzerland, operating internationally.
Beyond audio: It develops standards spanning both audio and video coding.

points.name: MPEG Audio Subgroup
points.description: Standards subgroup developing audio coding specifications.
points.bullets:
A standards body subgroup that develops audio coding standards for the international multimedia industry.
1. A standards body that develops audio coding standards and publishes them as international specifications for implementation by others.
points.profile:
Organization type: A standards body subgroup.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio coding standards within the broader multimedia standards development context.

points.name: ISO/IEC JTC 1
points.description: Joint technical committee developing international audio coding standards like MP3 through MPEG working groups.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops international information technology standards, operating a working group that defines digital audio and video compression formats for industry-wide adoption.
1. A standards body whose specifications are published as international standards documents that other organizations implement in software, silicon and systems.
2. Formal algorithmic specifications for digital media compression, encoding and decoding that standardize how audio and video data is represented and processed.
3. Standardized digital audio compression, encoding and decoding formats that enable interoperable media representation across devices and systems.
4. Published international standards documents that organizations license and implement in their own products, codecs and platforms.
5. Consumer electronics, media playback devices, broadcasting systems, streaming platforms and digital media infrastructure.
6. Technology companies, device manufacturers, software developers, broadcasters and industry consortia that implement the standards.
7. Its standards are implemented by technology companies, device manufacturers and software developers into their codecs, chips and media products.
8. It operates through a formal international standards development process that produces consensus-based specifications adopted across the global technology industry.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: ISO and IEC.
Organization type: A joint technical standards committee of two international standards bodies.
Business model: Publication of international standards.
Scale and maturity: A long-established joint committee operating since the late 1980s.
Geography: An international standards body operating globally with participation from national standards organizations worldwide.
Beyond audio: It develops standards across the full breadth of information technology, with media compression as one working group within a larger scope.

points.name: The Moving Picture Experts Group (MPEG)
points.description: Standards body developing international compression standards for audio and video, including MP3 and other widely used formats.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops international standards for the compression, decompression, processing, and coded representation of moving pictures, audio, and their combination. It specifies generic coding standards for audio and video compression and transmission. The standards are developed for use by the global technology and media industries.
1. A standards body that develops international coding standards and specifications published as formal documents.
2. Audio and video compression, decompression, and coded representation algorithms defined within a generic standard approach using a profiles and levels framework.
3. Standardized compression, decompression, processing, and coded representation of moving pictures, audio, and their combination.
4. International standards published as formal specifications and technical documents.
5. Devices, products, and systems across the global media, broadcast, and consumer electronics industries.
6. Technology companies, device manufacturers, software developers, and media enterprises implementing standardized audio and video codecs.
7. Its specifications are implemented by technology companies across the hardware and software value chain to ensure interoperable media compression and playback.
8. It uses a generic standard approach with a profiles and levels framework to define scalable and interoperable media coding specifications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: ISO/IEC, operating formally as ISO/IEC JTC1/SC29/WG11.
Organization type: A working group and standards body under ISO/IEC.
Business model: It does not operate on a commercial business model and publishes standards for international standardization.
Scale and maturity: The organization began activities in 1988 and is an established, long-standing international standards body.
Geography: It operates as an international standards body.
Beyond audio: It develops standards for both audio and video compression, processing, and transmission.

points.name: Definitive Technology
points.description: US audio brand making high-performance speakers and home theater systems.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs and manufactures high-performance loudspeakers, soundbars, and on-wall component speakers for consumer home audio and home theater installations.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware sold as physical products used in home audio systems.
2. Patented spatial array acoustic technologies and loudspeaker driver designs housed in aluminum enclosures.
3. Soundstage widening and spatial audio presentation using multi-channel speaker arrays.
4. Finished hardware products.
5. Home theater systems, surround sound installations, and wireless streaming audio setups.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished speakers and soundbars are sold directly to consumers for home audio installations.
8. It uses patented spatial array technology in ultra-slim aluminum enclosures to widen the soundstage beyond the physical width of the speaker.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is a brand under Sound United.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A established brand in the consumer audio market with products launching as early as 2009.
Geography: Based in the USA.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is on audio hardware.

points.name: HEOS
points.description: Wireless multi-room audio brand powering smart speakers and connected devices.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics brand that provides a wireless multi-room audio platform and accompanying software application for controlling audio playback across networked speakers and devices, primarily for consumers of its parent company's audio hardware.
1. A consumer electronics brand that builds a wireless multi-room audio platform and companion mobile application, sold as integrated software and finished hardware products running on the company's networked audio devices.
2. The platform uses wireless networking protocols to stream and synchronize audio across connected devices, managed through a mobile application that supports voice control.
3. The platform delivers multi-room audio synchronization, device grouping, and voice-controlled audio playback.
4. The platform is delivered as embedded software in finished hardware products, alongside a companion mobile application.
5. The system is used in smart speakers, home theater receivers, and networked audio systems in home environments.
6. The brand sells to consumers seeking networked home audio systems.
7. Its platform is integrated into the audio hardware products manufactured by its parent company and sold directly to consumers.
8. It is tightly integrated into a family of premium audio hardware brands, enabling multi-room control specifically across that proprietary ecosystem.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The platform is part of the Sound United portfolio and is integrated into Denon and Marantz audio products.
Organization type: The organization is a consumer electronics brand operating as a subsidiary of a larger parent company.
Business model: It generates revenue through the sale of finished wireless audio hardware products and smart home audio systems.
Geography: It operates globally as part of a multinational parent company.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio brand focused entirely on wireless multi-room audio systems.

points.name: Classé
points.description: Canadian high-end audio brand building premium amplifiers and home theater components for audiophiles.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that manufactures high-end audio components, including amplifiers, preamplifiers, and receivers, for audiophiles.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware sold as standalone units in consumer homes.
2. The company designs analog and digital audio amplification and signal processing circuits.
3. The company delivers audio amplification, input switching, and surround sound decoding for home audio systems.
4. Customers receive the technology as finished hardware components.
5. The products are used in music and home theater setups.
6. The company sells to consumers and audiophiles.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly to consumers through retail channels.
8. The brand targets the high-end audiophile market with premium music and home theater components.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The brand is owned by Sound United and was previously owned by Bowers & Wilkins.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand of a parent audio company.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: The brand is an established player in the high-end audio market.
Geography: The company is based in Canada.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: EBU PLOUD Group
points.description: Standards body working group developing loudness recommendations and guidance for broadcasters.
points.bullets:
A standards body within a broadcasting union that develops loudness recommendations and specifications, and provides practical guidance to broadcasters.
1. A standards body that develops loudness measurement and control recommendations delivered as published specification documents.
2. Loudness measurement algorithms and normalization standards for broadcast audio.
3. Loudness measurement, normalization guidance, and loudness control specifications.
4. Published recommendation documents and related specifications.
5. Broadcast production and transmission workflows.
6. Broadcasters and broadcasting unions.
points.profile:
Organization type: A working group within a broadcasting standards body.
Geography: Based in Geneva, Switzerland.
Beyond audio: It develops loudness guidelines within the broader activities of a broadcasting union.

points.name: Grimm Audio
points.description: Dutch company building high-end audio equipment and loudness normalization software.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional and high-end audio equipment that develops integrated active loudspeakers, subwoofers, music players, and USB interfaces, complemented by desktop loudness normalization software for broadcast standards compliance.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished active loudspeakers, subwoofers, and music players, supplemented by desktop loudness normalizer software that runs on standard computers.
2. Integrated speaker systems combining digital signal processing, digital-to-analog converters, and Class D amplification, alongside software algorithms for loudness normalization and true peak limiting.
3. The company delivers loudness normalization to EBU R128 and ATSC A/85 standards, true peak limiting, DSP-controlled frequency curves, and low-distortion bass reproduction through digital motional feedback.
4. Customers get finished hardware products and USB interfaces, alongside licensed desktop software and firmware updates distributed for its hardware systems.
5. The products are used in high-end home listening rooms, professional studios, and broadcast post-production workflows requiring loudness compliance.
6. The company sells to audiophiles, recording and mastering studios, and broadcast professionals.
7. Its finished hardware and companion software are sold directly to end users for use in playback and broadcast production environments.
8. The company distinguishes itself through a fully integrated system approach, combining proprietary DSP, amplification, and drivers within a single loudspeaker enclosure, alongside active participation in broadcast loudness standards bodies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company co-developed loudness software with BeatRig and cooperated with Seas on a carbon composite tweeter, while contributing to the EBU PLOUD loudness working group.
Organization type: The company is a privately held audio equipment manufacturer.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of finished audio equipment and software sales of its loudness normalizer.
Scale and maturity: The company is an established, mature manufacturer with a flagship loudspeaker line that has received ongoing firmware and software updates.
Geography: The company is based and operates in the Netherlands.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on high-end audio hardware and audio production software.

points.name: 3GPP SA4
points.description: Technical specification group defining voice and audio codec standards for mobile networks and devices.
points.bullets:
A standards body that specifies audio and voice codecs for mobile networks, defining interoperable encoding and decoding standards such as the Enhanced Voice Services codec and its immersive extension for use across devices and networks.
1. A standards body that develops technical specifications for voice and audio codecs that are implemented by device makers and network operators in their products.
2. Audio compression and coding algorithms defined in technical specifications that standardize how voice and immersive audio signals are encoded and decoded for transmission over mobile networks.
3. Narrowband and wideband voice coding, immersive voice and audio services, and audio compression for mobile network transmission.
4. Published technical specifications and standards that device manufacturers and network operators implement in their hardware and software.
5. Mobile phones, network infrastructure, and mobile communication networks.
6. Device manufacturers, network operators, and mobile network infrastructure providers that implement the standards.
7. Its specifications are implemented by device makers and network operators into their products and networks.
points.profile:
Organization type: A technical specification group operating as a standards body within a mobile communications standards partnership.
Business model: Development and publication of technical standards through a collaborative standards development process.
Geography: A global standards development partnership operating internationally.

points.name: 3GPP S4
points.description: Telecom standards working group defining codec specifications for mobile networks.
points.bullets:
A standards body working group that develops and maintains technical specifications for audio codecs for mobile telecommunications networks.
1. A standards body that writes codec specifications published as technical standards for network operators and device makers to implement.
2. Audio coding specifications designed for conversational and streaming voice services over mobile networks.
3. Codec specification and maintenance, including the IVAS codec for immersive voice services.
4. Technical specifications and reports published as standards documents.
5. Mobile telecommunications networks and conversational voice services.
6. Telecommunications standards contributors including network operators, network equipment makers and device manufacturers.
7. Its specifications are implemented by network equipment vendors and device makers into mobile networks and consumer devices.
8. It focuses specifically on codec standardization within the architecture of 3GPP mobile network specifications.
points.profile:
Organization type: A working group of a telecommunications standards body.
Business model: Standards development funded by organizational membership contributions.
Geography: It operates globally within international mobile telecommunications standards development.
Beyond audio: It is part of broader mobile telecommunications standards development spanning radio, core network and multimedia services.

points.name: Via Licensing Alliance
points.description: San Francisco licensing alliance administering patent pools for audio and video codecs.
points.bullets:
A patent pool administrator that aggregates standard essential patents for audio and voice codec technologies and offers pooled licensing programs to implementers.
1. A patent pool administrator that aggregates standard essential patents and sells patent licenses for audio, video, wireless, and power management technologies.
2. Standard essential patents covering Enhanced Voice Services and Immersive Voice and Audio Services voice coding technologies for 4G and 5G cellular networks.
3. Licensing of intellectual property rights for super wideband voice coding, immersive scene-based audio, object-based audio, and metadata-assisted spatial audio.
4. Aggregated patent pools and collaborative licensing programs with published rate structures.
5. Cellular networks, smartphones, and virtual and augmented reality headsets.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers and patent holders.
7. Its patent pools aggregate standard essential patents from licensors into a single license purchased by device manufacturers.
8. It operates the only collaborative licensing solution for EVS and IVAS technologies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Major licensors include Huawei, NTT, Dolby, ERI, JVCKenwood, NovaVoice Limited, and Cordial IP, with partial ownership held by General Electric, Koninklijke Philips, and Mitsubishi Electric.
Organization type: An independently managed collaborative licensing organization owned by industry-leading participants.
Business model: Patent licensing fees from implementers accessing the pooled standard essential patents.
Scale and maturity: It has 25 years of intellectual property licensing leadership and operates dozens of licensing programs.
Geography: Based in San Francisco, California, United States, and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The organization administers patent portfolios in the audio, video, wireless, and power and charging sectors.

points.name: Cordial IP
points.description: Audio patent licensor contributing essential patents to wireless voice codec standards for 4G, 5G, and 6G networks.
points.bullets:
A patent licensing organization that licenses standard-essential patents for wireless voice and audio codecs to mobile device manufacturers. The organization contributes patents essential to voice codec standards to a managed patent pool, granting implementers access to foundational voice technologies for cellular networks. It serves mobile and cellular device manufacturers who require access to these standard technologies.
1. A patent licensing organization whose standard-essential patents for voice codecs are sold as licensed intellectual property running in mobile and cellular devices.
2. Standard-essential patents for wireless voice and audio codecs, specifically Enhanced Voice Services and Immersive Voice and Audio Services.
3. High-quality voice communications over 4G, 5G, and 5G-Advanced networks, alongside next-generation spatial audio applications for future 6G technologies.
4. Licensed intellectual property and standard-essential patents offered through an aggregated patent pool.
5. Mobile and cellular devices shipped globally.
6. Manufacturers who implement cellular voice technologies and pay royalties through the patent pool.
7. Its standard-essential patents are licensed through an aggregator to device manufacturers implementing cellular voice standards.
8. It monetizes its standard-essential patents exclusively through a collaborative, aggregated patent pool model that offers a streamlined royalty structure.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Via Licensing Alliance, alongside pool members and founders including Dolby Laboratories, Etri, Huawei, JVCKENWOOD, and NTT.
Organization type: A standards and licensing sector organization.
Business model: IP or per-unit royalties.
Scale and maturity: A participant in a global patent pool targeting billions of active mobile and cellular devices.
Geography: A participant in a global licensing program.
Beyond audio: It operates exclusively in the audio technology stack, focusing entirely on wireless audio and voice codec patent licensing.

points.name: JVCKENWOOD Corporation
points.description: Japanese electronics company licensing voice codec patents and producing consumer audio products.
points.bullets:
An electronics company that produces high-quality audio and video products and supplies display audio units to truck makers, and a licensor contributing patents essential to voice codec standards.
1. An electronics company that builds finished audio and video hardware and display audio units, and licenses standard-essential voice codec patents.
2. High-resolution audio playback, in-car connectivity and voice codec standards.
3. High-resolution audio playback, enhanced connectivity and voice codec encoding and decoding.
4. Finished hardware, in-car receivers and licensed patents.
5. Commercial trucks and consumer audio and video setups.
6. Automakers, truck manufacturers and electronics licensees.
7. Its finished hardware is designed into commercial trucks by vehicle manufacturers and its patents are licensed to implementers of voice codec standards.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Daimler Truck North America, Freightliner, Western Star and Via LA.
Organization type: A publicly traded electronics company formed from the merger of two consumer electronics brands.
Business model: Hardware sales and patent licensing royalties.

points.name: NovaVoice Limited
points.description: Audio technology licensor monetizing voice codec patents for wireless networks.
points.bullets:
A patent licensing company that licenses Standard Essential Patents for wireless voice codecs to implementers of cellular and audio devices.
1. An IP licensor whose standard essential patents are sold as licenses for use in wireless communication codecs.
2. Standard Essential Patents covering Enhanced Voice Services and Immersive Voice and Audio Services codecs.
3. High-quality voice communications across 5G networks and next-generation spatial audio for future 6G networks.
4. Standard Essential Patents licensed through an aggregated patent pool.
5. Cellular devices and a broader range of non-cellular devices worldwide.
6. Implementers who utilize EVS and IVAS audio codecs in their products.
7. Its standard essential patents are pooled with other licensors to be licensed by implementers building wireless devices.
8. It monetizes its voice technology standard essential patents through a collaborative, pooled licensing pathway that offers implementers complete visibility into royalty rate structures.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Via Licensing Alliance, Huawei and Cordial IP.
Organization type: A privately held company operating within the standards and licensing layer of the audio technology stack.
Business model: It generates revenue by collecting per-unit royalties from implementers through aggregated patent licensing vehicles.
Scale and maturity: It licenses standard essential patents applied across more than one billion active devices worldwide.
Geography: It operates globally within the competitive standard essential patent licensing market.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on licensing standard essential patents for wireless audio and voice codecs.

points.name: NTT
points.description: Japanese telecommunications company licensing standards-essential patents for cellular voice codecs.

A telecommunications company and patent licensor that contributes standards-essential patents for voice codec standards to patent pools, providing intellectual property rights to device makers and implementers.
1. A telecommunications company that contributes standards-essential voice codec patents which are licensed to implementers through patent pools.
2. Voice codec standards including the EVS codec and the Opus codec.
3. Cellular voice coding and audio compression through standards-essential patented technologies.
4. Patents licensed through patent pools.
5. Cellular networks and voice communication devices.
6. Telecommunications equipment manufacturers and device makers implementing voice codec standards.
7. Its standards-essential patents are licensed to implementers through patent pool administrators.
8. It is a top patent owner in the Opus landscape and a contributor to the jointly-developed EVS codec standard.
