Key partners and customers: Its products are benchmarked against components from Knowles, TDK, and Infineon.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware component sales, including per-unit microphone pricing and custom solution contracts.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2009, with over 150 million units shipped worldwide.
Geography: Based in Wuxi, China.
Beyond audio: It extends beyond audio into multi-modal sensing systems combining audio, vision, and mmWave radar for robotics and interactive displays.

points.name: LumenVox LLC
points.description: Software company providing speech recognition, text-to-speech, and voice biometrics technologies.
points.bullets:
A speech technology company that provides legacy automatic speech recognition engines and voice biometrics software for the TTS market.
1. A software developer whose speech recognition and voice biometrics engines run in the cloud behind an API.
2. The core technology is based on Gaussian Models and Hidden Markov Chains.
3. It delivers automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech and voice biometric capabilities.
4. Customers get it through software engines and cloud APIs.
5. Its technology is used in systems requiring automated speech recognition and voice biometric authentication.
6. The organization sells to enterprises deploying speech recognition and voice biometrics systems.
points.profile:
Business model: It makes money through software licenses and API usage.
Beyond audio: The company's focus is entirely on speech and audio technology.

points.name: Soundboks
points.description: Danish audio company making extremely loud, durable, battery-powered Bluetooth speakers for outdoor parties and events.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that builds loud, durable, battery-powered Bluetooth speakers designed for parties, events and outdoor use.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished Bluetooth speakers sold as consumer hardware products.
2. Battery-powered portable speaker systems with Bluetooth wireless input, app-based sound control and multi-unit wireless linking.
3. Concert-level sound output up to 126 dB with rugged construction and long swappable battery life.
4. Finished hardware products sold directly to consumers.
5. Parties, events and outdoor use.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished speakers are sold directly to end users.
8. Extremely loud output and rugged construction combined with long swappable battery life for true portability.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A company that introduced its third-generation speaker in 2021 and a compact model in 2022.
Geography: Based in Denmark.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is audio.

points.name: Zound Industries
points.description: Swedish consumer audio company designing headphones, earphones, and portable wireless speakers under the Marshall and Adidas brands.
points.bullets:
A consumer and professional audio equipment maker that designs and manufactures headphones, earphones, portable wireless speakers, and guitar amplifiers for global retail distribution.
1. An equipment maker that builds physical audio hardware and sells it as finished consumer and professional products.
2. Acoustic, amplification, and wireless audio hardware engineered into physical form factors.
3. Personal audio listening, portable sound reinforcement, and electric guitar amplification.
4. Finished hardware products distributed through global retail partner networks.
5. Consumer headphones, earphones, portable wireless speakers, professional guitar amplifiers, speaker cabinets, and drums.
6. Consumers purchasing through global retail networks and musicians using professional audio equipment.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold by retail partners to consumers and musicians.
8. It leverages a 60-year musical instrument brand heritage to market consumer audio technology through a rock and roll culture aesthetic.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: HongShan Capital Group is its parent company and the Marshall family retains a minority stake.
Organization type: A privately held company operating as a subsidiary brand.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: It generates over $400 million in net sales and was acquired in a transaction valuing it at $1.1 billion.
Geography: It is based in Sweden and distributes its products to over 90 countries globally.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on designing, manufacturing, and distributing audio hardware.

points.name: Marshall Group
points.description: UK and Swedish audio company designing Bluetooth speakers and headphones for portable listening.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs, builds and sells portable Bluetooth speakers and headphones for consumers.
1. A consumer audio equipment maker whose portable speakers and headphones run as finished hardware products.
2. The company uses full-range drivers paired with passive radiators and custom wireless audio software.
3. The products deliver 360-degree stereophonic sound, multi-speaker wireless linking and adjustable equalization.
4. Customers get it as finished consumer hardware devices.
5. The products are used in portable, rugged and lifestyle-oriented settings.
6. The company sells directly to consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users through retail channels.
8. Its approach wraps modern wireless audio technology in a professional rock-and-roll amplifier heritage and styling.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization's professional amplification history serviced legendary acts like Hendrix, Motörhead, and Nirvana.
Organization type: The entity is a newly formed corporate group.
Business model: The company makes money through the direct sale of consumer hardware products.
Geography: The company prices its products in pounds and dollars, indicating operation across at least the United Kingdom and the United States.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio products.

points.name: Goodix
points.description: Shenzhen semiconductor company designing audio amplifier chips and software for smartphones and cars.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor and IP company that designs high-performance audio amplifier chips and associated acoustic enhancement algorithms, selling integrated solutions to smart device manufacturers and automotive electronics clients.
1. A fabless chip company that designs and sells digital input Class-D smart amplifier chips bundled with proprietary acoustic protection algorithms.
2. The core technology is a pure digital path amplifier architecture using proprietary pulse-width modulation alongside DSP-based speaker excursion and temperature protection algorithms.
3. The company delivers up to 7 W of peak speaker amplification, 124 dB of dynamic range, ultra-low noise floor, and micro-speaker excursion and temperature protection.
4. Customers receive the offering as physical integrated circuits fabricated using a custom 90 nm BCD process, accompanied by licensed proprietary software algorithms.
5. The chips and algorithms are used in smartphones, tablets, and automotive audio systems.
6. The company sells to global smart device manufacturers and automotive electronics clients.
7. Its chips and software are designed into mobile and automotive audio hardware by consumer electronics brands and automakers.
8. The approach is differentiated by a pure digital path amplifier architecture combined with an extremely compact footprint and high energy efficiency.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company collaborates with a semiconductor manufacturer for custom 90 nm BCD process development and acquired a research and development team originating from Philips and NXP.
Organization type: The organization is a publicly traded fabless semiconductor and IP licensing company.
Business model: It generates revenue through chip sales and IP or software licensing to device manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: It maintains a strong competitive position in the mobile audio market with a research and development team holding over four decades of heritage.
Geography: The company is based in Shenzhen and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The organization provides biometric and human-machine interaction technologies beyond its audio business.

points.name: Soundskrit
points.description: Audio technology company developing bio-inspired directional MEMS microphones for consumer audio devices.
points.bullets:
A microphone hardware company that develops bio-inspired directional MEMS microphones and associated acoustic design technology for consumer audio applications, aiming to replace multi-microphone arrays with a single chip.
1. A microphone component maker whose directional MEMS microphones are sold as finished hardware components for integration into consumer devices.
2. Bio-inspired MEMS microelectromechanical structures that replicate multi-microphone array directionality on a single silicon chip, exhibiting dipole and cardioid polar patterns across the audible spectrum.
3. Directional sound capture, background noise rejection, voice isolation, and acoustic pattern conversion across a full 20Hz to 20kHz frequency range.
4. Finished hardware microphones, digital PDM surface-mount components, and evaluation boards.
5. Consumer audio products, everyday communication devices, and applications requiring studio-quality directional audio capture.
6. Consumer electronics device makers and microphone module manufacturers.
7. Its microphones are designed into consumer audio products by electronics brands as replacements for traditional multi-microphone arrays.
8. It brings the directional capabilities of traditional multi-microphone arrays to a single MEMS chip that is robust to environmental noise.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: AAC Technologies provides a platform to develop and integrate its microphone technologies.
Organization type: A privately held hardware company.
Business model: Hardware component sales.
Scale and maturity: A company with multiple generations of directional microphones shipped in a breadth of consumer products.
Geography: Operates in the consumer audio hardware market.
Beyond audio: Its focus is entirely on audio hardware, MEMS technology, and acoustic design.

points.name: Teufel Audio
points.description: German consumer audio brand selling speakers, soundbars, and headphones direct-to-consumer across Europe.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs and sells loudspeakers, soundbars, home theater systems, Bluetooth speakers and headphones directly to consumers.
1. A consumer electronics company that builds finished audio hardware products sold as physical units for use in the home and on the go.
2. Acoustic transducer and enclosure engineering combined with proprietary wireless streaming software.
3. Sound reproduction and multi-room wireless audio streaming.
4. Finished hardware products and software features sold directly to end users.
5. Home theater setups, living rooms, desktops and portable listening settings.
6. Consumers purchasing audio equipment for personal or home use.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users through the company's own retail and online channels.
8. It operates as a direct-to-consumer seller rather than relying on third-party retail distribution.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It owns the Raumfeld streaming technology brand.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales through a direct-to-consumer retail model.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1979, it is established as Europe's largest direct seller of audio products.
Geography: Based in Berlin, Germany, with retail and online operations across Europe.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on consumer audio products and their direct retail sales.

points.name: Merging Technologies
points.description: Swiss pro audio company building high-end digital recording and mixing systems for the media and music industries.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio and video equipment and software that develops high-resolution digital audio workstations, digital-to-analog converters, audio interfaces, and audio-over-IP drivers for the elite music, film, television, mastering, and live performance industries.
1. A professional audio equipment and software maker whose digital audio workstations, sequencers, and converters are sold as finished hardware and software products running in studios and live venues.
2. High-resolution audio processing software supporting DSD256, immersive 3D panning and mixing engines, and audio-over-IP connectivity using the AES67 standard.
3. High track count digital audio workstation processing, direct stream digital support, immersive 3D audio panning and mixing for complex speaker layouts, and multichannel audio-over-IP routing.
4. Finished hardware converters and interfaces, standalone software applications, plugin suites, and audio-over-IP drivers.
5. Professional recording studios, mastering facilities, film and television post-production, and live event venues.
6. Professional audio engineers, mastering engineers, post-production facilities, and live event producers.
7. Its hardware and software products are used directly by professional audio engineers in studio and live event production workflows.
8. Its digital audio workstation supports high-resolution direct stream digital audio up to DSD256 alongside native immersive 3D mixing workflows for complex speaker layouts.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Sennheiser is its parent company, Neumann.Berlin is a collaborating brand, and Auro Technologies is a 3D audio partner.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales and software licenses.
Scale and maturity: An established company with over thirty years of experience acquired by a major audio group in 2022.
Geography: Based in Switzerland and serving global professional audio markets.
Beyond audio: The company also develops video products alongside its professional audio equipment and software.

points.name: gfai tech GmbH
points.description: Berlin-based manufacturer producing microphone arrays and acoustic cameras for sound and vibration measurement.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of finished hardware and software products for sound and vibration measurement and analysis. The company produces microphone arrays, acoustic analysis software, mobile data recorders, handheld sound cameras and impulse hammers for sound source localization and visualization.
1. An equipment maker that develops acoustic camera systems, microphone arrays and analysis software sold as finished hardware and software products.
2. Microphone arrays that determine the spatial distribution of acoustic signals combined with acoustic analysis software that visualizes sound sources.
3. Sound source localization, sound visualization, sound and vibration measurement, and acoustic sound imaging.
4. Finished hardware devices and companion analysis software products.
5. Industrial sound and vibration measurement, diagnostics and acoustic imaging settings.
6. Industrial and engineering enterprises performing sound and vibration measurement and analysis.
7. Its finished hardware and software products are used directly by enterprises for acoustic measurement and diagnostics.
8. The company introduced the first commercially viable acoustic camera.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of the Association for the Promotion of Applied Computer Science.
Organization type: A subsidiary manufacturer owned by a research and development association.
Business model: Hardware and software product sales.
Scale and maturity: Incorporated in 2006, profiled as a major player with reported sales and revenue from 2017 to 2022.
Geography: Based in Berlin, Germany, operating in the global acoustic sound imaging camera market.
Beyond audio: The company also develops computer-aided tools for energy-related applications.

points.name: Pulsar Instruments
points.description: UK manufacturer building sound level meters and noise dosimeters for occupational noise monitoring.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of noise measurement equipment that produces sound level meters, personal noise dosimeters and noise-activated warning signs for occupational health and safety applications, and supplies them to safety professionals through distributors.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished sound measurement instruments and warning signs sold as physical hardware to safety professionals and distributors.
2. Acoustic measurement instruments integrating microphones, data logging electronics and octave band analysis.
3. Sound level measurement, personal noise exposure dosimetry, and noise threshold alerting.
4. Finished hardware products, including handheld meters, wearable dosimeters and warning signs, supplied as individual units or as multi-instrument noise survey kits.
5. Occupational noise monitoring in workplaces, including shift work, lone working and confined spaces.
6. Health and safety professionals, industrial operations and distribution partners.
7. Its finished instruments are supplied through distribution partners to end users conducting workplace noise surveys.
8. Focuses on comprehensive, kit-based occupational noise monitoring that pairs wearable personal dosimeters with handheld integrating sound level meters.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Products are distributed by partners including Impex Produkter AS.
Organization type: Privately held, publicly trading company established in 1969.
Business model: Hardware sales, equipment rental services, warranty servicing and training provision.
Scale and maturity: A long-established company founded in 1969 operating internationally through a distributor network.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom with distributor representation across multiple countries including Spain and Norway.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on occupational noise measurement, monitoring and associated safety training.

points.name: Brüel & Kjr
points.description: Danish precision measurement manufacturer producing acoustic testing systems and vibration analysis equipment.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of precision measuring technologies that builds high-calibration systems, vibration testing equipment, and acoustic end-of-line test systems for OEMs.
1. A test and measurement equipment maker that designs and sells physical instruments and integrated test systems that run on the factory floor.
2. The systems are built on precision acoustic and vibration sensing transducers, signal conditioning hardware, and analysis software for production-line quality control.
3. The acoustic end-of-line test systems deliver automated pass/fail quality inspection, frequency response measurement, and defect detection for manufactured products.
4. Customers receive finished hardware equipment and accompanying software products.
5. The test systems are used in production lines and factories for end-of-line testing of manufactured goods.
6. The company sells to industrial OEMs and manufacturing enterprises.
7. Its test and measurement systems are deployed by OEMs on their production lines to verify product quality.
8. The organization is distinguished by its heritage and focus on high-precision calibration and metrology equipment for industrial applications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization operates as a subsidiary brand of Hottinger Brüel & Kjær following a merger with Hottinger.
Organization type: The company is a corporate subsidiary brand of a larger test and measurement group.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of measuring equipment and test systems.
Scale and maturity: The organization was originally founded in 1942 and operates at an established, global corporate scale.
Geography: The company is based in Denmark and operates internationally.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the company provides precision measuring technologies, vibration testing equipment, and high-calibration systems for industrial metrology.

points.name: CRYSOUND
points.description: Chinese acoustic instrument manufacturer building acoustic imaging cameras for industrial inspection.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio test and measurement equipment that designs and builds finished hardware devices for acoustic inspection and calibration, selling to industrial, automotive and engineering customers.
1. A maker of professional test and measurement hardware whose finished instruments are sold as standalone devices used in the field.
2. MEMS microphone arrays and condenser sensors combined with thermal imaging modules and beamforming algorithms to locate acoustic sources.
3. Acoustic source localization, gas leak detection, electrical discharge detection, mechanical fault detection and sound pressure level calibration.
4. Finished handheld hardware devices, including acoustic imaging cameras, sound calibrators and measurement microphones.
5. Industrial inspection settings, automotive testing, engineering facilities and hazardous environments.
6. Industrial enterprises, automotive manufacturers, engineering companies and acoustic test distributors.
7. Its finished measurement instruments are sold through distribution partners to end-users in industrial and engineering settings.
8. It integrates high-count MEMS sensor arrays with optional thermal imaging in handheld acoustic cameras capable of detecting smaller leaks and partial discharges from greater distances than comparable handheld devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: AcSoft distributes its acoustic testing products in the UK market.
Organization type: A privately held company established in 1997.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished measurement instruments and microphones.
Scale and maturity: A company established in 1997 whose products are used in over 80 countries by over 10,000 customers.
Geography: Based in Hangzhou, China, operating globally with distribution reaching markets including the UK and India.
Beyond audio: Its focus extends beyond audio into industrial inspection, combining acoustic imaging with thermal imaging for mechanical, gas and electrical fault detection.

points.name: Beltone
points.description: US hearing aid brand manufacturing advanced digital hearing instruments.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of finished hearing aids and hearing care accessories that develops and sells digital hearing instruments and companion apps for consumers with hearing loss.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished hearing aids, handheld remotes, and companion smartphone apps, sold as finished hardware and software products through its own retail clinics.
2. Digital hearing instruments use directional microphones, AI-powered sound adjustment, and wireless audio streaming, with companion apps running on smartphones for remote control and fitting.
3. Directional microphones, noise reduction, speech enhancement, wind noise reduction, feedback cancellation, AI-powered sound adjustment, direct audio streaming, tinnitus sound therapy, Bluetooth LE Audio, and Auracast broadcast audio.
4. Finished hearing aids, handheld remote controls, and mobile applications delivered through a network of hearing care clinics.
5. Hearing aids worn in the ear canal or behind the ear, smartphone-based remote controls, and tinnitus management tools.
6. Consumers with hearing loss seeking hearing aids and hearing care services.
7. Its finished hearing instruments are sold directly to consumers through its franchise retail clinics.
8. It operates as a retail hearing care provider with over 1,500 clinic locations, combining finished hearing aid hardware with direct consumer service and fitting.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A brand under GN Hearing and GN Group, sharing technology with ReSound and distributing Jabra Enhance Plus in its clinics.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded company.
Business model: Hearing aid sales and hearing care services through retail clinics.
Scale and maturity: A hearing care provider operating over 1,500 locations nationwide with over 75 years in the industry.
Geography: Based in Chicago, Illinois, USA, operating retail clinics across the United States.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio and hearing care company.

points.name: Vivtone
points.description: Direct-to-consumer hearing aid company manufacturing affordable FDA-registered OTC devices with Bluetooth connectivity.
points.bullets:
A maker of over-the-counter hearing aids that develops and sells customizable Bluetooth-enabled devices directly to consumers. The company builds FDA-registered hearing aids with companion mobile applications and sells them direct-to-consumer, targeting individuals with mild to moderate hearing loss.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished over-the-counter hearing aids with companion mobile applications.
2. Digital sound processing running in wearable hearing aids, paired with a mobile application that conducts in-app hearing tests.
3. Noise reduction, feedback cancellation, Bluetooth streaming, real-time frequency adjustments, and hearing test-based sound personalization.
4. The company sells finished hardware hearing aids and companion software applications directly to consumers.
5. The devices are used as over-the-counter hearing aids for mild to moderate hearing loss.
6. The organization sells directly to consumers.
7. Its finished hearing aids are sold direct-to-consumer through an online retail channel.
8. It is positioned as a budget-friendly direct-to-consumer alternative offering free lifetime audiologist support and installment payment plans.

Key partners and customers: The company partners with Afterpay and Klarna for consumer financing.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through direct hardware sales of hearing aids.
Scale and maturity: The company is an established direct-to-consumer brand.
Geography: The company operates online and sells to consumers.

points.name: SDA Software Design Ahnert GmbH
points.description: Software company developing simulation and measurement software for room acoustics.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that develops and distributes software for room-acoustic modeling, measurements, engineering, physics, and simulation for acoustic professionals.
1. A developer tools company whose simulation and modeling software runs as desktop software for acoustic engineers.
2. The core technology is acoustic simulation and modeling software based on room acoustics, physics, and engineering principles.
3. The software delivers room-acoustic modeling, acoustic measurement, and acoustic simulation capabilities.
4. Customers get it as software products used for acoustic engineering and measurement.
5. The software is used in architectural acoustic design and room-acoustic engineering settings.
6. The company sells to acoustic engineers and professionals.
7. Its software is used by engineers to model, measure, and design acoustic spaces.
8. The company's focus on physics-based room-acoustic modeling and simulation distinguishes its approach.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is a partner company of AFMG Technologies, cooperating in software development and distribution.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held software company.
Business model: It makes money through software licenses.
Geography: The company is based in Germany.

points.name: Fireflies
points.description: Software company automating meeting transcription and summarization across video conferencing platforms.
points.bullets:
A software company that provides a meeting transcription and analysis platform, building applications that automate the recording, transcribing and summarizing of voice conversations for enterprises and professionals.
1. A software developer whose meeting assistant application runs in the cloud behind a web interface and integrations with video conferencing platforms.
2. Cloud-based speech processing systems that combine speech-to-text transcription with large language models for natural language understanding.
3. Meeting recording, real-time transcription, speaker identification, conversation analysis and automated summarization with action item generation.
4. Software as a service delivered through a cloud platform and integrations with video conferencing systems.
5. Conference calls, video meetings and enterprise communication workflows.
6. Enterprises, professionals and teams using video conferencing platforms.
7. Its application integrates cloud speech recognition APIs from upstream model developers to deliver a finished meeting assistant product to end users.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: AssemblyAI.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A horizontal player in the AI notetaker market.
Geography: Operates across video conferencing platforms globally.
Beyond audio: Audio conversation analysis is its entire focus.

points.name: CyweeMotion
points.description: Software company providing sensor fusion technology for head-tracking in wireless earbuds to enable spatial audio.
points.bullets:
A software developer that provides sensor fusion algorithms for head-tracking in true wireless and open wearable stereo designs, enabling dynamic spatial audio for mobile or wearable devices.

2. Low-power sensor fusion algorithms running on a DSP core.
3. Head-tracking for dynamic spatial audio.
4. Licensed software optimized for a third-party DSP core.
5. True wireless earbuds and open wearable stereo devices.
6. Mobile or wearable device makers.

8. Its sensor fusion software is optimized specifically for a named third-party audio DSP core.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Fraunhofer and Cadence.
Organization type: A technology company.
Business model: Software licensing.

points.name: STAGETEC
points.description: German pro audio manufacturer building mixing consoles and signal management solutions for broadcast.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that develops mixing consoles, audio routing systems, and IP signal management platforms for broadcasters, theaters, and live venues.
1. An equipment maker that builds mixing consoles, audio routing hardware, and multimedia winch systems sold as finished hardware and software products running in fixed installations.
2. Digital audio networking, signal routing, and mixing console systems using AES67 audio over IP and drag-and-drop device management software.
3. Audio routing, mixing, IP signal management, device detection, remote monitoring, and automated movement of microphones, speakers, and cameras.
4. Finished hardware, mixing consoles, router boards, and software products.
5. Theaters, broadcast stations, parliaments, opera houses, and live venues.
6. Broadcasters, festival theaters, live acts, and institutions running AV installations.

Business model: Hardware sales and software products.

points.name: 64Audio

An equipment maker that designs and manufactures custom and universal-fit in-ear monitors for musicians, audio engineers, audiophiles, and gamers.

2. The core technology comprises proprietary acoustic designs incorporating specialized soundstage and bass response modules.

points.name: Empire Ears

A manufacturer of custom and universal in-ear monitors that designs and builds premium finished earphones for professional monitoring and high-end personal listening for audio professionals and audiophiles.

2. Hybrid and tri-brid driver configurations, custom electrostatic control transformers, specialized crossover networks and anti-resonance compounds developed through acoustic engineering.

4. The organization provides its models running on customers' edge devices.

Organization type: It is a privately held startup.

points.name: Li Creative Technologies

An audio software and AI solutions developer that builds 3D audio systems, dereverberation software and far-field microphone arrays for the automobile, audio chip, consumer electronics and streaming music industries.

points.name: Modus VR

A developer tools company that builds a 3D spatial design platform for modeling conference rooms and commercial spaces, letting integrators plan audiovisual equipment placement and preview coverage in real time.

points.description: Music library licensing audio tracks and metadata for AI training models.
points.bullets:
A production music and stock audio library that licenses a catalog of music, sound effects, and stems to media producers and as training data for generative AI models.
1. A data provider that licenses a catalog of pre-cleared audio recordings and associated text metadata for creative production and machine learning training.
2. A catalog of commercial production music, sound effects, and single-instrument stems paired with corresponding text metadata.
3. The organization provides pre-cleared tracks for commercial media production and structured audio datasets for training generative audio models.
4. The content is delivered as licensed digital audio files and metadata through an online marketplace and direct data licensing agreements.
5. The audio is used in film, television, game production, advertising, and the training of generative AI models.
6. The organization sells to media production companies, advertising agencies, dataset creators, foundation model developers, and AI infrastructure providers.
7. It aggregates content from independent artists and rights holders and licenses it directly to media producers and AI developers.
8. The company provides a broad catalog of pre-cleared commercial music with opt-out provisions for artists in AI training datasets.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It licensed over 800,000 recordings to Stability AI for use in training its generative audio models.
Organization type: It is a privately held commercial stock audio marketplace.
Business model: The company generates revenue through variant pricing for music licensing based on intended use and through dataset licensing for AI training.
Scale and maturity: It has been in operation as a digital sound library since 1996.
Geography: It is a worldwide music licensing company representing thousands of international artists, bands, composers, and publishers.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on stock audio licensing and music library aggregation.

points.name: Telecommunications Technology Association (TTA)
points.description: South Korean standards organization certifying devices to ensure consistent playback quality for spatial audio formats.
points.bullets:
A standards organization that develops and administers device certification programs for spatial audio technologies, ensuring consistent playback quality and fidelity for consumers.
1. A standards body that defines certification criteria and test programs for audio playback devices.
2. Certification standards and testing methodologies for spatial audio formats.
3. Certification of sound fidelity and consistent audio playback for spatial audio technologies.
4. Certification programs that device makers use to validate and badge their hardware.
5. Consumer audio devices supporting spatial audio playback.
6. Consumer electronics device makers seeking certification.
7. Its certification programs are adopted by device makers to validate audio performance in consumer products.
8. It develops certification programs in direct collaboration with the originators of the spatial audio format being certified.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Samsung and Google.
Organization type: A standards organization based in South Korea.
Business model: Certification fees and standards administration.
Scale and maturity: An established national standards organization.
Geography: South Korea.
Beyond audio: It develops certification and standards for broader telecommunications technologies beyond audio.

points.name: DJI
points.description: Chinese technology manufacturer building wireless microphone systems for content creation.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional and consumer audio equipment that designs and sells wireless microphone systems for content creators and videographers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished wireless microphone hardware sold as packaged products.
2. Wireless radio transmission systems linking compact transmitters with built-in microphones to portable receivers, incorporating 32-bit float recording.
3. Dual-channel wireless audio capture, 32-bit float recording, active noise cancellation, and portability with extended battery life.
4. Finished hardware products sold as complete wireless microphone systems with carry and charging cases.
5. Content creation, video production, and drone applications.
6. Consumers and content creators.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users through retail channels.
8. It applies its expertise in drone portability and power management to wireless microphone design.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its products are compared against wireless microphone systems from RØDE and Sennheiser in retail articles.
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A large, established technology manufacturer.
Geography: Based in China.
Beyond audio: The company is a major drone manufacturer for which audio products are a secondary extension.

points.name: Dirac Live
points.description: Software developer creating room correction algorithms for audio processors.
points.bullets:
An audio software developer that provides room correction algorithms which correct frequency and time errors around the listening area for consumer and professional audio hardware brands.
1. An audio software developer whose room correction algorithms run on-device in partners' audio processors.
2. Digital signal processing algorithms that measure acoustic errors and apply frequency and time domain corrections.
3. Room correction, frequency response correction, time domain correction, and active acoustic room treatment.
4. Licensed algorithms and calibration software tools sold separately or integrated into hardware products.
5. Home theater processors, stereo preamplifiers, streaming devices, and multi-channel audio systems.
6. Consumer electronics brands, audio equipment manufacturers, and end users.
7. Its algorithms are integrated by audio equipment manufacturers into their processors and amplifiers.
8. Active Room Treatment technology measures and treats the room acoustics directly rather than only correcting the sound after it leaves the speakers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: miniDSP, NAD, JBL Synthesis, and Bluesound.
Organization type: A privately held software company.
Business model: Software licenses, per-unit royalties, and calibration kit sales.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio digital signal processing and acoustic correction.

points.name: ZTE
points.description: Shenzhen telecommunications company contributing to the development of voice and audio codecs for mobile networks.
points.bullets:
A telecommunications equipment company that contributes to audio codec standardization and builds smartphones with integrated audio components for mobile networks.
1. A telecommunications equipment maker that builds network infrastructure and finished mobile devices, with audio capabilities embedded in smartphones.
2. Enhanced Voice Services audio coding technology standardized through the 3GPP process, and dedicated digital-to-analog converter and amplifier circuitry in mobile devices.
3. High-quality voice call audio compression and decoding, and high-fidelity analog audio output for mobile devices.
4. Telecommunications network infrastructure and finished consumer smartphones with embedded audio hardware.
5. Mobile telephony networks and consumer smartphones.
6. Mobile network operators and consumers.
7. Its codec contributions are standardized for industry use, and its finished devices are sold directly to consumers.
8. It bridges network-level voice codec standardization and consumer device audio hardware implementation.
points.profile:
Organization type: A publicly traded telecommunications equipment and consumer electronics company.
Scale and maturity: A large-scale global telecommunications equipment provider.
Geography: Based in Shenzhen, China, operating globally.
Beyond audio: A full-stack telecommunications company whose primary business spans network infrastructure, mobile devices, and consumer electronics, with audio as one component.

points.name: Hansaton
points.description: Swiss hearing aid brand designing digital hearing solutions for diverse hearing needs.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished hearing aids, charging accessories, and fitting applications for hearing care professionals and end users.
1. A manufacturer of finished hearing aid hardware, including digital receiver-in-canal, behind-the-ear, and custom in-the-ear devices, sold as consumer medical devices worn on the user.
2. Digital hearing aid sound processing platforms built around proprietary signal processing chips, incorporating AI-trained automatic programs and adaptive directional microphone systems.
3. The products deliver hearing loss compensation, adaptive sound processing, universal Bluetooth streaming, wireless connectivity, audio program switching, and battery management.
4. The organization provides its technology as finished hardware devices, along with companion mobile applications and electronic drying and charging stations.
5. The products are used in personal wearable hearing instruments, including behind-the-ear, receiver-in-canal, in-the-ear, completely-in-canal, and invisible-in-canal devices.
6. The organization sells to consumers through hearing care professionals and audiology clinics.
7. Its finished hearing instruments are fitted and distributed to end users through audiology clinics and hearing care professionals.
8. The company emphasizes co-creative design processes involving users and hearing care professionals, focusing on award-winning product aesthetics, usability, and form factors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is a brand under and backed by its parent company, Sonova.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand of a publicly traded hearing care company.
Business model: The company makes money through the sale of finished hearing aid hardware and related accessories to hearing care professionals.
Scale and maturity: The organization has operated since 1957 and has expanded internationally, including into the United States market.
Geography: The company is based in Hamburg, Germany, operates internationally, and is part of a group headquartered near Zurich, Switzerland.
Beyond audio: Hearing aid manufacturing is the company's entire focus.

points.name: Novation
points.description: UK music equipment manufacturer making MIDI controllers, synthesizers, and USB controllers for electronic music production.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds MIDI controllers, synthesizers and USB controllers for electronic music producers and musicians.
1. An equipment maker whose physical hardware interfaces are sold as finished products and run as standalone devices or connected to computers.
2. The core technology comprises MIDI control surfaces, synthesizer engines and USB connectivity protocols for interfacing with digital audio workstations and sound generation tools.
3. The company delivers physical control of digital audio workstations, MIDI performance control and sound generation.
4. Customers get its products as finished hardware and related firmware updates.
5. Its products are used in electronic music production studios and live performance setups.
6. The company sells to consumers, musicians and electronic music producers.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly to audio professionals through shared distribution networks.
8. Its approach is distinguished by a specialization in electronic music technology, specifically MIDI controllers and synthesizers, setting it apart from sibling brands focusing on audio interfaces or microphone preamps.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The brand operates as a subsidiary of Focusrite Group and ensures compatibility with devices from other manufacturers such as the MixPre series.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand of a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: The company makes money through the sale of hardware products and related intellectual property.
Scale and maturity: The brand maintains a niche but relevant position in the competitive professional audio equipment market.
Geography: The company operates within the professional audio equipment sector, leveraging shared distribution networks from its parent company.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on audio equipment and software.

points.name: Wilson Audio Specialties
points.description: High-end audio manufacturer building premium loudspeakers for audiophiles.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and builds high-end loudspeakers for consumers and audiophiles.
1. An equipment maker that builds passive loudspeakers sold as finished hardware in listening rooms.
2. Acoustic transducer and cabinet designs engineered for high-fidelity sound reproduction.
3. Full-range sound reproduction for high-fidelity audio playback.
4. Finished hardware products.
5. High-end home listening rooms and audio systems.
6. Consumers and audiophiles.
7. Its finished loudspeakers are sold directly into consumer home audio systems.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Audience
points.description: US power conditioning manufacturer building power conditioners and monitor speakers for audio systems.
points.bullets:
An audio equipment maker that builds power conditioners and passive monitor speakers for consumer and professional audio systems.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment whose finished hardware runs in standalone consumer and professional audio systems.
2. Passive loudspeaker drivers and electrical power conditioning circuits.
3. AC power filtering and audio monitoring playback.
4. Finished hardware.
5. Consumer audio systems and professional monitoring setups.
6. Consumers and audiophiles.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly into consumer audio systems.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company that was acquired and merged into a microelectronic component supplier.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on audio equipment.

points.name: IMAX Corporation
points.description: Entertainment company licensing immersive audio certifications for consumer electronics and hearables.
points.bullets:
An entertainment and certification company that operates a premium audio and video certification and licensing program, establishing standards for consumer electronics devices and content.
1. A certification and licensing body whose audio quality standards are implemented in consumer electronics products licensed by device makers.
2. Certified audio and video processing standards developed and maintained by the organization and its partners.
3. Premium spatial audio reproduction, optimized playback quality, and standardized audio remastering for certified devices.
4. Certified devices and licensed intellectual property sold to consumer electronics brands.
5. Televisions, PCs, laptops, tablets, smartphones, AVRs, speakers, soundbars, and in-ear hearables.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers and device makers.
7. Its certification is obtained by consumer electronics brands to validate the audio quality of their finished hardware.
8. It extends premium theatrical audio certification to in-ear hearables.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Xperi, DTS, Inc., and Breggz.
Organization type: A publicly traded entertainment corporation operating a certification and licensing program.
Business model: Certification and licensing fees.
Scale and maturity: An established global entertainment corporation.
Geography: Based in North America and operating globally.
Beyond audio: It operates a global network of large-format theatrical cinemas.

points.name: Kilohearts
points.description: Software company developing modular synthesizer and audio effects plugins.
points.bullets:
A software company that develops audio plugins, including modular software synthesizers and effects, for musicians and sound designers. It builds modular wavetable synthesizers and modular effects hosts that run as plugins inside digital audio workstations.
1. A software developer whose audio synthesizers and effects run as plugins in digital audio workstations.
2. Wavetable synthesis engines and modular effects processing algorithms running as software plugins.
3. Wavetable synthesis, advanced modulation, phase rotation, and modular sound design effects.
4. Software plugins licensed as perpetual licenses or provided through a subscription service.
5. Digital audio workstations and music production studios.
6. Musicians, sound designers, and audio producers.
7. Its plugins are sold directly to end users to run inside digital audio workstations.
8. It focuses on modern workflow tools rather than emulating obsolete hardware.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held software company.
Business model: Software licenses and subscription fees.
Beyond audio: Audio software development is its entire focus.

points.name: Media Networking Alliance
points.description: Industry alliance promoting networked audio adoption by raising awareness of interoperability standards.
points.bullets:
An industry alliance formed to promote and drive industry adoption of the AES67 audio networking standard.
1. An industry alliance that provides standardization advocacy and awareness programs delivered through industry outreach.
2. The organization promotes AES67, an interoperability standard for high-performance streaming audio over IP networks.
3. The organization delivers awareness, education, and implementation guidance for networked audio interoperability.
4. Customers receive guidance and advocacy through an industry consortium membership structure.
5. The standard is used in professional broadcast, live sound, and installed audio network environments.
6. The organization serves professional audio equipment manufacturers, broadcast facilities, and audio engineers.
7. Its advocacy supports the adoption of networking standards integrated by equipment makers into their professional audio products.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A founding member of the organization is a professional audio equipment manufacturer.
Organization type: An industry alliance and standards advocacy group.
Business model: The organization operates as an industry consortium funded by member companies.
Scale and maturity: The organization is an established industry group formed to support a specific audio networking standard.
Geography: The organization operates globally within the professional audio and broadcast industries.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on promoting audio networking interoperability and has no operations outside of this scope.

points.name: Jensen
points.description: US audio component manufacturer making legendary guitar loudspeakers and high-quality audio transformers.
points.bullets:
A loudspeaker and audio component brand that manufactures guitar loudspeakers and audio transformers, building reissues of vintage speakers alongside new designs for tube amplifier makers, studios and musicians.
1. A loudspeaker manufacturer that builds guitar loudspeakers and audio transformers sold as finished hardware components.
2. Guitar loudspeaker sound reproduction and audio signal transformation for microphones.
3. The company delivers its products as finished hardware components and loudspeakers.
4. Its loudspeakers are built into guitar amplifiers and its transformers are used in studio microphones.
5. The company sells to tube guitar amplifier makers and microphone manufacturers.
6. Its loudspeakers are designed into guitar amplifiers by amplifier makers and its transformers are integrated into microphones by microphone manufacturers.
7. It specializes in reissuing vintage loudspeaker designs from the 1950s and 1960s alongside new original designs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The brand was reintroduced by SICA, which manufactures the loudspeakers.
Organization type: It is a subsidiary brand operated by its parent manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of loudspeakers and audio transformers.
Geography: It is a brand based in the United States with manufacturing by its parent company.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Antares
points.description: Audio software company developing pitch correction and vocal processing plugins for music production.
points.bullets:
A developer of professional audio software that builds vocal processing algorithms and plugins for music recording and live performance, selling to musicians, producers, and engineers.
1. An audio software developer whose vocal processing plugins run as native software on Windows and macOS workstations.
2. Digital signal processing algorithms and machine learning models deployed via runtime environments for real-time vocal manipulation.
3. Pitch correction, vocal harmonization, vocoding, vocal compression, equalization, reverb, de-essing, and noise reduction.
4. Software products and plugins delivered as perpetual licenses and subscriptions managed through USB and cloud-based license managers.
5. Music recording studios, live performance rigs, and vocal production workflows.
6. Studios and musicians, including professional producers, engineers, and performing artists.
7. Its plugins are hosted by musicians and engineers on digital audio workstations and integrated into hardware vocal effects processors by equipment brands.
8. The company holds an established position as the industry standard for pitch correction algorithms in music production.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its licensing is managed through the PACE iLok platform, and its technology is integrated into hardware vocal effects pedals by HeadRush.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A long-established company with over 20 years in the market and a GRAMMY award.
Geography: The company operates in the professional audio sector.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on vocal production technology and audio processing software.

points.name: FabFilter
points.description: Dutch software company building virtual studio plugins for music recording, mixing, and mastering.
points.bullets:
A software company that develops premium audio effect and virtual instrument plugins for music recording, mixing, and mastering, targeting professional studios, semi-professional engineers, and serious home recording enthusiasts.
1. A software developer whose digital audio workstation plugins run as native software on users' computers.
2. Advanced digital signal processing algorithms for audio dynamics, frequency, and time manipulation, combined with highly flexible modulation architectures and detailed graphical user interfaces.
3. Equalization, compression, multiband dynamics, peak limiting, reverberation, saturation, analog synthesis, tape delay, and multi-mode filtering.
4. Software plugins compatible with VST, VST3, Audio Units, AAX, and CLAP formats.
5. Digital audio workstations in professional recording, mixing, and mastering studios, as well as home recording setups.
6. Professional studios, semi-professional engineers, and home recording enthusiasts.
7. Its plugins are purchased directly by end-users and instantiated within digital audio workstation software.
8. Clean, transparent processing paired with meticulous graphical interfaces and fast workflow establishes its products as industry standards in mixing communities.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Premium direct software sales of individual plugins and bundled collections.
Geography: Based in Amsterdam and operating in the professional audio market.
Beyond audio: The organization operates exclusively in the professional audio software sector with a pure focus on audio plugins.

points.name: RHA Audio
points.description: British headphone brand developing premium audio technology for Sonos headphones.
points.bullets:
An audio technology provider that develops headphone acoustic technology and hardware, acquired to support a parent company's entry into premium headphone manufacturing.
1. An audio hardware and technology developer whose designs and engineering are integrated into finished consumer headphones produced by its parent company.
2. Finished headphone hardware and underlying acoustic technology integrated into the parent company's products.
3. The parent company and its consumer electronics customer base.
4. Its acoustic technology and hardware engineering are designed into premium headphones manufactured and sold by its parent company.
points.profile:
Organization type: A subsidiary brand and acquired technology unit of a publicly traded parent company.
Beyond audio: Its technology is applied entirely within the audio hardware domain.

points.name: Mycroft
points.description: Open source voice assistant startup developing privacy-focused smart speakers.
points.bullets:
An open source voice assistant developer that built privacy-focused voice assistant software and finished smart speaker hardware for consumers and developers.
1. An open source software and hardware developer whose voice assistant platform runs on its own smart speaker hardware and is integrated with third-party chips.
2. Open source voice assistant software paired with integrated microphone array processors.
3. Wake word detection, speech recognition, natural language understanding, and smart home control via openHAB integration.
4. Finished smart speaker hardware, development kits, and open source software.
5. Smart speakers and smart home systems.
6. Consumers and developers.
7. Its voice assistant software and finished hardware are used directly by consumers and developers, with its open source codebase maintained by community forks.
8. The first open source voice assistant platform with a strong focus on privacy.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: XMOS and openHAB.
Organization type: Defunct startup whose open source software continues in community forks.
Business model: Hardware sales and crowdfunding preorders.
Scale and maturity: Generated over $1M in preorders for its second-generation smart speaker before ceasing operations.
Geography: Operated globally with an open source community.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus was voice assistant software and hardware.

points.name: Premium Audio Company
points.description: US audio company marketing premium home theater speakers and receivers under brands like Klipsch and Onkyo.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics manufacturer that designs, builds, and sells finished audio hardware under multiple heritage brands for consumers and home entertainment enthusiasts.
1. An equipment maker that builds A/V receivers, stereo receivers, amplifiers, hi-fi components, and speakers, sold as finished consumer hardware.
2. Finished hardware and consumer electronic products.
3. Home entertainment systems, home theaters, vehicles, and recreational vehicles.
4. Consumers, automakers, and furniture brands.
5. Its finished hardware products are distributed through retail channels and integrated into vehicles by consumer brands.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Klipsch, Onkyo, Integra, Pioneer, Sharp, La-Z-Boy, INFINITI, Airstream, Gentex, and Voxx International.
Organization type: A wholly owned subsidiary of a publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A large corporate division managing numerous legacy audio brands, established as a consolidated entity in 2020.
Geography: Based in the United States and operating globally.
Beyond audio: The organization's focus is entirely on consumer and premium audio products.

points.name: Acurus/Aragon
points.description: US audio company building high-performance processors and amplifiers for home theaters and mastering facilities.
points.bullets:
A maker of high-performance audio equipment that designs and manufactures immersive processors, preamplifiers, and power amplifiers for home theaters, screening rooms, mastering facilities, and two-channel listening rooms, and develops an acoustic optimization solution.
1. An audio equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished hardware products and accompanying acoustic optimization software for professional and residential audio environments.
2. Custom electronic, mechanical, and software designs form the basis of the proprietary processors, amplifiers, and acoustic optimization tools.
3. The hardware delivers immersive audio processing, signal amplification, and acoustic room optimization.
4. Customers receive finished hardware components and software products.
5. Its products are used in home theaters, screening rooms, media rooms, mastering facilities, and two-channel listening spaces.
6. It sells to consumers, audiophiles, and professional audio facilities.
7. Its finished hardware components are installed directly into residential and professional audio systems.
8. Its approach relies on custom parts based on proprietary electronics, mechanical, and software design.
points.profile:
Organization type: It is a privately held company operating as a subsidiary brand.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on audio hardware and acoustic optimization solutions.

points.name: API - Automated Processes, Inc
points.description: Pro audio company building premium analog mixing consoles and recording gear.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures analog recording gear and internal components for recording studios and musicians.
1. An equipment maker that builds analog recording consoles and components sold as finished hardware.
2. Analog audio circuitry designed for recording and mixing.
3. Signal processing, microphone preamplification, mixing and equalization in the analog domain.
4. Finished hardware products and internal components.
5. Recording studios and professional audio production environments.
6. Studios and musicians.
7. Its finished hardware is installed in recording studios by engineers and producers.
8. A focus on warm analog sound across a range of products from large consoles to internal components.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A company founded in 1969 with decades of operation in the professional audio market.
Geography: Based and operates in the United States.
Beyond audio: Professional audio equipment manufacturing is its entire focus.

points.name: ATR Service, Inc.
points.description: Pro audio service company restoring and upgrading analog tape recorders for studio recording.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that restores, remanufactures, and upgrades analog tape recorders, providing custom-engineered machines and specialized services for audio professionals.
1. An equipment maker that builds remanufactured analog tape recorder units and hardware upgrades, sold as finished hardware and direct services.
2. Analog magnetic tape recording and playback systems engineered to exceed original performance specifications.
3. High-fidelity analog recording and playback with enhanced sonic characteristics, warmth, and dynamic response.
4. Finished hardware, hardware upgrades, and direct service engagements.
5. Studios, mastering facilities, archives, and audiophile listening environments.
6. Recording studios, mastering facilities, archival institutions, and audiophiles.
7. Its remanufactured recorders and upgrade services are deployed directly into the analog production workflows of professional audio facilities.
8. It remanufactures discontinued but culturally significant analog tape machines to modern reliability and performance standards, sustaining demand for legacy formats in a digital industry.
points.profile:
Business model: Hardware sales, hardware upgrades, and direct service engagements.
Geography: It operates globally as a specialist within the professional audio market.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on professional analog audio equipment.

points.name: Audioscape Engineering Co.
points.description: US audio hardware company hand-making boutique analog gear for professional recording studios.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and builds boutique analog hardware for the recording studio market, selling handcrafted units in small batches to engineers, producers and musicians.
1. A professional audio equipment maker whose finished analog hardware units are sold as physical products and run in studios and audio production environments.
2. The core technology is analog audio circuitry designed and assembled through research and development into discrete hardware components.
3. The company delivers finished hardware units manufactured and hand-assembled one at a time in small batches.
4. The products are used in recording studios and audio production facilities.
5. The company sells to recording engineers, producers, studios and musicians.
6. Its finished hardware products are purchased and operated directly by end users in recording and production studios.
7. The approach is distinguished by boutique-quality, hand-built analog hardware manufactured in small batches one at a time at a reasonable cost.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of its finished analog audio equipment.
Scale and maturity: The company operates as a small-batch manufacturer hand-assembling units individually.
Geography: It is based in Daytona Beach, Florida, United States and manufactures its products locally.
Beyond audio: Audio hardware manufacturing is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: Augspurger
points.description: US pro audio manufacturer building high-performance monitoring systems and studio integration for recording facilities.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures high-performance studio monitors, subwoofers, and DSP-controlled amplifiers for recording studios, producers, engineers, and commercial audio facilities.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished professional monitor speakers, subwoofers, and power amplifiers sold as integrated hardware systems installed in studio environments.
2. Horn-loaded loudspeaker designs built with solid maple wood, beryllium compression driver diaphragms, high-sensitivity cone drivers, and multi-way DSP-controlled amplification with onboard acoustic tuning presets.
3. High-SPL monitoring, controlled directivity, immersive audio reproduction, low-frequency extension, and room acoustic calibration.
4. Finished hardware, including passive and active loudspeakers, subwoofers, and dedicated power amplifiers with integrated DSP, sold as complete audio systems.
5. Recording studios, mastering facilities, control rooms, immersive and surround sound mixing environments, and educational facilities.
6. Recording studios, audio engineers, music producers, artists, educational facilities, and commercial environments.
7. Its finished monitor systems are integrated into professionally designed acoustic studio spaces by studio designers and system integrators.
8. It manufactures solid maple wood horns and uses pure beryllium diaphragms to achieve controlled directivity and high sensitivity in its monitor systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It integrates loudspeaker drivers from TAD Laboratories into its systems and operates within the PAD Group of companies.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand operating under a parent professional audio group.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished monitor systems, subwoofers, and amplifiers, supplemented by professional acoustic system tuning services.
Scale and maturity: A well-established manufacturer with over three decades of experience in the professional audio market.
Geography: Based in Hanover, MA, USA, with installations in recording studios worldwide.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on professional audio monitoring, loudspeaker engineering, and studio system integration.

points.name: Professional Audio Design
points.description: Studio integration company supplying professional audio equipment, custom monitors, and acoustic design for recording facilities.
points.bullets:
An audio system integration and professional services company that designs, builds, supplies and installs professional monitoring systems and recording studio environments for studios, producers, engineers and educational facilities.
1. A professional services and equipment company that builds custom monitoring systems and recording studio environments, delivered as finished hardware and integrated installations in commercial facilities.
2. Loudspeaker engineering, acoustic design and system integration applied to professional listening environments.
3. High-performance custom monitoring, acoustic architecture, room tuning and technical project oversight for recording and mixing environments.
4. Finished hardware, custom-built monitors and integrated physical studio installations.
5. Recording studios, commercial listening environments and educational facilities.
6. Recording studios, producers, engineers, artists and educational facilities.
7. Its monitoring systems and integration services are installed directly into professional facilities and studios.
8. It combines loudspeaker manufacturing, acoustic architecture and equipment integration into a single end-to-end studio build service.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization operates within the PAD Group alongside Augspurger Monitors and Malekpour Design Partners.
Organization type: A privately held company operating within a collective group of professional audio brands.
Business model: Hardware sales and professional design and integration services.
Scale and maturity: An established organization with over three decades of operation in the professional audio market.
Geography: Operating globally with installations in studios around the world.
Beyond audio: Professional audio, loudspeaker engineering and studio design constitute its entire focus.

points.name: Malekpour Design Partners
points.description: New York pro audio company designing recording studios and integrating high-performance loudspeaker systems.
points.bullets:
A design and integration firm that provides studio design, acoustics, architecture coordination, technical planning, and equipment integration for professional listening and recording environments.
1. A design and systems integration firm whose primary business is delivering finished professional audio environments for studios.
2. Architectural acoustics, room tuning, and loudspeaker system engineering applied to physical studio spaces.
3. Studio acoustic treatment, equipment selection, monitoring system installation, and project oversight.
4. Finished, installed, and tuned studio environments encompassing room construction, acoustic treatment, and professional audio hardware.
5. Recording studios, production rooms, and commercial audio facilities.
6. Recording studios, producers, engineers, artists, educational facilities, and commercial environments.
7. Its design and integration services are commissioned directly by studio owners and operators to build out their physical facilities.
8. It provides a complete approach to facility creation from initial architectural concept through final acoustic tuning and equipment installation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a company within the PAD Group, working alongside Pro Audio Design and Augspurger Monitors.
Organization type: A privately held design firm operating as a subsidiary brand within a larger professional audio group.
Business model: Professional services fees for design, project oversight, and systems integration.
