points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Products are demonstrated at trade shows including LEaT con in Hamburg and ISE, with distribution handled by partners such as Laauser & Vohl.
Organization type: Owner-managed privately held family business founded in 1980.
Business model: Sales of finished professional audio hardware products including loudspeakers, amplifiers and integrated PA systems.
Scale and maturity: A long-established company in operation for over four decades, manufacturing in Germany with regional suppliers.
Geography: Based in Neckarwestheim, Germany, with manufacturing and design in Germany and distribution to professional audio markets.
Beyond audio: The company's entire business is professional audio hardware and associated system software, with an operational focus on regional sourcing, product longevity, packaging reuse and on-site solar energy.

points.name: Hollyland
points.description: Shenzhen wireless technology company making audio and video transmission systems for real-time team communication.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio and communication equipment that designs, manufactures and distributes wireless microphone and intercom systems for content production and team communication.

6. The company sells to professional AV systems integrators.
7. Its finished hardware and cloud platforms are deployed by integrators into professional AV installations.

Scale and maturity: A mature, award-winning company with multiple US patents.
Geography: Based in Calgary, Alberta, Canada.
Beyond audio: The company also develops integrated video solutions for education.

points.name: Outline
points.description: Italian manufacturer building high-performance loudspeaker systems and FPGA-based digital processors for concert sound.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that develops and manufactures high-performance loudspeaker systems, FPGA-based digital audio processors, and lab-grade acoustic measurement turntables for sound reinforcement, installed audio, and research applications.
1. An equipment maker that builds loudspeaker enclosures, digital signal processors, and precision measurement turntables sold as finished hardware.
2. The core technology comprises high-performance loudspeaker drivers, rotatable waveguides, FPGA-based digital signal processing, and computer-controlled precision mechanical turntables with Ethernet remote control.
3. The organization delivers sound reinforcement, digital audio signal processing, loudspeaker dispersion control, and automated acoustic measurement and polar plotting.
4. Customers receive finished hardware loudspeakers, digital processors, measurement turntables, and accompanying control software.
5. The products are used in live concert venues, permanent installed audio systems, and acoustic research and measurement labs.
6. The organization sells to sound reinforcement engineers, audio installation integrators, and corporate technology research labs.
7. Its finished loudspeaker and measurement hardware is distributed through audio equipment distributors and sold directly to professional end users.
8. The organization uniquely spans both professional loudspeaker manufacturing and high-precision acoustic measurement instrumentation, supplying turntables capable of orienting heavy loads up to 1000kg for major technology research labs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners and users include Apple, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Intel, Lucasfilm, Dolby, and MIT, alongside integration with Audio Precision, Audiomatica Clio, Listen Inc SoundCheck, Klippel, NTI, and ARTA measurement software, with distribution by Audio Link.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of loudspeakers, digital processors, and measurement equipment.
Scale and maturity: The organization has been established since 1973 and maintains a strong international presence in the professional audio industry.
Geography: It is based near Brescia, Italy, and operates internationally.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Owl Labs
points.description: Video conferencing technology company making 360-degree cameras, microphones and speakers for hybrid meetings.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio and video conferencing equipment that builds integrated 360-degree cameras, microphones and speakers for hybrid organizations. The company manufactures all-in-one smart devices and room accessories that automatically track and frame active speakers for remote participants.
1. An equipment maker that builds smart video conferencing devices and sells them as finished hardware running its own embedded software.
2. AI-powered camera tracking algorithms and 360-degree optics integrated with speaker and microphone arrays.
3. 360-degree video capture, automatic speaker tracking, acoustic pickup over extended ranges, and wireless multi-device pairing.
4. The company delivers finished hardware products alongside companion accessories and a mobile app.
5. The devices are used in conference rooms, boardrooms, classrooms and live hybrid meeting spaces.
6. The company sells to enterprises, small businesses and educational institutions.
7. Its finished hardware devices are purchased directly by organizations for use in their meeting spaces.
8. Its approach centers on all-in-one 360-degree devices that combine camera, microphone and speaker with AI-driven automatic speaker tracking.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The devices are compatible with Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Google Meet.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of conferencing devices and related accessories.
Scale and maturity: The company has raised $47 million in funding and is used by over 250,000 organizations.
Geography: The company is based in Boston, USA, and operates globally.

points.name: Penton Audio USA
points.description: US-based manufacturer of public address, voice alarm, and mass notification equipment using audio-over-IP systems for schools and general audio distribution.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of public address, voice alarm, and mass notification equipment that builds finished hardware systems and audio over IP distribution systems for commercial and institutional facilities.
1. An equipment maker that builds public address, voice alarm, mass notification, amplifiers, speakers, and audio over IP systems sold as finished hardware.
2. The core technology comprises audio over IP networking for LAN and WAN distribution, combined with amplification and loudspeaker driver systems built to EN54 and UL2572 compliance standards.
3. It delivers paging, voice alarm, mass notification, and general audio distribution across networked facilities.
4. Customers receive finished hardware products including speakers, amplifiers, and networked audio distribution equipment.
5. Its equipment is deployed in commercial buildings, K-12 schools, and facilities requiring voice alarm and mass notification.
6. The company sells to facility operators, system integrators, and institutions requiring public address and life safety communication.
7. Its finished hardware is installed in buildings by system integrators and facility managers for public address and emergency communication.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of public address, voice alarm, mass notification, and audio networking equipment.
Geography: The company is based in the United States and operates worldwide.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, its mass notification systems encompass life safety and emergency communication.

points.name: PlexusAV
points.description: Networked AV company delivering standards-based AV-over-IP networking solutions.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that builds standards-based AV-over-IP endpoints and management solutions for networked audio and video distribution, selling through open-architecture products to integrators and engineers.
1. An equipment maker that designs encoders, decoders, gateways, and networked audio endpoints sold as finished hardware products running on standard IP networks.
2. The core technology comprises ultra low-latency video codecs and networked audio protocols built on open standards for AV-over-IP convergence.
3. The equipment delivers ultra low-latency audio and video encoding and decoding, USB-C connectivity, and network transport over standard 1GbE infrastructure.
4. Customers receive finished hardware products and network management solutions built on open standards.
5. The hardware is used in networked AV installations, IT environments, and scalable AV-over-IP deployments.
6. The company sells to systems integrators and engineers.
7. Its finished hardware products are installed by systems integrators into enterprise IT and AV networks.
8. The company differentiates by building open-architecture products on open standards to avoid proprietary lock-in.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Products are built on standards including IPMX, NMOS, Dante, and JPEG-XS, with select products officially IPMX Certified.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of encoders, decoders, and network endpoints.
Scale and maturity: The organization is an established company exhibiting at trade shows.
Geography: The company is based in and operates in markets serviced by professional AV distribution.
Beyond audio: The organization builds products for combined audio and video over IP distribution.

points.name: Rational Acoustics
points.description: Audio technology company developing sound system measurement and analysis software.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and equipment company that builds audio analysis and optimization software for sound system measurement, alignment and room acoustics, sold to live sound engineers and system integrators.
1. A developer tools company whose dual-channel FFT-based audio measurement and analysis software runs as a software product on computers and is integrated into third-party digital mixers.
2. Dual-channel FFT-based real-time analyzer technology using time and frequency domain views for spectrum analysis.
3. Real-time audio spectrum analysis, sound system measurement, loudspeaker measurement and room acoustics analysis.
4. Software products, hardware products, training courses and professional consulting.
5. Live sound engineering, sound system alignment and room acoustics measurement workflows.
6. Live sound engineers, audio professionals and system integrators.
7. Its real-time analyzer technology is integrated by digital mixer manufacturers into their hardware products.
8. Combines its measurement software with training courses, hardware products and professional consulting for the sound system optimization field.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its Smaart platform is integrated into StudioLive SeriesIII mixers by PreSonus.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses or subscriptions, hardware sales, training fees and professional consulting fees.
Geography: Based and operates in the United States.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio test and measurement, sound system alignment and the associated education.

points.name: Renkus-Heinz
points.description: US pro audio manufacturer building digitally steerable loudspeaker arrays for public venues.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures loudspeaker systems, specializing in digitally steerable column arrays and beam-steering technology for installed sound reinforcement in large venues.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished professional loudspeaker hardware.
2. Multi-driver column arrays whose driver timing and processing are controlled digitally to steer vertical beam patterns, integrating point-source acoustics with digital beam steering.
3. Digitally steerable vertical pattern control, high SPL output and multiple independently controllable beams from a single column enclosure.
4. Finished passive and active loudspeaker hardware with associated control software for mobile devices.
5. Performing arts venues, transportation hubs, houses of worship, educational facilities, corporate buildings and governmental facilities.
6. Audio system integrators, consultants and facility operators installing sound reinforcement in large venues.
7. Its loudspeakers are specified by consultants and installed by integrators into venues for sound reinforcement.
8. Combines point-source driver design with digital beam steering to enable high SPL and precise vertical pattern control from arrays that can be flown, ground-stacked or used standalone.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of professional loudspeaker systems.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1979 with 51-200 employees and global offices.
Geography: Headquartered in Foothill Ranch, California, USA with additional offices around the globe.
Beyond audio: The organization is an audio pure-play whose entire focus is professional loudspeaker technology.

points.name: Revolution Acoustics
points.description: US audio company making invisible surface-mounted speakers for immersive room sound.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and finished hardware that designs and sells invisible surface-excitation transducers for installed audio, and handcrafted studio monitoring systems for recording professionals.
1. An equipment maker that builds surface-excitation transducers and studio monitor loudspeakers sold as finished physical hardware.
2. The transducers use planar wave physics to excite adhered surfaces into acoustic planar radiating sources, while the monitors use passive crossovers, high-excursion ceramic matrix drivers, and AMT tweeters paired with Class A/B amplification.
3. The transducers deliver invisible room-wide spatial audio with even frequency response and sound pressure levels across large surfaces, and the monitors deliver full-range frequency response and dynamic accuracy for mix translation.
4. The products are sold as finished hardware components and complete stereo monitoring systems.
5. The transducers are used in commercial and residential built-in installations, and the monitors are used in recording, mixing, and mastering studios.
6. The company sells to custom integrators, residential and commercial installers, and recording professionals.
7. Its finished hardware is distributed through authorized dealers and installed directly into architectural surfaces or studio environments.
8. The transducer approach turns standard building materials like drywall and glass into acoustic radiating surfaces to achieve a completely invisible form factor without high-frequency beaming.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Studio monitor development and voicing was handled in collaboration with mastering engineer Brian Lucey and loudspeaker designer Kevin Malmgren.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through the sale of finished hardware.
Scale and maturity: The company has over two decades of operation in its market.
Geography: It is based in the USA and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio hardware and monitoring technology.

points.name: Riedel Communications
points.description: German pro audio manufacturer building real-time networks and digital audio matrix systems for broadcast and live events.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio, video and communications networking equipment that designs, builds and distributes real-time networks, digital audio matrix systems, wireless intercoms and IP-based media networks for broadcast, pro-audio, event, sports, theater and security applications.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished hardware and networking systems used in professional real-time media and communications infrastructure.
2. The company develops digital audio matrix systems, wireless intercom systems, and audio and media networking protocols, including one that transmits audio over Cat-5 cabling.
3. The systems deliver real-time audio routing, digital audio matrixing, wireless intercom communications and media networking.
4. The organization provides finished hardware, networking equipment and communications systems.
5. Its products are used in broadcast, pro-audio, event, sports, theater and security applications.
6. The organization sells to broadcast, event, sports, theater and security professionals and organizations.
7. Its finished hardware and networking equipment are deployed directly into professional broadcast, event and communications infrastructures.
8. The company integrates real-time audio, video and communications networking into unified hardware systems for large-scale live and broadcast productions.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held manufacturing company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales and equipment distribution.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1987, the company employs over 1000 people across 30 locations worldwide.
Geography: The organization is headquartered in Wuppertal, Germany and operates in Europe, Australia, Asia and the Americas.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the company designs and manufactures real-time video and communications networks.

points.name: Stewart Audio
points.description: Professional audio manufacturer building networked amplifiers and integrated DSP systems for commercial and institutional spaces.

A manufacturer of professional-grade audio and control systems that builds networked audio amplifiers, amplifiers with integrated DSP, and control panels for professional and educational settings, and provides custom design services for specialty applications.

Organization type: A privately held manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales and custom design services.
Geography: Based in the United States and serving the professional and educational marketplace.

points.name: Televic Conference

points.bullets:
A maker of professional conferencing equipment that develops, manufactures and delivers systems for moderated live and hybrid meetings, providing audio capture, processing and distribution hardware and software for enterprises and institutions.
1. An equipment maker that builds conference systems sold as finished hardware and integrated software products for installation in meeting venues.

4. Customers receive finished hardware and integrated software products designed for installation in conference rooms and venues.
5. The systems are used in conference rooms, meeting venues and legislative or institutional settings requiring moderated live and hybrid meetings.

7. Its finished conferencing systems are installed directly into venues by integrators and institutional buyers.
8. The approach combines over five decades of specialization in moderated conferencing with integrated support for simultaneous interpretation across live and hybrid formats.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is an established privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through sales of finished hardware and integrated conference systems.
Scale and maturity: The company has operated for over 50 years in the conferencing technology market.

Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on conferencing and meeting technology with no business outside audio-related moderation and communication.

points.name: Theory Audio Design
points.location: Lake Forest, Orange County, CA, USA
points.description: California-based manufacturer building professional loudspeakers and controllers for commercial, residential, and outdoor spaces.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures loudspeakers, subwoofers, and amplified loudspeaker controllers for residential, commercial, and outdoor sound reinforcement installations.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished loudspeakers, subwoofers, and multi-channel amplified loudspeaker controllers sold as finished hardware.
2. Multi-channel Class-D amplification topologies with DSP matrices, IP network control, and Dante/AES67 audio networking integrated into loudspeaker controllers and passive loudspeaker transducer designs.
3. High-output sound reproduction, multi-channel surround sound decoding up to 9.4.4 configurations, multi-room audio distribution, TCP/IP system control, and all-weather outdoor sound reinforcement.
4. Finished hardware products including in-wall and on-wall loudspeakers, landscape bollards, subwoofers, soundbars, and IP-controlled amplified controllers, along with system configuration software.
5. Home theaters, whole-home residential audio systems, commercial spaces, outdoor landscape installations, and large-format sound reinforcement venues.
6. Residential and commercial installers, audio-visual integration firms, and consumers seeking professional-grade architectural audio systems.
7. Its finished hardware products are integrated into residential and commercial installations by audio-visual integrators and installation professionals.
8. It bridges professional sound reinforcement engineering with standardized architectural product lines designed for aesthetic integration in compact residential and commercial installations.

Key partners and customers: It uses Powersoft's patented Class-D amplification topologies and SmartRail power supplies, and is the sister brand of Pro Audio Technology.
Organization type: A privately held company operating a residential audio brand and a commercial sound reinforcement division.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished loudspeakers, subwoofers, and amplified controllers.
Scale and maturity: A company founded in 2018 that launched its commercial Theory Professional division in 2023.
Geography: Based in Lake Forest, Orange County, California, USA, operating through residential and commercial audio integration channels.

points.name: TOA Corporation
points.description: Japanese manufacturer building public address systems, voice evacuation equipment, and professional sound reinforcement products.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of commercial and professional audio equipment that makes amplifiers, speakers, mixers, wireless microphone systems, digital processors, and network audio and security equipment for sound reinforcement, public address, voice evacuation, and surveillance applications.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished commercial and professional audio and security hardware sold as physical products installed in venues and buildings.
2. Audio signal processing, acoustic transducers, RF wireless transmission, and IP-based audio networking and intercom systems.
3. Sound reinforcement, voice evacuation, public address paging, audio mixing, distributed network audio, and conference room acoustic noise control and beamforming.
4. Customers get it as finished hardware, including amplifiers, speakers, microphones, mixers, processors, intercoms, and security cameras.
5. Commercial buildings, public address systems, conference rooms, live venues, security installations, and background music systems.
6. Commercial integrators, professional audio installers, and enterprise facilities.
7. Its finished hardware is distributed by audio equipment resellers and installed in commercial buildings by integration firms.
8. It combines commercial audio and voice evacuation with security and intercom systems in a single hardware portfolio.

Key partners and customers: Pro Acoustics.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.

Beyond audio: The company also manufactures security cameras and video surveillance equipment.

points.name: Vanco
points.description: AV products manufacturer distributing audio/video equipment and installation accessories.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio and video equipment that engineers, manufactures and distributes amplifiers, architectural speakers, AV over IP distribution systems and installation accessories for professional AV integrators and distributors.

8. The organization operates four distinct brands to serve specific segments of the professional AV market, ranging from value-driven installation essentials to advanced AV over IP systems and architectural audio.

Key partners and customers: The company is a preferred partner for Procell professional batteries and the exclusive partner for Monster power and surge centers.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held international product manufacturing and distribution company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of finished audio and video equipment, speakers, accessories and power products.
Scale and maturity: The company has a 60-year legacy and operates from its U.S. headquarters with nationwide distribution.

points.name: Zycoo Co., Ltd.

A developer and manufacturer of IP communication and audio systems that builds unified communications platforms, IP PBX systems, and networked audio endpoints for enterprises, industrial facilities, and large venues.
1. An equipment maker that builds IP PBX systems, SIP-based intercoms, and networked public address endpoints sold as finished hardware and accompanying software for enterprise and industrial networks.

3. VoIP call routing, paging, intercom, voicemail, video calls, IVR, call recording, and public address audio distribution.

Key partners and customers: Asterisk, Almiria Kenya.
Organization type: Privately held company.

points.name: Anaccord Electronic Technology Co., Ltd

An equipment maker that designs and manufactures Hi-Fi integrated audio systems, power amplifiers, active speakers, and digital PA systems, and provides original equipment and original design manufacturing services for other brands.

points.profile:
Organization type: The company is a privately held electronics manufacturer.

points.name: Celestion

A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures high-performance loudspeakers, compression drivers and horns for guitar amplification, sound reinforcement and installed sound, selling to OEM partners and end users.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment that builds loudspeaker drivers, compression drivers and horns sold as finished hardware components.
2. Electromagnetic and acoustic transducer designs, including cone loudspeakers, ribbon tweeters, coaxial alignments and waveguide horns.
3. Low-frequency reproduction, high-frequency reproduction, full-range reproduction and sound dispersion control.
4. Finished hardware components and custom transducer design services.
5. Guitar amplifiers, sound reinforcement systems, clubs, theatres, live venues and installed audio systems.
6. OEM loudspeaker manufacturers, consumer electronics brands, audio brand partners and musicians.

Organization type: A privately held company.

Geography: Based in Suffolk, United Kingdom, with global operations.

points.name: M&W Pro Audio

A maker of professional audio equipment that develops digital mixers and microphone preamps for music and audio professionals, combining advanced DSP architectures with touch-screen interfaces.

2. Digital signal processing architectures running on dedicated hardware, paired with large touch-screen interfaces and quad-matched, parallel-input balanced microphone preamp circuit designs.
3. Live digital audio mixing, microphone preamplification, and workflow control via integrated touch-screen user interfaces.
4. Finished hardware products, including digital mixers and standalone microphone preamps.

6. Music and audio professionals.

Key partners and customers: The company was founded by industry veterans Greg Mackie and Peter Watts.
Organization type: A privately held professional audio manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of digital mixers and microphone preamps.

An equipment maker that designs and sells passive and powered speakers, subwoofers, amplifiers, multi-room distribution controllers, and installation accessories for custom residential and commercial installations.

1. An equipment maker that builds loudspeakers, amplifiers, digital audio platforms and IP endpoints sold as finished hardware installed in commercial buildings.
2. Analog and digital audio reproduction, power amplification, IP-based audio networking and digitally steerable beam steering loudspeaker arrays.
3. Distributed audio, background music, paging, mass communications, sound masking and adaptive ambient noise sensing and level adjustment.
4. The company delivers its products as finished hardware, including ceiling and pendant loudspeakers, IP endpoints, amplifiers and ambient noise sensors.
5. Commercial projects, campuses, building installations and systems requiring analog-to-IP paging upgrades.
6. Audiovisual professionals, systems integrators, paging system installers and commercial end users.
7. Its finished hardware is specified and installed by systems integrators into commercial building projects.
8. It provides an expansive portfolio of interconnected and integrated commercial audio systems backed by decades of experience.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It holds a significant equity stake in a German loudspeaker manufacturer and its products are installed by paging solution providers and featured by pro audio distributors.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer and commercial audio brand.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of finished audio and communication equipment.
Scale and maturity: An established global manufacturer with decades of experience in the commercial audio market.
Geography: Based in Texas, USA, operating globally.
Beyond audio: The organization also provides security and communication technology solutions alongside its commercial audio equipment.

points.name: AUDAC
points.description: Belgian professional audio brand building loudspeakers, amplifiers, and control systems for commercial and public spaces.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and sells loudspeakers, amplifiers, audio processors and control systems as a unified commercial audio ecosystem for installation professionals.
1. An equipment maker that designs professional audio hardware and control systems sold as finished products for installed venues.
2. The core technology comprises architectural acoustics, amplification electronics, digital signal processing and networked control systems engineered for unified operation.
3. The systems deliver sound reinforcement, audio signal processing and intuitive system control across multi-zone installed environments.
4. Customers get the systems as finished hardware products and accompanying control software.
5. The equipment is used in hospitality, retail, corporate, education and public spaces.
6. The company sells to systems integrators and installation professionals.
7. Its finished equipment is specified and installed by integrators into commercial and public venues.
8. Its approach distinguishes itself by providing a complete, tightly integrated hardware and control ecosystem designed for simplified installation and flexible multi-zone management.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held brand.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales and associated professional audio equipment.
Geography: It is based in Belgium and operates internationally.

points.name: Audfly Technology
points.description: Chinese audio technology company building directional speakers that project focused beams of sound without interference.
points.bullets:
A maker of directional audio equipment that builds super directional speakers which generate focused sound beams, providing independent non-interfering sound zones in open environments for commercial installations.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished directional speaker hardware for indoor and outdoor installations.
2. Sound-focusing technology that generates sound in a narrow beam akin to light, creating independent and non-interfering focused sound zones in open environments.
3. Directional audio projection that creates focused sound zones without interference in open spaces.
4. Finished hardware in the form of super directional speakers suitable for large-scale custom systems.
5. Large-scale custom systems used both indoors and outdoors in various open sound environments.
6. Commercial customers deploying large-scale audio installations in public or open environments.
7. Its finished speakers are integrated into custom audio systems by commercial installers.
8. It creates focused sound beams akin to light that form independent non-interfering sound zones in open environments.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of directional speaker systems.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is directional audio hardware.

points.name: Audiocenter
points.description: Global professional audio brand designing speakers, line arrays, subwoofers, amplifiers, and audio matrix processors.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures passive and active loudspeakers, line arrays, subwoofers, multi-channel amplifiers, and audio matrix processors for the professional audio and musical instrument markets.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished loudspeakers, line arrays, subwoofers, amplifiers, and digital signal processors sold as physical hardware for installation and live sound reinforcement.
2. Passive and active loudspeaker designs utilizing full-range drivers, soft-dome tweeters, and compression drivers, combined with Class-D amplification, digital signal processing, and Dante audio networking.
3. Sound reinforcement, low-frequency reproduction, multi-channel amplification with 70V/100V transformer output, digital signal processing, acoustic correction, and audio matrix routing.
4. The organization provides its products as finished hardware units, including self-powered active speakers and separate power amplifiers.
5. The equipment is used in medium-sized venues, professional audio installations, and musical instrument sound reinforcement settings.
6. The company sells to professional audio integrators, installers, and live sound rental companies.
7. Its finished audio hardware is deployed by integrators and rental companies in installed venues and live event settings.
8. The organization integrates customized transducers from named driver manufacturers into its own loudspeaker and line array designs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company uses customized Beyma low-frequency and high-frequency drivers in its speaker products.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held professional audio brand.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of finished audio equipment.
Scale and maturity: The organization maintains a research and development team and a global technical support network spanning Europe and America.
Geography: The company operates globally with research, supply, and technical support resources sourced from Europe and America.
Beyond audio: Audio hardware manufacturing is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: Audioropa, a brand of Humantechnik
points.description: German assistive listening brand developing professional audio transmission systems for individuals with hearing disabilities.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and produces audio transmission systems for professional applications, operating as a subdivision brand of a company that develops assistive listening technology for people with hearing disabilities.
1. An equipment maker whose finished hardware products are sold as professional audio transmission systems.
2. The company develops radio frequency and infrared audio transmission technology for wireless signal delivery.
3. The organization delivers wireless audio transmission and assistive listening capabilities.
4. Customers receive finished hardware products and integrated systems.
5. The products are used in professional audio installations and assistive listening environments.
6. The company sells to professional audio installers and institutions requiring assistive listening systems.
7. Its finished hardware products are installed directly in professional venues and facilities.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a subdivision brand of a privately held company.
Geography: The company is based in Germany.

points.name: Aura Audio
points.description: Finnish loudspeaker manufacturer building audio systems that require minimal processing to deliver high-quality sound.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures loudspeaker systems for sound reinforcement. It designs and builds enclosures that achieve uniform dispersion and pattern control with minimal digital signal processing, delivering sound quality for live and installed sound applications.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment that builds loudspeaker systems sold as finished hardware.
2. Acoustic and enclosure design is the core technology, using physical engineering to achieve pattern control and uniform dispersion without complex digital signal processing.
3. The systems deliver uniform dispersion, pattern control, and accurate sound reproduction of an audio source.
4. Customers get the systems as finished hardware products.
5. The loudspeakers are used in live venues and installed sound reinforcement settings.
6. The organization sells to audio professionals, sound reinforcement engineers, and venue installers.
7. Its finished loudspeaker systems are deployed directly by sound engineers and integrators in live and installed venues.
8. Its approach achieves pattern control and sound quality through physical acoustic design that requires minimal processing rather than relying on complex digital signal processing.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is an independent privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of finished loudspeaker systems.
Geography: It is based in Lieto, Finland.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Aurelys + Ambiance
points.description: Audio solutions company building modular speaker and framing systems for custom home cinema integration.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional and high-end residential audio equipment that designs modular speaker systems and architectural framing concepts for custom integration in private cinemas and home entertainment rooms.
1. An equipment maker that builds modular loudspeakers, screen-framing systems and integrated cinema-music sound systems sold as finished hardware.
2. Modular loudspeaker architectures and architectural screen-to-speaker framing concepts with multi-sonic mode capabilities for movie and music reproduction.
3. Bespoke sound reproduction, architectural integration around video displays and dual-mode cinema and music playback within a single system.
4. Finished hardware products and modular speaker building blocks sold to custom integrators.
5. Home entertainment rooms, dedicated private cinemas and architectural installations around video displays.
6. Custom installers and integrators building bespoke residential entertainment systems.
7. Its finished hardware is specified and installed by custom integrators into private residential cinemas and home entertainment rooms.
8. Its modular building blocks enable integrators to scale configurations to room layouts while combining architectural screen framing with dual-mode cinema and music reproduction.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of modular speaker systems and architectural framing products.
Geography: Demonstrates and launches products at integrated systems events in Europe.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on audio hardware and architectural integration for residential entertainment.

points.name: AV EMEA B.V.

A distributor and system integration company that represents a portfolio of consumer and professional audio brands across the custom installation and HiFi sectors. It provides sales, distribution, and support for audio equipment to integrators and retailers.

points.description: German pro audio manufacturer building loudspeakers, amplifiers, and mixers for permanently installed sound systems in public spaces.

A maker of professional audio equipment that develops and manufactures digitally steerable column loudspeakers, passive loudspeakers, audio amplifiers, wired microphones, and digital audio mixers for permanently installed sound systems in public and commercial spaces.

A maker of residential audio and home automation equipment that designs multiroom audio systems, music servers, amplifiers and active speakers for high-end smart homes.

points.name: BEC Akustik
points.description: German acoustic engineering company building discreet line array speakers for architectural spaces.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs and builds discreet line array loudspeakers for architectural and consulting applications. The company provides finished audio hardware that combines German engineering with visual unobtrusiveness for installation in built environments.

points.name: Blustream
points.description: UK AV equipment manufacturer building video and audio distribution products for commercial and residential installations.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that builds audiovisual distribution products, including HDMI extenders, matrix switchers, splitters, and AV over IP systems, for residential, commercial, and corporate installations.

2. Analog and electronic audio amplification and signal routing hardware.
3. Sound reinforcement for public address applications.

5. Public address systems.
6. Integrators and installers.

points.name: Shenzhen Moertek Technology Co.,Ltd

points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs, produces and markets professional audio and video conferencing hardware, including audio conference speakerphones, HD video conference cameras and web conferencing webcams, providing OEM, ODM, SKD and JDM manufacturing services to brands.
1. A maker of professional audio and video equipment whose finished hardware products are sold to other brands under contract manufacturing and original design arrangements.
2. The company integrates its proprietary core algorithms and image signal processor algorithms at the chip level within its hardware designs.
3. It delivers audio conferencing speakerphone functionality alongside high-definition video capture for unified communications.
4. Customers receive finished hardware products manufactured at the company's factory under OEM, ODM, SKD and JDM service agreements.
5. Its products are used in audio conferencing, HD video conferencing and web conferencing settings.
6. The company sells to brands seeking OEM, ODM, SKD or JDM manufacturing and design services for conferencing hardware.
7. Its manufactured hardware products are branded and sold by other companies in the professional conferencing market.
points.profile:
Organization type: The company is a high-tech manufacturing enterprise established in 2014.
Business model: It generates revenue through the design, production and sale of conferencing hardware products and contract manufacturing services.
Scale and maturity: The organization operates a 20,000-square-meter factory with over 500 employees and an engineering office with more than 30 engineers.
Geography: It is based in Shenzhen and Dongguan, China, operating under a related Hong Kong entity.
Beyond audio: The company also researches, designs, produces and markets professional video products, leveraging a technological heritage in image processing, video electronics and optical technology.

Geography: The organization is based in Shenzhen.

points.name: Soft dB - Sound Masking
points.description: Canadian acoustics company building adaptive sound masking systems for commercial offices.
points.bullets:
A maker of commercial sound masking systems that designs and provides adaptive acoustic privacy and comfort solutions for corporate, healthcare, hospitality, and other commercial environments.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment whose sound masking systems run as finished hardware and software in commercial buildings.
2. The core technology is a patented adaptive sound masking system that automatically adjusts its output to the ambient acoustic conditions of a space.
3. The system delivers adaptive sound masking and speech privacy control.
4. Customers get it as finished hardware and software products installed in commercial spaces.
5. The technology is used in corporate offices, healthcare facilities, hospitality venues, and other commercial environments.
6. The organization sells to AV integrators and acoustic consultants.
7. Its finished sound masking systems are specified by consultants and installed by integrators in commercial buildings.
8. Its approach is distinguished by a patented adaptive system that modifies output to match existing acoustic conditions in spaces of any size or layout.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Geography: The company is established globally and is expanding its sound masking division into Europe.
Beyond audio: The organization also provides broader acoustics and vibration solutions alongside its sound masking systems.

points.name: Soluxtra Universal Corporation
points.description: Speaker driver and module manufacturer providing end-to-end hardware solutions from acoustic simulation and prototyping to high-volume mass production.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of high-performance speaker drivers and speaker modules that provides comprehensive audio and hardware manufacturing solutions for product developers, offering early-stage technical support, advanced speaker production, and integrated hardware engineering from initial design concepts to final mass production.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures speaker drivers and modules as finished hardware components for integration into other products.
2. The core technology comprises speaker drivers and speaker modules developed using COMSOL multiphysics simulations, rapid prototyping, and acoustic performance testing on an automatic production line.
3. It delivers high-performance acoustic reproduction through engineered speaker drivers and integrated speaker modules.
4. Customers get finished speaker drivers and speaker modules manufactured on an automatic production line, along with mechanical engineering services.
5. The speaker drivers and modules are designed into audio products developed by hardware brands.
6. The company sells to product developers and hardware brands requiring speaker modules and manufacturing solutions.
7. Its speaker drivers and modules are integrated into finished audio products by hardware brands.
8. It combines early-stage technical support including COMSOL simulations and rapid prototyping with high-volume automatic production line manufacturing.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held manufacturing company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware manufacturing of speaker drivers and modules and related engineering services.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on audio hardware manufacturing solutions.

An audio equipment manufacturer that designs and produces loudspeakers and amplifiers for residential, professional audio and power electronics markets.

Business model: Hardware sales.

points.name: sonoro audio
points.description: German audio design company building multi-room hi-fi systems and custom installation products.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment and custom installation products that designs and sells hi-fi systems, all-in-one music systems, multi-room audio components, and rack-mountable streaming and amplification hardware for residential distributed audio.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware and multi-room streaming components sold as complete products and installation units for home audio systems.
2. The core technology comprises multi-room audio synchronization software, Audio-over-IP distribution over local networks, and analog amplification circuits integrated into consumer electronics hardware.
3. It delivers multi-room audio playback, zone grouping for up to 32 rooms, networked audio streaming, and sound amplification for distributed residential audio.
4. Customers get the technology as finished hardware products, including streaming amplifiers and standalone music systems, designed for standard 19-inch rack installations.
5. The products are used in residential settings, custom home installations, and multi-room home audio distributions.
6. The company sells directly to consumers and custom installation professionals outfitting residential spaces.
7. Its finished hardware is installed directly into residential properties by custom integrators and consumers.
8. Its approach combines German industrial design with rack-mountable custom installation hardware tailored for multi-room Audio-over-IP distribution.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The products integrate with existing hi-fi systems and all-in-one music systems via wired local networks.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held consumer electronics manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of finished audio products and installation components.
Scale and maturity: The company operates a sound workshop and product development facility on the Lower Rhine in Germany.
Geography: It is based in Germany and operates within the German consumer audio market.

points.name: SoundNet (Guangzhou) Audiovisual Technology Co., Ltd.
points.description: Chinese audiovisual technology company building AES67 networked audio systems for professional audio transmission and control.
points.bullets:
A software and embedded solutions provider that builds AES67-based networked audio ecosystems, covering acquisition, transmission, processing, and playback control for professional audio networking applications.
1. A network audio software developer whose embedded solutions and protocols run on ARM and RISC-V hardware in professional audio networks.
2. Proprietary clock synchronization algorithms and IP-based distributed architectures implement sub-millisecond transport and up to 80% packet loss recovery over standard networks.
3. Ultra-low latency lossless audio transport, unified management of thousands of nodes, and cross-platform device interoperability.
4. Embedded software solutions and full-ecosystem network audio software delivered for integration into local hardware.
5. Professional high-performance networked audio installations requiring AES67 and ST 2110-30 compliance.
6. Professional audio equipment manufacturers and companies worldwide requiring networked audio solutions.
7. Its embedded software is integrated by hardware manufacturers into professional audio products for AES67 network compliance.
8. It provides full-chain network audio solutions optimized for domestic ARM and RISC-V architectures, enabling native local hardware support for the AES67 protocol.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: An official OEM solution provider for RAVENNA.
Organization type: A privately held company specializing in audio network technology research and development.
Business model: Software licensing and OEM solutions for networked audio ecosystems.
Geography: Based in Guangzhou, China, developing products for companies worldwide.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio network technology and AES67 protocol-based solutions.

points.name: SOWA
points.description: Danish audio company building wireless, modular public address speakers.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures self-contained wireless public address speakers, wireless microphones, and companion mobile control software for portable and installed sound reinforcement.
1. A manufacturer of finished audio hardware and companion software whose wireless loudspeakers and microphones are sold as physical products operating in live and fixed installations.
2. Proprietary wireless networking technology providing automatic pairing, adaptive frequency selection, and synchronization across linked speaker nodes, paired with acoustic transducers in self-enclosed cabinets.
3. Wireless audio transmission up to 250 meters, unlimited speaker synchronization, multi-input mixing, microphone gain control, and Bluetooth audio streaming.
4. Finished hardware products, including active loudspeakers and microphones, alongside a mobile software application for remote control and system configuration.
5. Live venues, public address installations, and portable professional sound reinforcement settings.
6. Professionals requiring portable and networked sound reinforcement, audio system integrators, and venues.
7. Its finished hardware products are deployed directly by end users and integrators in live and installed sound environments.
8. An emphasis on sustainable materials, modular construction, and European craftsmanship in professional wireless speaker enclosures.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Materials sourced from Finland, Poland, and Germany, with products assembled in Lithuania.
Organization type: A privately held product design and manufacturing company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished loudspeakers and microphones.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with multiple distinct product lines and a legacy installed base.
Geography: Based in Denmark, assembling products in Lithuania and sourcing materials across Europe.
Beyond audio: Audio is the company's entire focus, specifically wireless public address and professional sound reinforcement hardware.

points.name: Speaksee Venue Accessibility BV
points.description: Software company providing AI-driven real-time speech-to-text and multilingual translation for live events.
points.bullets:
A software developer that builds AI-driven real-time speech-to-text and multilingual translation solutions for corporates, universities, government, event venues, AV event teams, and churches. The organization provides captioning and translation capabilities that integrate into existing audio systems and event workflows. Its products deliver captions and translations as overlays on presentations or via QR codes to attendees' own devices.
1. A software developer whose speech and translation models run in the cloud behind an API and are delivered to attendees' own devices via QR codes.
2. Large cloud-based generative speech recognition and machine translation models process audio streams in real time.
3. The organization delivers real-time speech-to-text transcription and multilingual translation.
4. Customers get the solution as a software product integrated into audio systems and event workflows, with output delivered to personal devices via QR codes.
5. The technology is used in corporate events, university lectures, government facilities, event venues, audio-visual event productions, and churches.
6. The organization sells to corporates, universities, government bodies, event venues, AV event teams, and religious institutions.
7. Its software is integrated into audio systems and event workflows by AV teams and venue operators.
8. The approach distinguishes itself by delivering captions and translations directly to attendees' personal devices via QR codes and overlaying them on presentations.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through software licenses or subscriptions for its captioning and translation solution.
Beyond audio: Its focus is solely on real-time speech-to-text and translation for event accessibility.

Organization type: A privately held company.

points.name: Spottune
points.description: Danish audio company building wireless sound systems for retail and commercial spaces.

An equipment maker that designs and manufactures stand-alone wireless smart-speaker audio systems for commercial spaces, delivering even sound coverage and simple installation for retail and hospitality brands.
1. An equipment maker that builds wireless smart speakers sold as finished hardware running in physical commercial venues.
2. Omni-directional 360-degree wireless smart speakers communicate via a dedicated 1.9 GHz wireless link and integrate with existing lighting tracks.
3. Even sound coverage, balanced acoustics at lower volumes, stable wireless playback without interfering with existing networks, and per-speaker volume control via software.
4. Finished hardware speakers, optional cloud software for centralized music management, and a system design requiring no complex cabling, external amplifiers, or on-site servers.
5. Retail spaces, hospitality venues, and commercial environments.
6. International retail and hospitality brands that value consistent sound, clean design, and easy operation across multiple locations.
7. Its finished hardware speakers are deployed directly into commercial spaces by hospitality and retail brands.
8. Its speakers integrate with existing lighting tracks and operate without complex cabling, external amplifiers, or on-site servers, using a dedicated 1.9 GHz wireless link to avoid network interference.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company.
Geography: Based in Denmark, operating worldwide.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and sells active and passive loudspeaker systems for live sound, touring productions, and fixed installations. It provides finished speaker systems engineered for consistent tonal quality and voicing, serving live sound and installation professionals worldwide.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished active and passive loudspeakers as physical hardware products.
2. The loudspeakers deliver precise voicing, consistent tonal quality, and coherent sound reinforcement.
3. Customers get its products as finished hardware.
4. Its systems are used in live events, touring productions, and fixed audio installations.
5. The company sells to live sound, touring, and integration professionals.
6. Its finished loudspeakers are deployed directly by live sound professionals and integrators in venues and events.

Geography: It is based in Bologna, Italy, and operates worldwide.
Beyond audio: Audio equipment manufacturing is its entire focus.

points.name: Empirical Labs
points.description: US pro audio company making studio compressors and recording equipment.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures analog signal processing hardware, including the Distressor compressor, a widely used studio unit, along with microphone preamplifiers, tape simulators and EQ units, and also develops software plug-in versions of its processors for recording engineers and producers.
1. An equipment maker that builds analog audio processors sold as finished hardware units, plus companion effect plug-ins that run in digital audio workstations.
2. Analog compressor, limiter, preamplifier and saturation circuitry built into hand-assembled hardware, with digital emulations of those circuits implemented as software plug-ins.
3. Dynamics processing including compression and limiting, saturation and tape simulation, EQ and microphone preamplification.
4. Finished hardware units sold to studios, and software plug-ins distributed with iLok licensing.
5. Recording studios, mixing and mastering rooms, and live sound rigs.
6. Recording studios, producers and engineers, from major facilities to project studios.
7. Its hardware processors sit in the signal chain of professional studios and are endorsed by well-known engineers.
8. Its gear is meticulously built and tested by hand, and its compressor was designed from a studio owner's pursuit of a specific sound rather than a market brief.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its plug-ins were developed in collaboration with a software emulation company, and its gear is endorsed by notable producers and engineers.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware unit sales and plug-in licenses.
Scale and maturity: A decades-old company with tens of thousands of its flagship compressor sold.
Geography: Based in New Jersey, USA, selling to studios worldwide.
Beyond audio: Audio is the company's entire focus, spanning analog studio equipment and matching software plug-ins.

points.name: Evolution Acoustics Pro

A maker of professional audio equipment that builds and sells monitoring systems for audio engineers. Its monitoring systems are designed by a speaker designer and voiced by a mastering engineer to help engineers achieve better mixes, faster.

5. The systems are used in studios and mixing environments.

points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a company.

points.name: Fir Audio / Audio Rif

A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures in-ear monitors for musicians and audio engineers. The company builds next-generation in-ear monitor products, building on its founders' experience designing and manufacturing advanced in-ear monitors. The organization produces finished audio hardware for musicians and audio professionals.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment whose in-ear monitors are sold as finished hardware products.
2. The core technology is in-ear monitor hardware design and manufacturing.
3. The specific audio capability is personal monitoring for musicians and audio engineers.
4. Finished hardware products.
5. Professional audio monitoring for musicians and audio engineers.
6. Musicians and audio professionals.
7. Finished hardware products are sold directly to musicians and audio professionals.
8. The founders bring over 20 years of experience designing advanced in-ear monitors.

Organization type: A privately held company.
Geography: The company was founded in 2018.

points.name: Groove Synthesis

A maker of professional electronic musical instruments that builds synthesizers combining wavetable synthesis with other techniques for musicians.

2. Wavetable synthesis combined with multiple other digital synthesis and signal processing techniques.
3. Generation of electronic musical sounds across a range of synthesis methods.

points.name: Heil Sound
points.description: American audio manufacturer building professional dynamic microphones for broadcasting and live sound.
points.bullets:
An audio equipment maker that designs and manufactures professional-quality dynamic microphones and related accessories for live sound, studio, broadcast and podcasting use.
1. An audio equipment maker that builds professional dynamic microphones, sold as finished hardware.
2. Its microphones deliver broad frequency response and natural, articulate sound reproduction for voice and instruments.
3. Its products are used in live sound stages, recording studios, satellite broadcast facilities and podcast setups.
4. Its customers include musicians, live sound and studio engineers, professional podcasters and broadcast stations.

points.profile:

points.name: HISONG
points.description: Audio technology company empowering creators with intelligent, professional-grade music production solutions.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds a portable wireless recording system combining a microphone, audio interface, wireless receivers and in-ear monitors, and develops a companion mobile app for music and audio creators.
1. A professional audio equipment maker that builds finished wireless microphone and monitoring hardware sold as complete kits, alongside a companion mobile app that runs on iOS and Android.
2. The system combines dual-mode microphone capsules, 24-bit/48kHz audio interfaces, wireless RF transmission and receiver designs, and on-board digital signal processing for noise reduction, reverb and limiting.
3. The hardware delivers wireless audio capture, multi-device analog and USB-C audio output, near-zero-latency in-ear monitoring, and AI-driven noise reduction, reverb and limiting.
4. The company's products are sold as finished hardware kits and as a companion mobile application.
5. The products are used in content creation, mobile video production, and music recording.
6. The company sells directly to consumers, including music creators, video creators and influencers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users through retail and online channels.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Geography: The company operates globally with a worldwide team.

points.name: iCON Pro Audio
points.description: Pro audio hardware company manufacturing DAW controllers, interfaces, and studio monitors for musicians and content creators.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds physical hardware control surfaces, audio interfaces, and microphones for musicians, engineers, and content creators.
1. A manufacturer of finished hardware products, including DAW controllers with motorized faders, control extenders, and microphones, sold as standalone physical devices in studios.
2. The hardware utilizes motorized faders, rotary encoders, transport controls, and USB connectivity paired with mapping software to translate physical user input into digital audio workstation commands.
3. The products deliver tactile control over digital audio workstation transport, track mixing, channel banking, and plug-in parameter automation.
4. Customers get the company's offerings as finished hardware units, accompanied by downloadable firmware updates and control mapping software.
5. The devices are used in project and professional recording studios, home music production setups, and broadcast environments.
6. The organization sells directly to musicians, audio engineers, and content creators.
7. Its finished controllers are integrated by end-users into their own digital audio workstation software environments.
8. The company's approach centers on providing dedicated, modular hardware control surfaces with extensible channel configurations across multiple product tiers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its hardware integrates directly with major digital audio workstation software platforms including Logic Pro, Cubase, and Pro Tools.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of its physical audio equipment and accessories.

Geography: The organization operates globally, serving content creators worldwide.

2. A membrane-based acoustic module that absorbs pneumatic pressure buildup to prevent eardrum stiffening.
3. Acoustic pressure relief, hearing protection and acoustic imaging in in-ear monitors.

6. The company sells directly to musicians and audio professionals.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to performers and audio professionals.
8. Its approach is distinguished by a patented membrane system that absorbs pneumatic pressure rather than merely venting it.
points.profile:

Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of finished in-ear monitors.
Scale and maturity: The company has been established for over 55 years.
Geography: It operates in the United States and is registered with the FDA.

A maker of professional audio equipment and accessories that manufactures acoustic enhancements for drums and microphones for capturing sound, serving drummers and audio engineers.

An audio software developer that makes audio processing plugins emulating classic analog circuits, compressors and limiters, with controls for both general tone shaping and detailed underlying circuit behavior, for recording and mixing engineers.
1. An audio software developer whose analog-modeled signal processing plugins run as native software on desktop digital audio workstations.
2. Digital signal processing algorithms that model the sound, nonlinear behavior and gain staging of analog circuits.
3. Dynamic range compression, limiting, tube preamplification, equalization and circuit component emulation.

6. Recording and mixing engineers, producers and musicians.

Organization type: Privately held company.

A maker of professional and audiophile audio equipment that develops, manufactures, and distributes audio electronics and systems, providing headphone amplifiers, converters, and tools for professional and audiophile markets.

points.bullets:
A developer of professional audio software and hardware that makes digital signal processing plug-ins for digital audio workstations and a programmable analog processor for the professional audio, music production, and sound design industries.
1. A software and equipment maker whose audio processing plug-ins run as native formats inside digital audio workstations and whose analog processing hardware runs as standalone racked units.

5. Recording studios, live sound systems, film post-production, music production, and sound design.

6. Technology companies, broadcasters, and software developers that implement the standards.

Organization type: A global, non-commercial standards body.
Business model: It does not sell products directly but enables patent holders to collect royalties from companies that implement its standards.
Geography: It operates globally across different industries and countries.

2. The core technology consists of proprietary neural network architectures and automated design tools that produce small, highly efficient deep neural networks optimized for low-power edge processing.
3. The specific audio capabilities it delivers include AI-based noise reduction, dereverberation, directional speech enhancement, beamforming, speaker identification, and vocal recognition.
4. Customers get it through licensed AI models, algorithms, and plugins integrated into third-party development frameworks and standard chipsets.
5. The models are used in hearing aids, true wireless earbuds, and in-cabin vehicle recognition systems.
6. The organization sells to device makers, hearing aid manufacturers, and chip companies.
7. Its models are integrated by chip vendors and platform providers into their hardware and development frameworks for use by device manufacturers.
8. What distinguishes its approach is the use of proprietary automated design tools to generate compact neural network architectures that achieve a tenfold reduction in processing power and memory.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include Asahi Kasei Microdevices, Bosch Sensortec, Lattice Semiconductor, SoftBank, and AAL.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: The company makes money through licensing fees and per-unit royalties for its AI models and algorithms.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2020, the SoftBank-funded company operates globally with locations in Asia and Europe.
Geography: The organization is based in Silicon Valley, USA, and serves customers worldwide.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the organization develops edge AI models for computer vision applications including face detection, object detection, and license plate reading, as well as EMG-based gesture recognition.

points.name: Absolute Audio Labs
points.description: Netherlands audio software company developing hearing aid and earbud firmware with noise suppression and AI-based feedback management.
points.bullets:
A B2B audio software developer that builds hearing aid firmware and audio processing suites for hearing aids and TWS earbuds, licensing its platform to device manufacturers.
1. An audio software developer whose hearing aid and earbud firmware runs on standard SoCs in customers' devices.
2. DSP algorithms including acoustic noise suppression, wide band compression, AI-based feedback management, microphone directionality, and bone sensing.
3. Noise suppression, feedback management, speech intelligibility, music perception, hearing protection, and clear phone call audio.
4. Software suites, firmware packages, and development frameworks licensed to device manufacturers.
5. Prescription hearing aids and TWS earbuds.
6. Hearing aid manufacturers and consumer electronics brands.
7. Its firmware is integrated by hearing aid manufacturers into devices built on standard SoCs.
8. A platform-agnostic software suite designed to run on standard 24-bit and 32-bit SoCs rather than tied to proprietary silicon.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Technical University of Delft and an AI model developer providing noise reduction plugins.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses and B2B software suites.
Scale and maturity: A startup that released its third-generation platform in 2024.
Geography: Based in the Netherlands.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is audio technology for hearing and voice applications.

points.name: Adobe Audition
points.description: Digital audio workstation providing audio editing and restoration tools for video creators.
points.bullets:
A software company that develops a professional digital audio workstation with spectral frequency editing, adaptive noise reduction, and broadcast loudness compliance tools for audio and video creators.
1. A software company that develops a professional digital audio workstation, sold as a software product running on desktop operating systems.
2. The workstation relies on spectral editing interfaces, adaptive noise reduction algorithms, and loudness compliance processing.
3. It delivers audio editing, audio restoration, noise reduction, and broadcast loudness compliance.
4. Customers get it as a desktop software product available via a Creative Cloud subscription.
5. It is used in audio post-production, broadcast workflows, and video production.
6. It sells to audio professionals, video editors, and broadcast content creators.
7. Its software is used by content creators as a standalone editing tool and integrated into broader video editing workflows.
8. It functions as a general-purpose audio editor with integrated spectral editing, distinguishing it from more specialized audio repair tools.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It integrates with Adobe Premiere Pro and supports third-party audio restoration plug-ins from CrumplePop.
Organization type: It is a software product of a publicly traded software company.
Business model: It makes money through Creative Cloud software subscriptions.
Beyond audio: It is part of a broader creative software suite that spans video editing, graphic design, and photography.

points.name: Elevear
points.description: German deep-tech startup developing AI-powered adaptive active noise cancellation algorithms.
points.bullets:
An audio DSP IP licensor that develops AI-powered adaptive active noise cancellation and occlusion cancellation algorithms for hearables. It licenses speech enhancement, idle noise reduction, and spatial audio processing software to device makers and chip companies, delivering firmware that runs on standard ANC-ready earbuds without requiring specialized hardware.
1. An audio DSP IP licensor whose software algorithms run on-device in customers' wireless earbuds and hearables via firmware updates.
2. Neural networks and adaptive filtering algorithms that run in real time on the embedded processors within true wireless earbuds.
3. Adaptive active noise cancellation, occlusion cancellation, own-voice preservation, idle microphone noise reduction, and 3D audio head tracking with low motion-to-sound latency.
4. Licensed IP and software algorithms delivered as firmware for ANC-ready true wireless earbuds and hearables.
5. True wireless earbuds and hearables.
6. Device makers and chip companies.
7. Its licensed algorithms are integrated by chip vendors and device makers into their wireless earbud platforms.
8. Its occlusion cancellation technology preserves the natural sound of the user's own voice and runs on standard ANC-ready hearables without requiring specialized hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization was acquired by Qualcomm and had prior partnerships with Analog Devices, Cadence, and Greenwaves.
Organization type: A deep-tech startup acquired by a publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: IP or per-unit royalties and software licenses.
Scale and maturity: A small R&D-focused company that secured investment from TVF in 2023 and was subsequently acquired.
Geography: Based in Aachen, Germany.
Beyond audio: Audio technology is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: SoftMax
points.description: Software technology company developing AI-powered noise suppression and speech enhancement algorithms for edge computing.
points.bullets:
An audio DSP and AI algorithm specialist that licenses neural network-based voice and audio processing algorithms to silicon and system-on-chip manufacturers for mobile and embedded devices.
1. An IP licensor that licenses audio and voice algorithms as software and intellectual property that runs on-device on partners' chips.
2. Deep learning architectures including U-net models with multi-view attention blocks and conformer blocks process complex sequential audio features for edge computing.
3. The organization delivers AI-driven noise suppression, speech enhancement, spatial audio processing, acoustic signal enhancement, and sound event localization.
4. Customers get it through algorithm licensing and software integration for edge AI deployment.
5. The technology is used in artificial intelligence PCs, mobile smart devices, and modern embedded systems.
6. The organization sells to silicon partners, system-on-chip manufacturers, and developers creating mobile and smart devices.
7. Its algorithms are integrated by silicon and system-on-chip vendors into their hardware platforms.
8. The approach distinguishes itself by utilizing specific deep learning architectures like U-net models with multi-view attention blocks and conformer blocks to process complex sequential audio features for edge computing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It operates as a subsidiary brand of the publicly traded semiconductor conglomerate Qualcomm, where it is known as Fluence technology.
Organization type: It is a subsidiary brand of a publicly traded semiconductor conglomerate.
Business model: The organization monetizes its intellectual property through algorithm licensing, software integration, and edge AI deployment for hardware partners.
Scale and maturity: It is an established corporate entity that leverages the resources and optimization frameworks of its parent semiconductor company.
Geography: The organization operates within the broader global ecosystem of its parent company, focusing on delivering efficient on-device inference worldwide.
