3. Adaptive active noise cancellation, wireless audio streaming, Bluetooth broadcast audio reception, and proprietary high-quality audio codec encoding.
4. Finished consumer hardware and firmware updates shipped directly to end users.
5. True wireless earbuds, over-ear headphones, smartphones, and televisions.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to consumers and compete with other branded wireless audio devices at retail.
8. It develops proprietary audio codecs and broadcast audio features restricted to its own smartphone and earbud ecosystem.

points.name: Samsung — Galaxy Buds Hearing Aid
points.description: FDA- and regulator-cleared hearing-aid and hearing-test features built into Galaxy Buds, placing Samsung in the regulated hearing-health device market.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics manufacturer that builds regulated hearing-health features into its own wireless earbuds for consumers, having received FDA clearance for a hearing aid feature and a companion hearing test.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished wireless earbuds with integrated, regulator-cleared hearing aid and hearing test software running on its own devices.
2. It delivers over-the-counter hearing aid functionality and self-administered hearing tests within its earbuds.
3. Customers receive the hearing health features as software integrated into finished consumer earbud hardware.
4. The features are used in consumer wireless earbuds.
5. It sells directly to consumers.
6. Its finished earbuds and integrated hearing health features are sold directly to consumers through retail channels.
7. It distinguishes its approach by securing regulatory clearance for medical hearing health features within mainstream consumer earbuds rather than dedicated hearing aid hardware.

points.name: Samsung — Eclipsa Audio
points.description: Royalty-free spatial/3D audio format co-developed with Google (and Arm/AOM) to rival Dolby Atmos, integrated into Samsung TVs and soundbars.
points.bullets:
A multinational electronics company that co-develops open-source spatial audio formats and integrates them into its consumer electronics products, providing royalty-free 3D audio technology for its TVs and soundbars.
1. A consumer electronics manufacturer that builds finished hardware and co-develops audio codecs that run as software in its televisions and soundbars.
2. Open-source spatial audio rendering and decoding algorithms based on the Immersive Audio Model and Formats standard.
3. Royalty-free 3D and spatial audio playback for streaming content and smart devices.
4. Finished hardware products and integrated software codecs embedded in consumer televisions and soundbars.
5. Televisions, soundbars and smart TV streaming services.
6. Consumers buying televisions and soundbars, and streaming services delivering content to those devices.
7. Its hardware platforms serve as the end device for consumers, and its audio format is adopted by streaming services and integrated by other device makers.
8. It establishes a royalty-free alternative to proprietary spatial audio formats by co-developing an open-source standard and integrating it directly into dominant consumer hardware.

points.name: Samsung — Soundbars
points.description: Samsung's home-theater soundbar and wireless-speaker line, marketed as the global No.1 soundbar brand and tied into the Samsung TV ecosystem via Q-Symphony.
points.bullets:
The soundbar program of a multinational consumer electronics conglomerate, making home-theater soundbars and wireless smart speakers for consumers, with deep integration into its own TV ecosystem. It markets Dolby Atmos-capable Q-Series soundbars, from compact models to flagship 11.1.4-channel systems, and has expanded into standalone Wi-Fi smart speakers that can pair into multi-speaker systems.
1. A consumer electronics manufacturer that builds finished home-audio hardware, sold as soundbars and wireless smart speakers that run as standalone products in consumers' homes.
2. Dolby Atmos immersive audio processing in multi-channel soundbar configurations up to true 11.1.4 channels, plus Q-Symphony technology that synchronizes soundbar drivers with the speakers built into its own TVs to play together.
3. Delivers immersive home-theater surround sound, high-fidelity multi-channel playback, wireless multi-speaker pairing, and TV-integrated audio that combines a soundbar with a television's built-in speakers.
4. Customers get finished hardware: complete soundbars and wireless speakers purchased as consumer products, paired with the company's TVs for full functionality.
5. Home theaters and living rooms, used as TV-companion soundbars and standalone or multi-room smart speakers in consumer households.
6. Consumers buying home audio equipment, who typically own or buy the company's televisions.
7. Its soundbars sit at the end of the value chain as finished retail products sold directly to consumers, differentiated by tight coupling with its own TV line.
8. TV-soundbar synchronization that makes the television's own speakers play in concert with the soundbar, exclusive to its TV ecosystem.

points.name: Google — Cloud Speech AI
points.description: Developer- and enterprise-facing speech platform on Google Cloud offering ASR, TTS, transcription, voice cloning, and real-time speech-to-speech model APIs.
points.bullets:
A publicly traded technology company that develops cloud-based and on-device AI models for speech recognition, speech synthesis, speech-to-speech conversation, voice cloning and audio-language understanding, offering them through APIs and enterprise platforms for developers and businesses.
1. An AI model developer whose cloud speech and audio-language models run behind APIs and enterprise platforms, with companion on-device speech models that run locally on customer hardware.
2. Large generative speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech-to-speech transformer models, including a universal speech model and multimodal audio-language models, served from cloud infrastructure with options for local execution.
3. Multilingual speech recognition, speech synthesis, voice cloning, real-time speech-to-speech interaction, audio sentiment analysis and conversational voice agents.
4. Cloud APIs, developer platforms, enterprise cloud software and on-device model deployments.
5. Contact centers, voice agent applications, enterprise voice analytics, mobile applications and conversational video agents.
6. Developers, enterprises and financial institutions.
7. Its models and APIs are consumed by developers and enterprises to build voice-enabled applications and analytics tools.
8. Deep integration with a broader cloud platform's data, analytics and generative AI services, providing server-quality speech models that also run locally on devices.

points.name: Google — Eclipsa Audio
points.description: Open-source, royalty-free spatial/3D audio format (based on IAMF) co-developed with Samsung and the Alliance for Open Media.
points.bullets:
A technology company that develops and sponsors open-source audio formats and codecs, providing a royalty-free spatial audio format for consumer electronics makers, content platforms and creators.
1. A technology company that develops open-source spatial audio format specifications and reference software plugins, which are implemented in hardware decoding products and integrated into cloud media platforms.
2. Spatial audio rendering and bitstream format technology based on the Immersive Audio Model and Formats specification.
3. 3D spatial sound, immersive audio and spatial audio rendering over headphones and speakers.
4. Open-source format specifications, royalty-free licenses and reference DAW plugins.
5. Televisions, soundbars, media streaming platforms and digital audio workstations.
6. Consumer electronics brands, content platforms, content creators and standards bodies.
7. Its open-source format specifications are adopted and implemented by consumer electronics brands into their hardware decoding products and integrated into cloud media platforms.
8. It develops and sponsors the format specifically to provide a patent-free, royalty-free alternative to proprietary spatial audio formats.

points.name: Google — Neural Audio Codecs
points.description: Research and open-source line of low-bitrate neural speech/audio codecs for efficient transmission.
points.bullets:
A multinational technology company that develops open-source neural audio codecs for compressing low-bitrate speech and audio for efficient transmission. The organization researches and releases low-bitrate neural speech and audio codecs used in real-time speech transmission platforms. It provides these codecs for telephony and conferencing applications.
1. An AI model and software developer whose neural audio codec models run on-device in mobile and embedded devices and are released as open source.
2. Neural networks running on-device on mobile and embedded devices that compress low-bitrate speech and audio for efficient transmission.
3. Low-bitrate speech and audio compression and real-time speech transmission.
4. Open-source software and models running on customers' devices.
5. Real-time speech transmission platforms and conferencing applications.
6. Developers and platform providers.
7. Its open-source codecs are integrated into real-time communication platforms.
8. Its codecs are developed and released as open-source models optimized for on-device mobile and embedded deployment.

points.name: Google — Assistant
points.description: Google's consumer voice-assistant and smart-speaker platform spanning Nest/Home hardware and the newer Gemini-powered conversational experiences.
points.bullets:
A multinational technology company that develops consumer voice assistants, cloud-based generative voice models, smart speakers and hearables, and a voice-assistant SDK for third-party device makers.
1. An AI model developer and equipment maker whose voice models run in the cloud behind APIs and consumer software, and whose finished hardware runs companion on-device software.
2. Large generative voice models in the cloud, full-duplex real-time conversational AI, native audio processing, synthesized data for keyword spotting, and embedded DeepMind SynthID audio watermarking.
3. Real-time full-duplex voice conversation, hotword activation, hands-free voice assistance, responsive audio adjustment, synthesized text-to-speech, and camera and screen-sharing visual context.
4. Cloud APIs, consumer software products, finished hardware, an SDK, and mic-path signal-processing guidance for smart gadgets.
5. Smart speakers, smart displays, wireless earbuds, hearables, smart-home ecosystems, consumer mobile devices, and third-party voice-enabled smart gadgets.
6. Consumers, developers, and third-party device makers.
7. Its cloud models are embedded in consumer software products and integrated by third-party device makers into their smart gadgets.
8. Integrates full-duplex real-time voice AI natively across a proprietary mobile operating system, consumer hardware ecosystem, and smart-home platform.

points.name: Apple — AirPods
points.description: Apple's consumer wireless earbuds and headphones product line, competing in the TWS/wearable-audio hardware market.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics maker that designs and sells wireless earbuds and headphones, alongside the custom silicon and embedded software that power them, for consumers in a tightly integrated device ecosystem.
1. A consumer electronics maker that designs finished wireless earbuds and headphones and the custom Bluetooth audio chips inside them, sold as finished hardware running its own embedded firmware.
2. Custom audio processing chips and embedded software running adaptive noise control, sensor fusion and generative audio features on the earbuds themselves.
3. Active noise cancellation, adaptive audio, conversation awareness, voice isolation, speech translation and in-ear biometric sensing.
4. Finished hardware devices and firmware updates delivered directly to consumers.
5. Wireless earbuds, over-ear headphones and hearables used for consumer listening, hearing assistance and hands-free voice access.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished audio hardware is sold directly to consumers and integrated with its own smartphones and operating systems.
8. Its custom chips and audio algorithms are built to operate exclusively within its own device ecosystem for seamless pairing and integration.

points.name: Apple — Hearing Health Features
points.description: Apple's software-based hearing aid and hearing-test offering built into AirPods Pro, competing in the regulated OTC hearing aid market.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics and software company that develops and ships FDA-authorized hearing aid and hearing test software for its wireless earbuds, targeting the over-the-counter hearing aid market for consumers with mild-to-moderate hearing loss.
1. An equipment maker and software developer whose audio health features are sold as embedded software inside finished wireless earbuds.
2. Software-based sound amplification algorithms and calibrated hearing assessments built into a consumer audio wearable platform.
3. Over-the-counter hearing aid sound amplification and self-administered hearing testing for mild-to-moderate hearing loss.
4. FDA-authorized software delivered via firmware updates to finished consumer hardware.
5. Consumer wireless earbuds and assistive listening devices.
6. Consumers with mild-to-moderate hearing impairment.
7. Its software features are integrated exclusively into its own finished consumer earbuds and sold directly to end users.
8. It delivers clinically validated, FDA-authorized hearing aid functionality through a software update to existing consumer earbuds rather than requiring dedicated medical hardware.

points.name: Apple — Siri Voice AI
points.description: Apple's voice assistant and speech AI platform spanning phones, wearables, speakers, and developer tools.
points.bullets:
A vertically integrated consumer electronics and software company that develops a voice assistant and on-device speech AI foundation models, embedding them into its own finished hardware and exposing them to third-party developers.
1. An AI model developer and equipment maker whose voice models and assistant run on-device in its own consumer hardware and behind developer APIs.
2. On-device deep neural networks, foundation models, and automatic speech recognition algorithms augmented by integrated third-party large language models.
3. Wake word detection, speech recognition, natural language understanding, live translation, audio intelligence, and spatial audio adaptation.
4. On-device models running in finished hardware, operating system software, and developer SDKs.
5. Smartphones, wearables, smart speakers, hearables, smart home ecosystems, and upcoming AI smart glasses.
6. Consumers, third-party smart home device makers, and software developers.
7. Its voice models and assistant are integrated into its own consumer hardware devices and embedded into third-party smart home products via developer APIs.
8. The organization tightly couples its proprietary on-device speech models with its own custom silicon, operating systems, and finished hardware.

points.name: Apple — Spatial Audio
points.description: Apple's 3D/spatial audio rendering technology and format, used across its headphones and music ecosystem.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics and software company that builds spatial audio rendering technology and music production software for consumers and audio professionals. It develops proprietary head-related transfer function algorithms for headphones and integrates Dolby Atmos mixing into its digital audio workstation. The organization delivers these technologies through its own finished hardware, mobile operating systems, and streaming services.
1. A consumer electronics and software company that develops spatial audio rendering algorithms and digital audio workstation software, sold as finished hardware and software products running on its own devices and platforms.
2. The core technology consists of spatial rendering algorithms using head-related transfer functions, including personalized profiles generated from 3D ear scans captured by a smartphone camera.
3. It delivers spatial audio rendering, personalized head-related transfer function processing, and Dolby Atmos mixing.
4. Customers receive the technology through finished hardware, device firmware updates, operating system software, and feature sets within a digital audio workstation and streaming service.
5. It is used in headphones, earbuds, smartphones, smart speakers, mixed-reality headsets, and digital audio workstations.
6. The company sells to consumers, music producers, and audio engineers.
7. Its rendering algorithms and software are embedded in its own consumer hardware devices and operating systems, and its digital audio workstation is sold directly to audio professionals.
8. Its approach is distinguished by using smartphone camera hardware to scan users' ears and generate custom spatial audio sound profiles integrated tightly across its hardware and music services.

points.name: Sony — WH-1000X and WF-1000X Series
points.description: Sony's flagship consumer noise-cancelling headphone and earbud line sold to everyday listeners and reviewed as the benchmark for ANC performance.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that develops and sells flagship noise-cancelling headphones and true wireless earbuds to everyday listeners, alongside licensing a high-resolution Bluetooth audio codec to the mobile device market.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware sold directly to consumers, and a software developer whose Bluetooth codec runs on consumer mobile devices.
2. Active noise cancellation algorithms, ear-scanning personalization software, and the LDAC high-resolution Bluetooth audio codec.
3. Active noise cancellation, high-resolution Bluetooth audio streaming, LE Audio with Auracast support, and ear-scanning personalization.
4. Finished wireless headphones, earbuds, and portable music players, alongside a licensed Bluetooth codec integrated into mobile operating systems.
5. Over-ear headphones, true wireless earbuds, and portable music players.
6. Consumers for finished hardware, and mobile device makers for codec licensing.
7. Its finished headphones and earbuds are sold directly to consumers, and its audio codec is integrated into mobile operating systems by smartphone makers.
8. Its noise-cancelling headphones are consistently reviewed as the benchmark for active noise cancellation performance and sound quality in the consumer market.

points.name: Sony — LDAC
points.description: Sony's Bluetooth high-resolution audio codec, licensed broadly to chipmakers and device makers across the industry as a B2B audio-transmission standard.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics conglomerate and audio codec IP licensor that develops and licenses a Bluetooth high-resolution audio coding technology to chipmakers and device makers, while also incorporating it into its own line of wireless headphones and music players.
1. An audio codec IP licensor whose Bluetooth audio codec runs on partner semiconductors and in finished consumer hardware.
2. A variable-bitrate audio coding algorithm that compresses and decompresses 24-bit/96kHz audio for transmission over Bluetooth at up to 990 kbps.
3. High-resolution wireless audio streaming with bitrates up to 990 kbps and 24-bit/96kHz audio support.
4. Licensed IP and software algorithms integrated into partner SoCs, alongside finished consumer audio hardware products.
5. Wireless headphones, earbuds, portable music players, Bluetooth audio SoCs and Android mobile devices.
6. Chip companies, consumer electronics brands and consumers.
7. Its codec IP is integrated by chip vendors into their Bluetooth audio SoCs, which are then designed into consumer audio devices by electronics brands.
8. Its codec was adopted as the default high-resolution audio codec integrated directly into the Android Open Source Project.

points.name: Sony — 360 Reality Audio
points.description: Sony's music-specific, object-based immersive/spatial audio format aimed at streaming platforms and home/headphone playback.
points.bullets:
A technology company that develops a music-specific, object-based immersive spatial audio format and provides it to streaming platforms and headphone users. It builds and licenses the format, which creates a 360-degree sound field for home audio systems and headphone playback.
1. A technology company that develops an immersive spatial audio format, delivered to streaming platforms as a licensed format and to consumers through headphones and compatible speakers.
2. An MPEG-H-based object-based immersive audio format that uses personalized head-related transfer functions generated through a companion mobile application to render spatial sound over headphones.
3. Spatial audio rendering, 360-degree sound field creation, personalized HRTF generation, and AI-driven audio processing including noise cancellation.
4. Licensed to streaming platforms and delivered to consumers through a mobile application and compatible headphones and speakers.
5. Music streaming platforms, home audio systems, and headphone playback.
6. Music streaming platforms and consumers.
7. Its spatial audio format is licensed to streaming platforms and delivered to consumers through compatible playback devices and applications.
8. It combines an MPEG-H-based object-based spatial audio format with personalized HRTF generation tailored to individual users' ear geometry.

points.name: Sony — ULT Speaker Line
points.description: Sony's bass-focused ULT consumer audio brand spanning portable Bluetooth speakers and bass-boosted headphones for casual listeners.
points.bullets:
A multinational electronics conglomerate that designs, manufactures and sells finished consumer audio hardware, including portable Bluetooth speakers, home Hi-Fi systems, tower speakers and noise-cancelling wireless headphones under its ULT bass-focused brand for casual listeners and consumers.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished consumer audio hardware products that run self-contained as standalone electronics.
2. Integrated audio electronics combining speaker drivers, amplification, Bluetooth connectivity and active noise-cancelling signal processing in finished consumer hardware.
3. Bass-emphasized sound reproduction for portable and home speakers, wireless audio playback over Bluetooth and active noise cancellation for over-ear headphones.
4. Finished consumer hardware products sold directly to end users through retail channels.
5. Portable travel and outdoor speakers, home Hi-Fi and tower speakers, and wireless over-ear headphones for everyday consumer use.
6. Consumers seeking portable, home and personal audio electronics through retail.
7. Its finished audio products are sold directly to consumers through retail channels and sit alongside its broader consumer electronics portfolio.
8. The ULT brand applies a unified bass-emphasis sound signature across portable speakers, home Hi-Fi and headphones within a broad consumer electronics portfolio.

points.name: Sennheiser — Momentum
points.description: Sennheiser's premium consumer headphone and true-wireless earbud line, now produced under license by Sonova's Consumer Hearing business.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and premium consumer headphones that designs and builds high-end microphones, over-ear headphones, true-wireless earbuds and soundbars for musicians, audio professionals and consumers.
1. An equipment maker whose finished audio hardware is sold as physical products running standalone in the consumer and professional markets.
2. Electro-acoustic transducer designs, acoustic tuning methodologies and open-back headphone architectures combined with active noise cancellation and Bluetooth audio processing.
3. Active noise cancellation, high-resolution audio codec support, Bluetooth LE Audio and Auracast broadcast reception, and parametric equalization.
4. Finished hardware products and consumer electronics devices sold directly to end users.
5. Over-ear headphones, true-wireless earbuds, soundbars, live music venues, recording studios and audiophile listening setups.
6. Consumers, audiophiles, musicians and audio production professionals.
7. Its consumer hardware products are manufactured and distributed under license by a hearing aid company, while its professional equipment is sold directly to end users.
8. A long-standing focus on acoustic transducer design and open-back headphone architecture combined with a distinct acoustic tuning philosophy.

points.name: Sennheiser — AMBEO
points.description: Sennheiser's immersive/spatial audio technology, applied to home-theater soundbars, 3D microphones, and licensed automotive sound systems.
points.bullets:
An audio equipment maker and spatial audio technology developer whose AMBEO program builds immersive soundbars and 3D microphones for consumers and professionals, and licenses spatial audio algorithms to automakers.
1. A maker of professional and consumer audio equipment that builds finished hardware products and spatial audio software algorithms sold as finished devices and licensed software.
2. Spatial rendering algorithms and Ambisonics decoding technology, implemented in dedicated soundbar hardware with top-firing drivers and in 3D microphone capsules.
3. Immersive and spatial audio playback for home theater, Dolby Atmos-style sound reproduction, 3D Ambisonics audio recording, and in-car spatial sound rendering.
4. Finished hardware products, including soundbars, subwoofers and microphones, and licensed spatial audio software and algorithms.
5. Home theaters and living rooms, field recording rigs, professional audio production, and in-car audio systems.
6. Consumers, professional audio recordists and Pro AV users, automakers, and consumer electronics retailers.
7. Its finished hardware is sold to consumers through retail channels and consumer electronics brands, and its spatial audio algorithms are integrated by automotive suppliers into their in-car sound systems.
8. It combines finished immersive audio hardware products with a licensable spatial audio software and algorithm portfolio under a single branded program.

points.name: Sennheiser — TeamConnect
points.description: A business-communications line of ceiling and conferencing microphone arrays with dynamic beamforming for corporate meeting rooms.
points.bullets:
An audio equipment maker that builds ceiling and conferencing microphone arrays with dynamic beamforming for corporate meeting rooms.
1. A manufacturer of finished audio hardware and companion control software sold as integrated conferencing systems.
2. Dynamic beamforming microphone arrays combined with a voice lift algorithm and Dante audio networking.
3. Dynamic beamforming, voice lift for room coverage, and acoustic capture for conferencing.
4. Finished hardware microphone arrays and companion control software.
5. Corporate meeting rooms, large conference rooms and boardrooms.
6. Enterprises, corporate AV buyers and systems integrators.
7. Its hardware products are installed in corporate meeting rooms by systems integrators and integrated into broader AV platforms.
8. Its dynamic beamforming technology automatically adapts to room acoustics and talker positions in ceiling-mounted arrays.

points.name: Sennheiser — Evolution Wireless
points.description: Sennheiser's performance/broadcast microphone family (wired evolution vocal mics and digital/analog wireless systems) for musicians, content creators and broadcasters.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs, manufactures and sells wired microphones, wireless microphone systems and in-ear monitoring systems for musicians, broadcasters, content creators and live sound engineers.
1. An audio equipment manufacturer that builds wired and wireless microphones and in-ear monitors, sold as finished hardware for stage, studio and broadcast use.
2. Analog and digital wireless radio transmission systems and dynamic and condenser microphone capsules.
3. Vocal and instrument sound capture, wireless audio transmission and in-ear monitoring.
4. Finished hardware products, including handheld microphones, headset systems, bodypack transmitters, receivers and in-ear monitors.
5. Live stages, broadcast studios, recording studios, field production and content creation setups.
6. Musicians, broadcasters, content creators, live sound engineers and audio professionals.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold to audio professionals through retail and pro-audio dealers.
8. It provides a broad ecosystem of stage and broadcast microphones spanning digital wireless systems and wired dynamic and condenser designs under a single brand.

points.name: Qualcomm — Snapdragon Sound
points.description: Qualcomm's end-to-end wireless audio platform/certification program for smartphones, earbuds, and headphones, bundling chipsets, DACs, codecs and connectivity to deliver consistent high-quality consumer wireless audio.
points.bullets:
A chip company that designs semiconductor platforms and reference designs for wireless audio, combining processors, DACs, codecs and connectivity for consumer electronics brands and device makers.
1. A chip company that designs audio SoCs and reference platforms that are sold as semiconductors and run in consumer earbuds, headphones and smartphones.
2. Integrated circuits combining audio processing, digital-to-analog conversion, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi connectivity, and on-device neural networks.
3. High-resolution lossless wireless audio transmission, on-device AI processing, noise suppression and direct cloud connectivity.
4. Chips, reference designs, certified platforms and licensed algorithms.
5. Smartphones, wireless earbuds, headphones, audio glasses and portable DACs.
6. Consumer electronics brands, device makers and health-tech platform providers.
7. Its chips and reference designs are designed into consumer hearables and smartphones by device manufacturers.
8. Bundles processors, audio codecs, DACs, connectivity and on-device AI into a single certified end-to-end platform.

points.name: Qualcomm — QCC Bluetooth Audio SoCs
points.description: Dedicated family of Bluetooth audio system-on-chip products sold directly to earbud and headset manufacturers for true wireless stereo (TWS) and hearable hardware.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs and sells Bluetooth audio system-on-chip platforms for true wireless stereo earbuds, headsets and hearables, supplying consumer electronics brands across multiple price tiers.
1. A chip company that designs low-power Bluetooth audio system-on-chip products which are sold to device manufacturers and run as the embedded processor in earbud and headset hardware.
2. Integrated Bluetooth audio system-on-chip architectures featuring multi-core processors, low-power wireless transceivers and on-chip digital signal processing.
3. Bluetooth audio streaming with advanced codecs, true wireless stereo pairing, active noise cancellation and call noise reduction.
4. Finished semiconductors sold to device makers, accompanied by an extension partner program for third-party software integration.
5. True wireless earbuds, wireless headphones, hearables and Bluetooth audio transmitter modules.
6. Consumer electronics brands, earbud and headset manufacturers, and wireless module makers.
7. Its semiconductors are designed into true wireless earbuds and hearables by consumer electronics brands.
8. It targets a full range of price tiers with specific dedicated Bluetooth audio chip families while maintaining an extension program that lets third parties build differentiating software on its platforms.

points.name: Qualcomm — aptX
points.description: Qualcomm's family of proprietary Bluetooth audio codecs (Classic, HD, Adaptive, Lossless, LL) licensed broadly across the Android and headphone ecosystem for wireless audio transmission.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor and telecommunications company that develops a family of proprietary Bluetooth audio codecs and licenses them broadly across the Android and headphone ecosystem for wireless audio transmission.
1. A semiconductor and IP licensor that develops proprietary Bluetooth audio codecs and wireless processors, sold as licensed IP and integrated into its own chipsets and SoCs.
2. Audio compression algorithms and wireless audio processors designed to encode and decode high-resolution and low-latency audio over Bluetooth links.
3. High-resolution Bluetooth audio streaming, low-latency audio transmission, scalable codec bitrates, and noise cancellation.
4. Licensed intellectual property, integrated circuits, and system-on-chips.
5. Android smartphones, true wireless earbuds, noise-cancelling headphones, portable DACs, and wireless speakers.
6. Device manufacturers, consumer electronics brands, and portable audio makers.
7. Its codecs and chips are designed into consumer audio devices by electronics brands and supported natively in mobile operating systems.
8. A vertically integrated codec portfolio spanning classic, high-definition, adaptive, and lossless formats, tied directly to its own wireless audio SoCs.

points.name: Qualcomm — Hexagon DSP/NPU
points.description: Qualcomm's DSP/NPU processor architecture embedded across Snapdragon chips, providing on-device AI/DSP acceleration used for voice, noise-suppression and audio-processing workloads.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs Snapdragon processors with integrated Hexagon DSP and NPU architectures, providing on-device AI and DSP acceleration for audio, voice and noise-suppression workloads to device makers and developers.
1. A fabless chip company that designs Snapdragon processors with embedded Hexagon DSPs and NPUs, sold as packaged SoCs running in consumer and automotive devices.
2. Digital signal processors and neural processing units integrated into Snapdragon SoCs, providing low-power on-device AI and DSP acceleration.
3. On-device noise suppression, real-time voice AI processing and multicore automotive audio DSP pipelines.
4. Processors and chipsets, accompanied by an SDK and a cloud-based AI model profiling platform for developers.
5. PCs, automotive audio platforms, mobile devices and value-tier consumer electronics.
6. Device makers, automotive platform integrators, consumer electronics brands and developers.
7. Its processors are designed into consumer and automotive devices by electronics brands and automakers.
8. It tunes dedicated Hexagon NPUs for always-on, low-power mobile and PC workloads and partners with AI model developers to optimize their models specifically for its NPU architecture.

points.name: Harman — Lifestyle Audio Brand Portfolio
points.description: Harman's consumer-facing home and portable audio brands sold through retail channels, recently expanded via the Sound United acquisition.
points.bullets:
A consumer and automotive audio equipment maker that designs, engineers, and markets finished audio products under a portfolio of owned brands, for consumers, automakers, and professionals.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished consumer and professional audio hardware and smart speakers sold through retail channels and integrated into consumer devices.
2. Audio transducers, amplification electronics, wireless connectivity, and AI-powered stem separation running in portable speaker and amplifier hardware.
3. Audio playback, sound reinforcement, acoustic tuning, and music stem separation.
4. Finished hardware products, smart speakers, and tuned audio profiles integrated into consumer mobile devices.
5. Earbuds, headphones, home audio systems, portable speakers, smart speakers, car audio systems, and professional studios.
6. Consumers, automakers, consumer electronics brands, and professional content creators.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to consumers through retail channels and its tuning profiles are integrated into mobile devices by consumer electronics brands.
8. It operates a vast portfolio of distinct legacy audio brands spanning mass-market consumer, premium home, and professional segments under a single corporate umbrella.

points.name: Harman — Connected Car Audio
points.description: Automotive audio and connected infotainment systems engineered for and co-branded with global automakers.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker and systems integrator that engineers and supplies comprehensive automotive audio and connected infotainment systems, co-branding them with premium audio labels for global automakers.
1. An equipment maker that designs finished automotive audio hardware, amplifiers, speakers, and connected car infotainment systems sold as integrated modules to vehicle manufacturers.
2. Digital signal processing algorithms, acoustic-driven computational design, and connected car telematics units engineered to automotive grade specifications.
3. Noise cancellation, isolated sound zone personalized audio, spatial audio rendering, and 5G telematics connectivity.
4. Finished hardware including speakers, amplifiers, telematics control units, and complete infotainment systems integrated directly into vehicle platforms.
5. Passenger vehicles, electric vehicles, and powersports motorcycles.
6. Automakers and vehicle manufacturers.
7. Its complete audio and infotainment systems are designed into new vehicles by global automakers and co-branded with premium audio labels.
8. It operates a portfolio of multiple legacy premium audio brands and co-brands its systems directly with automakers rather than selling standalone components.

points.name: Harman — Professional Audio Solutions
points.description: Commercial and installed pro-AV audio systems for live performance, touring, broadcast, and enterprise venues.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs and manufactures professional audio, video, lighting, and control systems for entertainment and enterprise venues, encompassing loudspeakers, microphones, mixing consoles, and signal processors under multiple subsidiary brands.
1. An equipment maker that manufactures finished professional audio hardware and integrated systems sold as physical products.
2. Analog and digital signal processing hardware, acoustic transducers, and digital mixing console architectures.
3. Sound reinforcement, audio mixing, signal processing, microphone capture, and audio distribution for installed and live environments.
4. Finished hardware, including loudspeakers, microphones, mixing consoles, and signal processors, distributed through professional audio channels.
5. Live performance venues, touring sound rigs, broadcast studios, corporate spaces, hospitality environments, cinemas, and retail locations.
6. Audio professionals, touring sound engineers, broadcast facilities, venue operators, and enterprise integrators.
7. Its finished hardware and integrated systems are deployed directly by audio professionals and installers in entertainment and enterprise venues.
8. Operates the broadest portfolio of professional audio brands in the industry, covering every price point from entry-level speakers to high-end touring line arrays.

points.name: Xperi — DTS:X
points.description: An object-based immersive audio format and codec family competing with Dolby Atmos across home, cinema, and mobile devices.
points.bullets:
An audio technology IP licensor that develops object-based immersive audio formats and codec technologies for consumer electronics brands and cinema operators.
1. An audio technology IP licensor whose audio codecs and spatial audio formats run on partners' chips and integrated platforms.
2. Object-based immersive audio codecs and spatial audio rendering algorithms that encode and decode multichannel soundtracks with less compression.
3. Object-based spatial audio rendering, immersive surround sound, wireless audio streaming, and headphone virtualization.
4. Licensed IP, patents, and trademarks integrated into partners' products.
5. Home theater systems, sound bars, mobile devices, cinema sound systems, Windows PCs, and gaming consoles.
6. Consumer electronics brands, chip vendors, software platforms, and hardware manufacturers.
7. Its audio codecs and formats are integrated by device makers and semiconductor vendors into consumer hardware platforms.
8. It uses less compression in its immersive audio format to retain higher fidelity audio compared to competing object-based formats.

points.name: Xperi — HD Radio
points.description: A digital radio broadcasting technology and licensing platform integrated into connected cars.
points.bullets:
An IP and technology licensing company that develops and licenses digital radio broadcasting technology and connected car media platforms, delivered via its brands, to automakers and consumer device manufacturers worldwide.
1. A digital radio broadcasting technology and licensing platform whose IP and software are integrated into connected car infotainment systems.
2. Digital radio broadcasting technology and connected car media platform software.
3. Digital radio reception and delivery of integrated in-vehicle infotainment and entertainment experiences.
4. Licensed IP and software platforms integrated by automakers into connected car systems.
5. Connected cars, consumer devices and media platforms.
6. Automakers, consumer device manufacturers and media platform operators.
7. Its licensed digital radio technology and media platforms are designed into connected vehicles and consumer devices by OEMs.
8. It pairs its digital radio broadcasting technology with a connected car media platform to deliver integrated broadcast and streaming entertainment.

points.name: Analog Devices — Automotive Audio Bus
points.description: ADI's A2B digital networking standard distributes audio and control data over a single twisted-pair cable for in-vehicle infotainment and noise-cancellation systems, sold to automakers and Tier-1 suppliers.
points.bullets:
A global semiconductor company that develops the Automotive Audio Bus (A2B) digital networking standard and related transceiver integrated circuits for in-vehicle infotainment and noise-cancellation systems, selling to automakers and Tier-1 automotive suppliers.
1. A semiconductor company that designs and manufactures mixed-signal transceiver integrated circuits and licenses a digital audio networking protocol for embedded automotive systems.
2. The core technology is a digital audio bus protocol that distributes audio and control data along with power over a single unshielded twisted-pair cable in a daisy-chain network.
3. The technology delivers low-latency digital audio distribution, high-bandwidth multimedia connectivity, and Ethernet tunneling for software-defined vehicles.
4. Customers get the technology through transceiver chips, evaluation boards, software stacks, and development tools.
5. The integrated circuits and protocol are used in automotive infotainment systems, all-digital road-noise-cancellation systems, and in-cabin personal sound zones.
6. The organization sells to automakers, Tier-1 automotive suppliers, and embedded electronics developers.
7. Its transceiver chips and networking protocols are designed into vehicle audio architectures by automotive manufacturers and their direct suppliers.
8. The technology combines power and bidirectional audio and control data over a single unshielded twisted-pair cable, reducing vehicle wiring harness weight and complexity.

points.name: Analog Devices — MEMS Microphones
points.description: ADI's iMEMS microphone line (ADMP series) supplies miniature silicon microphones for consumer electronics, competing for design wins in phones and earbuds.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor manufacturer that produces miniature silicon MEMS microphones for consumer electronics, targeting high-performance applications in phones, tablets, and earbuds.
1. A chip company that designs and manufactures MEMS microphones sold as finished hardware components integrated into consumer electronic devices.
2. Microelectromechanical systems technology combining audio signal processing expertise with integrated high-pass filtering to achieve high signal-to-noise ratios.
3. Acoustic capture with high signal-to-noise performance supporting beamforming and noise cancellation in consumer audio devices.
4. Finished hardware components supplied directly to consumer electronics manufacturers for integration into their products.
5. Smartphones, tablets, earbuds, portable media players, and consumer audio devices requiring beamforming and noise cancellation.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers, including makers of smartphones, tablets, and portable media players.
7. Its microphone components are designed into consumer electronics products by device manufacturers.
8. Targets higher-priced, high-performance microphone parts rather than competing solely on cost in the consumer MEMS microphone market.

points.name: Analog Devices — SigmaDSP
points.description: SigmaDSP is ADI's family of programmable audio processor and codec ICs (ADAU series) paired with the SigmaStudio tool, sold to third-party makers of car audio, custom-install and consumer audio gear.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that designs and sells programmable audio processors, codecs and mixed-signal converters, paired with graphical development software, for third-party manufacturers of car audio, consumer electronics and custom-install equipment.
1. A chip company that designs and sells low-power audio DSPs, codecs and mixed-signal converters, shipped as semiconductor ICs and integrated into partners' hardware platforms.
2. Programmable digital signal processor cores, analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog converters, and mixed-signal audio front ends integrated into audio codec and processor ICs.
3. Audio digital-to-analog and analog-to-digital conversion, digital signal processing for active noise cancellation, LDAC codec transmission, and multimedia audio processing.
4. Semiconductor ICs, audio system-on-chip devices, and licensed processor cores, paired with a graphical software development tool for programming audio DSPs.
5. Car audio DSP units, earbuds with active noise cancellation, networked audio processors, custom-install audio gear and consumer audio devices.
6. Device makers, audio equipment manufacturers, automotive audio brands and consumer electronics brands.
7. Its audio ICs and processors are designed into finished audio hardware by equipment makers and third-party electronics brands.
8. Its audio processors are paired with a dedicated graphical development tool for programming DSP signal flows, lowering the barrier for hardware designers to implement custom audio processing.

points.name: THX — Certification Program
points.description: Independent testing and certification program that validates audio/video performance across many consumer electronics categories for device manufacturers.
points.bullets:
An audio certification standards body that develops and licenses audio and video performance standards, and provides independent testing and certification of consumer electronics products for device manufacturers.
1. A standards body and technology licensor whose certification programs and spatial audio technology are delivered as licensed specifications and test programs run in its own labs.
2. Standardized sets of test parameters for audio and video performance, alongside spatial audio rendering algorithms.
3. Independent validation of audio and video fidelity, headphone certification, display certification, and spatial audio rendering.
4. Licensed certification programs, performance specifications, and spatial audio technology.
5. TVs, monitors, headphones, earbuds, universal Blu-ray players, wireless speaker systems, home theaters, cinemas, and automotive and live entertainment environments.
6. Consumer electronics device manufacturers, display makers, and headphone brands.
7. Its certification standards and technologies are licensed to consumer electronics brands and integrated into their end products.
8. It combines a legacy cinema sound heritage with an independent, test-driven certification process across both audio and video performance categories.

points.name: THX — Spatial Audio
points.description: Licensed spatial-audio software and tools used by game developers, music producers, and headset/soundbar manufacturers for immersive sound.
points.bullets:
An audio IP licensor and certification company that licenses spatial audio software, tools and personalization algorithms, and certifies audio and video performance for device makers, content creators and the entertainment industry.
1. An audio IP licensor whose spatial audio software and certification programs are sold as licensed algorithms and tools that run on consumer audio devices and in content production workflows.
2. Spatial rendering algorithms and audio personalization technology built on licensed VisiSonics 3D audio technology.
3. Spatial audio, immersive sound rendering and advanced audio personalization.
4. Licensed IP, software tools and certification programs.
5. Gaming headsets, earbuds, soundbars, headphones, cinemas, home entertainment systems, automotive and live entertainment.
6. Game developers, music producers, headset and soundbar manufacturers, consumer electronics brands and cinema operators.
7. Its software is integrated into consumer audio devices by manufacturers and its certification is applied to finished products as a quality standard.
8. Combines licensed spatial audio software with a long-established brand certification program recognized across the entertainment industry.

points.name: THX — AAA
points.description: Achromatic Audio Amplifier (AAA) amplifier technology and Onyx-branded personal DAC/headphone amp products for the personal/portable audio market.
points.bullets:
An audio technology and certification company that licenses amplifier designs and certifies audio-visual equipment, and also builds finished personal audio accessories for consumers.
1. An amplifier IP licensor and finished equipment maker whose main business is licensing amplifier designs to device makers, alongside selling its own portable DACs as finished hardware that run via USB.
2. The core technology is an amplifier architecture using multiple operational amplifiers in parallel to reduce distortion and increase power output.
3. The organization delivers low-distortion headphone amplification and digital-to-analog conversion.
4. Customers get it through licensed amplifier designs integrated into devices and as finished portable USB DAC hardware.
5. The technology is used in portable headphone amplifiers, home theater gear, cinema sound systems, and high-resolution personal audio setups.
6. The organization sells to consumer electronics brands, music streaming services, and consumers.
7. Its licensed amplifier designs are integrated into portable audio devices by consumer electronics brands, and its finished hardware is sold direct to consumers.
8. The company pairs its amplifier and certification programs with its own direct-to-consumer USB hardware and an open-source immersive audio initiative.

points.name: Bose — QuietComfort
points.description: Bose's noise-cancelling headphone and earbud line for personal, on-the-go listening.
points.bullets:
A consumer audio equipment maker that designs and manufactures noise-cancelling headphones, earbuds, and speakers for personal listening.
1. An equipment maker whose finished audio hardware is sold to consumers.
2. Active noise cancellation, bone and air conduction audio, and spatial audio rendering algorithms run on embedded audio DSPs inside its headphones.
3. Active noise cancellation, spatial audio, open-ear listening via bone and air conduction, and hi-res audio playback.
4. Finished hardware products and over-the-air firmware updates for consumer audio devices.
5. Over-ear headphones, true wireless earbuds, wired USB-C earbuds, and home audio systems.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished audio hardware is sold directly to consumers and through retail channels.
8. Its approach to active noise cancellation and comfort in premium headphones is a benchmark in the consumer audio market.

points.name: Bose — Hearing Health
points.description: Bose's hearing-aid technology, licensed to and co-branded with OTC hearing device partners like Lexie and used in its own SoundControl device.
points.bullets:
A consumer audio company that develops hearing aid technology and self-fitting hearing devices for the over-the-counter hearing aid market.
1. An equipment maker that builds hearing aid technology sold as licensed IP to partners and as finished self-fitting hearing aids.
2. Self-fitting hearing aid technology and Bluetooth-based assistive listening technology.
3. Hearing amplification, self-fitting audio tuning, and Auracast broadcast audio reception for assistive listening.

8. It applies consumer headphone design and long-term research to self-fitting hearing aids regulated as over-the-counter medical devices.

points.name: Bose — Automotive Systems
points.description: Bose's automotive OEM audio business supplying factory sound systems and in-car noise-cancellation technology to automakers.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker and audio technology provider that designs and supplies factory-installed premium automotive sound systems and in-car noise-cancellation technology for automakers.

points.name: Bose — Home Audio
points.description: Bose's home entertainment line of smart speakers, soundbars and multi-room systems for the living room, distinct from its portable personal headphones.

A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs and sells finished home theater systems, soundbars and portable Bluetooth speakers, as well as legacy stereo and radio systems, directly to consumers.

points.name: Sonos — Multi-room Home Sound Systems

A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs and sells wireless speakers, soundbars, subwoofers and streaming components for whole-home audio and home theater use.

points.name: Sonos — Ace

points.name: Sonos — Voice Control

A maker of consumer audio equipment that builds smart speakers and networked home sound systems, and develops a proprietary on-device voice assistant for hands-free control of its own hardware for consumers.

points.name: Yamaha — Digital Mixing Consoles
points.description: Yamaha's line of professional digital mixing consoles for live sound, recording, broadcast, and installed applications, spanning compact to high-end tiers.

A maker of professional audio equipment that builds and sells a broad range of digital mixing consoles for live sound, recording, broadcast, and installed applications. The organization provides compact to high-end touring tier hardware, integrated networking capabilities, and control surfaces for audio engineers and musicians.

points.name: Yamaha — ProVisionaire Installed Sound
points.description: Yamaha's installed-sound and conferencing ecosystem, unifying DSPs, amplifiers, speakers, microphones, and immersive acoustic-enhancement technology for corporate, education, and venue markets.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio and conferencing equipment that builds a complete installed-sound ecosystem of DSPs, amplifiers, speakers, microphones, and acoustic-enhancement technology for corporate, education, and venue markets.

points.name: Yamaha — RIVAGE PM Series
points.description: Yamaha's flagship large-format digital mixing system built on a proprietary digital audio network, aimed at top-tier touring and broadcast production.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds large-format digital mixing systems and digital consoles for live sound reinforcement, touring and broadcast production, alongside a broader portfolio of musical instruments and professional audio gear.

5. Large-scale live sound reinforcement, touring productions, and broadcast facilities.

points.name: Yamaha — MusicCast

An audio equipment manufacturer that builds consumer home-audio products, including networked wireless multiroom AV receivers, amplifiers, and speakers for consumers.

points.name: Klipsch — Reference Wireless

points.bullets:
An audio equipment maker that builds and sells active wireless speakers for consumer home-theater and multi-room installations, built around the WiSA wireless audio standard.

points.name: Klipsch — Automotive Audio Systems

An audio equipment maker that designs and supplies premium OEM in-car audio systems, co-developing branded speaker systems and tuning with automakers and Tier-1 suppliers for vehicle models.

points.name: LG — Sound Suite

A consumer electronics company that builds and sells a modular wireless home theater soundbar ecosystem for consumers.

points.name: LG — XBOOM

An equipment maker that produces a line of portable Bluetooth speakers for consumers. The organization builds rugged, party-style audio devices sold as standalone consumer electronics products. It markets these speakers directly to consumers seeking portable audio for social gatherings.

2. Portable audio systems housed in rugged enclosures with Bluetooth wireless connectivity.

points.name: JBL — Headphones and Earbuds

A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures loudspeakers, subwoofers, power amplifiers, and acoustic simulation software for concert halls, stadiums, and commercial installations.

points.name: JBL — BandBox

points.name: Pioneer — Home AV
