6. Enterprises, game studios, publishers, developers, and government agencies.
7. Its cloud APIs are integrated by enterprises and developers into their content production systems and voice applications.
8. It combines generative voice synthesis with built-in neural audio watermarking and deepfake detection models designed for security and provenance.

points.name: Resemble AI — Deepfake Detection
points.location: Toronto, Canada and San Francisco, California, USA
points.description: A security product line that detects AI-generated voice, image, and video content to prevent fraud and verify identity in real time.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds deepfake detection, identity verification and neural audio watermarking models for enterprises and government agencies.
1. An AI model developer whose deepfake detection and watermarking models run in the cloud behind APIs and within communication platforms.
2. Multimodal neural networks analyze voice, image and video content for synthetic generation artifacts, while neural audio watermarking algorithms embed imperceptible signals for provenance.
3. The company delivers real-time synthetic media detection, replay-attack checks, telephony-resilient voice analysis, identity matching and audio watermarking.
4. Customers access the detection and watermarking models through cloud APIs and native integrations into meeting platforms.
5. The detection models are used in enterprise meetings, telephony systems and fraud-prevention workflows.
6. The company sells to banks, government agencies and enterprises.
7. Its detection models are integrated into enterprise communication platforms and security workflows.
8. The organization embeds imperceptible neural watermarks into synthetic media at creation time to enable subsequent provenance verification.

points.name: Roland — Digital Audio Networking
points.description: Roland develops professional digital-snake and live-mixing/networking technology (REAC/RSS) and digital live consoles used to route audio over networks in touring and installed sound systems.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that develops professional digital audio networking protocols and manufactures digital live mixing consoles used to route audio over networks in touring and installed sound systems. It builds proprietary digital snake protocols and integrates them into hardware mixers and software for live sound reinforcement. Its products are used by live sound engineers in venues, touring rigs and installed sound environments.
1. A manufacturer of professional audio equipment and networked live mixing consoles that run as finished hardware in touring and installed sound systems, complemented by proprietary digital audio networking protocols.
2. Digital audio networking protocols for routing multichannel audio over Ethernet and digital mixing and signal processing engines running in dedicated live sound hardware.
3. Multichannel audio routing over Ethernet networks, live digital mixing, digital snake signal transport and networked audio integration with third-party audio networking cards.
4. Finished hardware products including digital live mixing consoles and hardware integration cards, alongside proprietary digital audio networking protocols.
5. Touring sound systems, installed sound systems, live venues, churches and concert stages.
6. Live sound engineers, production companies, installation integrators and touring musicians.
7. Its digital mixing consoles and networking protocols are deployed directly by live sound engineers in touring and installed sound systems, with hardware integration supported by third-party audio networking card compatibility.
8. It develops its own proprietary digital snake protocols rather than relying solely on open networking standards, and embeds them in dedicated live mixing hardware.

points.name: Roland — Guitar Amplification and Effects
points.description: Under the Roland brand itself (predating/parallel to its BOSS subsidiary), Roland makes guitar amplifiers and standalone effects pedals aimed at guitarists rather than keyboard/synth players.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures guitar amplifiers and effects pedals for guitarists and musicians.
1. An equipment maker whose finished hardware products are sold to musicians.
2. Analog and digital signal processing circuits for guitar amplification and effects generation.
3. Guitar amplification, chorus, phasing, flanging, sustain and synthesizer-based guitar effects.
4. Finished hardware including guitar amplifiers and standalone effects pedals.
5. Stages, studios and live performance rigs where guitarists play.
6. Guitarists and musicians.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to musicians through musical instrument retailers.
8. It produces some of the longest-running and historically landmark guitar amplifier and effects products in the music industry.

points.name: Cisco — Webex Room Devices
points.description: Cisco's line of conference-room hardware (cameras, displays, microphones, bars) running RoomOS for video collaboration.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that manufactures conference-room hardware, including cameras, displays, microphones and integrated bars, running its own collaboration operating system for enterprise video conferencing.
1. A manufacturer of finished video conferencing hardware and companion software sold as physical endpoints that run a proprietary operating system in enterprise meeting rooms.
2. A combination of ceiling-array microphones, integrated camera bars and proprietary collaboration software running on dedicated meeting room hardware.
3. AI-powered camera framing, zero-lag whiteboarding, ceiling microphone audio capture and unified video conferencing.
4. Finished hardware devices accompanied by proprietary operating system software and firmware updates.
5. Enterprise conference rooms, huddle spaces and unified communication meeting rooms.
6. Enterprises standardizing on dedicated collaboration hardware for their meeting spaces.
7. Its finished hardware and software are deployed directly into enterprise conference rooms by organizations.
8. Its devices run a proprietary operating system while maintaining certification for multiple third-party video conferencing platforms.

points.name: Cisco — Webex CCaaS
points.description: Cisco's cloud-based contact-center-as-a-service and communications platform aimed at enterprise CX/voice deployments, distinct from meeting-room hardware.
points.bullets:
An enterprise software company that provides a cloud-based contact-center-as-a-service and communications platform for customer experience and voice deployments. The platform delivers cloud communication services and contact center capabilities through cloud-based APIs and services for enterprise contact-center customers.
1. A cloud communication platform provider whose contact-center-as-a-service software runs in the cloud behind APIs.
2. The platform delivers enterprise contact center voice communications and customer experience capabilities.
3. Enterprises get it as a cloud-based software-as-a-service platform and through cloud-based APIs.
4. The platform is used in contact centers and enterprise voice customer experience deployments.
5. The company sells to enterprises operating contact centers and needing cloud communications.
6. Its cloud communication platform is deployed directly by enterprises to run their contact center operations.

points.name: Nokia — MPEG-I Immersive Audio
points.description: Nokia contributes core rendering technology and standardization work to the MPEG-I immersive audio standard for VR/AR audio experiences, a separate consumer/XR market from cellular voice calls.
points.bullets:
A multinational telecommunications company contributing core spatial rendering technology and standardization work to the MPEG-I immersive audio standard for VR and AR audio experiences. It develops rendering algorithms and evaluation software tools for consumer mobile devices targeting extended reality applications.
1. A technology contributor whose spatial audio rendering algorithms and reference software are contributed to industry standards and run on consumer mobile devices.
2. Spatial audio rendering algorithms, including late reverberation rendering, augmented reality support, and rendering of multiple higher-order ambisonics captures.
3. Immersive audio rendering, late reverberation, augmented reality audio support, and higher-order ambisonics capture rendering for extended reality environments.
4. Baseline technology, core experiments, and evaluation software tools contributed to standardized immersive audio specifications.
5. VR and AR headsets, consumer mobile devices, and 6G extended reality audio experiences.
6. Standards bodies, extended reality device makers, and mobile network operators.
7. Its core rendering technology is standardized and integrated into mobile devices and extended reality platforms by consumer electronics brands.
8. Contributes baseline technology and standardization work directly to the MPEG-I immersive audio standard while researching early-adopter feedback for mobile rendering.

points.name: Kyutai — Moshi
points.description: Kyutai's open-source full-duplex speech-to-speech conversational AI architecture, bundling the Moshi dialogue model, Mimi audio codec, and Helium language-model backbone, aimed at developers and labs building real-time voice AI.
points.bullets:
An AI research lab that develops and openly releases full-duplex speech-to-speech conversational AI models, neural audio codecs, and language model backbones for developers and research labs building real-time voice AI.
1. An AI model developer whose speech models and neural codecs are released openly and run in the cloud and on local compute infrastructure.
2. Dual-stream transformer architecture built on a text-trained language model backbone, utilizing a neural audio codec to tokenize audio for simultaneous listening and speaking.
3. Real-time full-duplex speech-to-speech conversation, speech modeling, audio tokenization, and simultaneous listening and speaking.
4. Open-source model weights, code, and technical reports released under permissive licenses.
5. Real-time conversational voice AI agents and speech interface research.
6. Developers, research labs, and other AI model developers.
7. Its foundation models and architectures are integrated and built upon by other AI developers creating downstream voice AI products.
8. Models user speech and its own speech in parallel using a dual-stream transformer architecture to achieve full-duplex conversation.

points.name: Kyutai — Pocket TTS
points.description: A separate, lightweight CPU-efficient streaming text-to-speech model line aimed at on-device/embedded app developers, distinct from the server-oriented Moshi conversational platform.
points.bullets:
A research lab that develops on-device text-to-speech models for embedded application developers. It builds lightweight, CPU-efficient streaming speech synthesis models designed to run directly on local hardware, and provides training scripts and evaluation tools alongside them.
1. An AI model developer whose speech models run on-device on consumer hardware.
2. Lightweight neural networks designed for efficient CPU inference in streaming environments.
3. Streaming text-to-speech synthesis and voice cloning.
4. Open-source models, language packs, training scripts, and evaluation tools distributed via code repositories.
5. On-device and embedded applications.
6. Embedded application developers and open-source community contributors.
7. Its models are integrated by inference platforms and application developers into end-user software.
8. Its models are optimized for low-footprint, CPU-efficient streaming synthesis on local devices rather than server-side cloud processing.

points.name: ByteDance — Doubao
points.description: ByteDance's conversational AI model line that powers real-time voice assistant and voice-agent functions for automotive and consumer deployments.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose large language and conversational voice models power real-time voice assistant and voice-agent functions for automotive and consumer deployments.
1. An AI model developer whose real-time conversational voice models run in the cloud behind an API.
2. Large language models and full-duplex conversational voice models running in the cloud.
3. Real-time conversational voice agents, voice command functions, full-duplex spoken interaction with reduced false responses and talk-overs.
4. Cloud APIs integrated by automotive and consumer electronics makers.
5. In-car voice assistant systems and real-time conversational voice agents.
6. Automakers and consumer electronics brands.
7. Its cloud models are integrated by automakers into their in-car voice assistant systems.
8. Full-duplex deployment of its conversational models reduces false responses and talk-overs compared to half-duplex predecessors.

clusters.name: Public Address & Paging Systems
clusters.description: These companies make amplifiers, speakers, PA/paging, and conferencing equipment for commercial installed-sound and public-address markets.

clusters.name: Generative Music & Audio Models
clusters.description: These organizations develop AI models and platforms that generate, synthesize, or analyze music, speech, and voice content from prompts or audio input.

clusters.name: Smart Glasses & Health Hearables
clusters.description: These companies make AI-enabled digital stethoscopes and acoustic exam tools that capture heart, lung, and body sounds for remote diagnosis and telemedicine.

clusters.name: Headphones & Bluetooth Speakers
clusters.description: These companies design, manufacture, and sell finished headphones, earbuds, and in-ear monitors directly to consumers and musicians.

clusters.name: Guitar Effects & Amp Modelers
clusters.description: These companies design and sell guitar/bass effects pedals, amp modelers, and multi-effects hardware aimed at musicians.

clusters.name: PA Mixers & Microphones
clusters.description: These companies manufacture mixing consoles, loudspeakers, amplifiers, and microphones for live sound reinforcement and PA applications.

clusters.name: Hi-Fi & Home Theater Speakers
clusters.description: These companies design and build finished loudspeakers and home audio systems sold directly to consumers.

clusters.name: Audio Codec IP Licensing
clusters.description: These organizations develop and license proprietary or standardized audio/voice codec technologies (compression formats and transmission protocols) to chipmakers and device manufacturers rather than selling finished products.

clusters.name: Consumer Headphones & Home Audio
clusters.description: These companies design and sell finished consumer audio products—headphones, earbuds, speakers, soundbars, and car audio systems—sold directly to end users.

clusters.name: DAWs & Audio Plugins
clusters.description: These companies build digital audio workstations, mixing/mastering plugins, and sound libraries that musicians and audio engineers use directly for music production and audio editing.

clusters.name: Audio Amplifier & Converter Chips
clusters.description: These companies design semiconductor ICs—Class-D amplifiers, DACs/ADCs, and audio codecs—that power finished audio and voice-enabled products.

clusters.name: Loudspeaker Driver Manufacturers
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture raw loudspeaker drivers, woofers, tweeters, and compression drivers sold as components to speaker and audio-system builders rather than finished products.

clusters.name: Speech & Audio Datasets
clusters.description: These organizations collect, license, or crowdsource speech and audio recordings used as training data for voice and audio AI models.

clusters.name: Studio Interfaces & Outboard Gear
clusters.description: These companies design and build finished studio/live-sound gear—mixing consoles, audio interfaces, outboard processors, and signal processors—sold to recording studios and sound engineers.

clusters.name: Studio Monitor Manufacturers
clusters.description: These companies design and build studio reference monitors and professional loudspeakers used for critical listening, mixing, and mastering.

clusters.name: MEMS Microphone & Microspeaker Suppliers
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture MEMS microphones and microspeakers as silicon/transducer components sold into smartphones, wearables, hearables, automotive and IoT devices rather than selling finished audio products themselves.

clusters.name: Acoustic Test & Simulation Tools
clusters.description: These companies build measurement instruments, analyzers, and simulation software used to test, characterize, and model acoustic and audio performance.

clusters.name: Edge AI Audio Processors
clusters.description: These companies design low-power chips, NPU cores, and neuromorphic processors that run on-device AI inference for voice and audio sensing in embedded and battery-powered devices.

clusters.name: Concert & Venue Loudspeaker Systems
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture loudspeakers, amplifiers, and system software for live sound, touring, and installed audio venues.

clusters.name: Speech Recognition & Voice Assistants
clusters.description: These companies develop AI models and cloud/API platforms for speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and conversational voice assistants.

clusters.name: Audio Standards Bodies
clusters.description: These organizations develop, certify, and license technical standards governing audio formats, codecs, and device interoperability.

clusters.name: Wireless Microphone Systems
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture wireless microphone transmitters, receivers, and RF systems for live sound, broadcast, and film production.

clusters.name: Automotive Audio Systems
clusters.description: These companies design and supply branded or OEM sound systems built into vehicles, from premium automaker-partnered audio to aftermarket car speakers and amplifiers.

clusters.name: Hi-Fi Components & Streamers
clusters.description: These companies make finished hi-fi and home-theater components—speakers, amplifiers, receivers, DACs, and streamers—for home listening setups.

clusters.name: Wireless Earbuds & ANC Headphones
clusters.description: These companies design and sell finished wireless headphones, earbuds, and hearables directly to consumers under their own brand names.

clusters.name: Text-to-Speech & Voice Agents
clusters.description: These companies build AI-driven voice generation and conversational agent platforms, spanning text-to-speech, voice cloning, and real-time voice agents.

clusters.name: Portable PA & Live Loudspeakers
clusters.description: These companies design and build the loudspeakers, line arrays, and PA systems used for live sound reinforcement, touring, and installed venues.

clusters.name: Live Sound Mixing Consoles
clusters.description: These companies build digital and analog mixing consoles for live sound, broadcast, and studio applications.

clusters.name: Conference Room Audio & Headsets
clusters.description: These companies build the microphones, speakerphones, headsets, and room systems used for business video/audio conferencing.

clusters.name: AI-Powered Mastering & Repair
clusters.description: These companies provide AI-driven software services and plugins for automated mixing, mastering, noise reduction, and audio restoration.

clusters.name: Power Amplifiers & Sound Processors
clusters.description: These companies design DSP processors and amplifier modules/hardware that pro audio and installed-sound equipment makers integrate into speakers, consoles, and system controllers.

clusters.name: Bluetooth Audio SoCs
clusters.description: These companies design semiconductor chips and system-on-chips that handle Bluetooth wireless audio processing for earbuds, headsets, and speakers.

clusters.name: OTC & Direct-to-Consumer Hearing Aids
clusters.description: These entities design and sell finished hearing aids and OTC hearing devices directly to consumers.

clusters.name: High-End Audiophile Loudspeakers
clusters.description: These companies design and build finished loudspeakers—from luxury and audiophile home speakers to studio monitors—as complete consumer or professional products.

clusters.name: Studio Microphone Manufacturers
clusters.description: These companies design and build professional condenser, dynamic, and ribbon microphones for studio recording, broadcast, and live sound.

clusters.name: Stem Separation & Speech Enhancement
clusters.description: These companies build AI-driven software that isolates or separates vocals, instruments, and speech from mixed audio recordings for music, broadcast, and communication applications.

clusters.name: DAWs & Music Production Hardware
clusters.description: These companies build the professional software and hardware tools—DAWs, mixing consoles, plugins, and audio interfaces—used by producers, engineers, and DJs to create and perform music.

clusters.name: In-Ear Monitors & Micro-Drivers
clusters.description: These companies manufacture miniature transducers—balanced armature receivers, micro-speakers, and MEMS-based drivers—that are integrated into hearing aids, in-ear monitors, and earphones made by other brands.

clusters.name: Broadcast Audio & IP Networking
clusters.description: These companies make broadcast and professional audio mixing consoles, interfaces, and converters built around IP-networked audio protocols for studio, live, and broadcast production.

clusters.name: DACs & Headphone Amplifiers
clusters.description: These companies design and sell finished high-fidelity audio gear—DACs, headphone amps, speakers, and streamers—targeting enthusiast listeners.

clusters.name: Architectural & Installed Loudspeakers
clusters.description: These companies design and build finished loudspeaker systems—passive and active speakers, amplifiers, and cabinets—for live sound, studio, residential, and portable use.

clusters.name: Immersive Audio Formats & IP
clusters.description: Companies that develop or license spatial/3D audio algorithms, codecs, and immersive-sound formats for integration into earbuds, TVs, speakers, and voice devices rather than selling finished products themselves.

clusters.name: AV Integration & Signal Distribution
clusters.description: These companies manufacture the processors, amplifiers, mixers, connectors, and networked audio/video distribution hardware used to build out live sound and commercial AV installations.

clusters.name: Live & Cinema Sound Electronics
clusters.description: These companies manufacture mixing consoles, amplifiers, PA systems, and speakers for live performance, broadcast, and installed sound venues.

clusters.name: 3D Audio Rendering & Middleware
clusters.description: These companies develop spatial audio, room correction, and 3D sound rendering algorithms licensed into consumer electronics, automotive, gaming, and home theater products.

clusters.name: Prescription Hearing Aids & Implants
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture finished hearing aid and hearing device products sold to end users.

clusters.name: OEM/ODM Audio Manufacturing
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture finished audio hardware—speakers, headphones, amplifiers, mixing consoles, and processors—as contract OEM/ODM suppliers for other global audio brands.

clusters.name: Home Theater Receivers & Speakers
clusters.description: These companies design and sell finished consumer audio hardware—home theater receivers, wireless and multi-room speakers, and related home entertainment audio systems—often as multi-brand manufacturers or ODMs.
